Which office handles what

Two neighboring suites in the Courthouse Annex on Tippins Street in Baxley divide the job. Suite 101 houses the Board of Tax Assessors, who put a value on your land and house. Suite 102 houses the Tax Commissioner, who sends the bill and collects payment.

A wrong turn costs you a trip. Take value questions, record errors, exemptions and appeals to the assessors. Take balances, payment options and back taxes to the tax commissioner. You can look up a parcel at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the commissioner's page links to online payment.

Appling County offices a seller may need
OfficeLocationPhone
Board of Tax Assessors69 Tippins Street, Suite 101, Baxley(912) 367-8108
Tax Commissioner69 Tippins Street, Suite 102, Baxley(912) 367-8105
Clerk of Courts69 Tippins Street, Suite 103, Baxley(912) 367-8126
Probate Court36 South Main Street, Baxley(912) 367-8114

The tax commissioner's counter is open weekdays, from 8 to 5. Liens against a parcel are recorded through the clerk, so Suite 103 matters when a county claim is attached to a house headed to market.

Appling County housing in brief

Appling County spreads across about 507 square miles of southeast Georgia. Baxley is both its seat and its biggest town. About 19,100 people live here, 3.5 percent more than in 2020. Owners hold 72.5 percent of households. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $76,700, against median household income of $46,651. Only 21 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction rarely competes with a resale, and a seller here is mostly pricing against other older homes in town and the outlying farm roads. The county and the cities of Baxley, Graham and Surrency prepare a joint comprehensive plan, which is worth a look if you own land on the edge of town.

How a house is valued each year

The assessors set value as of January 1 and tax 40 percent of it. Take that assessed figure, subtract exemptions, and multiply by the millage rate. A mill equals a tenth of a cent per assessed dollar.

You may file a return from the start of the year to April 1, though you only need to when the parcel changed, say through a new building or extra acreage. Skipping a required return adds a 10 percent penalty on the unreported value and interest. Equipment and other personal property need a return each year by April 1.

Notices arrive in May. They list the value and carry an estimated bill using the previous year's rates, but the county tells owners this estimate is not a bill. The commissioners and school board have not finished budgets when the notice goes out, and millage usually gets set around September.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Appling County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What due date to expect

Georgia's default is December 20, with 60 days after billing to pay, yet your own bill's printed date is what counts. Most counties follow December 20.

The bill goes to the person who owned the house on New Year's Day. Even if you close in June, a statement can show up in fall for a home you no longer hold. Who actually pays is settled by your contract and the closing statement.

  • Pay in the tax commissioner's suite, by mail, or through the county's online portal.
  • Get any open year's payoff in writing before closing day.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit from the tax commissioner, applied for within 30 days of placing it and renewed every year before April 2.

Phone (912) 367-8105 to learn this year's bill date and what late charges apply.

How to dispute a value

Put the appeal on paper and bring it to Suite 101 within 45 days of the date printed on your notice. It has to be in hand by that day, and late filings are refused.

The tax rate cannot be appealed. Grounds are limited to taxability, value and uniformity, and you choose the path on state form PT-311A. Assessors get the first look. If the number stands, a Board of Equalization takes over, made up of citizens the grand jury appoints. You can pick arbitration instead, and a hearing officer is open only to non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.

After a loss, a written notice for Superior Court must reach the assessors within 30 days after the decision is mailed or handed over. Before the court hears the case, state law requires payment of tax matching the last year in which tax was found due. The state revenue department has no power to overrule a local board on one parcel.

Can you claim a homestead exemption in Appling County?

Yes, for the home you legally live in. Here, unlike some counties, you apply at the Tax Assessors' office rather than with the tax commissioner.

Apply the year the house becomes your main residence, or up to April 1 of the next year. Once approved, it carries forward on its own unless you want to switch types. Appling has raised its local amounts above the state minimum, and the county tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category. Ask the assessors at (912) 367-8108 for the current dollar amounts.

The savings belong to you, not the property. Your buyer must file separately, which means the first bill after closing will likely arrive without the exemption. The county commissioners also keep a posting about a school district ad valorem exemption on their meetings page.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Appling County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Expect to pay it out of the proceeds. Unpaid tax follows the parcel, and a recorded county lien has to clear before the buyer gets clean title. Liens are filed with the clerk.

Each year's bill lands on the January 1 owner, and nothing is refunded for a partial year. Seller and buyer divide the year in the sales contract, and the closing attorney forwards the county's share. For an inherited house, the Probate Court on South Main Street handles the estate.

  • Get a payoff figure from Suite 102 for each year still open.
  • Search the clerk's files for liens on the parcel.
  • Put your latest assessment notice in the closing folder.
  • Read the settlement statement for a tax line before signing.

A cash buyer can close faster, but the payoff figures and lien check still come first. If you inherited the house, sort out the estate with the Probate Court before anyone signs a listing, since the buyer's attorney will ask who has authority to convey. Bring the death certificate and any court papers to the Baxley office, and ask the Tax Commissioner whether the bill is still in the decedent's name so the payoff letter shows the right owner.

Frequently asked questions

Can I pay my Appling County tax bill online?

Yes. The tax commissioner's office points owners to a county online payment portal, and it also takes payments in person at Suite 102, 69 Tippins Street in Baxley, and by mail. The office phone is (912) 367-8105.

What fraction of market value does Appling County tax?

Forty percent of the January 1 fair market value. Exemptions come off that assessed figure first, then the millage rate is applied to what is left. One mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

Is there any way to appeal after the notice period ends?

No. An appeal cannot be filed after the 45 days run out. The following year's notice brings the next chance, so note the deadline the day it arrives.

Who pays the tax in the year a house sells?

The owner at New Year is billed, but the sales contract can move the cost to the buyer for the months after closing. The closing attorney typically prorates the year and pays the county, so check that the settlement statement shows it.

Which phone number is for value questions?

Call (912) 367-8108, the Board of Tax Assessors, for values, records, appeals and exemptions. Dial the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105 for billing and payments.

Bacon County at a glance

Bacon County sits in southeast Georgia with Alma as the seat, and it is mostly open country. Around 11,070 people call it home, slightly fewer than the 11,140 counted in 2020, so you will not find crowds. A typical listing is a house on a country lot, often with a well, a septic tank and room for outbuildings.

Alma is the lone city. Rockingham, Coffee and Sessoms are small outlying communities, so many owners hold land well outside town.

Home values and what buyers compare

Home prices rank near the bottom statewide. Owners occupy 68.6% of the housing.

Local housing numbers (2020-2024 unless a date is shown)

Owner-occupied homes, middle value$101,400

Only fourteen permits were issued in all of 2025, so hardly any new houses are going up and a shopper will compare yours with older stock. Turnover is slow too. Price your place against recent closings close by, not against a statewide average.

In 2020, 4,807 housing units existed here and about 11.6% were vacant, while 31.7% of occupied units were rentals. Empty houses mean your listing may compete with several that need work.

Who to see in Alma

Both the tax commissioner and the assessors are in the Bacon County Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. Call 912-632-5614 during office hours, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. The commissioner's website has more.

  • Suite 101, tax commissioner: bills, what you owe, liens, mobile home permits
  • Suite 101, tax assessors: your value, returns, exemptions, appeals
  • Suite 200, Clerk of Superior Court: deed copies

Look up a parcel on qPublic. The website is general information only and state law wins if the two differ, so phone the office whenever the exact amount matters.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bacon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

November 15 is the usual due date, with bills mailed at least two months ahead. That date can shift in a given year, so follow what your own bill says.

Two installments are available, but any balance left after the deadline keeps growing. A check in the mail is on time if postmarked by the due date, and weekends and holidays push the date to the next business day. Look for the drop box at the right edge of the front lot. Paying by card costs an extra 2.75% to the processor, at least $2.00.

  • Interest is added each month at prime plus three percentage points
  • A 5% penalty hits at the 120-day mark, repeats at each further 120 days, and caps at 20%
  • Homesteaded parcels billed under $500 are spared the penalty
  • Mobile homes have their own April 1 due date, with a 10% penalty

Can a tax lien follow a Bacon County sale?

Yes, if the bill is still open. A month after the bill goes unpaid, the office may record a FiFa, a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket. The county cautions that it can follow you on a credit file for seven years or more. Delinquent notices are sent only now and then, so phone for today's figure before paying.

Georgia puts the lien on the person who held title on January 1. To shift it to your buyer, take the signed closing statement to Suite 101 inside 90 days of the due date. If a bill finds you after you have sold, pass it along to the buyer.

  1. Get a written payoff figure from Suite 101.
  2. Let the title company deduct it at closing.
  3. Save your settlement statement.

How to contest your value

Count 45 days from the date on your assessment notice. Hand the assessors a written dispute on the standard state form, giving one reason: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Your filing also picks the route the case takes. Pick the Board of Equalization and the assessors get a chance to revise the figure, which opens 30 days to answer any amended notice. A dispute that survives goes to a board hearing, then possibly Superior Court. Non-homestead real estate above a set value can use a hearing officer instead. Arbitration needs a certified appraisal and settles the question for good.

You can also state your own value on a return filed between January 1 and April 1. Real estate returns roll forward without refiling. Personal property needs a fresh return each year.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bacon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions that can lower the bill

Homestead matters most for owner-occupants. A statewide baseline applies, Bacon County layers its own exemptions on top, and the bigger of the two is what you get. You must own and occupy the house on January 1, and your form has to be in the assessors' hands by April 1 in your first year. After approval it renews each year without refiling.

  • Tax deferral for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less
  • Qualifying farmland is assessed at 30%, not the usual 40%
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection programs value land by its current use and bind you to a 10 or 15 year covenant
  • Historic and brownfield programs use the same January to April filing window

Call 912-632-5614 for the local amounts and what proof to bring. Claiming homestead on a second property anywhere, in or out of Georgia, is unlawful.

Selling with taxes owed

Start by getting the numbers. Find out what is owed for each unpaid year, whether a FiFa has been filed, and for a mobile home, whether the April 1 permit tax is current. After that, decide whether to pay now or let the closing agent pay it.

Inherited houses, rentals and vacant properties often carry several unpaid years, and a title search will turn up every recorded lien. Land enrolled in a conservation or forest program needs one more check: ask the assessors what the covenant requires of the next owner, because buyers will want to know.

When you visit Suite 101, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest bill and, if you are already under contract, the signed closing statement. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can close without repairs, though the tax balance is still paid out of your proceeds. Skipping listing, showings and buyer financing also skips weeks of lender appraisal delay, which helps when a bill or lien date is near.

If you sell after the bill is mailed but before it is due, say in the contract who pays it. Get the payoff in writing, keep the receipt, and send the office the closing statement so the record follows the new owner.

Frequently asked questions

What share of market value is taxed in Bacon County?

Assessed value is 40% of fair market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that, and the millage rate, set yearly by the county commissioners and the school board, is applied to what remains.

How can I pay a Bacon County bill?

You can pay in person at Suite 101 in Alma, mail a check postmarked by the deadline, use the drop box, or pay by card online. Call 912-632-5614 with questions.

Does selling split the bill between buyer and seller?

Your closing statement divides it, not the county. If you want any lien recorded against the buyer, deliver the signed statement to Suite 101 within 90 days of the due date.

Is there a refund if I sell in March?

No. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year, and Georgia gives part-year owners no refund.

Who sends the notice of my home's value?

The Board of Tax Assessors, in the same building. Call 912-632-5614, and remember the 45-day appeal clock starts on the notice date.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Baldwin County?

Baldwin County in brief

Milledgeville, the county seat, is a college town that was Georgia's capital from 1804 to 1868. Georgia College and State University and Georgia Military College fill the town with students and staff. The old Governor's Mansion and the historic district add older homes, so the housing here spans many decades.

At 267 square miles, the county runs hilly in the north and flat toward the south. Your property could be a city lot or acreage far out, and buyers for each look nothing alike.

Housing and market numbers

Renting is common in Baldwin County. Only 61.1% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the middle value of an owned home is $181,900.

Baldwin County numbers for 2020-2024, except where a date appears
What was measuredLatest figure
Owner-occupied homes, middle value$181,900
Gross rent per month, middle value$923

Housing units (July 2025)20,797
Building permits issued (2025)95
Residents (July 2025 estimate)44,029

In 2020 the county tallied 19,988 housing units, 17.4% of them vacant. Of the occupied ones, 42.1% were rented. Between 2010 and 2020 the county lost 4.2% of its people, then gained a little, and 48.8% of residents lived in rural areas. With rentals so common, an investor may be the best fit for a tenant-occupied house you want to sell as it stands.

Where to go in Milledgeville

Visit the tax commissioner at the Baldwin County Government Building, 1601 N. Columbia Street, Suite 100, Milledgeville, GA 31061, or phone 478-445-4813. It is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:45 in the afternoon, and closed on holidays. The county's tax site has details.

Disagree with your house's value? Ring the tax assessors at (478) 445-5300. You can pull up parcel data on qPublic. Each of the five county board members is elected from a single district, and the board helps set the county's portion of the millage rate. The school board adds its own rate.

  • Tax commissioner: what you owe, payments, liens, closing statements
  • Tax assessors: your value, returns, exemptions, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Baldwin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Most bills come due November 15 after going out at least 60 days earlier. Some carry December 15 instead. Whatever date is printed on your bill is the one to follow, and the commissioner can clear up any doubt.

Paying in two parts is allowed, though the unpaid remainder keeps accruing. A check sent by mail is on time when its postmark is no later than the deadline. If the deadline lands on a weekend or holiday, you get the next business day. Out front there is a drop box. Paying by card brings a processor fee of 2.57% (3% for American Express), minimum $1.50.

  • Monthly interest runs at prime plus 3 points
  • Penalties start at 5% once 120 days pass, add another 5% every 120 days, and stop when they total 20%
  • No penalty for homesteaded property when the bill is under $500
  • Mobile homes: April 1 due date, 10% penalty, and a possible State Court citation

Selling with an unpaid bill

Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff in writing. The closing agent then deducts that amount from what you receive. In Georgia the year's tax follows the January 1 owner. The office records a lien under that owner's name unless Suite 100 gets a closing statement that shows the buyer took over the bill, and it must arrive within 90 days after the due date.

A bill that still reaches you after closing should go on to the buyer, with a settlement statement copy sent to the office. An unpaid bill can lead to a FiFa lien on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court, and the county says such an entry can stay on credit files for seven years or longer.

Insist on a dated payoff. Interest accrues monthly but delinquent notices rarely go out that often, so last week's figure can come up short. Rentals, inherited houses and vacant ones may owe for several years, so request the history for each year you held the property.

Step by step, a clean sale usually looks like this:

  1. Bring your deed or parcel number and any bills you still have to Suite 100.
  2. Get the payoff in writing, with the date it is good through.
  3. Hand the closing agent that figure.
  4. Return the signed closing statement to the office within 90 days of the due date.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can close fast, which helps when a penalty date is near. The tax still gets paid at closing, but you avoid repair requests and lender delays.

How to appeal your assessment

The clock runs 45 days from the date on your assessment notice. Submit a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors on the state form and pick a ground from four: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

The filing also chooses your route. Take the Board of Equalization path and the assessors may amend the value first, after which you have 30 days to contest the amended notice. If that fails, a hearing is set, and Superior Court is the step beyond it. Only non-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or more can go to a hearing officer, who has to be a certified appraiser. Arbitration calls for a certified appraisal, and its result is final.

Before filing, open your parcel on qPublic and compare it with nearby houses. Collect photos of damage, a repair estimate or a recent appraisal, and keep copies of whatever you submit. A lower value saves money only while you own the house, but an appeal still pending can give a buyer something to discuss.

State revenue staff have no power to overrule the assessors, a board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or a court on one parcel. For a mobile home the clock is 45 days from the bill's mailing or from April 1, whichever comes last.

Exemptions worth checking

Homestead relief here comes from two layers, the state's and Baldwin County's own, and you get whichever is bigger. Your application has to reach the assessors by April 1 in the first year. After approval it renews by itself.

  • Be the owner and the resident on January 1 of that first year
  • A second homestead claim anywhere, in Georgia or out of state, is barred
  • Owners aged 62 and up with household income at or under $15,000 may defer the tax
  • Farmland that qualifies is assessed at 30%, not 40%, and current-use programs tie you to a 10 or 15 year covenant

Timing matters. A buyer who closes after the April 1 cutoff will generally have to wait until the next year to benefit. Tell the buyer's agent whether a homestead exemption is on the property now, because the new owner has to apply separately.

Call (478) 445-5300 for today's amounts, and bring proof of age, income or service if your exemption depends on it.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about my Baldwin County tax bill?

The tax commissioner answers at 478-445-4813. Walk-ins go to Suite 100 at 1601 N. Columbia Street in Milledgeville.

Can I pay online in Baldwin County?

Yes. The county runs an online payment page and charges a processor fee on cards. Paying in person, by mail or in the drop box works too.

Does a sale wipe out the bill for that year?

No. The January 1 owner stays on record for that year, and only a closing statement delivered within 90 days of the due date changes who a lien names.

What fraction of value is taxed in Baldwin County?

Forty percent of market value, or 30% when the land qualifies as agricultural. Exemptions are deducted first, and then the millage rate is applied.

What is the deadline to contest a Baldwin County value?

Forty-five days, starting on the date of the notice. Mobile homes follow a different start: the bill's mailing or April 1, whichever falls later.

Banks County in brief

Banks County fills the northeast corner of Georgia, with Homer as the county seat. The cities are Baldwin, Commerce, Gillsville and Lula, and the towns are Alto, Homer and Maysville. Several of these straddle a line with Habersham, Jackson or Hall, so a mailing address can name a town that sits partly in a neighboring county. Open the parcel record to learn which tax commissioner bills you.

Growth has been brisk lately. The 2020 census counted 18,035 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 21,273, up 17.6% from the adjusted 2020 base. About 95.6% of residents lived in rural areas in 2020.

Home values and what buyers see

The middle household income is $77,063 for 2020-2024, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $278,100.

The long view is steeper than the recent one. Banks County had 6,497 people in 1960, 14,422 in 2000 and 18,395 in 2010, then slipped to 18,035 in 2020 before the newer estimate jumped. A county that nearly tripled between 1960 and 2010 has houses of very different ages, from farmhouses to recent subdivisions, and buyers compare them closely.

Where to send tax questions

The tax commissioner bills and collects for the county, the state, the school board and community improvement districts. In person, go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547. The county payment page shows weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

Call 706-677-6204 about a bill. For your valuation, an appeal, or word that a property was sold or a business closed after January 1, call the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. A postmark from the U.S. Postal Service dated by midnight of the deadline counts as on time, but a postage-meter date does not.

  • Suite 7: property taxes in person
  • Tax commissioner phone: 706-677-6204
  • Board of Assessors phone: 706-677-6223

Your assessment notice

Every owner of taxable real property gets a notice each year. It shows the fair market value set by the Board of Tax Assessors and the assessed value, which state law fixes at 40%.

The assessors look at sales in groups, sorted by neighborhood, property type and use, and they adjust a whole group when market evidence says values have drifted. Any change shows on your notice. If you disagree, you have 45 days from the notice date to appeal on grounds of taxability, value or non-uniform assessment.

Bills usually arrive in September. A parcel still under appeal at that point is billed on a temporary value, the smaller of last year's value or 85% of the original notice value this year, and the bill is still due on the printed date. When the appeal ends, the commissioner decides whether a supplemental bill or a credit follows.

Handling the tax during a sale

The tax commissioner does not prorate tax between a buyer and a seller. That is settled at closing, usually with the purchaser assuming it, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. Since the tax attaches to the property, whoever holds title should confirm it is paid.

A property that sold, or a business that closed, after January 1 still owes tax for the full year, and the Board of Assessors should be told. If a mortgage company pays your tax, the office would like you to forward them a copy of the bill.

Because Banks County has grown so fast, many neighbors are selling newer houses, and buyers tend to ask for the tax history. Having a recent bill and a receipt ready speeds up the conversation and keeps a contract from stalling over a small balance nobody knew about.

  • A missing bill is no excuse, and copies are online or at the office
  • Partial payments are accepted until the bill is paid, by arrangement at 706-677-6204
  • Write the parcel ID on a check or money order

If an appeal is still open at the due date

Pay at least the appealed amount by the due date or a 1% penalty applies. You cannot put payment off, and the assessors cannot extend the deadline. Interest of 1% per month, capped at $150, builds on the rest, and paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

If you plan to sell during an appeal, tell your closing agent. The final figure may change, a supplemental bill or credit may follow, and you should agree in writing who keeps any refund.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Banks County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How exemptions get approved

Nothing is automatic, and each exemption needs its own application. The name on the deed must match the applicant, who must own, occupy and claim the home as a legal residence on January 1. Bring proof of residency and of citizenship or legal authorization, plus current registration or receipts for vehicles owned in Banks County.

A married couple counts as one applicant and gets one exemption. Once granted it renews, and a refinance does not call for a new filing. A change of name or ownership through marriage, death or divorce means reapplying with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. A faxed or emailed application is rejected. An original must arrive, or carry a non-metered postmark, by the April 1 deadline for a first-year claim.

If you are selling, remember that the exemption belongs to you and not to the house. Tell the buyer to file a fresh application, ideally right after closing, so they do not miss the April 1 cutoff in their first year.

Forms and instructions are on the county's Tax Assessors page, and the local amounts are there too.

First steps for a seller with tax due

Call 706-677-6204 and ask what is owed on the parcel for this year and any earlier ones. If part of the balance is under appeal, say so on the same call, since the temporary-value bill applies. Then give your closing agent the amount and the Suite 7 address, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer.

If an exemption is on the property and you are moving, tell the tax commissioner once you no longer qualify. After a change of ownership, the new owner has to apply on their own.

Gather these before you list or close: your deed or parcel ID, the latest bill, any appeal paperwork, and the contact for your mortgage servicer if it pays your tax. A cash buyer who purchases as-is skips repair requests and lender timelines, but the tax still has to be cleared out of the proceeds at closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay a Banks County property tax bill?

Go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex at 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. Mailing a payment or using the online payment link also works.

Will the Banks County tax commissioner divide the bill between me and the buyer?

No. The office stays out of buyer and seller proration. Your closing documents decide who pays.

Can I submit a faxed homestead form in Banks County?

No. An original must be received or postmarked by the deadline, and faxed or emailed copies are not accepted.

May I pay a Banks County bill in pieces?

Yes. Partial payments are accepted until the bill is satisfied, and you should call 706-677-6204 to set it up. Interest keeps accruing on what remains.

What if no bill ever came?

You still have to pay by the due date. A copy is on the county website or available from the tax commissioner.

Barrow County in brief

Barrow County is a compact 163 square miles at the eastern fringe of metro Atlanta, with Winder as its seat. Growth has been fast. The population was 21,354 in 1980, 46,144 in 2000, 69,367 in 2010 and 83,505 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate is 99,773.

  • Cities: Auburn, Statham and Winder
  • Towns: Bethlehem, Braselton (mostly Jackson County, partly Gwinnett and Hall) and Carl
  • Census-designated place: Russell
  • Unincorporated: Barrow Heights, Mulberry and Whistleville

Braselton spans several counties, so an owner there should check the parcel record to learn which county mails the bill.

Market numbers for sellers

Building has not slowed, with 1,584 permits issued in 2025. A seller in a newer subdivision near Winder or Auburn will be listed beside many similar houses, so price and condition carry extra weight.

About 78.5% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the county averages 518.5 people per square mile. In 2020, 30,019 housing units were counted and the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5%, which points to a tight supply of houses for sale.

Who sends the bill and who sets the value

The tax commissioner works from 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The phone number is (770) 307-3106, and the office answers weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. You can also go through the Barrow County Tax Portal. Card payments carry a 2.5% service fee, minimum $1.50. For vehicle transactions, bring a Georgia driver's license or ID card showing a Barrow County address.

Values come from the Tax Assessors Office, found at that same street address, which takes calls from 8 to 5 on weekdays. The commissioner chooses the due date and mails the bill yet has no influence on your value. Your notice can be printed from qPublic.

Notices, bills and appeals

Property notices, for real estate and for personal property such as aircraft, boats and business equipment, normally go out May 1. Final tax bills wait until September and come due in November. Your own bill sets the date that counts.

Do not pay from a notice. It only estimates the tax on your assessed value. To dispute it, file within 45 days using qPublic, the mail, or a visit to the Tax Assessors Office.

  • Grounds you can use: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • Tracks: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator
  • On a single parcel, state revenue officials have no power to overturn a board, hearing officer, arbitrator or court

Weekday calls to the assessors are welcome for questions on a notice or the appeal steps. Anyone planning a challenge should phone early, well inside the 45 days.

What you can look up online

Two sites cover most of it. The tax portal lets you search any property in the county, pay property tax and renew car tags. The assessors' qPublic pages let you print current and prior year notices from the assessment section, which helps when a buyer's agent asks what the value was last year.

Mind the returned-check rule on the tax portal. If your bank dishonors a check, a service fee is added under state law, and the county uses Envision Payment Solutions for recovery, reachable at 1-877-290-5460. For a closing, a certified payment avoids the problem, and the portal's property search is a quick way to confirm the parcel details before you sign.

Selling mid-year and city bills

A house inside a city limit may owe the city as well as the county, so the city clerk can tell you whether a second bill exists. With three cities and three towns in the county, a county payoff may not cover what a municipality is owed.

Under Georgia law, whoever owns the house on January 1 owes the entire year, even with a sale on January 2, and part-year refunds are not given. Have the title company get a fresh payoff from each billing office and pay both at closing. Splitting the cost with the buyer is something your closing paperwork handles.

Behind on an earlier year? The commissioner's office can say whether a lien was recorded. Ask before accepting an offer, since any recorded lien must be cleared before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Barrow County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Before you list: a short checklist

Have your paperwork ready before the first showing and a Barrow County sale runs more smoothly. Take these steps in order.

  1. Print this year's and last year's assessment notices from qPublic for the buyer's agent.
  2. Phone (770) 307-3106 for the amount owed on the parcel, earlier unpaid years included.
  3. Ask about recorded liens, and check with the city clerk for a municipal bill if you are in Auburn, Statham, Winder or another town.
  4. Put in the contract who pays this year's bill. The county will not split it.
  5. Pass the payoff figures from every billing office to the title company.

If you dispute the value, the 45 days count from the notice date and not from the day you decide to sell. Look at the notice date the moment it arrives, because a late filing will not be heard.

Selling for cash as-is tends to close quicker, with no lender appraisal and no haggling over repairs. The tax steps above still apply, and the balance comes out of your proceeds at the table.

Surplus money after a tax sale

The county handles tax sale surplus through Weissman Excess Funds Management. The firm publishes open records on the funds it handles, typically refreshed on the 1st and 15th of each month, and you request information by email.

Barrow County does not release excess funds to third parties. Someone who lost property to a tax sale should contact the Tax Commissioner's Office or the firm directly about a claim, rather than pay a stranger to chase it.

Homestead exemption

Owners who make a house their primary residence qualify for a standard Georgia homestead exemption, and many counties add larger local ones. Depending on the county, you file with the tax commissioner or the assessors.

Phone (770) 307-3106 to find out which Barrow County office takes yours, and bring proof of residency. The exemption comes off assessed value first, and then the millage rate hits what is left.

If you are the one selling, an exemption you hold does not pass to the buyer. The new owner has to apply in their own name, so mention it to their agent and save them a surprise on the first bill.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Barrow County tax commissioner?

Its office is at 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. Phone (770) 307-3106 any weekday from 8:00 to 4:30.

Does a Barrow County assessment notice require payment?

No. A notice only estimates the tax from your assessed value. The real bills usually follow in September.

What is the way to appeal a Barrow County value?

File within 45 days of the notice, online through qPublic, by mail, or at the Tax Assessors Office, 30 N. Broad Street.

Are tax sale surplus funds paid out to third parties in Barrow County?

No. The county does not release excess funds to third parties, and claims run through the Tax Commissioner's Office and its excess funds partner.

Who pays if I sell a Barrow County house mid-year?

Georgia law makes the January 1 owner liable for the full year, with no part-year refund. Split the bill with the buyer in the closing paperwork.

Who sends the bill and who sets the value

The people who send your bill and the people who value your property are different offices. The Bartow County Tax Commissioner mails and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors decides what your land and house are worth. Payments, mobile home accounts and tax sale overage claims all go to the commissioner's suite in the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building, 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, Cartersville. The property tax line is (770) 387-5111, and the counter takes visitors Monday to Friday from eight until five, holidays aside.

Bartow has a sole commissioner form of government. A single elected commissioner approves the budget and fixes the millage in a public meeting held in that building. Cartersville is the county seat. Adairsville, Euharlee, Kingston and Taylorsville have their own charters, while Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities that still pay through the county office.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, duplicate bills, excess funds forms
  • Board of Tax Assessors: your value, returns and the notices that start your appeal clock
  • County Commissioner: sets the rates and the budget each summer

Bartow County for a home seller

Up in northwest Georgia, the Cartersville end of the county now acts like an Atlanta exurb along I-75. Population moved from 100,157 in 2010 to 108,901 in 2020, with an estimate of 120,800 for mid-2025. A large industrial base, a battery plant and data center development have lifted the tax digest, and that growth has let the millage keep falling.

Housing totals 50,010 units in 2025, and 72.8 percent of households own. The middle owned home is valued at $289,000, middle rent is $1,268 a month and middle household income is $82,243. Cartersville addresses fall under Cartersville City Schools, and most others go to the Bartow County School District, so verify the district before you tell a buyer which one applies.

Due dates and how to pay

Expect your real estate statement near September 15. Payment is due November 15. Mobile homes work differently and are due April 1.

The January 1 owner is the person billed. If you bought after that date, call the tax office and request a duplicate in your name, since the first statement went to the seller before you. Not receiving a bill does not change the deadline.

  • Online payment is a link on the Tax Commissioner page, which also points to qpublic for parcel lookups
  • Any debit or credit card payment, online, at the counter or by phone, picks up a 2.5 percent convenience charge
  • Make a mailed check payable to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner and send it to the Cherokee Avenue address

Georgia holds off interest for 60 days after the bill's postmark, though overdue balances may collect penalties on top. Ask the counter what your own account shows.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bartow County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Millage rates and billing summary

The 2026 rate is 7.11 mills inside city limits and 6.76 mills in the unincorporated county, down from 7.40 and 6.87 the year before. The commissioner chose the rollback rate, and rates have trended down since 2013.

Each mill is a dollar of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and the assessed figure is 40 percent of fair market value. Your bill also carries a school levy, so it reflects more than the county rate. For the combined millage on your parcel, ask the tax office.

Bartow County billing at a glance

Reading your statement

When the bill arrives, check three things before you do anything else: the parcel and owner name, the district shown for schools, and the combined millage. A wrong name or district is easier to fix in September than at the closing table, so read the statement the day it arrives.

A bill that arrives after you have sold belongs in the buyer's hands, so forward it right away. Mobile home owners should note that the April 1 account is separate from any real estate bill on the same land, and each has to be settled on its own.

Homestead exemption

Apply before April 1. Only the house you actually live in counts. Rentals, multi-family buildings and commercial or industrial property do not qualify.

The standard exemption is $15,000 of value. Local leaders hope to raise it to $30,000 in a future year, so phone the office for the amount on your current bill. A move to another Bartow house means a new application for the new address, and whoever buys yours must file too, because your exemption stays behind.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bartow County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to challenge your value

To dispute the value, mail a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark no more than 45 days after the notice date. Every Georgia county uses that window, and it applies to fair market value disputes.

Ahead of any notice, an owner may file a return from January 1 to April 1 naming the value they think is right. Tax charged in error can be reclaimed within three years of paying it, and a winning appeal brings an automatic refund. Before you write, write down your reasoning and collect sale prices of nearby houses and dated photos of damage.

Selling with taxes due

A tax debt stays with the property, so closing is when it should be cleared. Since the statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, a seller who held title that day normally gets it even when the deed transfers in October. Your closing agent can lay out how the year is divided and who mails the check.

If back taxes pile up and the county sells a parcel for more than the debt, the extra money is held for people with a claim, and the commissioner's page links an excess funds form. Selling before a levy usually costs less than waiting, so get a written payoff and set it beside any offer.

Here is how the work usually runs:

  1. Phone (770) 387-5111 for the balance and the name on the bill.
  2. If a lender escrows your tax, check with the servicer that this year is paid.
  3. Send the title company the written payoff.
  4. Make sure the closing statement shows who covers which stretch of the year.

Selling for cash, as-is, avoids repair demands and lender delays. Back taxes still come out of your proceeds, which is why an early payoff request pays off. Bring your deed or parcel number and your latest statement when you call or visit, and keep any receipt for your records.

Frequently asked questions

When are property taxes due in Bartow County?

Due November 15, with statements mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

What is the last day to apply for homestead in Bartow County?

April 1, and the exemption covers only your primary residence.

How many days do I get to appeal a Bartow assessment?

Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice. Your written appeal, sent to the Board of Tax Assessors, needs a postmark inside that window.

Will Bartow County send my bill to the lender?

No, the statement goes to the owner as of January 1, so ask your lender whether escrow covers it. A buyer who closed later in the year can call (770) 387-5111 for a duplicate.

Does Bartow County charge a fee to pay by card?

Yes. Debit and credit payments add 2.5 percent, wherever you make them. A mailed check has no such fee.

Which office does what

Two offices handle property tax here. The Tax Commissioner, at 324 East Pine Street in Fitzgerald, takes care of bills and payments. What a property is worth is the Board of Tax Assessors' call. The commissioner's number is (229) 426-5144, answered on weekdays, and the counter stays staffed until half past four. The assessors are at (229) 426-5147.

A payment, a lien or a wrong mailing address is a commissioner matter. A value, a homestead file or an exemption belongs with the assessors. Appraisers keep inspecting properties, stop at every parcel with a building permit, and look for a current decal on each mobile home.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, receipts, liens, online payments
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, returns, exemptions, notices of assessment
  • Clerk of Superior Court: your warranty deed copy, from the courthouse deed room

Ben Hill County at a glance

This is a small south Georgia county. Fitzgerald is its only city and also the seat. The population slipped from 17,194 at the 2020 census to an estimate of 17,099 for 2025. A typical home is valued at $112,700 while a typical household earns $41,758, so a tax bill takes a bigger bite here than in a pricier market.

Housing totals 8,166 units in 2025, and owners occupy 63.3 percent. Middle gross rent is $688 a month and the average commute is only 16.8 minutes. Buyers at these price levels watch every dollar. Clear any tax question before you list, and keep a recent paid receipt handy for a buyer who asks.

Due dates and late charges

Land, houses and business personal property are normally due December 1. Georgia's default is December 20 and counties are allowed to move it, which is why the day on your own statement is the one to follow. Mobile homes are due April 1, and a call to the office will confirm that for your account.

Late accounts pay 1% interest a month. Once 90 days go by, a one-time 10% penalty applies, though a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes it. Beyond 90 days the balance can become a FiFa lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, which credit bureaus may see, and the commissioner is then free to levy on the parcel.

The owner receives the statement, never the lender. When escrow covers your tax, forward the bill or verify that the servicer is paying.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Ben Hill County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to pay

At the counter, cash and checks add no charge, and mailing a check is fine as well. The county's GovtWindow portal takes online payments, and PayPal and cards are offered only on the website. The convenience charge for each online method appears before you confirm, which leaves you free to back out and pay by check.

  • In person: 324 East Pine Street, Fitzgerald, Georgia 31750
  • By phone for questions: (229) 426-5144
  • Portal help line: (877) 575-7233
Late-payment and payment-method rules
Payment ruleBen Hill County
Real estate due dateNormally December 1

Homestead exemption

You qualify by owning and occupying the home on January 1, with your application in the assessors' hands before April 1. Once granted, it continues yearly while you stay. A move calls for a fresh application at the new address, and a late filing just pushes the benefit out a year.

An owner who reaches 62 may apply for an additional exemption. Business inventory can earn a freeport exemption where local voters have approved one. Local legislation can raise the base amounts, so call the assessors for the dollar figure that applies to you.

If you are selling, your exemption does not travel with the house. The buyer files a new application, and telling their agent early avoids a surprise on the first bill.

How values are set and challenged

From winter into early spring, up to April 1, you can file a return stating your own value. If the board sees it differently, it mails a notice with its number. Taxable value equals 40% of market value, and a mill is one dollar for every $1,000 of it.

Appeal within 45 days of the notice date. Your case then goes to the county Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. If the outcome still bothers you, deliver written notice to the assessors and move on to superior court. A claim for tax charged by mistake must be made within three years of payment.

Before you appeal, ask the assessors what comparable sales they used and compare your house with those. Photos of problems, such as a failing roof or an unfinished room, back up a lower value. Keep a copy of whatever you deliver and note the date, because the clock starts on the notice date and not on the day you open the envelope.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ben Hill County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Sorting out taxes before closing

Know the balance and the billed owner before you sign. A statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so it may bear your name even when the deed passes to the buyer later in the year. Get a printed balance from the commissioner and ask the closing agent how the year is shared.

A lien stands in the way of clean title. Sellers mostly clear it out of the sale money, wiring the commissioner's payoff figure. A house that needs repairs can still sell while taxes are owed, and that is one reason some owners go with a cash buyer who accepts it as is.

At the counter on East Pine Street, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest statement and any lien notice. Ask for the payoff in writing with its good-through date, because interest builds each month.

Mobile homes

In Georgia a mobile or modular home is personal property. Its owner files a return and obtains a location permit every year, and the permit waits until the whole tax is paid. April 1 is the due date for that account, so confirm the date on yours with the commissioner.

Assessors look for a current decal when they inspect. If you sell one, the next owner takes over the paperwork trail, so pay the tax and settle the permit before the handoff and keep the paid receipt.

Owners who moved without updating an address should ask the assessors whether mail came back undelivered, so future notices reach the right place. A missed notice does not stop the 45-day appeal clock.

If you inherited a mobile home or bought one without the paperwork, ask the commissioner what is on file before you list it. A clean permit history makes the sale simpler, and a buyer or lender will usually ask for proof that the tax is current.

Frequently asked questions

When is real estate tax due in Ben Hill County?

Most bills are due December 1, but the date printed on your statement controls. Call (229) 426-5144 to confirm.

What does a late Ben Hill County payment cost?

Interest runs 1% per month, and a 10% penalty is added after 90 days. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 skips the penalty.

Where do I apply for homestead exemption in Ben Hill County?

Apply with the Tax Assessor, and make sure the paperwork arrives before April 1. You must own the home and live there on January 1.

What is the appeal window in Ben Hill County?

Forty-five days from the notice date. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, with superior court after that.

Can I pay my Ben Hill County taxes without a fee?

Yes. Paying cash or check at the counter or mailing a check costs nothing extra, while online payments add a convenience charge.

Where to take tax questions

The Tax Commissioner has Suite 105 on the ground floor of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville, Georgia 31639. For a bill or a payment, call (229) 686-7461. Visitors are welcome on weekdays from eight until five. Real property, personal property, mobile home, motor vehicle and timber tax all run through this one office.

Value is a different office's job. Berrien's Board of Tax Assessors sets it and takes homestead applications, and the commissioner's staff will direct you there if you are unsure.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, receipts, help paying, liens
  • Tax Assessor: values, returns, homestead and other exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies from the courthouse deed room

Berrien County in brief

Berrien covers 458 square miles of rural south central Georgia, and a single school system, the Berrien County School District, serves every address. The headcount went from 19,286 in 2010 down to 18,160, then back up to an estimated 18,932 for 2025. Nearly three quarters of residents in 2020 lived outside urban areas, so most owners hold rural parcels rather than town lots.

The county has 8,328 housing units in 2025 and a 71.0 percent owner rate. Median household income is $52,876, the middle owner-occupied value is $131,600 and middle gross rent is $782 a month. Only 115 building permits were issued in 2025, so most listings are older farmhouses and country lots, and buyers price them that way.

Due dates and late charges

Every year, houses, land and business equipment are due November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1 instead, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

Each month of delay adds 1% interest. If the bill is still open three months past the deadline, a flat 10% penalty is added. At 30 days overdue, the office can record a FiFa lien with the Clerk of Superior Court, and in the end the commissioner may levy on the parcel.

Parcel searches and online payments run on the GovtWindow platform, and the help desk number is (877) 575-7233. Georgia classes a mobile or modular home as personal property, so a yearly return and a location permit apply, and the permit is withheld until that year's tax is paid in full. The commissioner also bills timber tax, a point that matters to anyone selling acreage.

How the bill is calculated

Georgia taxes 40% of market value, and Berrien's county commissioners and school board each pick a millage yearly. The sequence is short: start from assessed value, subtract exemptions to reach net taxable value, then multiply by the mills. Each mill raises a dollar on every $1,000 of that net figure.

Rather than guess, ask the commissioner for the millage on your parcel. Statements are mailed to the owner, so a lender that escrows needs a copy. Check that your servicer has the Berrien bill, and keep your own copy for the closing file.

  • Returns: you may state your own value at any point in the first three months of the year
  • Notice: the assessors send one when their value differs from the return
  • Bill: the commissioner applies the mills to net taxable value

Homestead exemption

The test is ownership and residence on New Year's Day. Mail or deliver the application to the tax assessor's office so it is received before April 1. Filing is open all year, yet a late application only helps the next tax year, so do not wait.

Selling the house ends your claim, and the buyer applies on their own. Mention it to the buyer's agent so the new owner knows to file before April 1.

Once approved, the exemption continues each year at that address. If you move to a different Berrien house, you file again. Homeowners at 62 may apply for an added exemption, and business personal property can qualify for freeport relief. The dollar figures change with legislation, so the assessors are the source for current amounts.

Disputing your value

Count 45 days from the notice date. Either the county Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears the case, and a disappointed owner can send the Board of Tax Assessors written notice of a move to superior court.

If you appeal a market value by mail, the postmark must be no later than day 45. Tax that was collected in error or illegally can be recovered with a written claim made within three years of payment. Keep your receipts, since the three years run from the day you paid.

Rural parcels and timber

Country land is common here, and it brings a few extra checks. Timber is taxed and billed by the commissioner, so a seller with standing trees should ask whether any timber tax is open. A mobile home on the land is a separate account with its own April 1 deadline and its own permit.

List each account when you talk to the buyer's side. A clean payoff on the house alone does not tell the title company that the mobile home or timber account is also paid, and a missed one can delay a closing. If the deed came to you through an estate, ask the commissioner whether the bills for earlier years went to a prior owner, and settle them all in one visit so the record is complete before you sign.

Tax steps before selling

Ahead of any offer, get the balance from the commissioner in writing and find out who the bill is addressed to. January 1 ownership drives the statement, which means yours may arrive even after a fall closing. How the year's tax is split between you and the buyer will be laid out by your closing agent.

A recorded FiFa is public record, and it has to be paid off before the buyer can receive clean title. An old farmhouse with back taxes, an inherited deed or deferred repairs can still sell as is, because the payoff comes out of the sale money. Any cash buyer will want the same payoff number you hold. If the house is a rural parcel, also ask whether any timber tax or a mobile home account is attached to the same owner, since the commissioner bills those too, and settle each one before the deed is signed.

A cash sale avoids lender appraisals and repair lists, which suits a farmhouse with deferred upkeep. The tax payoff remains. You pay the balance from your proceeds at the table, and knowing the number early keeps the closing date steady.

Bring these to Suite 105: your deed or parcel number, the latest statement, any lien notice, and your closing agent's name. Get the figures in writing with the date they are good through, since interest builds monthly.

Frequently asked questions

When does Berrien County want its property tax?

Real estate and business personal property are due every November 15. A mobile home account is due April 1.

What does overdue Berrien County tax cost?

You pay 1% interest per month starting at the due date, plus a 10% penalty after 90 days of nonpayment.

Where is the Berrien County tax office?

Suite 105 of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville. Call (229) 686-7461; the office keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

How fast must a Berrien County assessment appeal be filed?

Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears it.

Does the Berrien tax bill go to my lender?

No, statements are mailed to owners alone. With an escrow account, send the bill along or check that the servicer is paying.

Macon-Bibb tax offices

Macon and Bibb County merged into one government on January 1, 2014, and the small city of Payne joined in 2015. An owner therefore deals with a single local government, a single county school district and a single tax commissioner.

The Tax Commissioner is at 188 Third Street, Macon, Georgia 31201, open weekdays from eight to five. Call (478) 621-6500 or write to taxinfo@maconbibb.us. This office mails the statements, prepares the yearly tax digest for the state, and splits what it collects among the State of Georgia, the county government and the school board. Your value is set elsewhere, by the Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 621-6701.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, liens, tax sales, excess funds claims
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead applications, appeal filings
  • Solid Waste Department: the garbage fee that rides along with the property bill

Housing market for a seller

About 157,556 people lived in Bibb as of July 2025, barely above the 157,346 counted in 2020. Owners and renters are nearly even. The 2020 count showed exactly 50 percent each, and the newer survey puts owners at 51.4 percent. Where a house is rented, the bill still goes to whoever held title on January 1, never to the tenant.

The 2025 housing count is 72,122 units, with 59,921 households. Owned homes have a middle value of $174,500, middle rent is $1,066 a month and middle household income is $51,234. If you own a rental, expect investors to be your likeliest buyers, and a tenant's lease will shape how fast the house can close.

Billing dates and due dates

Real and personal property statements go out by mid-September, and the bill comes in two installments, October 15 and November 15. A weekend due date moves to the next business day.

The first bill goes to the owner of record on January 1. If a transfer is reported in the 90 days before a due date, the office checks it and bills the new owner. Lenders receive a data file of amounts due, but the paper statement is mailed to the owner, who stays responsible for any missed payment even with escrow.

Mobile homes keep a schedule of their own: statements out by January 30, payment due April 1, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid. If a mobile home account is late, the state penalty applies, which is 10 percent of the tax or $5 if that is more, plus monthly interest.

Paying late or in pieces

  • You may pay part now, though interest and penalties keep running on the remainder
  • Mail counts as on time only with a USPS date stamp
  • After a levy begins, pay a delinquent account in person

The commissioner will take any number of partial payments, but the part left unpaid keeps adding penalties and interest. Do not rely on a postage meter date for mailing proof. For delinquent accounts the office wants payment brought in by hand, above all after a levy and sale notice begin.

Ahead of a FiFa lien, a notice of intent goes to the owner, who has 30 days to pay in full. The lien is then entered on the General Execution Docket held by the Clerk of Superior Court, which can happen once a balance is open past 90 days. Pay the tax with fees, penalties and interest and the lien is cancelled. The counter never sells liens, and the office says it does not report to credit bureaus.

Every residential premises, occupied or vacant, also gets a quarterly garbage bill from the Solid Waste Department. It is a different charge from the property tax, and an appeal of your value does not pause it. A low-income household may request an exemption, filed with the Solid Waste Department by 5 p.m. each November 1.

At closing, ask the title company whether any garbage charge is still open for the quarter. It is billed to the premises and is a separate account from the property tax, so settle it on its own.

Homestead exemption

Homestead approvals come from the Tax Assessors. To qualify you own and live in the home on January 1, and an application in by April 1 covers the current year. Approval does not need annual renewal, but a move or a new deed means applying again.

State law and local acts set the amounts, so read the figure on your bill. Call the assessors at (478) 621-6701 to learn what your account carries and whether any senior relief fits. After closing, the buyer must file their own application, so mention it to their agent. If you moved out and keep the house as a rental, you no longer qualify and should say so.

How to appeal your value

Write your appeal, say which appeal method you want, and get it to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. You can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. Because the Tax Commissioner is an independently elected office that neither supervises nor answers to the assessors, take appeal questions to the assessors.

Mobile homes get a later cutoff: 45 days after the bill goes out, or April 1 if that is later. Tax collected by mistake or unlawfully can be reclaimed within three years of paying it.

Selling before a tax sale

With a FiFa on file, the county may levy on the parcel and sell it. Auctions take place on the courthouse steps, 206 7th Street, at 11 a.m. on the first Tuesday of any month with a sale scheduled. Bidders must show up personally. Bidding starts at the amount of tax, penalties and fees owed. The winner receives a sheriff's tax deed instead of the land, and payment, in cash, certified funds or a money order, is due within two hours.

A right of redemption survives the sale. For one year after it, the owner or any interested party can repurchase the tax deed by paying the winning bid, taxes the buyer covered later, special assessments and a 20 percent premium. Only after that year can the buyer begin foreclosing the right, using certified mail and newspaper notice for four straight weeks. A bid above the debt leaves excess funds in the office's hands, and lienholders are paid ahead of the record owner.

Pay the tax from your sale proceeds ahead of any levy, and the house never goes through that process. Request a written payoff, hand it to the closing agent and save the receipt. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands may close fast enough to beat a sale date, and you would skip lender delays and repair requests. Need a deed copy? The Clerk of Superior Court deed room is at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201.

Frequently asked questions

When must Macon-Bibb property tax be paid?

Two installments: October 15 and November 15. Statements go out by September 15. Dates on a weekend move to the next business day.

Does Macon-Bibb accept partial tax payments?

Yes, as many as you like. Whatever you still owe keeps drawing interest and penalties, and it may end up liened.

What is the appeal deadline for a Macon-Bibb assessment?

Send it in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors' number is (478) 621-6701.

Where do I get a copy of my Bibb County deed?

Go to the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201, where warranty deeds are kept.

Does a postmark prove I paid on time in Macon-Bibb?

A USPS postmark does. A postage meter date does not count.

Brantley County in brief

Out in rural southeast Georgia, Brantley County has Nahunta as its seat. It covers roughly 442 square miles of mostly dry ground, with the Satilla River running through it. The population was 18,021 in 2020 and is about 18,936 by mid-2025. The middle home value is $99,600, and owners occupy 79.9 percent of housing (2020 to 2024).

Only 77 building permits came out in 2025, which makes new building rare. Sellers are mostly longtime owners of a single-family house, a tract of land or a mobile home. Density was 40.7 people per square mile in 2020, and 99.3 percent of residents lived in rural areas. Buyers tend to be local, and many properties are big lots or mobile home sites.

Tax offices and phone numbers

The Brantley County Government Annex, 10405 Main Street North in Nahunta, houses both property tax offices. The commissioner sends and collects the bills. The assessor decides what each parcel is worth. Neither can lower your rate, because elected boards set it.

How homes are valued

Every schedule was updated in 2025 along with a full re-evaluation of all properties. The assessor keeps files on 13,406 real property parcels, 602 personal property accounts and 2,346 mobile homes without a homestead exemption.

Georgia assesses at 40 percent of the property's January 1 value. The return season runs January 1 to April 1. An owner who files nothing receives an assessment notice in mid-May, and that notice starts the appeal clock.

  • Submit a return before April 1 if you want to declare your own value
  • Open the notice as soon as it arrives and note the date it carries
  • Phone the assessor at 912-462-5251 with any questions while time remains

Because the re-evaluation changed values across the county, a home that looked cheap on paper a few years ago may now carry a noticeably different assessment. Pull the current record before you set a sale price, and print it for your file so you can show a buyer what the county has on record.

Before you list, check the county's record of your house against reality. Wrong square footage, a demolished shed or an unrecorded addition are simpler to correct before a buyer's appraiser notices.

How to challenge your assessment

Your assessment notice opens a single 45-day window. The challenge begins at the Board of Tax Assessors, then follows Georgia's usual path to the Board of Equalization and finally Superior Court. Arbitration can replace the board hearing.

You may argue value, uniformity or taxability. Disliking the size of the bill is not a ground, because the bill follows the millage rate, and that cannot be appealed.

  • Write the appeal out and keep your own copy
  • Collect recent nearby sales and any repair quotes
  • Ask the assessor how a hearing is requested

The count runs from the notice date, so a mailbox you rarely check can cost you days.

Even if you plan to sell, an appeal may be worth filing when the assessed value looks too high, since a lower figure helps whoever holds the house on January 1. Tell your closing agent about any appeal still open, so the paperwork says who keeps a refund if one comes.

What local housing patterns mean for a seller

Listings are scarce and owners stay put. The county has 6,599 households, and 94.3 percent of residents stayed in the same home over the past year. Median gross rent is $755, and a mortgaged owner spends a median $1,087 monthly. Three practical points follow for anyone weighing a sale:

  • Brantley is part of the Brunswick metropolitan area, and Wayne, Glynn, Camden, Charlton, Ware and Pierce counties touch it, so buyers often shop those neighbors too.
  • Nearly 19 percent of residents are 65 or older, so estate and heir questions come up often. After an owner's death, ask the probate court how to proceed.

Selling with tax owed

First ask the tax commissioner for a payoff amount, since back county taxes must be cleared for a buyer to receive clean title. Next, the settlement agent can figure out what each side owes for the year.

If the house is a mobile home, confirm whether it is billed on its own or together with the land, since the assessor tracks non-homesteaded mobile homes as separate accounts. Homestead status affects this, so ask the assessor which treatment your home has.

Owners hurt by the Highway 82 fire can call the county commissioners' office at 912-462-5256, extension 5, about recovery resources. Ask the assessor how fire damage is reflected in your record before you price the property.

For the office visit, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest bill and receipts for earlier years, and get the payoff in writing with its good-through date. How can I pay my Brantley County tax bill?

Pay online at brantleytax.com or in person with the tax commissioner at Suite D of the Government Annex, 10405 Main Street North, Nahunta. The office number is 912-462-5723, and it is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30.

The deadline is 45 days after the date printed on the notice, and it is firm. File in writing before it ends.

Does the Brantley County assessor set my tax bill?

No. The assessor only sets the value. Millage rates come from the county commissioners and the school board, and the tax commissioner mails the bill.

Can I sell a Brantley County house if taxes are unpaid?

Yes, as long as the back taxes are paid at or before closing. Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff and see that it shows on the settlement statement.

When are Brantley County property tax returns due?

Each year the window runs from January 1 to April 1. If you miss it, an assessment notice arrives in mid-May and the 45-day appeal period begins.

Bryan County in brief

Bryan County is in the Savannah metropolitan area and Fort Stewart cuts it in two. Pembroke, the county seat, sits in the rural north. Richmond Hill, the biggest city, is a Savannah suburb in the south, and a public-road trip between the two leaves the county. That divide is why the county keeps two offices for nearly every property tax service.

The county counted 44,738 people in 2020, and mid-2025 is 52,062, up 16.4 percent from the 2020 base. Homes have a middle value of $343,200 and household income has a middle of $103,408. Builders pulled 733 permits in 2025, and 77.7 percent of housing is owner occupied. The north tends toward larger rural parcels, while the south has newer subdivisions in the Savannah commuter zone.

Property tax offices

The assessor and the tax commissioner each run one office in Pembroke and one in Richmond Hill. The assessor sets values. The commissioner handles billing, collection and distribution. The assessor's side neither sets the rate nor collects a dollar.

Due dates and late charges

This year's bills were mailed October 16 and are due Tuesday, December 15, 2026. In general, bills go out around September and give at least 60 days to pay, so the date can shift from year to year. See the county's property tax page.

Late payment brings these charges:

  • Interest runs at 0.875 percent per month, or fraction of a month, beginning the day after the deadline
  • At 120 days past due, a 5 percent penalty is added
  • Each further 120 days adds another 5 percent, with 20 percent as the ceiling
  • A bill 30 days delinquent lets the tax commissioner, serving as ex-officio sheriff, start tax sale proceedings

Under Georgia law the January 1 owner of record stays on the bill for the year, and the office asks for the recorded deed once a sale closes.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bryan County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How value is set and how to appeal

The assessor sets fair market value. Forty percent of it, less any homestead exemption, becomes the taxable value, and the commissioner then applies the millage rate. The county posts the current millage rates on its tax page.

Appeals have strict rules, and late appeals are refused. The window is 45 days from the date on the notice:

  • Use the county's written appeal form
  • Get it physically to the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office before 5:00 p.m. on deadline day
  • Nothing sent by email or fax is accepted, and a postmark proves nothing

The assessor's staff photograph homes to refresh records, so a county vehicle may pause outside yours. After a sale, the new owner sees a value the following year, when the first notice arrives.

Questions about a value belong with the assessor at 912-653-3889, option 1. The assessor's page also offers a guide called Understanding Your Notice of Assessment, which walks through each line of the notice. Read it before you decide whether an appeal is worth filing.

Who is billed when a house changes hands

The commissioner does not prorate taxes by the date of sale, by how much the property was used or by who owns it now. Any split between buyer and seller therefore happens at the closing table.

Once you sell, give the tax commissioner the recorded deed and closing papers so the next bill finds the new owner. Leave them at either office, mail them to P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or email propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. Address changes and homestead applications belong with the assessor.

Find out from your closing attorney how this year's bill will be shared and whether the December deadline lands before your closing. For any open bill, get a payoff figure from the commissioner so it can come out of the sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as is will still expect that figure, and having it in writing keeps the closing on schedule.

Steps for a Bryan County seller

A sale in Bryan County is easier when you handle the paperwork in a set order. Because there are two offices of each kind, pick the one closer to you and stay with it.

  1. Call the tax commissioner and ask for the balance on every account under your name: the house, any mobile home, and any business property.
  2. Check whether the December deadline falls before your closing date, and decide with the buyer who pays.
  3. Request a written payoff for any open bill and give it to the closing attorney.
  4. After closing, deliver the recorded deed so the next bill is mailed to the new owner.
  5. Tell the assessor about any homestead exemption you held, since the buyer must apply separately.

If a bill is already delinquent, move faster. At 30 days past due the commissioner can begin tax sale proceedings, and a sale in progress is far harder to close around than a simple payoff. A call to either office on the same day you get a contract is cheap protection.
