Homestead, mobile homes and business property

The county's sample calculation uses a $2,000 homestead reduction from assessed value. Applications go to the assessor, and your status on January 1 decides eligibility, so ask that office which exemptions match your age, income or veteran status.

Mobile homes are billed under their own rules. Without a homestead exemption, the bill arrives in January and is due April 1. With one, the home is taxed along with its land, and that bill is due around November 15. Taxes must be paid, with a receipt in hand, before any mobile home is moved, even out of the county.

A business must file a personal property return with the assessor by April 1 in every year it operates, and state-set values apply if it does not. Timber sales go on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, and heavy-duty equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in its purchase year.

If you own more than one kind of property, ask the commissioner which accounts exist under your name. A forgotten mobile home or business account can hold up a closing just as a missed house bill can.

Frequently asked questions

What is the 2026 due date for Bryan County property tax?

The 2026 bills are due Tuesday, December 15, 2026, and were mailed on October 16. After the due date, interest of 0.875 percent per month applies.

How long do I have to appeal a Bryan County assessment?

Forty-five days from the date on the notice, in writing, delivered to the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office by 5:00 p.m. on the last day. Late appeals are refused.

Does Bryan County split property tax by sale date?

No. The commissioner's office does not prorate by sale date, so the buyer and seller settle the bill between them at closing.

Where should the deed go after a Bryan County sale?

Send the recorded deed and closing documents to the Bryan County Tax Commissioner, P.O. Box 447, Pembroke, GA 31321, or to propertytax@bryancountyga.gov. You can also drop them at the Pembroke or Richmond Hill office.

What happens if I do not pay Bryan County property tax?

Interest and penalties accumulate, and penalties stop at 20 percent. Once a bill is 30 days delinquent the commissioner may start tax sale proceedings, so call early if you cannot pay in full.

Bulloch County at a glance

Bulloch County sits in southeast Georgia, and Statesboro is the county seat. Georgia Southern University and the East Georgia State College campus are in Statesboro, so the housing market leans toward students and the people who rent to them. The 2025 estimate is 86,949 residents, up from 81,099 in 2020. In 2020, 50.1 percent of occupied homes were rentals, and the median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $222,500.

Many sellers here own a rental or an inherited house, and both bring tax questions that the sections below take up.

Who to contact

Offices are open weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. One thing is unusual in Bulloch: returns and homestead applications go to the assessors rather than the tax commissioner.

Bulloch County property tax offices
OfficeAddressPhoneHandles
Tax Assessors113 North Main Street, Statesboro912-764-2181Values, returns, homestead, appeals
Tax Commissioner113 North Main Street, Suite 101, Statesboro912-764-6285Billing, collection, payments

Email works for general questions: propertytax@bullochcounty.net. The tax commissioner's web page links both a record search and a payment portal. If you pay by card, the processor adds a convenience fee that the county never sees.

To check whether a bill is current, the online record search is quicker than a phone call. Save the phones for payoff letters, exemptions and corrections to the record.

Valuation, millage and returns

Assessors value your property as of January 1, then tax 40 percent of that figure. A mill works out to a dollar per thousand of the taxed amount. Two bodies pick rates: the county commissioners for county tax and the school board for school tax.

New owners file a first return covering the real and personal property they held on January 1, and Bulloch accepts those at the assessors' office until April 1. After that the return rolls forward at the last finalized value. File again only if you add property, make improvements or want to put a different value on record.

Email returns are refused. A faxed return has to land before 5:00 p.m. on the final day. The assessors cannot waive penalties or stretch a deadline, so treat each date as fixed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bulloch County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Put your appeal on paper within 45 days of the date on the notice of change. Email is not accepted, and a fax counts only if it arrives before 5:00 p.m. on day 45.

The path has four steps:

  • Send the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, which reviews it and replies.
  • If the board keeps the value, the County Board of Equalization hears the case.
  • You may ask for arbitration instead of that hearing when you file.
  • Anyone still dissatisfied can go on to Superior Court.

You can argue taxability, value, or uniformity against similar properties. Grumbling that the tax itself is too high will not work, since that follows from the millage rate. The county's How Do I menu also has a request link for assessment appeals.

Homestead exemption and other relief

To qualify for any homestead exemption you must own the house and call it your legal residence on January 1. Apply at the assessors' office between January 1 and April 1. Once granted, the exemption repeats each year until the deed changes hands.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 comes off the taxed value.
  • Age 65 and up: $4,000 off state and county taxes, for households within the assessors' income cap.
  • Age 62 and up: a school tax exemption capped at $10,000 of assessed value, with its own income cap.
  • Owners with a service-connected disability, and surviving spouses of military members: larger exemptions under state law.

A deferral is also open to owners 62 and older who pass an income test. The deferred amount usually falls due when title changes or the balance hits 85 percent of the property's value, so a sale ends it and the balance comes out of your proceeds.

Farm owners have until April 1 to ask for a conservation use covenant. It runs ten years, costs a $10 recording fee and carries a penalty of twice the taxes saved if it is broken. Talk to the assessors before you sell covenanted land.

Selling a Bulloch County rental or rural tract

Rentals stood vacant at a 9.0 percent rate in 2020, against 1.4 percent for owner homes. Typical gross rent for 2020 to 2024 is $995. A landlord listing a Statesboro rental is selling into a market where roughly half the occupied homes are rented.

  • Student rentals near the university are priced and bought differently than family homes.
  • Rural tracts outside Statesboro often carry farm or timber use, so ask the assessors about covenants first.
  • The county keeps a separate timber harvest page, worth a look if trees were cut before the sale.

Before listing, open the parcel's online tax record. Whatever acreage or exemption the assessors have on file shows up there, so mistakes are easy to catch. Landlords should also confirm that the name on each bill matches the deed.

Bulloch County tax calendar for sellers

The year moves in a fixed order. January 1 is the date everything is measured against: ownership, residence for homestead, and the value the assessors use. Returns and homestead applications are taken at the assessors' office until April 1. If your value changes, a notice goes out and the 45-day appeal clock starts from its date.

If you plan to list in spring, file before April 1 while you still own and live in the house, because the exemption only counts for the year you apply. Selling later in the year does not erase the bill for that year, so expect the closing attorney to deal with it on the settlement statement.

Do Bulloch County cities send their own tax bill?

Four of them do. Statesboro, Brooklet, Portal and Register run their own billing and collection, so a house inside any of those limits gets a county bill and then a separate city bill.

At closing, the payoff request has to cover both bills, and the title company needs to know which city, if any, holds your parcel.

Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff, and ask whoever runs your closing how this year's share will be split. The due date is printed on the bill.

Steps to clear taxes before a sale

First look up the parcel online to see whether any year is open. Then phone 912-764-6285 and request a written payoff from the tax commissioner. If the house is in Statesboro, Brooklet, Portal or Register, request that city's figure too.

Hand the letters to the closing attorney or title company, who pays the taxes from your proceeds. Your exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer files a new application with the assessors by April 1. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline but not the payoff, so ask for it early.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes homestead applications in Bulloch County?

The Tax Assessors, 113 North Main Street, Statesboro. The filing season ends April 1, and an approved exemption repeats yearly without refiling.

What is the appeal window in Bulloch County?

Forty-five days from the notice date. Submit it on paper or by fax, because email appeals are not taken.

Does a Statesboro homeowner get one tax bill or two?

Two. The city runs its own collection, so each year you receive one bill from the county and another from Statesboro.

How do I pay Bulloch County property tax?

Go to Suite 101 at 113 North Main Street in Statesboro, or use the online payment link. For questions call 912-764-6285. Cards carry an extra processor fee.

Can the Bulloch assessors forgive a late filing penalty?

No. The assessors have no authority to relieve penalties or grant filing extensions, so meet each deadline.

Selling land or a house in Burke County

Burke County runs along Georgia's eastern edge, across the river from South Carolina, and Waynesboro is the seat. At 827 square miles of land it is one of the biggest counties in the state, and it sits inside the Augusta metro area. Seven municipalities lie within it: Blythe, Girard, Keysville, Midville, Sardis, Vidette and Waynesboro.

Mid-2025 population was 24,408. The median home value is $151,600 and 70 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Sellers often hold farmland, timber or an older house in town, and in a county this large the parcel may sit a long way from the courthouse, so much of the paperwork below is easier done by phone or online.

Offices and contacts

Both offices share 524 Myrick Street in Waynesboro: the Board of Assessors in Suite B and the tax commissioner in Suite A. The assessors set values and send no bills. The commissioner collects for the county, the state and the Board of Education and has no say in values.

Burke County tax offices
OfficePhoneWeekday hoursAlso useful
Board of Assessors, Suite B706-554-26078 to 5Board meets the second Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m.
Tax Commissioner, Suite A706-554-32238:30 to 5Open 9 to noon on the first and third Saturday of the month

Mail for the commissioner goes to box 671 in Waynesboro, GA 30830, and the assessors use box 46 in the same town. Maps and records can be searched online through the county's assessor page and the tax commissioner's own website.

Appraisers from the assessor's office sometimes visit to update records. They wear a Burke County photo ID badge, drive a marked vehicle, measure the outside of buildings and photograph the exterior. If nobody is home they leave a door hanger or business card. To check on a visitor, call 706-554-2607.

How can a Burke County owner contest a value?

You have 45 days from the notice date to appeal. Assessment notices usually go out in July, so watch your mail then. The commissioner's site describes four routes.

  • Board of Equalization. The Board of Assessors looks at the appeal first and may change the value with a new notice. If it does, you get 30 more days to challenge that notice. If the value stays, the appeal moves to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Hearing officer. This is open only for non-homestead real property above $500,000, and a state-certified appraiser serves as the officer.
  • Arbitration. Say so in your filing, then submit a certified appraisal within 45 days of the board's acknowledgement, which it must send within 10 days. A hearing follows within 30 days of authorization.
  • Superior Court. Mail or file a written notice with the Board of Assessors within 30 days of the earlier ruling.

Arbitration costs depend on the outcome. The county pays if your value lands closest to the arbitrator's figure, and you pay if the board's value is closer.

Homestead exemption

Burke accepts applications year-round at the commissioner's office or the Board of Assessors, but to count for the current year the paper must be postmarked or received by the last day of the appeal period. The commissioner's FAQ gives April 1 as the cutoff for the billing year. On January 1 you must hold title, live in the house and claim it as your residence.

Codes you may see on the county's homestead page:

  • S1, the standard exemption: $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school tax, with no age or income test.
  • S3 and S4, for owners 62 and 65 with income under $10,000, which add a $10,000 school exemption.
  • S5, SD, SS and SE, which cover disabled service members and the unremarried spouses of those who died in war.
  • SG, for the spouse of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • L3 and L4, local school exemptions for owners 65 and older.

A refinance leaves an exemption in place unless the name on the deed changes. Vehicles you own must be registered in Burke County. The county commissioners, the Board of Education and the cities of Waynesboro, Sardis, Girard, Midville and Keysville have opted out of the statewide floating exemption.

Payment options and rules

The commissioner takes cash, checks, money orders and major cards, with a convenience fee on cards. You can also pay on the website or by phone at 1-844-898-2374 with your bill number.

A few answers from the commissioner's FAQ matter if you are selling:

  • Part payments are accepted, but interest and penalty keep running on the balance.
  • If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, phone the commissioner before sending any partial payment.
  • An appeal does not pause billing. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of market value and corrected after the final ruling.
  • A surviving spouse may petition for a year's support through an attorney or the probate court.

A mobile home that is not on homestead and was in the county on January 1 owes tax and must show a current decal. Unpaid taxes bring a 10 percent penalty plus interest, and a missing decal draws a fine of $100 to $300.

What happens to unpaid Burke County taxes?

Delinquent parcels can go to tax sale, and the commissioner's website posts each sale date along with the list of parcels. Check that list for your parcel number if any year is behind.

Before you list, look up the parcel number on the commissioner's site and confirm that no earlier year is open. Returns are taken January 1 through April 1. Tangible personal property worth $7,500 or less in fair market value is exempt, though motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes are not. A buyer's attorney will check the real property bill and any personal property or mobile home account tied to the address.

Closing checklist for sellers

Call the commissioner at 706-554-3223 and ask for a written payoff, then give it to the closing agent. Ask the agent how this year's bill will be shared between you and the buyer, because the county bills one owner and the split is a private agreement.

Confirm that your homestead exemption is yours alone: the buyer has to apply on their own once they hold title. If you farmed or cut timber on the land, bring any return or covenant papers you filed. A cash sale changes none of this, and the payoff letter is still the figure the closing agent needs. Keep the commissioner's phone line handy through closing, since the office is open weekdays and two Saturday mornings a month.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Burke County resident pay in person?

At the tax commissioner, 524 Myrick Street, Suite A, Waynesboro. The number is 706-554-3223. Weekdays run 8:30 to 5, and on the first and third Saturday the office opens 9 to noon.

How soon must a Burke County appeal be filed?

Within 45 days of the notice date. If the Board of Assessors changes the value, a further 30 days applies to the amended notice.

Must I pay my Burke County tax bill during an appeal?

Yes. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value, and the county corrects the bill after the final decision.

Is a part payment accepted in Burke County?

Yes, though interest and penalty keep running on the remainder. If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, call the commissioner first.

What does the Burke County standard homestead exemption cover?

The S1 exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school taxes, with no age or income test. You must live there on January 1 and apply by April 1.

Which Jackson offices handle Butts County property tax?

Two suites in one building, 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson, split the work. Suite 1 holds the Board of Tax Assessors, who put a value on your house. Suite 2 holds the Tax Commissioner, an elected official who sends the bill and accepts payment. The offices are independent, so a valuation notice question and a payoff question get answered at separate counters.

  • Assessors: 770-775-8207, open weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-775-8206, open weekdays, 8:00 to 4:00, and shut on approved holidays.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: keeps recorded deeds and liens, and can hand you a copy of your warranty deed.

The taxable amount is 40 percent of the market value as of each January 1. County government and the school board choose separate mill rates, with one mill meaning a dollar per thousand dollars taxed.

Installment dates and how bills are sent

Real estate and business equipment bills are paid in two parts here, while manufactured housing runs on its own April 1 schedule. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day.

Butts County payment dates
Property typeDue date
Land, houses and equipment, first halfSeptember 15
Land, houses and equipment, second halfDecember 7
Mobile and manufactured homesApril 1

The paper statement is mailed to the owner, not the mortgage servicer. Servicers do receive a data file from the office, yet an escrow lender may still want your copy. After a sale, the new owner is billed under their own name. If a statement turns up for a house you no longer own, phone the office.

Part payments are welcome, and you can make several. Interest and penalties keep building on whatever is unpaid, and an account with any balance can be liened. If you pay by mail, send the check early or drop it off at the counter so timing is not a question.

The 2026 countywide reappraisal

For 2026 the county hired a mass appraisal firm, Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions, to review about 13,000 parcels. Field crews began in July 2025. Appraisers measured buildings and took photos from outside, and the assessors say none of them go inside a home.

The new values date from January 1, 2026. Appeals grew past 3% of total value, which gives the Board of Assessors an extra 180 days to respond to 2026 appeals.

Thinking of listing? Search for your parcel on the assessors' site before you set an asking price, and find out if an appeal is still pending on it. A late change in value changes what the tax commissioner bills.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Butts County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

An appeal begins on paper, using form PT-311-A, delivered to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the notice date. Name the method you prefer on the form. The commissioner lists four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Assessors review your evidence first and may adjust the value if they find an error. If not, the case moves to the Board of Equalization, a panel of local residents chosen by the Grand Jury, or to arbitration if you requested it up front.

  • Evidence that helps: a recent appraisal, sales of similar houses, or photos of defects.
  • Saying the bill is too high is outside the grounds, since appeals address value and taxability only.
  • The board cannot waive a late filing or forgive a penalty.

Homestead and farm deadlines

File for homestead by April 1. Owners 62 and older use a second form that shows $20,000 off county tax and $15,000 off school tax. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and moving or changing the name on the deed means a fresh application.

The assessors' office takes real and personal property returns between January 1 and April 1. Form PT-283A for farm use valuation closes the same day, and staff ask for a call first.

The exemption is yours alone. Whoever buys and moves in must file separately, ahead of the following April 1.

How a lien forms on a Butts County house

First comes a 30-day warning letter, called a notice of intent, from the tax commissioner. If the tax is still unpaid 90 days after the due date, the commissioner may record a FiFa, which is the lien, on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. It is cancelled once you pay the tax plus fees, interest and penalties.

Butts County does not sell liens over the counter. Once a levy and tax sale ad has begun, the office wants payment made in person. A recorded FiFa is public record and may reach your credit file, although the office does not report to the credit bureaus.

No title company will close a sale with a lien open. Ask the commissioner for a written payoff that shows a good-through date, and give it to the person running the settlement. A levy or sale notice in your mailbox means you should call that day. Cash buyers expect clean title too, so the payoff is needed either way.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Butts County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Order of steps if you are selling soon

Begin at the assessors' search page, where your parcel shows the current value and any open appeal. Next, ask the tax commissioner whether both installments are paid and whether any older year carries a balance. If a notice of intent has arrived, treat it as urgent, because the 90-day mark is when a FiFa can be recorded.

Gather the warranty deed from the Clerk of Superior Court if you cannot find your copy, and keep any appraisal or photos you used in an appeal. At closing the settlement agent pays the open amount from your proceeds, and the buyer then handles the next bill in their own name. Owners of a manufactured home should also check the April 1 date, since that bill runs on a different schedule.

Selling in Butts County

Butts County covers 184 square miles of land in West Central Georgia and belongs to the Atlanta metro area. Jackson is the seat and largest city, with Flovilla and Jenkinsburg as the smaller cities. Interstate 75 and U.S. 23 pass through. Population was estimated at 27,218 in July 2025, and 74.3% of households own their home.

For 2020 to 2024, an owned home has a median value of $240,600, gross rent is $941 and household income is $69,241, across 8,941 households. Request a payoff before you pick a closing date, because the amount owed shifts as interest builds.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Butts County house with back taxes still be sold?

Yes. Back tax, interest and penalties are paid from your proceeds at the closing table, and the lien is then released. Call 770-775-8206 for a payoff letter with a good-through date, since the figure grows monthly.

Which Butts County office answers a bill question?

Bills, payoffs and liens go to the Tax Commissioner, 770-775-8206. Values, exemptions and appeals go to the Board of Assessors, 770-775-8207. You will find both at 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson.

Does my lender receive the Butts County bill?

Not the paper bill. The office sends lenders on record an electronic file, so an escrow lender may already know the amount. After switching lenders, tell the new one and forward your statement.

When must I apply for homestead in Butts County?

April 1 is the deadline for both the standard exemption and the one for owners 62 and older. Anything filed later counts toward the next tax year.

How long is the Butts County appeal window?

You get 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice. Submit a written appeal to the Board of Assessors, which has no power to lengthen that period.

The Woodbine tax office

Sellers should know that the tax office will not split a year's tax between buyer and seller. The tax stays the owner's liability. Your closing attorney or title company calculates the division and asks the office what is owed on the parcel.

When the bill arrives and when it is due

Mid-September is when bills go out, with payment due 60 days later. Whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year is the one billed, so forward the notice to your buyer if you sold afterward. Still no bill on October 15? Phone 912-576-3248.

State revenue guidance for Camden mentions December 20 as the usual statewide deadline, which a county can shift or split into installments. Taxpayers also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts. The local schedule wins, so trust the date on your own statement.

Late charges and how a lien builds

A bill is delinquent from the day after it is due. The interest rate is the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent yearly, a partial month is charged as a full month, and the minimum charge is $1. A flat 5% penalty applies at 120 days overdue, and again at 240, 360 and 480. Homestead bills of $500 or less escape the penalty, and so do new owners who lived outside Georgia, never received a bill and pay within a year.

What follows a missed Camden County due date
WhenWhat happens
Day after the due dateInterest begins
Week after the due date30-day lien warning is mailed
About a week after the warning period endsLien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, adding a filing cost of $28.50 to $33.50
120, 240, 360 and 480 days overdue5% penalty each time
After filingA tax sale can be scheduled
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Camden County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can I get my house back after a tax sale?

Yes, but only for a limited time. The tax lien dates back to the January 1 valuation and ranks ahead of every other lien. On each December 31 the tax commissioner has to issue an execution on delinquent accounts, telling the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

To redeem, you repay the winning bid and any later taxes the buyer covered, then add 20% of that total for year one, or part of it. Every further year or part adds 10%. Once twelve months pass, the buyer can serve notice that ends redemption for good. Even then, the earliest anyone can take possession is one year and forty-five days after the deed.

With that timeline in mind, selling before the sale date usually leaves you more equity than waiting.

Appeals, returns and refunds

Your 45 days begin with a Notice of Reassessment. Address the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors and get it postmarked within that window. Because assessed value equals 40% of January 1 market value, a rising market pushes assessed value up too.

If you overpaid, there is a separate route: ask in writing for a refund of tax assessed or collected in error, within three years of paying.

  • Returns go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • Homestead applications are taken year-round, but April 1 is the cutoff for that year.
  • Skipping the application is treated as waiving the exemption.

Pull together deeds, survey papers and any receipts for improvements before you apply or appeal, so the office can match its records to your file in one visit.

Do Kingsland, St. Marys and Woodbine send their own tax bills?

Maybe. It depends on the address. A city can levy its own property tax and have its clerk bill it, unless the city and county agreed to combine everything on one county statement. Vehicle tax is the exception: only the county tax commissioner collects it.

Ask the Woodbine tax office if a city bill applies to your address, then ask the city clerk for any balance, because unpaid city tax can stall a closing as readily as county tax.

Two more rules apply around a purchase. A mobile home needs a county location permit within 30 days of placement, then again every January 1 to April 1. A long-term note secured by real estate must be recorded in the county within 90 days and carries intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Camden County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you are behind on Camden County taxes

Being late does not stop you from selling. The lien rides along with the property, so the buyer's title company will insist that it be paid, and the usual way is to pay it from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for the exact balance, including interest, any 5% penalties and the lien filing cost if a lien has been recorded.

The sooner you act, the less it costs. Each missed 120-day mark adds another 5%, and once a tax sale is on the calendar your choices shrink. A fast sale to a buyer who pays cash, with the payoff handled at closing, is one way to clear the account before the next step in the schedule above arrives.

What Camden's housing market looks like

Georgia's southeastern corner belongs to Camden, bordered by Glynn County north and Florida's Nassau County south. Kingsland is its largest city, with St. Marys and Woodbine rounding out the list, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 both cross it. The Navy submarine base at Kings Bay is a major local presence, and Cumberland Island National Seashore lies inside the county.

About 60,143 people lived here as of July 2025. Owners occupy 67.8% of homes, a typical owned home is valued at $261,400, rent runs $1,235 a month, and 446 permits for new housing were issued in 2025.

Steps to settle taxes when you sell

Begin with a call to 912-576-3248 to get the balance on your parcel and learn whether an earlier year is open. A house inside a city needs a second figure from the city clerk. Pass both numbers to the closing attorney or title company, who settles them from your proceeds and splits the current year with the buyer.

If a bill never came, do not wait for it. Interest builds anyway, so call early. A cash sale may close faster than a financed one, but it needs the same tax figures.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does the Woodbine tax office divide the bill between buyer and seller?

No, the office stays out of prorating, and the tax remains the owner's liability. The closing attorney or title company works out the split from the balance the office confirms.

I never received a Camden County statement. What now?

Phone 912-576-3248. Owners with nothing in hand by October 15 are asked to call. Interest keeps building on a late balance whether or not the bill reached you.

How fast does a Camden County lien follow a missed due date?

A 30-day warning goes out the week after the due date. About a week after that period ends, the lien is filed at the Clerk of Superior Court, and a $28.50 to $33.50 filing cost lands on your bill.

After a Camden County tax sale, can the owner redeem?

Yes. Repay the buyer's price plus 20% for year one and 10% for each year after. The right stays open until the buyer finishes the notice steps that bar it, which can start twelve months after the sale.

Is there a late penalty on a small Camden County homestead bill?

No. A homestead bill of $500 or less is excused from the 5% penalty, though interest still runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent.

Collecting and valuing: two different offices

Taxes are collected at 423 College Street, Room 401, by the Carroll County Tax Commissioner. Bill questions go to 770-830-5843. The tag and tax counter, at 770-830-5826, helps customers from 8 to 5 on weekdays and wraps up title transactions at 4:30.

Setting values falls to the Board of Tax Assessors, 770-830-5812. Here the assessors also take returns and homestead applications, unlike counties where the collector does. The tax commissioner neither assesses nor sets millage, and the rates come from the county commissioners and the school board.

  • Late interest, returned mail, a bill total: tax commissioner.
  • Value, exemption, return or appeal: assessors.
  • Copy of your warranty deed: Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse.

Paying by card adds 2.5%, at the counter or on the commissioner's website, and that fee goes to the processor.

Due date, late interest and penalties

Real estate and business personal property are normally due December 1. Manufactured homes run on April 1, and vehicle tax falls due on the owner's birthday. A check in the mail counts when it bears a United States Postal Service postmark; a postage-meter stamp is not accepted. The statement is mailed to the owner, never the mortgage company, so if your lender escrows, give them your copy.

Late balances pick up interest monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty attaches, and it recurs every 120 days until it totals 20%. Homestead accounts under $500 do not face that penalty.

Why settle a Carroll County lien before listing?

Once 120 days have gone by, the commissioner can file a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court. The filing is public, credit bureaus can read it, and the office cannot control how they use it. Failing payment, the commissioner may levy on the house, though the office describes that as a last resort.

Carroll also holds tax sales, where bidders must show up with cash, certified funds or a bank letter. Your house does not have to end up there. When you sell, the title company requests a payoff, prints it on the settlement statement and pays the county from your proceeds, so nothing reaches the courthouse steps.

Carroll County appeal rules

Assessment notices must go out by July 1. Your written appeal is due within 45 days of the notice date, and once that window closes the right is gone. Each notice shows fair market value, assessed value and a tax estimate based on last year's millage.

Filing means choosing among three tracks. One is the Board of Equalization, with a later appeal to Superior Court. Another is arbitration, which gives up Superior Court. The third is a hearing officer for non-homestead parcels worth more than $1 million, and it keeps Superior Court rights.

  • Accepted grounds: taxability, value, uniformity with similar parcels.
  • Rejected: a claim that the levy itself is too high.
  • The math: fair market value times 40%, less exemptions, times the millage rate.

Programs that end when the house sells

To count for this year, a homestead application must reach the assessors before April 1, with the warranty deed if you are applying for the first time. Once approved, it carries on by itself until you move or the deed changes.

Carroll County relief for older owners
ProgramWho qualifiesWhat a sale does
Elderly school tax exemptionAge 62 or older, net income of $10,000 or lessEnds when title changes
General exemptionAge 65 or older, same income capEnds when title changes
Tax deferralAge 62 or older, household income of $15,000 or lessDeferred tax becomes payable

Under a deferral the tax stays on the property until it changes hands or climbs to 85% of fair market value. A sale therefore makes the full amount payable out of your proceeds.

Two farm programs rest on a 10-year promise made to the assessors: farmland taxed at 30% of fair market value, and conservation-use land taxed by its present use. Before listing acreage under either one, ask the assessors how a sale affects the covenant.

Other special assessments

Several more exist, each with strings attached that a buyer may care about. A building on the Georgia or National Register of Historic Places can qualify for preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it, once the Department of Natural Resources certifies it as rehabilitated or landmark historic property.

Brownfield property enrolled in the state's Hazardous Site Reuse and Redevelopment Program can see its taxable assessment effectively frozen for ten years during cleanup. Forest land conservation use needs a 15-year covenant and tracts above 200 acres, and the house on that land does not get the break.

  • Mobile homes: file a return and obtain a location permit, with the current year's tax paid in full first.
  • Real and personal property returns can be filed with the assessors from January 1 to April 1.
  • If you file a new return stating a different value, your appeal rights survive another change by the board.

Carroll County context for sellers

On the Alabama line in west Georgia, Carroll spans 499 square miles of land. Carrollton is the seat and largest city, and the rest of the municipalities are Villa Rica, Temple, Bowdon, Mount Zion, Whitesburg and Roopville. Interstate 20 runs across the north end. Population reached an estimated 131,036 in 2025, from 119,148 in the 2020 census.

Between 2020 and 2024 an owned home had a median value of $255,100 and rent a median of $1,153. Of 44,106 households, 71.3% own, and 1,065 building permits were issued in 2025.

What a seller's year looks like

Winter and early spring are filing season: returns and homestead go to the assessors by April 1. Summer brings assessment notices, mailed by July 1 at the latest, and your 45-day appeal clock starts the day a notice is dated. Autumn ends with the December 1 payment. A sale in the middle of that cycle does not wipe out the year's bill, so plan the closing around it and let the settlement statement show who pays what.

Before you list: a short checklist

Get a written total from the tax commissioner, with any interest included. Ask the assessors to confirm your homestead exemption is on file and that the name on record matches your deed. If any acreage sits under a covenant, raise that with the assessors before you sign anything.

Give the payoff to the closing agent early. A cash buyer wants the same paperwork as a financed one, and the payoff letter lets the county release its claim when the deal closes. If your lender received the bill instead of you, ask them for a copy so the figures agree.

Frequently asked questions

When do Carroll County property taxes come due?

December 1 covers real estate and business personal property, and manufactured homes are due April 1. Check the date printed on your statement.

What does lateness add to a Carroll County bill?

Interest builds monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty starts at 120 days and repeats every 120 days up to 20%, except on homestead accounts under $500.

Is there a fee for card payment in Carroll County?

Yes, 2.5%, charged at the counter and online alike. It goes to the payment processor, not the county. Ask the commissioner's office about other ways to pay.

Does the Carroll County Tax Commissioner set my tax?

No. The commissioner bills what the assessors' values and the millage rates produce. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board, and value questions go to 770-830-5812.

What is the Carroll County homestead cutoff?

April 1, at the Tax Assessor's Office, 423 College Street. A late application counts for the next tax year, and first-time applicants should bring their warranty deed.

Tax commissioner offices and hours

Two counters serve Catoosa County. The tax commissioner has an office at 796 LaFayette Street in Ringgold and another at 205 Forrest Road in Fort Oglethorpe, and both answer at (706) 965-2571.

Ringgold keeps an irregular schedule: doors open at 7:30 on Tuesdays, close at 6:00 on Thursdays, and run 8:30 to 5:00 the other three weekdays. Fort Oglethorpe is open 8:30 to 5:00 every weekday, with title work ending at 4:45 (5:45 on Thursdays).

Values are set by the Catoosa County Tax Assessor, 798 Lafayette Street, phone 706-965-3772. That office maintains over 28,000 real estate parcels and about 6,900 personal property and mobile home accounts. Its field appraisers show photo identification and drive marked county vehicles.

The December 20 bill and your taxing district

County taxes are generally due by December 20, and the one statement also carries the levies of the City of Ringgold and the City of Fort Oglethorpe. The district code on your bill tells you which jurisdiction applies.

Catoosa County taxing districts
District codeArea it covers
01Unincorporated county
02City of Ringgold
03City of Fort Oglethorpe

Voting districts do not line up with taxing districts, so go by the code printed on the bill. The tax commissioner's bill guide explains every column, and three are worth knowing before you sell.

  • Due date: the last day to pay with no chance of interest or penalty.
  • Sales tax credit: savings tied to the prior year's local option sales tax proceeds.
  • Notice of Assessment: an estimate, not a bill, and it may leave out exemptions you hold.

Mobile and manufactured homes in the county on January 1 are taxed by April 1 with a location permit. Missing that date adds a 10% penalty, a FiFa and a possible sale of the home.

How to appeal your assessment

File within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. There are three ways to do it: in person at 798 Lafayette Street, by mail to the Tax Assessor at that address (Ringgold, GA 30736), or through the assessor's page on the qPublic property site.

When you file, name your path: Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration. The dispute may concern taxability, value or uniformity, but not the amount of tax levied. Owners of mobile homes who want a different value have 45 days to file with the assessors, then 21 days after a changed value to go to the Board of Equalization.

One common surprise: the notice estimates your tax at last year's rate. The county commissioners, the school board and the Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe councils then work out a rollback rate, and that can bring the actual bill down.

Where do I apply for homestead?

Catoosa takes homestead applications at the tax commissioner's office, unlike counties where the assessors do. Bring a Georgia ID, and a first-time homeowner should bring the warranty deed. Applications can be submitted any time but must be received by April 1 to count for that year.

The Board of Assessors decides eligibility. If you are turned down, the office must tell you, and you can appeal. After approval the exemption renews itself until your residence, ownership or exemption type changes.

Catoosa has local exemptions that replace the state amounts when they are higher. The commissioner's website sorts them into regular, veteran and senior groups and keeps a separate page on deferral. Find out which one fits you before you choose a closing date.

Clearing taxes at a sale

Ask the tax commissioner for the full amount owed, then have the closing attorney or title company pay it from the proceeds. The commissioner's home page warns that unpaid taxes can lead to a levy and a sale, and links a Delinquent Tax Sale Information Guide and a list of excess funds from earlier sales.

Georgia attaches the lien to the property as of its January 1 valuation, ahead of other liens, which is why title companies insist on a payoff. If a tax sale notice has already arrived, phone the office that day, since timing controls your options.

  • Order the balance from the tax commissioner before you sign a contract.
  • Ask about excess-funds or tax sale notices tied to the parcel.
  • Keep the payoff letter with your closing papers.

If a bill arrives for a house you already sold, forward it to the buyer. Statements go to the owner on record, so recording the deed quickly keeps later bills from going astray.

Why might an appraiser visit?

The assessor's public notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and lists the reasons: a return being filed, an appeal, new construction or improvements, a records review for a property division or transfer, and a conservation use application. A visiting appraiser carries photo identification and drives a marked county vehicle. To confirm a visit, call 706-965-3772.

Georgia law requires uniform values based on the current Catoosa County sales market, and the Board of Assessors revalues every property each year. A sale or a split of a lot is the sort of change the office is likely to notice, so keep permits, survey papers and receipts for improvements within reach.

Catoosa County housing and location

Catoosa covers 162 square miles on the Tennessee line, with Ringgold as the seat and Fort Oglethorpe as the largest city. Tunnel Hill is a town. The county belongs to the Chattanooga metropolitan area, and 76.3% of residents live in urban areas. Interstate 75 and U.S. 27 carry most of the traffic.

The 2020 census counted 67,872 people. For 2020 to 2024 the county had 26,653 households, 74.2% in owner-occupied homes, with a median owned-home value of $240,900 and a median household income of $74,639.

Sale-day steps for Catoosa sellers

Order your payoff early and ask whether the parcel has any open notice of sale. Confirm which district your bill falls in so the closing agent contacts the right city, if any, for its share. Remember that your exemption ends with the sale and the buyer files on their own before April 1.

A cash sale does not change these steps, since the title company still needs the same payoff before it will release funds. If you are close to a tax sale date, call the commissioner at (706) 965-2571 before anything else. Whatever the sale type, hand the payoff letter to the closing attorney early, so the settlement statement already shows the county's share on closing day and nothing is left for a later bill to claim.

Frequently asked questions

Which day is the Catoosa County property tax deadline?

Generally December 20. One bill carries the county, Ringgold and Fort Oglethorpe taxes. The date printed on your own statement controls.

Can I treat a Catoosa County Notice of Assessment as my bill?

No. It lists the fair market value and an estimate built on last year's millage rate, and it may omit exemptions. A rollback of the rate can lower the actual bill.

Where do I apply for homestead in Catoosa County?

At the Tax Commissioner's office, with a Georgia ID and a warranty deed if you are a first-time owner. The application must be received by April 1 to count for that tax year.

When are Catoosa County mobile homes taxed?

By April 1 for homes in the county on January 1, when the location permit is issued. A late payment draws a 10% penalty, a FiFa and possibly a sale of the home.

Who takes a Catoosa County property appeal?

The Tax Assessor at 798 Lafayette Street in Ringgold, in person, by mail or online. Forty-five days run from the mailing date of the notice, and you choose Board of Equalization, Hearing Officer or Arbitration when you file.

Selling in Chatham County?

Who bills and who values in Chatham County

Two offices stand behind every Chatham bill. Values and exemption approvals come from the Board of Assessors. Billing, collection and distribution of the money to each taxing body come from the Tax Commissioner, whose office takes no role in valuation or millage.

The Tax Commissioner's 2026 brochure lists the bodies billed on one statement: the county, the Special Service District, the school board, transit, and the cities of Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Which ones apply depends on your address, and your bill's line items show it.

  • Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100, tax.chathamcountyga.gov, offices at 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., 295 Police Memorial Dr. and 1145 Eisenhower Dr., open weekdays from 8:30am until 5:00pm.
  • Board of Assessors: 912-652-7271, boa.chathamcountyga.gov, Suite 113, Pete Liakakis Government Building, 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue.
  • Mail: Chatham County Tax Commissioner, P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412.
  • Three satellite tax offices, on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21, take appointments only.

Chatham County in brief

Georgia's northernmost coastal county is Chatham, home to Savannah, the seat. Of its 632 square miles, 206 are water. Besides Savannah there are seven municipalities: Bloomingdale, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Tybee Island, Thunderbolt and Vernonburg.

Population climbed from 295,291 in 2020 to an estimated 311,855 by mid-2025. The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median owned home at $302,700 and typical rent at $1,471 a month, with 56.8% of households owning. Builders pulled 4,426 permits during 2025.

Due dates and payment

Land and buildings are billed in halves, due June 1 and November 15. Business and other personal property gets a single bill, also due November 15.

Chatham County billing calendar
BillDue
Real property, first installmentJune 1
Real property, second installmentNovember 15
Personal property, one billNovember 15

The first real property bill goes out by April 1 and the second by September 15. Payment can be mailed to P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412, made online, or made in person. Credit card and eCheck payments online carry convenience fees, although the brochure says eChecks are free. A returned check or eCheck is charged 5% of the amount, with a $30 minimum, under O.C.G.A. 16-9-20.

Anything unpaid on the due date is delinquent and draws interest and penalties. A delinquent parcel may also carry a tax lien, which a title company will want cleared first.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Chatham County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your Chatham County assessment

Deliver a written challenge to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date on your Annual Notice of Assessment. It is that notice, and not a tax bill, that starts the clock. Georgia provides a uniform appeal form, and the allowed grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

On that first appeal you name your method. The brochure lists three:

  • Board of Equalization, then Superior Court if you still disagree.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within 45 days. The Board of Assessors can accept or reject it, and you may still petition Superior Court.
  • Hearing Officer, available only for non-homestead real property worth $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value.

Bring recent sales, photographs of similar homes that sold, and lease or income figures. The Board measures square footage around the outside perimeter, so a smaller interior living area alone does not prove an error.

Returns and farm use

Returns can be filed from the start of the year through April 1, using forms on the assessors' website. Your first return rolls over yearly at the last final value. Disagree with that figure? File a new return stating your own value, which keeps your appeal rights intact if the Board revises it again.

Farmland in active use may be assessed at 30% of market value rather than 40%, and conservation use land is valued at its present use. Both need a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years, so find out from the Board what a sale does to it before listing.

Homestead exemption

The regular exemption takes $12,000 of assessed value off the county levy and $2,000 off the school and state levies. For any homestead exemption you must own the house, live there and claim it as your legal residence on January 1, so rentals do not qualify.

  • Stephens-Day and the state floating homestead exemption: the county awards whichever saves more, then adds any other exemptions you qualify for.
  • Special Chatham senior exemption: age 65 by January 1, combined net income of $10,000 or less, $30,000 off county and school assessed value, plus relief from most state assessments.
  • Senior school exemption: age 62, combined net income of $25,000 or less.
  • Exemption for a 100% service-connected disability: bring a VA letter, and note the amount can change each year.
  • Year's Support: when a spouse or minor child petitions Probate Court within two years after a death, the court can award tax relief for the year named in the petition.

Applicants need a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration in their name, with the mailing and homestead addresses matching. An application received inside the 45-day notice window counts for that year, and a later one is held for the next. Buying another home or changing the deed means filing again.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chatham County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who pays when a Chatham County house sells?

You are billed as the seller, since Georgia taxes whoever owned the property when the year began. Selling in March or August does not shift the bill to the buyer, and no refund is given for part of a year.

Splitting the year is a private arrangement made at closing. A sale between the June and November deadlines leaves the second installment open, so ask the closing attorney whether it is paid at the table or credited to the buyer. Include any delinquent balance in the payoff so no lien stays with the title.

The exemption belongs to you, so the new owner files separately. If you inherited the house, reread the Year's Support option above. Before settling on a closing day, request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100.

Pre-listing steps

Look up your parcel on the assessors' site to see the value and exemptions on file, and ask the Tax Commissioner whether either installment is open. For a house in a city such as Pooler or Tybee Island, the same office bills the city share, so the payoff should cover every line. Cash buyers ask for the same payoff letter, and having it in hand keeps closing on schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Do Chatham County owners pay once or twice a year?

Real property is paid in two halves, June 1 and November 15. Personal property is a single payment on November 15.

Which Chatham County office answers valuation questions?

Call the Board of Assessors, 912-652-7271. The Tax Commissioner, 912-652-7100, collects payments and cannot alter a value or millage rate.

Is there any appeal once the 45 days run out?

Usually not. The deadline runs from the notice date, and if a notice never reached you, ask the Board of Assessors what options remain.

Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?

No. The exemption stays with the person who filed, and a purchaser must apply fresh at the Board of Assessors with a Georgia license and a matching vehicle registration.

Will I owe tax if I sell in the fall?

Yes, for that year, since you held title in January. A still-open November installment shows up on the closing statement as a payoff or a credit.

Chattooga County, GA Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Chattooga County, GA Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Chattooga County, GA Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Chattooga County, GA Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Chattooga County? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Chattooga County?

Paying the bill and finding the right office

Billing and collecting belong to the Chattooga Tax Commissioner, who cannot change a value or a millage rate. Appraisals and exemption approvals come from the Board of Tax Assessors, whom the county commissioner appoints. Appeals are heard by a Board of Equalization picked by the Grand Jury. County tax rates come from the county commissioner, and school rates from the Board of Education.

  • Location: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747. Mail: P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. Hours run 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday, but the doors stay shut on Wednesdays.
  • You can look up and pay a bill at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • A mailed payment is accepted with a USPS postmark, not a metered one.

The bill is mailed to the homeowner and only sometimes to the lender. With an escrow account, forward your copy to the mortgage company.

Chattooga County context

Chattooga sits in Georgia's northwest corner, with 314 square miles and Summerville as the seat. Trion, Lyerly and Menlo are the other cities. Several county properties are on national historic registers, which can matter because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

Estimated population in 2025 was 25,300, close to the 24,965 counted in 2020. Homes held by their owners make up 66.8% of the total, with a median value of $115,600 for 2020 to 2024 and rent around $790. Just 2 building permits were issued in 2025.

Deadline and late costs

Land, buildings and business equipment are normally due December 1. Interest starts accruing on December 2, and 120 days later a 5% penalty is added, though a homesteaded parcel owing less than $500 escapes that penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1 and pick up 1% interest for each month of delay.

A levy on the property is possible for unpaid taxes, though the Tax Commissioner treats it as a last resort. A bill more than 30 days late can be recorded as a tax FiFa (lien) at the Superior Court clerk's office. These records are public and credit bureaus may read them, which the tax office cannot prevent.

Excess funds from past tax sales are listed on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Chattooga County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemptions

The Tax Commissioner lists both state exemptions and local ones that take the place of the state amount when they are bigger. Owning and living in the home on January 1 is required, and applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. Filing is open year-round, yet only an application received by April 1 applies to that year.

Chattooga County homestead exemptions
ExemptionEligibilityBenefit
StandardAny qualifying homeowner$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,000Sliding 20% to 100% share of assessed value, county tax only, for the residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value, school tax only
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

Be careful with the floating exemption: it may raise a bill at first because it replaces other state and county exemptions. Owners with a service-connected disability qualify for a separate exemption, as do unremarried widows of service members killed in armed conflict and of firefighters or peace officers who died on duty.

Deferral and lower assessments

A homestead owner age 62 or older, with gross household income up to $15,000, may defer tax but never erase it. Repayment generally comes due once ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, so a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Land in genuine farming can be assessed at 30% rather than 40%, and conservation use property is valued as currently used. A covenant promising at least 10 years of that use is required for both.
  • Qualifying historic buildings may get preferential assessment covering the structure and as many as two surrounding acres.
  • Manufacturers may claim the Freeport exemption for raw goods, work in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, applying to the Board of Tax Assessors from January 1 to April 1.

How to contest a Chattooga County value

Counting from the notice date, you have 45 days. The assessors get the appeal first and take a second look at their value. After that, the case can go to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a last written notice filed with the assessors moves it on to Superior Court.

You may contest taxability, value, or uniformity against neighboring properties. Saying the tax is too high will not work, because the county commissioner and Board of Education set that rate. A mobile home owner disputing a revised value has 30 days to get to the Board of Equalization.

Returns are accepted until April 1. After a first return, real property returns carry forward unless something changes, but personal property returns are needed every year.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chattooga County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling in Chattooga County

The person who owns the property on January 1 owes the whole year, and part-year owners get no refund. Let the closing attorney divide the year on the settlement statement.

Your exemption does not transfer, so a purchaser moving in must file by April 1. For a deed copy for the closing file, visit the deed room kept by the Clerk of Superior Court in the Chattooga County Courthouse. With a median home value of $115,600, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can weigh on a sale, so request a payoff early.

Practical steps before closing

The tax office is closed Wednesdays, so schedule calls and visits for the other weekdays or check the bill online. Request a written payoff and find out whether any older year is open. A mobile or manufactured home has its own April 1 account, separate from the December bill, so check that one on its own.

Hand the payoff to the closing attorney early. Cash buyers want the same documents as anyone else, and a clean payoff keeps a lien from slowing the sale. Remember also that the buyer, not you, will file for a new homestead exemption after closing, so mention the April 1 date to them. If you inherited the house or are selling for an estate, ask the closing attorney about how the January 1 owner rule applies before the deed is signed.

Frequently asked questions

What is the usual Chattooga County deadline?

Land, buildings and business equipment are due December 1. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

Can I visit the Chattooga tax office on a Wednesday?

No, Wednesday is the closed day. On the other weekdays the office runs from 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM.

How costly is a late payment in Chattooga County?

Interest begins on the following day. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, unless the property is homesteaded and the liability is under $500.

Does a Chattooga County homestead exemption need yearly renewal?

No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?

Go to the Superior Court clerk's deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse.

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia

Which office bills and which one values?

Two offices on Marietta Highway in Canton share the work. The Tax Commissioner bills real estate, personal property, public utility, timber, motor vehicle and mobile home taxes, then sends the collections to the state, county, school and city governments. The Tax Assessors' Office decides what your property is worth and which exemptions you get.

  • Tax Commissioner: 678-493-6400, cherokeecountytax.com. The main office is at 2780 Marietta Hwy, Canton, with an annex at 155 Towne Lake Pkwy, Woodstock. Both are open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Assessors' Office: 678-493-6120, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton. Returns are filed here until the season ends April 1.
  • City tax offices bill separately inside Ball Ground, Canton, Holly Springs, Mountain Park, Nelson, Waleska and Woodstock, so find out whether your address is incorporated.

The Assessors' Office posts a public notice that appraisal staff may visit after an appeal, a new return, new construction or a conservation use application. Visitors carry county photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and answering their questions is voluntary.

Cherokee County in brief

Cherokee has 434 square miles, of which 422 are land. Interstate 575 runs through the middle from Kennesaw by way of Woodstock, Holly Springs and Canton to Ball Ground, and the southern end nearest Atlanta is the most densely settled. One school district, the Cherokee County School District, serves every address.

Population reached 299,273 in 2025, 12.2% above the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-held house is worth $435,100, median household income is $108,115 and 77.3% of homes are owner-occupied. Builders pulled 1,524 permits in 2025.

Due date and millage rates

Cherokee mails bills in September and wants payment by November 15. A balance left after that date is delinquent, and the Tax Commissioner notes that a lien then attaches to the property. Mobile home bills arrive each January and are due April 1.

One mill equals a dollar for each thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of market value in Georgia. The county's rates for 2026 and 2025 are below.

The fire levy explains why bills differ between a Canton address and an unincorporated one such as Hickory Flat or Lake Arrowhead. A city may add its own levy on top of these county figures.

How to appeal your assessment

Write out your appeal and get it to the assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice went in the mail. The state's uniform form asks you to choose a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration. The grounds may be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

County appraisal staff value property with sales comparison, cost and income approaches and test the results statistically by area, neighborhood and class of property. A good appeal answers those methods with your own evidence.

  • Recent closed sales of similar houses nearby, with dates and prices.
  • Photos and repair estimates that show condition problems the record may not reflect.
  • A copy of your settlement statement or warranty deed if you bought the property recently.

Complaints about the size of the tax fall outside an appeal, because assessors do not set millage rates. The governing bodies named on your bill do that.

Where to apply for homestead

Apply in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, carrying a valid Georgia driver's license or ID that shows the property's address. Take your settlement statement or warranty deed too, because staff print and complete the application on the spot.

The state's standard homestead exemption covers an owner-occupied primary residence, and the county can add to it. Applications are taken all year but must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year, and skipping the application waives the exemption. Ask the office which Cherokee County exemptions for seniors, disabled service members or surviving spouses fit your situation, since the amounts change.

An exemption follows the person who applied, so a buyer starts over with a new application.

What selling does to the tax bill

Title on New Year's Day decides who is taxed, and the Tax Commissioner has no legal way to prorate a part year. If you and the buyer want a split, you must agree on it at closing.

A buyer who closes in the fall will not automatically get a bill. The Tax Commissioner asks for the closing statement so the bill can be reissued in the new owner's name, which works for purchases completed before November 15 of that tax year. If October 1 passes with no bill in hand, phone 678-493-6400 or print one from the website. Even when the bill stays in the seller's name, the lien follows the property if it turns delinquent.

A properly completed PT-61 transfer form on file at the Superior Court clerk's office can stand in for a new real property return in the sale year, as long as nothing was subdivided or built.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cherokee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When property goes to tax sale

The winning bidder at a tax sale receives a tax deed but cannot take possession, build, or evict tenants straight away. For 12 months the owner, a lender or anyone else with an interest may buy the property back.

The redemption price is the bid, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus special assessments, plus a premium of 20% of the amount for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each year after that, plus sheriff and advertising costs. After 12 months the buyer may serve a notice of foreclosure of the right to redeem by certified mail to the recorded owner and each interest holder, and the notice must also be printed weekly for four straight weeks in the county newspaper.

If an auction brings in more than is owed, the surplus is held separately. O.C.G.A. 48-4-5 lets the owner of record at that time, plus security deed holders, claim it. Claimants are not required to pay or hire anyone to get it.

Sale checklist for Cherokee sellers

Print your bill at cherokeecountytax.com or call 678-493-6400 to learn the balance, and ask if any earlier year is open. Send the closing statement to the Tax Commissioner after you close so the next bill goes to the right name. Tell the buyer to apply for their own homestead exemption at the Assessors' Office before April 1.

If the house sits inside one of the seven cities, ask that city's tax office for its balance too. A cash sale follows the same steps, and because it can close sooner, request your figures early.

Frequently asked questions

When must a Cherokee County bill be paid?

November 15. Bills are mailed in September, and taxes not paid by that date are considered delinquent.

Will the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner prorate at a sale?

No. The office has no legal provision for prorating partial-year ownership, so any split is settled by the parties at closing.

Where can I file for homestead in Cherokee County?

File in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton, with a Georgia license or ID showing the property address.

How long can an owner redeem after a tax sale?

Twelve months from the sale date. After that the buyer may start the foreclosure of the right to redeem by sending notice.

How can I find my Cherokee County tax bill if I did not receive one?

Call the Tax Commissioner at 678-493-6400 or print a copy from cherokeecountytax.com. The office suggests doing so if a bill has not arrived by October 1.

How Athens-Clarke property tax works

Because Athens and Clarke County merged into a single government, one office, the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division, sends the bill for the whole county. Payments fund the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

October 20 is the general due date for real estate and business personal property. A bill left unpaid can be levied on and eventually sold. Beyond interest, the division adds a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark after the due date, up to four times, for a possible 20% total.

  • Land and buildings are taxed where they are located, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Taxable value is 40% of market value, with exceptions written into law (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Standing timber is not taxed until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

Athens-Clarke housing at a glance

Clarke is Georgia's smallest county by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. Athens and Winterville are the cities, and the town of Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County. The University of Georgia shapes the housing market.

The 2025 estimate is 129,921 people, just 1.0% above the 2020 base. Owners live in only 41.4% of homes, so most households rent, and typical rent is $1,219. An owner-held home has a median value of $298,900 and median household income is $53,625. Many Athens houses are rentals, and an investor-owned home gets the same bill as any other.

How to appeal your assessment

Send a written appeal to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the day the assessment notice was mailed. When the assessors keep the value, your file goes to the Board of Equalization automatically. The Athens-Clarke assessors answer questions at 706-613-3140.

Athens-Clarke appeal timeline
StepTiming
Written appeal delivered to the assessors45 days from notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing date15 days after the appeal reaches that board
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that letter
Appeal to Superior CourtWritten, 30 days after the Board of Equalization rules

At the hearing the assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling goes to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clarke County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Returns you may need to file

File the real estate return, Form PT-50R, with the tax commissioner in room 250 of the Courthouse before filing season closes April 1, in any year you acquired or altered the property. Nothing has changed since last year? Then you may skip it. A required return that is not filed draws a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest and possibly other penalties.

Personal property has a tougher rule: Form PT-50P goes to the Board of Assessors every April 1, changed or not. The tax commissioner also warns buyers of businesses, boats and aircraft to check for unpaid personal property tax before closing, since attorneys usually search real estate taxes only.

Exemptions and refunds

The state homestead exemption belongs to people who own a home and live in it as their primary residence. You can apply whenever you like, but to start in a given year the application must be in by April 1, and not applying counts as waiving it. Some counties add larger local exemptions, so ask the Athens-Clarke offices which ones apply to a given house before you assume the standard amount is all there is.

If tax was assessed and collected in error or illegally, you may request a refund in writing, provided you begin the request within three years of payment. When an assessment is under appeal and the final taxable value comes in lower, the refund is processed automatically once that value is final. Equipment, machinery and fixtures used by a business are assessed at 40% of fair market value, and the assessor may value a going business as a whole.

What happens if taxes go unpaid?

Athens-Clarke County runs its own tax sales. The tax commissioner serves as ex officio sheriff, and Georgia law requires the property to be advertised for four consecutive weeks in the legal section of the county newspaper, the Athens Banner-Herald.

  • Sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, ordinarily in front of the courthouse, and run as a public outcry auction.
  • The opening bid equals the taxes due plus costs, and the property goes to the highest bidder or may be bid in for the county.
  • Payment is due at the sale, by cashier's or certified check from an FDIC-insured institution.
  • The tax commissioner then executes and records a tax deed. The purchaser owes taxes as they come due, and any amount paid may be added to the redemption price.

An owner who sees a notice for their address should contact the tax commissioner at once. Redemption rights exist under Georgia law, and the county's tax sale page has the current list of properties.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Clarke County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What should I settle at closing when selling in Clarke County?

The owner in January pays the year's tax, and nothing is refunded for the months after a sale. Whether the buyer credits you for their share of the year is a matter the two of you settle on the closing statement.

Interest does not start until 60 days after the bill's postmark. If October 20 has gone by and a balance remains, ask for a payoff figure that includes penalties and pay it from the sale proceeds so the title is clear.

Rental owners selling an occupied house should confirm that business personal property, such as appliances listed on a business return, has no balance. Questions about exemptions, returns or values go to the assessors, and bills and payments go to the Property Tax Division.

Steps for a Clarke County seller

Read your latest bill first, since it lists both market and assessed value. Call the Property Tax Division for the balance. If the value looks wrong and your 45 days are not over, call the assessors at 706-613-3140. Landlords should ask whether a business return lists items that carry their own tax.

A cash sale uses the same payoff process as a financed one, so request the figure early and give it to the closing attorney. The buyer files their own homestead application by April 1 once they move in.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Athens-Clarke County due date?

October 20 in the usual case. The Property Tax Division lists that date for real estate and business personal property.

What is the Athens-Clarke County appeal window?

It is 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, and call 706-613-3140 with questions.

Who conducts tax sales in Clarke County?

The tax commissioner, acting as ex officio sheriff. Auctions start at 10:00 a.m. on each month's first Tuesday, usually in front of the courthouse.

Must I file a property return every year in Athens-Clarke County?

Not for real estate if nothing changed. Real estate returns are due January 1 to April 1 in years the property changed or was acquired, while personal property returns are due every April 1.

Do most Clarke County residents own their homes?

No. Owners live in 41.4% of homes for 2020 to 2024, so renters are the majority.
