Who bills and who values property

Two Clayton County offices touch every parcel. Valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors. Billing and collection sit with the Tax Commissioner, who also divides the money among the county, the cities, fire services and the school board. The millage rate is not either office's call: county commissioners set the county rate and each other taxing body sets its own.

Both offices share the Jonesboro government complex at 121 South McDonough Street. Assessors: Annex 3, fourth floor, (770) 477-3285. Tax Commissioner: Annex 3, second floor, property tax line (770) 477-3311. A value question sent to the commissioner, or a payoff question sent to the assessors, just gets passed along, which costs a seller days.

Ownership and value are locked in on January 1. A house sold in October is still billed to the person who held it that January, so lay the tax bill next to the closing statement and compare.

Clayton County at a glance

Clayton sits just south of Atlanta, densely built, with the courthouse in Jonesboro and most of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport inside its lines. The 2020 census counted 297,595 residents, 106,200 households and 114,038 housing units, 6.9% of them vacant. Renters edged out owners, at 50.5% of occupied homes to 49.5%.

That mix means a landlord selling with tenants in place is a common situation here, and the lease is one more thing to settle before a closing date. Part of the county lies inside city limits, so find out from the Tax Commissioner whether your parcel gets a city bill on top of the county one, because a seller's payoff has to cover both.

When bills are due

The Tax Commissioner describes a yearly rhythm. Notices of assessment arrive in spring or early summer. Millage rates get worked out between about mid July and mid August, and the bills themselves follow around mid September. The due date is usually in mid November, with a payment window of 60 days after mail-out. Exact dates move from year to year. The printed bill has them, or call (770) 477-3311.

If your value is under appeal when bills go out, you receive two bills. One covers 85% and falls due with everyone else's. The other covers the remaining 15% and comes due, or comes back as a refund, after the appeal settles. Request both before the house goes on the market.

Georgia adds two rules of its own. Interest begins 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and delinquent balances can draw penalties too. Anyone claiming tax was assessed in error has three years from payment to start that claim. Refunds from an appeal come after the final value is set.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clayton County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

The appeal clock runs 45 days from the mailing date on the notice, and only a written appeal counts. Homestead applications and other special assessment requests share that date. Filing late costs you that year's challenge. Take it to the assessors in Annex 3 or file through the online appeals site.

After the first review, the notice lists four routes.

Appeal routes after the first review
RouteWhat it can decideCondition printed on the notice
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, exemptions or taxabilityOpen to any owner who files in time
Nonbinding arbitrationValue onlyRequires a certified appraisal
Hearing officerValue or uniformityReal property that is not a homestead and is valued above $500,000, plus large personal property accounts
Superior CourtAs agreedOnly by written agreement with the assessors

Ask early: the assessors must hand over the records behind your value within 10 business days of a request. Bring comparable sales, plus photos of any defects an assessor could not see from the street. The rate itself is off the table, because an appeal reaches value, uniformity and taxability only.

Homestead exemption

Homestead status covers the single house you own and occupy as your main residence on January 1. Nobody can claim two. Applications go to the Tax Commissioner. File between January 2 and April 1. Anything later is held for the next year. Once approved, it renews on its own. You only have to report if you stop qualifying.

Clayton voters were also given a local base-year homestead freeze on the county-purposes value for these groups:

  • Residents age 65 or older
  • Disabled former service members
  • Unremarried surviving spouses of peace officers or firefighters killed in the line of duty
  • Residents who are 100 percent disabled

Whether your parcel is covered is a question for the commissioner's office.

A homestead exemption follows the occupant. A buyer files separately after moving in, so the next bill on the house can run higher than yours did.

What if taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid taxes lead to an execution on the property and, eventually, a tax sale. The Tax Commissioner's property portal carries tax sale notices, a bidder pre-registration form, and an excess funds claim form for owners who are owed money after a sale.

A tax sale transfers a tax deed and not clear title, and Georgia gives the former owner a right to redeem. Lenders will not lend against a house with a lien, and whatever is owed comes off your proceeds at closing. If you are behind, call (770) 477-3311 first and ask what it takes to clear the account by your target closing date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Clayton County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with a bill outstanding or an appeal pending

Nothing at the county level divides the year between buyer and seller. The contract and the settlement statement, prepared by the closing attorney, do that. Have the closing office request a payoff covering the county bill and any city bill. Run through this list before listing:

  • Download the current bill from the Tax Commissioner's portal and see if a city bill applies too.
  • Check for a pending appeal, which brings a second bill for the remaining 15%.
  • Confirm that any homestead exemption will be removed after the sale.
  • Keep the closing statement as your proof the bill was paid.
  • Hand the closing attorney your latest assessment notice and any appeal paperwork so the payoff request is accurate.

A sale with tenants or a repair list can still close on a cash timeline, and a cash sale skips the buyer's loan appraisal and underwriting. Compare any written cash offer with what a listing would net after repairs, showings and the wait.

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline to appeal a Clayton County value?

Send a written appeal within 45 days of the date printed on your assessment notice. Deliver it to the assessors at 121 S. McDonough Street, Annex 3, fourth floor, or use the county's online appeals site. Miss it and the value stands for that year.

Which Clayton County office handles bills and which handles values?

Bills, payments, exemptions and payoff figures come from the Tax Commissioner, (770) 477-3311. Values, notices and appeals belong to the assessors, (770) 477-3285. The assessors collect no money, and the commissioner cannot change a value.

Do I pay anything while a Clayton County appeal is pending?

Yes, most of it. A parcel under appeal gets two bills, and the 85% bill is due on the regular date. The remaining 15% is settled after the decision, which can leave a small balance or a refund.

Can I sell a Clayton County house that has unpaid taxes?

Yes. The closing office pays the back taxes out of your proceeds, so ask for a payoff figure good through the closing date. If the parcel already went to a tax sale, the tax deed buyer holds an interest until redemption, so call (770) 477-3311 first.

Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. The exemption goes with the person living in the house. The buyer applies on their own with the Tax Commissioner, and an application filed after April 1 takes effect the following year.

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who sends the bill

Cobb's county and school levies are combined on one statement mailed by the Tax Commissioner, who collects on behalf of the commissioners and the school board. If your lot lies outside every city, that is the only bill. A parcel in Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna or Powder Springs gets a second bill, because each of those seven cities collects for itself.

Valuation is someone else's job. The Board of Tax Assessors determines fair market value annually, and 40% of that figure is what gets taxed. The formula reads (Fair Market Value x 0.40) x (Millage Rate / 1,000), and one mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. Rates are chosen yearly by the county, the schools and each city on its own.

When the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant applies to an eligible homestead, you will see it as its own reduction line, apart from any exemption.

Due date and penalties

Mailing happens by August 15 and the deadline is October 15. The tax digest has to be approved first, usually in mid to late July, and until then the office cannot take money, so prepaying is impossible.

Payment counts as timely when the office holds it by October 15 or when a Postal Service postmark shows that date at the latest. Meter and kiosk stamps are rejected. No bill by August 30? Print a copy from the commissioner's website, because a lost bill is no defense against penalty or interest.

Partial payments are welcome, yet any balance left after October 15 picks up a 5% penalty along with monthly interest. Call 770-528-8600 to work out an arrangement. Bounced checks cost $30 or 5%, whichever is larger, plus bank charges.

Ways to pay

Pick from four methods:

  • Online by e-check or card, with no convenience fee on e-check
  • Phone, at 1-866-535-2622
  • Mail, to P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061
  • In person or by drop box at the offices below

The county keeps none of the card fees.

In-person payment locations

Main Property Tax Division736 Whitlock Avenue, Marietta

With an escrow account, once the lender notifies the office, bills are sent to you and the lender alike. Verifying that the payment went through is still on you. A double payment is refunded. The payment coupon is optional as long as the parcel ID is written on the check.

If you disagree with your valuation

Put your dispute in writing and deliver it to the Board of Tax Assessors inside 45 days of the notice date. The commissioner plays no role. You can contest value, uniformity or taxability, but the millage rate is off limits. When the assessors do not settle it, the case goes to the Board of Equalization.

Appealing leaves the deadline where it is. A parcel in dispute is billed a reduced appeal amount, either 85% of assessed value or 100% of the last uncontested value. Pay at least that by October 15 and the 5% penalty is avoided. The unpaid remainder can gather up to $150 a month in interest, which full payment on time prevents.

The commissioner's online estimator uses the prior year's millage rates and figures county tax only, leaving out city tax and special classifications. A second version for new home buyers takes a market value, a tax district and exemptions. Whatever either shows, the official bill controls.

Homestead exemptions and relief

Owners who occupy the house as their main home on January 1 qualify for the basic homestead exemption. At 62, seniors can claim additional breaks, among them a full or reduced school tax exemption. More exemptions exist for owners with a 100% service-connected disability, other disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants, nonprofits and religious groups.

Applications can go in online, at an office or by mail, and they need to arrive or be postmarked ahead of the appeal deadline printed on your assessment notice. Later ones roll to next year. Held an exemption elsewhere before? Add a letter proving it was removed. Rentals cannot carry a homestead, and keeping one after you stop qualifying means paying back the savings with penalties and interest.

After a marriage, divorce, death or change in ownership, file a new application with the supporting paper: a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Special classifications such as conservation use, historic property and forest land go through the assessors.

When Cobb County taxes go unpaid

A late account first draws a written notice. After another 30 days the office may issue a Fi. Fa., a tax execution that acts as a lien. It adds $23 when the tax is under $100 or $33 when it is over $100, along with administrative costs, and late fees are not waived.

When a sale is scheduled, it happens on the first Tuesday of the month at Superior Court Plaza, corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue. You must pre-register and bid in person between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Winners pay in cash or by certified check. The thing sold is a tax deed, not a lien. The former owner then has 12 months to redeem by paying the bid, later taxes the buyer covered, special assessments, and a premium of 20% for the first year or fraction and 10% for each year after.

  • Request a written payoff before the house is listed.
  • If a Fi. Fa. has been filed, its fee is part of the payoff.
  • Once a tax sale occurs, the 12-month redemption window starts.

Selling when taxes are owed

Prorating is not part of the commissioner's work. The parcel carries one full year of tax, and the closing paperwork decides who pays what when the sale closes. Because the tax stays with the property, whoever holds title at the time should see that it gets paid.

Once the sale closes, tell the commissioner about the new owner and have your homestead exemption taken off. The buyer applies for theirs as described above. Before listing or signing a contract, collect:

  • Your current bill and your most recent assessment notice
  • Any city bill for the same parcel
  • Notes on any appeal still open

Tenants, repairs or a delinquent bill do not stop a sale, and any payoff is taken from your proceeds in every case. A cash buyer is not waiting on a lender, so a clear payoff figure keeps a quick closing on schedule.

Frequently asked questions

When do Cobb County property taxes come due?

The deadline is October 15, and bills are mailed by August 15. A payment is timely if it reaches the office or carries a Postal Service postmark by then. Anything unpaid afterward draws a 5% penalty and monthly interest.

Does Cobb County allow installment payments?

Not formally. The office takes partial payments, but the balance left after October 15 keeps accruing penalty and interest. Call 770-528-8600 to arrange something. An appeal does not defer payment, though only the appeal amount is due by the deadline.

Will Cobb County split the tax bill between me and the buyer?

No. The bill covers the entire year, and the office leaves the split to you and the buyer. Your closing paperwork sets each side's share, and the closing attorney or title company normally pays out of proceeds.

What if my Cobb County tax bill never arrived?

You still owe it, penalty and interest included. Print a copy from the commissioner's website and write the parcel ID on your check, or call 770-528-8600. Fix your mailing address so it does not happen again.

How long can an owner redeem after a Cobb County tax sale?

For 12 months after the sale. The owner, a creditor or any other interested party can redeem by paying the bid, later taxes, special assessments and the stepped premium of 20% then 10%. The buyer works out the exact figure.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Coffee County housing at a glance

Coffee County is in south Georgia's Wiregrass region. The county seat and biggest town is Douglas, joined by Ambrose, Broxton and Nicholls. Land area comes to 575 of its 603 square miles.

In 2020 the census found 43,092 residents, 15,277 households and 17,331 housing units, of which 11.9% sat empty. Homeowners lived in 63.9% of occupied units and renters in 36.1%. If you are selling acreage, read the land programs below first, because farm or conservation enrollment changes what the buyer takes on.

Which office handles what

Coffee County splits tax work between two neighboring offices. For values and appeals, go to the Tax Assessors Office, 224 West Ashley Street, Suite C, Douglas, weekdays 8:00 to 5:00, phone 912-384-2136. Personal property has a separate number, 912-493-1100.

Next door in Suite B, the Tax Commissioner takes care of bills, payments and homestead applications. Walk-in hours are 8:00 to 4:50 on weekdays, and the number is (912) 384-4895. Write to P.O. Box 1207, Douglas, GA 31533, or pay online through the commissioner's site. Anything about a bill belongs here, since the assessors deal only in values.

Cities add their own property tax, and some counties fold it into one bill. If your house is in Douglas, Broxton, Nicholls or Ambrose, ask the commissioner whether you will see one bill or two.

Filing deadlines

Mark April 1. Homestead filings, personal property returns and the conservation use, preferential and forest land programs all close then, although the land programs also accept applications during the appeal window. Your status is judged as of January 1, when you must own the home and be living in it.

Coffee County filing dates
Filing or programDeadline
Homestead exemptionJanuary 1 to April 1
Personal property returnApril 1
Conservation use, preferential and forest land applicationsApril 1, or during the appeal window

Parcels are also re-examined across a three-year cycle by contract appraisers from GMASS, who carry ID badges and drive marked vehicles. A recent sale within 12 months, a building permit, a value return, fire damage, a demolition or an appeal can bring a visit to your lot. Most of that fieldwork happens from January 1 through May 1, so a seller may meet an appraiser in spring.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Coffee County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to challenge your value

Counting from the date printed on the assessment notice, you have 45 days. The county prefers real property owners to file through the appeals module on its qPublic site, and computers in the lobby let you do it in person. Personal property appeals go on paper, postmarked by the deadline if mailed.

Each appeal lands with the assessors first. Should they stand by the number, a Board of Equalization hears it next, and Superior Court remains open to an owner who is still unsatisfied. Arbitration is an alternative to the hearing. You can argue taxability, value, or uniformity with comparable properties. You cannot argue that the bill itself is too big.

No notice in the mail? Phone the assessors and check which address they have. The copy they hand you is treated as the official notice.

Exemptions and land programs

Homestead applications go to the Tax Commissioner's office, any time from New Year's Day to April 1 of the first year you want the break. Once approved, it continues each year until the owner changes. The county offers:

  • A standard homestead exemption.
  • A $4,000 exemption for owners 65 or older.
  • A school tax exemption for owners 62 or older under an income limit, capped at $10,000 of assessed value.
  • A $50,000 exemption for qualifying disabled former service members, extended to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.
  • A deferral for homestead owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax is due when ownership changes or when the deferred amount plus interest reaches 85% of the property's fair market value.

Lawmakers can change these amounts, so check each one with the Tax Commissioner before counting on it. In a year when the Homeowners Tax Relief Grant is funded, expect to see it as a credit on your bill.

Landowners have extra choices. Qualifying farmland can be assessed at 30% of market value instead of the usual 40%. Conservation use requires a 10-year covenant and a $10.00 recording fee filed with the application. Breaking it costs twice the taxes saved, with 1% monthly interest added if the break is never reported. A buyer who keeps the land in the same use can sign onto the covenant.

Billing calendar and late costs

December 20 is the default state due date, but a local government can move it. Some counties choose December 1, November 15 or installments. What matters is the date printed on your Coffee County bill, and the Tax Commissioner can confirm it. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked, with penalties possible later.

If you paid tax that was assessed in error, a written refund request within three years can recover it. Refunds from appealed values come automatically after the value is final. A balance left unpaid can turn into a lien and a tax sale, which any closing office will insist you clear.

Tell your closing attorney if the land is enrolled in conservation use, because a buyer who changes how it is used can trigger the penalty.

Selling a Coffee County house: taxes at closing

The January 1 title holder is the one taxed, and how the year gets divided between you and the buyer is a matter for the contract and settlement statement. Your closing attorney should ask the Tax Commissioner, (912) 384-4895, for a payoff that includes any city bill. After closing, report the sale so your homestead exemption comes off, and remind the buyer to file theirs by April 1.

  • Get the balance as it stands today and find out about any city bill.
  • See whether the parcel sits in conservation use, which carries a covenant to the buyer.
  • Plan for dropping your homestead exemption.
  • Hold on to the closing statement. It proves the taxes were paid.
  • Bring a copy of your assessment notice and any appeal papers to the closing attorney.

Repairs you have put off, tenants in the house or back taxes can slow a conventional sale. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, which leaves the payoff figure and the title work as the main things setting the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call in Coffee County with a tax question?

Call the Tax Commissioner, (912) 384-4895, about bills, payments and homestead filings. Call the Tax Assessors Office, 912-384-2136, about values and appeals. Because the assessors only set values, a bill question sent to them gets forwarded.

When is the Coffee County homestead filing deadline?

April 1 of the first year you want the exemption, and you must own and live in the home on January 1. File with the Tax Commissioner. An application that comes in later generally waits until the next tax year.

How long do I have to appeal a Coffee County value?

Forty-five days from the date on your assessment notice. Real property owners are steered to the qPublic appeals module, while personal property appeals go on paper.

Does Coffee County conservation use pass to a buyer?

It can. If the buyer keeps the same qualifying use and signs the covenant, there is no penalty. Changing the use within the 10-year period costs twice the taxes saved, so mention enrollment to your closing attorney.

How is the tax bill handled at a Coffee County closing?

The balance, including any city bill, is paid from your proceeds, and the contract sets each side's share of the year. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff dated to your closing.

Selling in Colquitt County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Colquitt County?

Who mails the Colquitt County bill?

The Moultrie Tax Commissioner handles mailing and collection. Value comes from the Tax Assessor's Office, and the commissioner controls neither value nor millage.

Visit 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, GA 31768, or write to postal box 99. Counter hours are 8:00am to 4:30pm, Monday through Friday, and you can reach property tax staff at (229) 616-7410. The same office runs motor vehicle registration. Solid waste has its own desk at 101 East Central Avenue, Office 168, (229) 616-7405, and the landfill opens Saturdays from 8:00am to noon, handy when you are cleaning out a house before listing.

  • Assessor's Office: appraisals, assessment notices, exemption approvals.
  • Board of Equalization: hears appeals, with members the grand jury appoints.
  • County commission and school board: separate mill rates, set separately.
  • Tax Commissioner: the bill itself, payment, liens and levies.

Colquitt County in brief

This is Southwest Georgia farm country, about 557 square miles, its courthouse and biggest city both in Moultrie. US 319 connects Moultrie to Interstate 75 roughly 24 miles east.

An estimated 47,438 people lived here in 2025, in 19,775 housing units, and 63.7% of homes were owner-occupied. Median owned value is $121,400 and gross rent is $818, so price a listing with that modest market in view.

When bills are due

Real estate and business personal property are generally due December 10, with mailing at least 60 days before. Go by the date your own bill prints, because it can shift.

Bills carry the owner's name, not the lender's. When a mortgage has no escrow, passing the bill to the lender is your job. The office cannot guarantee delivery, and interest, penalty and costs apply either way.

Manufactured and mobile homes have a deadline of their own, and the Tax Commissioner can tell you yours. Before moving a unit into or out of the county, get a relocation permit from the Compliance office in the Courthouse Annex at 229-616-7417.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Colquitt County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late bills and liens

Past the due date a bill picks up interest monthly and, later, a penalty. Rather than calculating it yourself, request a written payoff. Homesteaded parcels with bills under $500 owe no penalty.

If nothing is paid, a FiFa follows. That tax lien is entered at the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket and can stay on a credit record for at least seven years. The commissioner may also levy against the property and in the end sell it, though levy is meant as a last resort.

Delinquent notices go out only periodically, so the figure on the last one you got may have grown by the time you pay or close.

Who owes the tax when the house sells

Ownership on January 1 decides who is on the hook. If you held the house that day, the bill and any lien stay yours even after a June sale. You can move the debt to the buyer by handing the commissioner the closing statement no later than 90 days after the due date.

When your closing prorates the tax, take the settlement statement to the East Central Avenue office. That lets the commissioner record a lien against the new owner if the bill goes unpaid. Any bill that arrives for a house you have already sold belongs with the buyer, so forward it.

Ask the title company how the county gets its money, and obtain a payoff from the commissioner dated near the closing. A recorded lien will not stop a sale. Its payoff comes out of the sale funds at the table. A cash buyer closes the same way, minus a lender to satisfy. Bring the deed, your latest bill and any lien paperwork.

Exemptions and farm programs

Colquitt offers a standard exemption plus several based on age, military service or income. Each is subtracted from assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40% of fair market value. File your first application with the Tax Assessor's Office, with a copy of your warranty deed if you just bought. It has to be in their hands by April 1.

  • Standard homestead: takes $2,000 off assessed value for county, school and state levies.
  • Elderly school tax (62 or older): up to $10,000 off, if net income is $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general (65 or older): up to $4,000 off, with a $10,000 income test that leaves out Social Security and some retirement income.
  • Disabled veteran or qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption (62 or older): gross household income of $30,000 or less, covering state and county tax but not school tax.

Where a local exemption is larger than the state amount, the local one wins. The assessors can tell you which applies. Farmland has its own paths: assessment at 30% for bona fide agricultural use, and conservation use or timber programs that require a covenant of at least 10 years. Historic property and certain hazardous-site redevelopment parcels may also qualify. Owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until a sale or until the deferral and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

What a seller should do before listing

Call the Tax Commissioner at (229) 616-7410 first and ask what is owed today, including any open FiFa. Because of the January 1 rule, the bill may still carry your name at closing. If the house had a homestead exemption, plan to tell the Tax Assessor's Office after the sale so it comes off your account, and expect the buyer to apply on their own.

Give the title company the deed and the bill. If the closing prorates the tax, keep the settlement statement safe: the commissioner needs it within 90 days after the due date for the buyer to be billed. A seller with a mobile home on the lot should also check the relocation permit rule before anyone moves the unit.

How to dispute your value

Write the appeal and file it within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The choices are the equalization board or an arbitrator, and either result can go on to Superior Court.

Through April 1 each spring you may also file a return giving your own opinion of the property's January 1 value. Say nothing and you are treated as returning last year's value and exemptions. For a mobile home, the sequence is 45 days to appeal to the assessors, then 21 days from their notice to go to the equalization board.

Where do I pay Colquitt County property tax in person?

Go to the Tax Commissioner's office at 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, any weekday between 8:00am and 4:30pm. A convenience fee from the card company applies to card payments.

What date is Colquitt County property tax normally due?

Usually December 10 for real estate and business personal property. The date printed on your bill is the one to follow, since it can change.

Can I sell a Colquitt County house with a recorded tax lien?

Yes. The lien is paid off from the sale funds at closing. Get a current figure from the commissioner and give it to the title company.

Which Colquitt County office takes homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor's Office takes them. It must receive yours by April 1, and a later filing counts toward the next tax year.

What is the appeal window for a Colquitt County assessment?

The window is 45 days from the date on the notice. Choose the equalization board or an arbitrator, and know that Superior Court is open afterward.

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Where to handle property tax

Columbia County property tax is run by the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division at 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor, Evans, GA 30809. Call 706-261-8299. Hours are 8 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday, except holidays.

That same division takes homestead applications, operates the delinquent tax unit, and posts the county digest and a tax worksheet. Valuation belongs to a separate assessment office. A question about why your house carries the value on the notice does not belong at the commissioner's counter, although staff can send you to the right contact.

  • Bills, payments and payoffs: Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division.
  • Homestead applications: same office in Evans.
  • Delinquent accounts and sheriff's tax sales: Delinquent Tax Division.
  • Mobile home permits: Planning and Zoning in Evans, or city hall in Grovetown or Harlem.

Columbia County in brief

Columbia is a fast-growing suburban county on the Savannah River, part of the Augusta metro area. Grovetown and Harlem are its cities, and Appling, Evans and Martinez are unincorporated communities. Appling is the legal county seat, but county government actually operates in Evans.

The 2020 census counted 156,010 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 169,189 is 8.4% higher. There are 65,264 housing units, and owners hold 78.1% of them. A typical owned home is valued at $305,300 and rent averages $1,409. Those figures describe the county as a whole, not any one street.

How a Columbia County tax bill is built

The county's tax worksheet lays out the steps. Multiply fair market value by 40% to get assessed value, then multiply that by the millage rate to get the tax. Millage is stated in dollars for each thousand of assessed value. It comes from the proposed budget divided by the tax digest, which is the total of all assessments.

Exemptions come off before the rate is applied. The county posts a downloadable tax calculation workbook meant for estimating only, and a change in rates, values or fees changes the final amount. Use it to compare scenarios, then get the official figure from the division.

Online payment goes through the county's pay-tax page, where a card adds a third-party processing fee and an eCheck adds $1.50 per item. With an escrow account, check with your lender before paying so the bill is not paid twice.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Columbia County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemptions

The county offers a regular exemption plus several for age, disability and military service, and each one reduces the assessed value rather than the market value. The Evans office accepts applications all year. To have the exemption count for the current year, file by April 1.

  • Regular homestead (S1): up to $10,000 off assessed value, for state, county and school purposes, excluding bond taxes and city taxes.
  • Age 62 (L3): $40,000 off for county and school, with net income of both spouses not over $15,000.
  • Local school exemption, age 70 (L6): the school tax on the home and up to three adjoining acres, no income limit.
  • Disabled veteran (S5): $126,526 off, with a VA letter showing 100% service-connected, total and permanent disability, refreshed every three years.
  • Total and permanent disability (L5): $40,000 off, with two physician affidavits and the same $15,000 income cap.
  • Surviving spouse of a military member (SS): $126,526 off, and a full exemption for the spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed in the line of duty.

For the application, bring a Georgia driver's license with your current address, the vehicle registration card for Columbia County, a recorded deed, and income returns if the exemption tests income. Any change to the deed, a refinance for example, requires a new application.

The January 1 rule when you sell

Under Georgia law, the person who held title on January 1 owes that year's tax. The county tax office does not split the bill between buyer and seller, because that split is a closing matter. A lien stays in the January 1 owner's name unless proof within 90 days of the due date shows the buyer contractually took the tax.

Two practical steps follow. First, read the proration line on the settlement statement and confirm the title company will pay the county rather than leave it for the buyer to find. Second, if a Columbia County bill is still unpaid at closing, ask the Property Tax Division for the exact payoff for the closing date. The division mails each bill to the owner named in its records, so a seller who has moved should confirm the address on file.

The pay-tax page lets you view the tax on a parcel online, which helps you spot a balance before a buyer's title search does. After closing, tell the Property Tax Division about the sale so your homestead exemption is removed, and expect the buyer to file a fresh application of their own with a recorded deed. A pending sale does not change the bill, so keep paying until the closing office has the payoff in hand.

Delinquent taxes and tax sales

The county starts with a letter or phone call, and if that fails it moves to a levy and a sheriff's tax sale. Most matters are settled without a sale, and the county has one of the highest collection rates in Georgia.

Sheriff's tax sales are public auctions that open at the amount of tax owed, held on the first Tuesday of the month when the office schedules one. The sale notice runs in the Augusta Chronicle legal ads about a month ahead, as well as on the county site.

An owner who is behind should talk to the division before the levy stage. Selling before a sale date is possible, because the payoff is settled from the proceeds at the closing table, but get the numbers in writing first. A cash buyer can close quickly enough to beat a scheduled sale, as long as the title is clear and the payoff is confirmed.

Other rules that touch a sale

Columbia County property tax topics and where to ask
TopicRuleContact
Homestead filingApply by April 1 for the same tax yearProperty Tax Division, Evans
Mobile homesPermit needed from Planning and Zoning or a city hallGovernment Center in Evans
Delinquent taxLevy and sheriff's tax sale if unpaidDelinquent Tax Division
Online paymentCard fee by processor; eCheck $1.50 per itemCounty pay-tax page

Read the due date on your bill, or ask the division. Georgia's usual window to contest a value is 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the notice itself states the deadline for your parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I apply for a Columbia County homestead exemption?

At the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor. Applications are accepted year-round, but the benefit for the current year requires filing by April 1.

Do I need to reapply after refinancing?

Yes. Any change to a deed, a refinance for example, requires a new homestead application.

Is there a Columbia County exemption with no income limit?

Yes. The local school exemption for homeowners 70 or older covers the school tax on the house and up to three contiguous acres, with no income limit.

How often are Columbia County tax sales held?

On the first Tuesday of the month, when the office schedules one. They are sheriff's tax sales run as auctions, and the notice is published in the Augusta Chronicle about a month earlier.

Can I pay Columbia County property tax online?

Yes, through the county's pay-tax page. A credit card carries a third-party fee, an eCheck carries $1.50 per item, and escrow customers should check with their lender first.

Where to take property tax questions

Owners deal with two Newnan offices. For bills and payments, call the Tax Commissioner (87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100) at 770-254-2670. For values and homestead claims, call the Assessor's Office (37 Perry Street) at 770-254-2680.

The commissioner's counter keeps weekday hours of 8am to 4:30pm. Millage is set twice over, once by the county commissioners and once by the school board, and a board appointed through the grand jury hears value disputes. For a deed copy, see the Clerk of Superior Court in the Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, 770-254-2690.

  • Value or exemption question: Assessor's Office.
  • Bill, payoff or lien question: Tax Commissioner.
  • Deed copy: Clerk of Superior Court.

Coweta County for a seller

Southwest of Atlanta in the Georgia Piedmont, Coweta counts as Metro Atlanta. Newnan serves as seat and largest city. The five cities are Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills, the last two reaching into Fulton County.

The county grew from 127,317 people in 2010 to 146,158 in 2020, with 160,240 estimated for July 2025. Owners make up 78.4% of households. A typical owned home is valued at $357,500, and rent averages $1,488 a month. In a market this owner-heavy, a tax line is routine on closing statements.

Tax calendar

Bills go out October 1 and are due December 1, so you get at least 60 days. Should your printed bill show a different date, follow the printed one.

You may drop payment off at the drive-through box, pay online by card (the card company charges a fee), or mail a check postmarked by the due date. A due date that lands on a closed day rolls to the next business day.

Broader Georgia property tax questions can go to the state Department of Revenue, local government services division, at dor.georgia.gov.

  • January 1: ownership and use on this date fix the year's tax.
  • Through April 1: returns, first-year homestead filings and special program applications.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home tax, with a location decal issued after payment.
  • October 1: bills go in the mail.
  • December 1: due date for land, buildings and personal property.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Coweta County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late bills and penalties

Late bills carry monthly interest of prime plus three percentage points, plus a 5% penalty that starts at day 120 and recurs every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded bills under $500 are exempt from the penalty.

About a month after nonpayment the commissioner can file a FiFa lien on the General Execution Docket at the superior court clerk's office. That lien can follow your credit for seven years or longer. Delinquent notices only go out occasionally, so phone for today's balance before mailing a check.

A mobile or manufactured home is riskier to neglect. If the April 1 payment and permit are missed, expect a 10% penalty and possibly a State Court citation or a sale of the home.

Who owes the tax after a sale

Liens go on the January 1 owner. If a bill finds you after the sale, hand it to the buyer. To move the lien, show the commissioner the contract or closing statement within 90 days after the due date.

If the closing prorated the tax, take the settlement statement to the Newnan Station Drive office. Once it is on file, a bill left unpaid produces a lien against the new owner.

Timing matters. October is when bills are mailed, so a spring or summer closing normally comes before that year's bill exists, and the title company has to estimate. Use last year's total from the commissioner as a benchmark and ask the closer how the estimate was built.

One bill covers a full year, including months before the sale, so spell out the tax split in the contract. Then buyer, seller and closer all work from one set of numbers. Bring your latest bill and any assessment notice to closing, and see that the commissioner's payoff appears on the settlement statement. A cash buyer follows the same split, and with no lender appraisal to wait for, the estimate usually gets settled sooner.

Before you sign a listing agreement

Ring the Tax Commissioner, 770-254-2670, and find out what the parcel owes, FiFa included. Homestead exemptions belong to the occupant, so tell the Assessor's Office after closing and let the buyer file a new claim. Gather your last bill, your assessment notice and the settlement statement from your purchase so the closer and the commissioner's office can match the numbers quickly. Read the notice carefully as well. The appeal window is only 45 days, so a notice that lands just before you list needs a quick decision.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Coweta County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals are due 45 days after the assessment notice. File a written appeal on the state's uniform form with the Board of Assessors and say which route you want. You can contest taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Coweta County appeal routes
RouteBest suited toWhat follows
Equalization boardMost homeownersHearing, then Superior Court if needed
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court if needed
ArbitrationOwners holding a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; the ruling is final

On the equalization route, the assessors may revise the value and mail a new notice, and you then have 30 days to appeal that. If they leave the value alone, the appeal advances to a hearing automatically. With arbitration, the assessors have 45 days to acknowledge the appeal, and if they turn down your appraisal they must certify the case to the Clerk of Superior Court.

Exemptions and special programs

To claim homestead, you must have owned the house and lived there on January 1 and get the application in by April 1 of the first year. Later filings take effect the next year. The assessors decide each claim and you can appeal a denial, but homestead cannot be claimed on a second property.

Local exemptions in Coweta replace the state amount whenever they are larger. Ask the assessors what proof they need for age, income or military service. After approval it renews on its own until you move or ownership changes.

  • Deferral: owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less can put tax off until ownership changes or the balance plus interest hits 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural use: qualifying farmland is assessed at 30% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: 10-year or 15-year covenants.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse: preferential assessment, applied for during the first four months of the year it begins.

Anyone buying an enrolled tract should check with the assessors on whether the covenant carries over.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends my Coweta County property tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner, 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan. Mailing is October 1, and the office phone is 770-254-2670.

Is December 1 the due date for every Coweta County bill?

It applies to land, buildings and personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1. Your printed bill shows which date is yours.

Can a hearing officer decide a Coweta County homestead appeal?

No. That route is reserved for the value of non-homestead real property at $1,000,000 or more.

Where can I get a copy of my deed in Coweta County?

Ask the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263, or call 770-254-2690.

Does every unpaid Coweta County bill draw a penalty?

Not a homesteaded bill under $500. Others pick up a 5% penalty at 120 days, again every 120 days, capped at 20%.

Who bills and collects property tax

Two offices handle Crawford County property tax. One of them mails and collects bills. The other decides what each parcel is worth. A seller usually needs to call both.

Find the Tax Commissioner at 640 GA Hwy 128 in Roberta, weekdays 8:15 am to 4:45 pm, holidays excepted, or call (478) 836-3575. Bills for real and personal property, vehicles, mobile homes and timber all come from here. Appeals and name or address changes do not.

The assessors, at (478) 836-2800, take returns, exemption applications and written appeals. A house inside Roberta may also owe city tax, which is collected at Roberta City Hall.

Crawford County land and housing

This is west central Georgia, within the Macon metro area, with the courthouse in Knoxville and the largest town in Roberta. About 325 square miles of land hold roughly 37 people per square mile, so most parcels are rural and many include acreage. If you are selling only part of a tract, ask the assessors how a split is treated.

Estimates for July 2025 show 12,206 residents and 5,388 housing units, and 81.4 percent of homes have their owners living in them. Median home value is $164,100 and rent runs $914 a month. Few households change addresses from one year to the next.

Which office handles which task

Match your question to the right desk before you phone.

Crawford County tax tasks and the office for each
TaskOfficeContact
Pay a current real or personal property billTax Commissioner, Suite 134(478) 836-3575; mail to P.O. Box 634, Roberta, GA 31078
Delinquent amount owedTax CommissionerCall first for the exact payoff before mailing

Move a mobile home into the countyPlanning and Zoning OfficeRelocation permit before registration
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Crawford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

When is Crawford County property tax due?

Real estate is usually due December 20. The bills typically go out in mid-October and carry the name of whoever held title when the year began.

A county may shift that to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments, and interest does not begin until 60 days after the postmark. Check the date on your own bill before you schedule a closing.

  • Late tax accrues interest monthly at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, reset each calendar year from the first weekly Federal Reserve posting.
  • A further 5 percent penalty lands at every 120-day mark past the due date.
  • Once a bill is placed on the General Execution Docket, FiFa charges are added.
  • Mobile homes taxed off-digest fall due May 1 and then draw a 10 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest monthly.

Lenders do not get bills from this office. Owners with escrow should check that the servicer has the figures, and anyone whose mailed copy never showed up can request a duplicate.

How the tax amount is set

Tax is 40 percent of the assessors' fair market value multiplied by the millage rate, with the parcel valued as of January 1. The county commissioners choose one rate and the school board another. The garbage fee appears on the same statement.

A rollback rate is the rate that would collect last year's revenue after values rise. Going above it means three public hearings. Its news section carries the tax digest and a five-year levy history.

Get the millage for your parcel from the Tax Commissioner. Last year's bill is an unreliable guide because both boards can change rates annually.

How to contest your valuation

Appeals go in writing to the Tax Assessors, never the Tax Commissioner. You have 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed, and notices usually arrive in spring.

Filing a return during the first three months of the year lets you put your own value on record. You need not file every year. Because the appeal must be postmarked inside the window, keep a mailing receipt.

If the Board of Assessors leaves the value unchanged, ask the assessors' office what the next level of appeal is and what deadline applies. A seller who gets a spring notice shortly before listing the house should read it closely, since the value feeds that year's bill and a buyer's expectations.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Crawford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions

Homestead is the big one. You can apply year-round, but April 1 closes the digest. To qualify you must own the house, live in it on January 1, claim Georgia as your legal residence and hold title in your own name. Service members must also name Georgia as their home state.

  • Added relief begins at 62, and the applicant must have reached that age by January 1 of the filing year.
  • Disability claims need statements of total disability from two separate sources.
  • A military service exemption is also offered through the assessors.
  • Agricultural, preferential, conservation use, historic and tax-exempt status all run through the same office.

Skipping the application counts as waiving the exemption. An heir who takes over a house should ask the assessors about filing in the new owner's name instead of assuming the old one carries over.

Before you list

Four steps help a Crawford County seller avoid surprises. Phone the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure and ask about any city bill if the house is in Roberta. Check with the assessors on whether your homestead exemption is on file and whether any acreage is enrolled in a special program. Read the spring assessment notice so you know the value a buyer will see. Then put the tax split in writing in the contract.

A cash buyer can skip a lender's appraisal and move faster, but the payoff, the January 1 owner rule and the exemption change at closing all still apply. After the sale, the buyer files for their own exemption.

Unpaid tax before a sale

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff before signing anything. The office tells people mailing overdue payments to phone first, because penalties and execution charges move the total.

The statement is addressed to the January 1 owner, so a seller closing in the fall is the named taxpayer for that year. Put the split in the sale contract and ask the closing agent to carry the payoff into the settlement numbers.

Mobile homes add a step. All taxes must be paid and a current decal displayed before one is moved out of the county.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Crawford County property tax?

In person at 640 GA Hwy 128, Suite 134, in Roberta, or by mail to P.O. Box 634 in the same town. The office takes checks, cash, money orders and credit or debit cards, and online payment is available.

Does Crawford County mail my tax bill to my mortgage company?

No. The office does not bill lenders. If you pay through escrow, make sure the servicer has the amount, and phone (478) 836-3575 for a duplicate if yours never arrived.

Who do I contact to change the owner name on a Crawford County parcel?

The Tax Assessors, at (478) 836-2800. Notices go to the last known address of the January 1 owner, and the commissioner's desk does not process these updates.

Can I still file for homestead in Crawford County after April 1?

You can still turn in the form, but it will not reach that year's digest, because April 1 is the cutoff.

Can I appeal a Crawford County value after the deadline?

A late appeal risks being turned away, because it must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. Keep the notice, note that date, and mail your written appeal to the Tax Assessors well ahead of the last day.

Which offices deal with a Crisp County tax bill?

Crisp County splits the job. A collector's office takes in county and school tax, while appraisal staff in Cordele put the value on each parcel. Elected county commissioners adopt the millage rates that convert a value into a bill.

The collector's website is crispcountytax.com, and the appraisers and commissioners are at crispcounty.com. The county's administrative building is at 210 S. 7th Street in Cordele, and the appraisal staff answer at (229) 276-2635. For counter hours, payment options and your exact balance, call the Crisp County tax commissioner directly.

County commissioners meet in Room 305 of the Government Center every second Tuesday morning at nine. That board approves the budget and fixes the property tax rate, which makes the meeting the place where any argument over the rate happens.

Crisp County in brief

Crisp sits in south central Georgia. The courthouse and the county's one city are both in Cordele. Arabi is a town, and Wenona and Coney are smaller communities.

Population has been sliding. It was 23,439 in 2010 and 20,128 in 2020, and the newest estimate of 19,237 is another 4.4 percent lower. The county has 9,989 housing units and 7,908 households, and owners occupy 55.5 percent of homes. Median owned value is $140,200, with typical rent at $778 monthly.

Values here are modest and new building is light, so many buyers will be local households. Ask the Assessors to show you recent sales nearby. If you are torn between selling and renting the house out, remember how low local rents run.

Property tax dates and rules

Most of the dates that matter to an owner come early in the year, with the bill itself arriving at the end.

Crisp County property tax calendar
TopicRule
Returns of propertyJanuary 1 through April 1, filed with the county tax office
Homestead applicationAny time, up to April 1 of the first year of the exemption
Official bill due dateDecember 20, unless the county adopts December 1, November 15 or installments
Interest grace60 days from the postmark of the bill
Assessment appealPostmarked within 45 days of the notice mailing
Refund claimWithin three years of payment
Mobile home permitWithin 30 days of placement, then January 1 to April 1 yearly

Your bill's printed date governs, since a county may choose an earlier one. Before you set a closing day, confirm the date with the tax commissioner.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Crisp County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead and returns

You may file for homestead whenever you like, but April 1 is the last day for the first year. A recent purchase calls for an early filing so the exemption reaches that year's bill. If you are the seller, expect your exemption to stop at closing. Your buyer files under their own name, and one who files after April 1 waits a year.

Between January 1 and April 1, an owner can also turn in a return at the county tax office giving their own view of value. Nobody is forced to, yet it leaves a written number on file ahead of the assessors' notice, which helps if the value later looks too high.

Late payments and refunds

December 20 is the official due date unless the county picks an earlier day or installments. Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark, though penalties can still land on a late balance, so a seller who is behind should not lean on the grace period. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed today, and if the house is under contract, have it paid from the proceeds.

Tax paid in error can be refunded, but the claim must start within three years of payment, so file the receipt and bill with your closing papers. A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set, and renewal falls between January 1 and April 1 each year.

How to question your assessment

Begin with the notice of assessment. A challenge is directed to the Board of Tax Assessors, not the collector, and must be postmarked within 45 days of the date the notice was sent.

Appraisal staff may visit parcels during the digest year to measure structures, list construction details and photograph the property. If an appraiser visits, ask what changed in the record. Tell the office about repairs, water damage or an unfinished room that lowers value, since the record is built from what the county has on file.

  • Last day to file a return describing your own view of value: April 1.
  • Questions about a review notice: (229) 276-2635.
  • Put the appeal on paper and keep a postmarked copy.
  • A claim for tax paid in error has to begin within three years of the payment.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Crisp County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How the millage process works

County tax rates come from the Board of Commissioners, and school rates from the school board. A county that wants to collect more than the rollback rate must hold public hearings under Georgia law. The Crisp County public notices page carries the current tax digest along with a five-year history of levy.

Before listing, compare that levy history with the bill on your house, since buyers always ask what the yearly tax runs. For figures on your parcel, the Assessors have the value on file and the tax commissioner has the millage.

Selling when you still owe tax

Request a payoff statement from the tax commissioner, and let the settlement agent pay it from the sale proceeds. Settling at closing means the county bill does not trail the house to its new owner. A cash sale works the same way, and with no lender appraisal to wait on, the payoff is often the last thing between you and the closing date.

  • Cities levy their own tax and the city clerk bills it, so a house inside Cordele or Arabi may carry a second bill. Ask whether either city's tax is collected with the county's.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of being set in place, renewed each winter before April 1.
  • A buyer's lender has 90 days to record a long-term security instrument, with intangible tax of $1.50 per $500 of the note, usually collected by the superior court clerk.

An heir selling an inherited Crisp County house should gather the last bill, confirm whether a homestead exemption was on file, and ask the Assessors whether a new application is needed in the heir's name.

Before the closing, assemble a short folder for the settlement agent: your most recent bill, the assessment notice, the payoff statement and, for a mobile home, the location permit. Ask whether any city bill from Cordele or Arabi applies, and keep proof of each payment. A complete folder cuts delays when the title work is finished and the closing date is set.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes Crisp County property tax payments?

The tax commissioner, whose website is crispcountytax.com. Ask that office for counter hours, payment methods and your balance.

What is the deadline to appeal a Crisp County valuation?

Forty-five days after the assessment notice is mailed. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors with a postmark inside that window.

How long is the interest-free window after a Crisp County bill is mailed?

Georgia gives 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, although late balances can still pick up penalties. The official due date is December 20 unless the county has chosen an earlier one.

Is Crisp County growing or shrinking?

Shrinking. Counts fell from 23,439 in 2010 to 20,128 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 19,237.

What is the typical home value in Crisp County?

The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $140,200. Individual sales can land above or below that.

Cash Home Buyers in Georgia

Dawson County tax offices

Property tax in Dawson County runs through two departments in the same courthouse. The Tax Assessor sets values and receives exemption forms. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and disburses all taxes under Georgia law, and also serves as the state's motor vehicle tag and title agent.

The commissioner is at 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, in the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville. The office answers at (706) 344-3520 on weekdays between eight and five. It has its own site at dawsoncountytax.com and takes property tax payments by phone at (706) 701-2576. The assessor is down the hall at Suite 1201, on (706) 344-3590, and runs a separate website with a property search, a sales search and a tax estimator.

Call the commissioner for the due date that applies to your parcel, and ask the assessor about anything to do with value or exemptions.

Dawson County home values and growth

Dawson County is growing fast. The population was 26,798 in 2020 and is estimated at 35,365 for July 2025, a gain of 32.0 percent. Dawsonville is the only city and holds the courthouse. Part of Lake Lanier reaches the southeast corner, and ridges and mountain slopes run along the north and west.

  • Typical value of an owned home (2020 to 2024): $406,700.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,626.
  • Housing units: 14,876, with 11,573 households.
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 78.7 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,069.

At these values, the 40 percent assessment on a Dawson County house makes for a sizable tax base. Lake and mountain views, forest edges and steep lots all change how a house is valued, so read your assessment notice with those features in mind. The estimator on the assessor's website lets you answer a buyer's question about yearly tax with the county's own tool.

Special assessment programs

The assessor offers several programs that lower the value being taxed. Most need a 10-year covenant and an application filed between January 1 and April 1.

Dawson County special assessment programs
ProgramHow the land is taxed
Preferential agriculturalBona fide farm property assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40 percent, with a 10-year commitment
Conservation useAssessed at current use value, 10-year commitment, with savings that can top 50 percent in some cases
Environmentally sensitiveCurrent use value for land kept natural and meeting Department of Natural Resources rules, 10 years
Residential transitionalCurrent use value for homes in areas shifting to other uses, 10-year covenant
TimberStanding timber untaxed until sold or harvested, then taxed at 100 percent of value
Equipment and fixturesAssessed at 40 percent of fair market value

If you are selling acreage under one of these covenants, ask the assessor what happens to the covenant when ownership changes. The commitment runs for ten years, and a buyer should hear about it before the contract is signed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Dawson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exemption and return deadlines

April 1 is the date to remember. Real property returns, personal property returns, conservation use and forest land applications, requests for parcel splits or combinations, and exemptions are all taken from January 1 through April 1. No extension is given for any type of exemption.

  • Regular homestead applications can be accepted year-round, but they must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year.
  • Senior and other specialized exemptions follow the same April 1 deadline.
  • Exemption applications are taken in person only.
  • Once you have an exemption, you do not reapply unless you move to another address.

The county also posts a list of assessment notices that came back undeliverable, as Georgia's O.C.G.A. 48-5-306(c) directs. If you changed addresses or inherited a parcel, check that list on the assessor's website so a missed notice does not cost you the appeal window.

How to appeal a Dawson County valuation

An appeal must be in writing and arrive within 45 days of the assessment notice. Late ones are invalid. The grounds are limited to taxability, uniformity with similar properties and value.

The assessors review the appeal first. If they leave the value alone, a three-person Board of Equalization named by the Grand Jury hears it. A taxpayer or the assessor who disagrees with that result may then go to Superior Court.

Appeal volume has been heavy. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, a county where appeals reach 3 percent of parcels, or 3 percent of the digest's value, gets an extra 180 days to decide them, and Dawson County hit that threshold in 2024. Field appraisers who handle appeals and reviews carry photo identification and drive marked county vehicles. If you have a question about a visit or a notice, call (706) 344-3590.

How the tax is calculated

The levy applies to 40 percent of fair market value, fixed at the start of each year. Millage is set annually, and a mill is a dollar of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value. The money pays for police and fire services, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

Fair market value means the amount a knowledgeable buyer would pay and a willing seller would accept in an arm's-length sale. The assessors use cost, market and income approaches. The market approach compares sales of similar properties, which is why a run of high-priced sales on your road tends to push your value up.

Ask the tax commissioner for the millage that applies to your address, and use the assessor's estimator to test a figure before you compare it with the bill.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Dawson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Request the balance from the tax commissioner before the sale contract is final. Tax is charged to the owner on January 1, so a seller who closes later in the year may hold that year's bill. Write the split into the contract.

  • Mobile home bills carry their own date. They are due April 1.
  • You can pay at the counter in Suite 1222 or on the pay-by-phone line, (706) 701-2576.
  • If the house is under a conservation or agricultural covenant, tell the buyer and the assessor.
  • If an estate is selling, ask the assessor which documents are needed to update the owner and the homestead record.

Get the payoff in writing and route it through the settlement agent so the check goes straight to the commissioner and you keep the receipt. A cash buyer can close faster, but the tax bill and any covenant still have to be sorted out before the deed is recorded.

What to bring when you visit the offices

A short trip saves a second one. Bring the parcel number or the property address, a photo ID, and your latest assessment notice or tax bill. For a homestead filing, remember that applications are taken in person only, so plan to go yourself rather than mail the form.

Visit the commissioner in Suite 1222 for balances, payments and mobile home bills. Visit the assessor in Suite 1201 for values, covenants, exemptions and the list of undeliverable notices. If you are not sure which office owns your question, start with the assessor for anything about value and the commissioner for anything about money owed.

Buyers sometimes ask for a tax estimate during showings. Pull the number from the assessor's estimator ahead of time and keep it with the listing paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Dawson County tax commissioner's office?

It is at 25 Justice Way, Suite 1222, inside the courthouse in downtown Dawsonville. Staff answer weekdays from eight to five at (706) 344-3520.

Can I pay my Dawson County property tax by phone?

Yes. The commissioner's website lists (706) 701-2576 for paying property tax by phone. You can also call the main office at (706) 344-3520 or pay at the counter.

What is the filing deadline for a Dawson County homestead exemption?

April 1. Regular homestead applications can be taken year-round, but one that arrives after April 1 does not count for that tax year, and applications must be made in person.

What is the Dawson County appeal period?

You have 45 days after the assessment notice arrives, and the appeal must be in writing. Late filings are invalid.

What happens to a farm or conservation covenant when I sell?

The commitment runs for 10 years, so ask the assessor how a change of ownership affects it before you list. Tell the buyer about the covenant up front.

Decatur County tax offices in Bainbridge

Two offices in the Bainbridge courthouse split the work. One prepares the digest, mails the bills and takes payment. The other, the assessors, puts a value on every real and personal parcel. Both operate inside the courthouse on West Water Street.

Collection happens on the ground floor of the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Monday to Friday between 8 and 5. Call (229) 248-3021 about property tax, (229) 248-3019 for motor vehicles or (229) 248-3009 for the tag office. Letters go to P.O. Box 246, Bainbridge, and decaturcountytax.com is the office's website. Valuation questions go to (229) 248-3008 or to P.O. Box 1106 in the same city.

Roughly 20,000 property tax bills and 3,300 mobile home bills go out each year. What comes in is sent on to the state, county, schools, library and cities every other week.

Decatur County housing at a glance

The population has been flat lately: 27,842 in 2010, 29,367 in 2020, and an estimate of 29,432 for 2025. Bainbridge holds the courthouse. Attapulgus, Bainbridge and Climax are cities, and Brinson is a town, so check whether your parcel also owes a city bill.

  • Housing units: 13,601, with 10,621 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.1 percent.
  • Typical value of an owned home, 2020 to 2024: $158,800.
  • Typical rent: $838 monthly.
  • Housing permits in 2025: 135.

With a slow-moving market and modest values, a back-tax balance or an out-of-date record can weigh more on a sale here than it would at a higher price point.

Tax due dates and deadlines

Decatur County sets December 20 as the yearly deadline for property tax and April 1 for mobile homes.

Decatur County tax dates
TaskDate or deadline

How to appeal and file forms

Look at the top right corner of the assessment notice. The final appeal day is printed there, 45 days after mailing, and it moves from year to year, so rely on your own paper.

The assessors' office also receives returns for real and personal property and applications for homestead, conservation use, preferential agricultural assessment, forest land conservation use assessment and Freeport. Blank forms are on the Department of Revenue's forms page, and completed ones can go in by email, ordinary mail or the drop box outside the courthouse.

  • Returns and special-use applications: January 1 through April 1.
  • Homestead under Code Section 48-5-44: file once the house is your primary residence, through April 1 of the next year.
  • Property records and parcel data: the county's qPublic site at qpublic.net/ga/decatur.
  • Board sessions: second Tuesday monthly, 8:30 in the morning, Grand Jury Room.

Will an appraiser visit my Decatur County property?

Possibly. State law, O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, lets assessor representatives with proper identification enter property during normal business hours. Reasons include permits that were issued, a return of value, a revaluation of part or all of the county, parcel sales and appeal reviews.

The office uses building permits and other sources to update its records, and appraisers visit where improvements were made or information looks wrong. If you added a room, finished a garage or tore something down, the permit trail may already have reached the assessors. Check what the record shows before a buyer's agent does.

The assessors also assemble the tax digest, the compilation of property values, motor vehicle values, timber values and exemption amounts that goes to the State Revenue Commissioner. A change in your parcel's record flows into that report.

Selling with back tax or a mobile home bill

Only the commissioner can quote a payoff. Phone (229) 248-3021, give the parcel number and your expected closing date, and ask for the number in writing.

  • A mobile home has its own April 1 bill, so check that account separately from any land.
  • Cities in the county levy their own tax, and the city clerk bills it unless the city and county agreed to a single bill. Ask the commissioner whether yours is combined.
  • Refunds for tax wrongly collected must be requested within three years of the payment.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask the assessors which documents they need to update the owner before the bill goes out.

Bills are charged to the owner on January 1 under Georgia's rules, so the sale contract should state who covers the part of the year after closing. Have the settlement agent send the payoff directly to the commissioner and keep the receipt.

Steps before you list

A little groundwork keeps a closing on schedule. First, pull your parcel on the qPublic site and compare the record to the house as it stands today. Second, call the commissioner for a written balance. Third, ask the assessors whether a homestead, conservation or agricultural application is on file and whether it will carry over to the buyer.

If the bill is unpaid when the contract is signed, the title company will want it cleared at closing. A buyer paying cash usually still asks for the same paperwork, though the closing can be quicker because no lender is waiting on a tax certification.

On closing day, the settlement agent should hold the payoff figure and send it straight to the commissioner's office at 112 W. Water St. or by mail to P.O. Box 246. Ask for a receipt that shows the parcel number, and keep it with your closing papers. If the sale happens after the December 20 deadline and the bill is still open, interest and penalties may already be running, so get the current number rather than relying on the amount printed on last month's bill.

If you own a mobile home on the lot, remember it has its own account and its own April 1 date. A buyer's title agent will look for both accounts, so settle them together.

Questions about the value on a parcel or a missing form go to the assessors at (229) 248-3008. Questions about what you owe go to the commissioner. Keeping the two straight avoids being passed back and forth between desks while a buyer waits.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Decatur County property tax in person?

At the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Bainbridge, GA 39817, first floor. The counter runs weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax number is (229) 248-3021.

What is the Decatur County payment deadline?

December 20, with mobile homes due April 1. Confirm against your own bill, since a county may adopt another date.

How many days does a Decatur County owner have to appeal?

Forty-five days counted from the mailing date of the notice. The last filing day is printed in the notice's top right corner.

Does Decatur County have a drop box for tax forms?

Yes. The assessors list a drop box outside the courthouse, along with email and regular mail, as ways to submit forms and applications.

When does the Board of Assessors meet?

On the second Tuesday of each month at 8:30 a.m. in the Grand Jury Room.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a DeKalb County, GA Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in DeKalb County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in DeKalb County?
