DeKalb County offices for value and billing

Two separate offices split the job. The Property Appraisal Department sets what your home is worth. The Tax Commissioner's Office then sends the bill and takes payment, and it has no say over the assessed amount.

The DeKalb County Board of Commissioners adopts the millage rate each July. The Tax Commissioner's central property tax office is staffed weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. at 404-298-4000. Call the Property Appraisal Department at 404-371-0841 about a value or a missing assessment notice.

Cities add their own levies. Atlanta, Brookhaven, Chamblee, Clarkston, Decatur, Doraville, Dunwoody, Lithonia, Pine Lake, Stone Mountain, Stonecrest and Tucker each have local exemption rules, and Avondale does not award local exemptions.

Due dates and penalties

Bills go out in August, and the installment dates are September 30 and November 15. Paying in one lump sum means paying by September 30. If a deadline falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it moves to Monday.

The penalty for a late first or second installment is 5%, and a postmark after the date triggers it. Metered and kiosk postage dates are not accepted as proof, so near a deadline ask the post office to hand-cancel the envelope. Online payments must arrive by midnight on the deadline, Eastern time.

Balances still open 120 days after the deadline pick up a further 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days. Accounts with a balance after December 31 become subject to a lien.

DeKalb County tax year calendar
Step in the tax yearTimingWho handles it
Assessment notice mailedMay; 45 days from the notice date to appealProperty Appraisal
Millage rate setJulyBoard of Commissioners
Homestead application onlineJanuary 1 to mid-JulyTax Commissioner
Bills mailedAugustTax Commissioner
Mailed payments windowAugust 15 to November 15Tax Commissioner
Installments dueSeptember 30 and November 15Tax Commissioner
Lien exposureBalances open after December 31Tax Commissioner

Ways to pay a DeKalb tax bill

Current-year payments can be mailed to DeKalb County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division, P.O. Box 117545, Atlanta, GA 30368-7545. Prior-year payments go to the Delinquent Collections Division, P.O. Box 100001, Decatur, GA 30031-7001. Checks must be in U.S. funds.

  • Phone: 678-501-7995, with no fee for an e-check
  • Online: the county's GovHub payment portal, searchable by parcel ID, address or owner name
  • Card: a 2.31% fee with a $1.50 minimum per transaction; international and commercial cards add 3.95%
  • A returned payment costs 5% of the check with a $30 minimum

Partial payments are accepted, and the first installment must be paid before the second. The portal handles real estate and business personal property accounts only. Mobile home, public utility and heavy equipment accounts go by mail or to a county counter.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your DeKalb County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest a DeKalb County assessment

Read the May assessment notice and count 45 days from the date printed on it. The filing instructions come with the notice. State law lets the appeal rest on value, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemption, filed in writing with the board of assessors.

Georgia offers three tracks: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer for non-homestead property valued above $500,000, or arbitration for value. A taxpayer still unhappy can file a notice of appeal for superior court inside 30 days of the decision, once taxes equal to the last year's amount are paid, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-29 requires.

An unresolved appeal does not stop the bill. DeKalb issues a temporary value, normally the lesser of the last final value or 85 percent of the current value. You can ask in your appeal to be billed at 100 percent instead. Interest applies to appeal differences settled after November 15, as O.C.G.A. 48-5-311(e)(6) provides.

Homestead exemptions

To claim the basic homestead exemption you must occupy the house as your main home on January 1 and hold title. You also need every vehicle registered at that address, a Georgia ID or license showing the property address, income taxes filed from the home, and no homestead claim anywhere else. Applications are not automatic, and neither a lender nor a closing attorney files one for you.

  • Special exemptions exist for owners 62 and older, disabled residents and disabled veteran owners, and several depend on income
  • An applicant must already hold a homestead exemption to add a special one
  • Applications are taken in person year-round and online from January 1 to mid-July
  • A county assessment freeze is available when you apply by April 1, and it does not cover school, city or state taxes

City programs differ. Brookhaven has a $40,000 basic exemption, Chamblee $50,000, and Doraville $10,000 plus a 2.5 mill reduction. Clarkston gives homeowners 65 and older an extra $20,000. Decatur and Stone Mountain take applications at city hall rather than through the county.

Who owes the tax when a house sells mid-year?

Taxes follow the property, and Georgia sets the year-long liability at January 1. Whoever held the parcel on January 1 owes the full year, however soon after the sale closes. The January 1 owner of record gets the mailed bill, and a buyer whose deed is recorded afterward gets one too.

Who actually pays is a contract matter. New owners should check with the closing attorney, mortgage company or escrow agent, or read the closing statement. Unpaid taxes keep accruing against the parcel, and DeKalb does not send bills to mortgage lenders, so an escrow account does not remove your duty to confirm payment.

Before listing, pull your parcel on the payment portal and confirm nothing is open. A parcel with a balance after December 31 can be liened, and the lien, called a FiFa, is the first step toward a tax sale. Sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month in front of the DeKalb County Courthouse, and buyers pay with cash, a bank-issued cashier's check or a wire. Money left over after taxes and costs is held as excess funds until an entitled party claims it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy DeKalb County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Housing context

DeKalb County had an estimated 774,394 people in mid-2025, a 1.3% gain on the April 2020 base, living in 287,239 households. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,979, and those without one $715. Owners on fixed incomes should look at the senior and income-based exemptions.

Closing checklist for DeKalb sellers

Start with the parcel lookup on the payment portal and print the balance. If the first installment is unpaid, pay it before the second. Ask the closing attorney or escrow agent to confirm in writing who covers the part of the year after closing, and keep the receipt for any payment you make.

If you filed for a homestead exemption, the buyer will need to apply on their own for the next year, since nothing carries over automatically. A cash buyer skips the lender's tax certification, but the title search will still show any open balance or lien, so clear it before the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

When is the second DeKalb County property tax installment due?

November 15, shifted to Monday when it lands on a Saturday or Sunday. A late payment carries a 5% penalty if the envelope is not postmarked by the due date.

Which office explains a DeKalb assessed value?

The Property Appraisal Department, at 404-371-0841. The Tax Commissioner's Office, at 404-298-4000, handles billing and has no authority over the value.

Can I pay my DeKalb tax bill in installments?

Yes. The county splits the bill into two installments, due September 30 and November 15, and the first must be paid before the second. Paying everything at once means paying by September 30.

Does the DeKalb homestead exemption apply automatically?

No. You must file an application, and a missed filing waives the exemption for that year under O.C.G.A. 48-5-45(a)(2). You can apply for the following year if you miss the cutoff.

What follows when DeKalb property taxes go unpaid?

Penalties and interest build, a lien can be filed after December 31, and the lien is the first step toward a tax sale. Pay the balance with fees and the lien is marked satisfied.

Dodge County, GA Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Dodge County at a glance

Eastman, the biggest city, doubles as the Dodge County seat, in the middle of Georgia's southern half. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns. Most sellers here have a rural or small-town parcel, and county offices in Eastman handle nearly every step of a sale.

The population was 19,663 in 2025, down 1.7% since April 2020. The county has 8,643 housing units, and builders took out just 5 permits in 2025. About 70.6% of homes are lived in by their owners, the middle home value is $118,100, and median gross rent is $723.

With prices this low, an unpaid tax balance or a missed exemption filing eats a larger share of what you net. Look up the parcel's tax status before listing.

Who to call about Dodge County property tax

The Tax Commissioner is at 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors are at 478-374-8122. County government works out of 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the clerk of courts answers at 478-374-2871.

Across Georgia the split is the same. The commissioner collects money and, in most counties, takes homestead filings. The assessors answer for the appraised value and for appeals. You can pay online through the Tax Payments link on the county website. The cities and towns inside the county have their own numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

A house inside city limits may get a second bill, so ask the county and the city clerk how city tax is collected.

Assessment notices and the appeal window

Assessment notices go out in the mail each summer. Your 45 days to appeal start on the mailing date, so jot that date down the day the envelope shows up. Miss it and that year's value stands until the next notice.

File an appeal by email, by U.S. mail, or through the appeal module on the qPublic site. No notice in your mailbox, or confused by the one you got? Phone the assessors at 478-374-8122.

New, renewal and continuation covenants for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels carry a $30.00 processing fee. If you own farm or timber land, find out from the assessors whether a covenant is recorded before you list.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Dodge County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Appeal options once you file

The statewide appeal form asks you to choose one of three routes. File it with the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors, because the state revenue office cannot change a local value.

Appeal tracks
TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationDisputes over worth, uniform treatment, whether the property is taxable, or a turned-down exemptionAssessors can revise the notice themselves; otherwise a hearing is set and a ruling follows
Hearing officerWorth or uniformity of real property that is not a homestead and is valued above $500,000A ruling, then superior court if the dispute continues
ArbitrationValue onlyYou send in a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment, and a hearing follows within 30 days
  • To take a ruling to superior court, send the assessors written notice inside 30 days of the decision
  • After an appeal is filed, the board sets up a settlement conference and sends notice inside 45 days
  • Superior court waits until you have paid the previous year's amount of tax
  • If the final value lands at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure, you can recover costs and attorney's fees

When Dodge County taxes are due

Unless the county picks something else, bills are due December 20. A county can choose December 1, November 15 or installments instead, and interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill. Go by the date printed on your Dodge bill, and call 478-374-2154 for a replacement if yours is lost.

Late balances can add penalties to the interest. Before closing, ask the tax commissioner for the amount your parcel owes, get it in writing, and hand a copy to the closing agent.

Returns of value are accepted from January 1 through April 1. Owners who paid last year and send nothing in are treated as repeating last year's final value, which is why most homeowners never file one.

Homestead exemption

Dodge County has no local homestead exemption beyond the statewide one. File once the house is your primary residence. To get the benefit in the first year, the application has to be in by April 1.

Skip the application and that year's exemption is gone. The ordinary exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value, which itself is 40 percent of what the house would sell for. Ask which office takes the form so you walk to the right window.

A refund is possible only for tax that was assessed or collected by mistake, and you have three years from payment to claim it. Selling does not earn you a partial-year refund, because who owned the house on January 1 settles who owes the whole year.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Dodge County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Taxes at a Dodge County closing

Because liability sits with the January 1 owner, a fall closing still leaves you holding the whole year's bill. The purchase contract sets the split, and the settlement statement shows each side's share.

Two recorded items come up at closing. The buyer's long-term loan produces a security deed that has to be recorded in the county within 90 days, with an intangible tax that the superior court clerk usually collects. The sale itself brings Georgia's transfer tax, owed by the seller and calculated from the price at the clerk's office. Any county tax lien sits on the general execution docket there, and that is where a title search finds it.

Selling a rural parcel

Listing land or a house outside town? Collect the papers buyers request first: the parcel record from qPublic, an answer from the assessors on any conservation or forest covenant, and a written balance from the tax commissioner.

A cash buyer can often close faster, but the title search still checks for liens on the general execution docket and for unpaid tax. Clearing those items first means nothing stalls the closing at the last minute. Put the payoff letter and the receipt in your closing folder.

Rural sales also turn on a few small details. Confirm the acreage and boundaries on the assessor's map against what your deed says. Find out if a mobile home or outbuilding shares the parcel and whether it was returned for tax. If the parcel lies inside Chauncey, Eastman, Milan, Chester or Rhine, add the city clerk to your list of calls so no second bill turns up after the sale.

Frequently asked questions

Which number reaches Dodge County's tax office?

Reach the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

How long do I have to appeal a Dodge County assessment?

You have 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. Appeals can go in by email, U.S. mail, or the appeal module on the qPublic site.

Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?

No. Only the statewide exemption applies, and owners request it through the county by April 1 of the first benefit year.

When are Dodge County property taxes due?

The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?

Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.

Dooly County in brief

Vienna is the seat of this rural central Georgia county. Lilly, Byromville, Pinehurst, Unadilla and Vienna are cities, and Dooling, Drayton and Findlay are towns. Unadilla is the largest.

About 11,156 people lived here in 2025, a drop of 0.5% from April 2020, spread across 4,906 housing units. Only 22 building permits were issued in 2025. Roughly 64.7% of homes are owner-occupied, and the typical owned home is valued at $107,400, with median gross rent at $758.

Farm, small-town and acreage properties make up nearly every sale, so the Vienna county offices end up handling most of the paperwork.

Tax offices and hours

A seller will deal with three county offices. The first two share 105 W. Cotton Street in Vienna.

Dooly County offices
OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1; mailing address P.O. Box 371229-268-4212Mon to Thu, 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m.; closed Fri
Assessors Office105 W. Cotton Street, Room 2229-268-4719Weekdays, 8 to noon and 1 to 5
Commissioners' Office113 N. Third Street, Room 1229-268-4228Call for hours

Online payment and tag renewal (through Georgia DRIVES) are linked from the commissioner's page. The office is closed Fridays, so schedule payoff requests and counter payments for Monday through Thursday.

Millage rate

The county's 2025 proposal was 17.45 mills. That is 0.445 mills above the no-increase rate of 17.005 mills and would bring in 2.62% more property tax revenue. Hearings took place at the commissioners' office, 113 N. Third Street.

The proposal was only a starting point, so ask the tax commissioner which rate your current bill uses.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and mills are applied to that smaller figure. The county levy is just one line on the bill; school and city rates may be added for your parcel.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Dooly County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest a value

First call the Assessors Office, 229-268-4719. Each year the board mails a notice of assessment, and an owner who rejects the stated fair market value gets 45 days, counted from the mailing date, to file. The postmark has to fall inside that window.

  • You can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption
  • The PT-311A form has you pick equalization board, hearing officer or arbitration
  • Emailing the form works only when the board has adopted a written policy for electronic service
  • Nothing is sent to the state revenue department

Filing instructions come with the notice, so save the envelope or write down the postmark date. If tax was collected by error or illegally, ask for a refund in writing within three years of paying.

Returns and exemptions

Returns of value go to the county tax office between January 1 and April 1. Paid last year and filed nothing? Your value is simply carried over. For homestead, apply once the house is your primary residence and before April 1 of the first benefit year. A missed application forfeits that year.

Only the state exemptions apply, though the commissioner can tell you if anything extra exists. A tax information pamphlet with homestead details is linked from the commissioner's page; request a current copy rather than trusting older numbers.

A freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory is also possible if voters approve it, and you request it from the board of assessors during the return period. It matters to owners of a shop or warehouse, not a typical house.

Mobile homes and vehicles

Mobile homes come with their own paperwork. A location permit from the tax commissioner is due within 30 days of placement and renews every first quarter. If one sits in the county on January 1, it must be returned for taxation by April 1 along with the permit.

  • A mobile home on land you are selling needs its permit and return current
  • Vehicle registration renews with the commissioner in the 30 days ending on the owner's birthday
  • A newly bought vehicle needs registration within 30 days
  • Only the tax commissioner can collect motor vehicle tax

Have the commissioner confirm any mobile home's status ahead of the buyer's lender.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Dooly County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing costs tied to property tax

Georgia charges a full year of property tax to whoever owned the land on January 1. In Dooly County that means a sale in June still leaves the seller holding the bill for the year. The contract can hand a share to the buyer, and the settlement statement is where you verify it.

Two other charges appear when the deed is recorded. The seller pays the real estate transfer tax, and the closing agent computes it from the state schedule. The buyer's mortgage carries an intangible recording tax, and its security instrument must be recorded in the county inside 90 days. County or state tax liens, if any, are posted on the clerk's general execution docket.

Unless the county picks a different date, bills are due December 20, and interest is held off for 60 days after the postmark. Ask the commissioner for a payoff figure and give it to your closing agent.

A short plan for selling a Dooly County property

Begin in Vienna. See the commissioner Monday through Thursday for a written balance, then walk to the assessors' room for the parcel's value, any covenant and each exemption's status. Settle any mobile home account or old permit tied to the land during the same visit.

Hand the written balance to your closing agent so the payoff comes out of the proceeds. A cash buyer can usually close quickly in a county this small, but the title search for liens on the execution docket still happens.

Watch the calendar. The January 1 owner is billed, so a summer closing leaves the year's tax with you unless the contract shifts it. Have your agent or attorney put a proration clause in the contract, then check it against the settlement statement.

An estate sale needs one extra call. Ask the assessors which papers they want in order to change the owner and homestead record, and do it before the sign goes up. A record still showing the former owner can hold up the payoff letter.

Bills: 229-268-4212. Values: 229-268-4719. Keep both numbers handy.

If you are unsure whether a question is about money or value, ask the person at the first desk you reach and let them point you across the hall. Both offices work out of the same building in Vienna, so one trip can cover both.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Dooly County tax office open?

Monday through Thursday from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Friday. Find it at 105 W. Cotton Street, Room 1, Vienna, or call 229-268-4212.

What is the deadline to dispute a Dooly County value?

Forty-five days after the notice went in the mail. File in writing with the county board of tax assessors rather than the state, and call 229-268-4719 with questions.

Does Dooly County have a homestead exemption?

The state exemption is available, and no local add-on applies, so ask the commissioner about anything more. Apply by April 1 of the first year you want it, since a missed application waives that year.

What was Dooly County's proposed 2025 millage rate?

The county proposed 17.45 mills, an increase of 0.445 mills over a no-increase rate of 17.005 mills. Check your current bill with the tax commissioner for the rate in force.

Who owes the tax if my Dooly County house sells midyear?

The person who owned it January 1 is liable for the full year under Georgia law. A contract can pass part to the buyer, so check the proration on the closing statement.

Who handles property tax in Dougherty County

Dougherty County puts collection and valuation under one roof. The Tax Department answers to an appointed tax director, and no elected tax commissioner sits above it. Returns arrive there, and the office collects ad valorem tax for the county government, Albany city government, the school system and the state.

Its bills reach real estate, cars, business equipment, mobile homes and timber. The Board of Assessors works inside the department and assigns each parcel its value. A parcel search runs through qPublic, and the county news page links a short video that walks through it.

  • Value, notice of assessment or appeal: Board of Assessors, 229-431-2130 or DocoAssessor@dougherty.ga.us.
  • County millage rate: voted on by the county commissioners.
  • School millage rate: voted on separately by the school board.
  • Paying a bill, bill dates and a payoff number for a closing: the Tax Department.

The 2026 revaluation

Albany-area owners opened 2026 notices that came out of the county's first full revaluation in over a decade, and plenty of values moved sharply. The county repeated one point: the notice is an assessment and carries no payment due. It shows market value, homestead information and appeal steps. Taxes follow once appeals close and the digest and rates are final.

Commissioners explained that valuation belongs to the assessors, while the commission handles the county budget and its own rate. A bigger value need not mean a proportionally bigger county bill.

House Bill 581 adds a second layer. It limits annual growth in the taxable value of qualifying homesteads for each participating taxing authority, and counties, cities and school districts each had a choice to opt out. The local school board did opt out after public hearings, and the school system says existing homestead exemptions stay in place. SB 33, the HOME Act of 2026, ends the opt-out. The statewide floating exemption then applies from January 1, 2027, with 2026 values as the starting baseline. Ask the Tax Department what that means for your school bill.

The county keeps posting explanations of assessments, appeals, homestead exemptions and the millage-setting process on its website and social media pages.

How a Dougherty County appeal works

The appeal is a written filing to the Board of Assessors, due 45 days after the notice's mailing date. Each notice has its own mailing date, and the clock starts there, so mark it the day the envelope arrives.

An appeal can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it uses a single statewide form. You declare your preferred route on that form, and the route decides who hears the case.

  • The county Board of Equalization.
  • A hearing officer.
  • An arbitrator.

County leaders encouraged owners whose value doubled or tripled to appeal, and the assessors answer questions at 229-431-2130. Useful evidence includes a recent sale of a comparable Albany house, contractor estimates and photos of damage.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Dougherty County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exemptions and special assessments

A homestead exemption goes to people who held title and lived in the house on January 1. Filing is now allowed through the 45-day appeal window as well as the old April 1 deadline. The standard version removes $2,000 from the 40 percent assessed value for county and school tax. An age 65 version removes $4,000 from county tax where household income stays within $10,000 for the prior year, after the retirement income exclusions.

Rural land follows separate rules. The Board of Assessors lists three programs, each requiring an application between January 1 and April 1 and a $25 fee:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment: bona fide farmland is assessed at 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment: qualifying farm, timber, sensitive and transitional residential land is valued by current use.
  • Forest Land Protection Act: an exemption for land used in good faith to produce trees, timber or wood fiber.

Eligible owners are individuals, family farm corporations, estates, trusts and non-profits. They commit to the use for 10 years, and a single owner may enroll no more than 2,000 acres statewide. Check with the Tax Department for any local exemptions Dougherty County adds beyond the state list.

Albany and Dougherty County housing figures

Dougherty County has lost residents since 2010, and renters now outnumber owners. The county covers 326 square miles of land.

Albany and Dougherty County housing profile
Housing measureFigure
Residents counted in 201094,565
Residents estimated for mid-202582,616
Homes and apartments, mid-202540,638
Share of homes lived in by owners (2020 to 2024 survey)45.3%
Middle value of an owned home$134,400
Middle monthly rent$935
Middle household income$49,044

Owners live in fewer than half of occupied homes here, and only 32 building permits were issued in 2025.

Selling a Dougherty County house

Deed and lien searches run through the Clerk of Superior Court. Real estate records can be searched online, and the office sits in the Judicial Building at 225 Pine Avenue, Suite 126, open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday at 229-431-2198. Pull the record on your own parcel before you list so a forgotten lien does not surprise anyone at closing.

Georgia assigns a year's tax to whoever held the property on January 1 and refunds nothing for a partial year. A seller who closes in March still faces a bill covering twelve months, so the purchase contract and settlement statement decide how the cost is divided. A typical 60-day payment window ends December 20, but the Tax Department supplies Dougherty County's actual dates.

Before you list, gather three things:

  • Your parcel number from qPublic and a copy of the 2026 notice.
  • A written balance from the Tax Department that shows any older unpaid years.
  • Your homestead status, which follows the January 1 owner and resident.

Albany houses with deferred repairs, tenants or an open estate sometimes sell as-is for cash, with the tax balance paid out of the proceeds. Liens are filed with the clerk, so confirm the balance and any recorded lien before you sign.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Dougherty County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to expect at closing

On closing day the settlement agent pays the tax balance from your proceeds and sends it to the Tax Department. Ask for the receipt and keep it. If an appeal on your 2026 value is still open, ask the assessors how that affects the bill so you and the buyer agree on the number before the contract is final.

Any homestead exemption you hold stays tied to you as the January 1 resident, so the buyer applies on their own after moving in. Tell the buyer about the floating exemption changes coming from January 1, 2027, since the 2026 value becomes their baseline.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Dougherty County assessment notice ask me to pay?

No. It reports market value, homestead details and appeal steps. Tax is calculated later, once appeals end, the digest is final and the county, city and school rates are set.

How long do I have to appeal in Dougherty County?

Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice, in writing to the Board of Assessors. Each future notice starts its own 45 days.

Which board votes on the millage rate in Dougherty County?

The commissioners vote on the county rate and the school board votes on the school rate. Assessors only determine value.

Is the Dougherty school system in the HB 581 exemption?

It opted out after public hearings and says existing homestead exemptions remain. SB 33 removes that option from January 1, 2027, so ask the Tax Department how it will reach your bill.

Do I still owe the full year's bill after selling in Albany?

Yes, on paper. Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible and gives no partial-year refund. The settlement statement usually splits the cost with the buyer, so get the balance from the Tax Department first.

Douglas County offices that touch your bill

The county splits the work between an appraisal team and an elected collector. Appraisal sets values and handles appeals for the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and takes homestead forms, and the commissioner's website explains the bill, notices, exemptions and the delinquent list.

  • Appraisal Department: write to 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134 or call 770-920-7228. Walk-in filing is on the annex's second floor at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: ground-level office in the Government Annex, open to the public on weekdays with a closure at noon for lunch.
  • Finance Department: publishes millage rate documents and hearing dates.

Field appraisers also canvass neighborhoods. Their visits cover permit follow-up, new construction, additions, remodels, sales, appeals and returns, with measuring and photographing along the way. Each wears a photo badge and drives a marked vehicle.

Assessment notices and the filing deadline

Annual notices usually land between April 15 and July 1, and the 45 days to appeal are counted from the date printed on the notice. The department stresses that it cannot extend that date, and it recommends filing early and keeping your own copy in case the online system misbehaves.

You can post the form, hand it in at the annex, or use the online property search. A dropbox in the parking lot covers evenings. Faxed or emailed forms are turned away, and anyone filing for an owner needs a signed authorization letter.

Request your property record card, plus the comparable sales the county holds, before you commit to an appeal. Boats, aircraft and business equipment get a notice only if the value shifts or the county rejects a return filed in the first quarter.

How an appeal moves from the assessors to court

An appeal advances in stages, and you can stop at whichever stage gives you a fair number. The default track ends before a Board of Equalization seated by the grand jury.

  1. The assessors take a fresh look and mail a written answer, called the 30-day letter, that says whether the value changed.
  2. If the value holds, the file moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. If it drops and you are satisfied, the appeal lapses once the 30 days expire.
  3. If it changes and you still disagree, say so in writing before the 30 days end.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails notice of a hearing date, and the county recommends appearing with your own proof of market value.
  5. After the hearing, either side can take the result to Superior Court within 30 days of the mailing, and the owner pays a $25 filing fee at the court clerk's office.

Other routes open when you file. Arbitration looks at value alone. A hearing officer handles non-homestead parcels valued above $500,000 and rules on value and uniformity. Going to Superior Court directly needs the assessors' agreement and allows every kind of argument. The four grounds for appeal are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Homestead exemptions

The Tax Commissioner takes homestead applications online and at the counter year-round, with April 1 as the cutoff for the cycle in progress. You must be both the owner and a resident as of January 1. Bring a state ID or driver's license plus a vehicle registration carrying the homestead address. A second window opens for the 45 days after a notice.

Exemption types the county offers:

  • The standard homestead exemption.
  • Age 62 and age 65 senior exemptions, plus a 65 fixed-income version with an income requirement.
  • Disability, supported by two kinds of proof or certificates from two doctors, with a Social Security Administration letter.
  • Disabled veteran, shown by a VA statement of service-connected benefits paid at 100 percent on January 1.
  • Surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, and of police officers or firefighters killed on duty.

Douglas is also among the counties with a valuation freeze, meaning a base-year figure holds the taxable value while the owner lives there. The Tax Commissioner can give the base year and the conditions.

Douglas County housing figures

The county has about 720 residents per land square mile across 200 square miles. Growth is 6.9 percent over the 2020 base, to an estimated 154,293 people, and 801 building permits were issued in 2025.

Because about two of every three occupied homes have an owner living in them, an assessment jump reaches many households at once. Set the value on your notice beside nearby sales before choosing to appeal. Owners without a mortgage report typical monthly costs of $507.

Selling and the tax bill

Under Georgia practice, ownership on January 1 fixes who owes for the year, and a later sale returns nothing to the seller. December 20 is the common due date, with a 60-day payment window. Douglas County's bill date and your parcel's balance come from the Tax Commissioner.

Check the commissioner's site for the delinquent list, upcoming tax sales and excess funds, which will show any unpaid earlier year. Liens from county taxes are recorded on the general execution docket at the clerk, and the commissioner can confirm whether your parcel has one.

Dividing a lot before you sell starts with a survey submitted to the Zoning Administrator. After the approved, stamped survey is recorded, new deeds are signed and filed with the clerk, while a deed specialist inside Appraisal updates the tax records. Heirs and delinquent owners sometimes pick a no-repair cash sale, with the tax paid at closing.

Preparing for a sale

Before listing, pull your property record card and read the square footage, bedroom count and condition notes against what the house really has. Errors in the record are a common reason for an inflated value, and a buyer's agent will see the same card.

Next, ask the Tax Commissioner for a written balance and confirm your homestead status. If you applied for a senior or disability exemption, find out whether it carries over to the next owner. It does not follow the house automatically, so the buyer will need to apply on their own.

Finally, give the closing attorney the payoff figure so the tax is paid out of the proceeds. A cash buyer skips the lender's checklist, but the title search still turns up any open balance.

Frequently asked questions

Does Douglas County take an appeal by fax or email?

No. Post it, bring it to the annex or use the online property search. If a representative files, include a letter of authorization.

How long do I have to appeal a Douglas County assessment?

You have 45 days from the date printed on the notice, and the department cannot extend that date. Notices usually arrive between April 15 and July 1.

How much is the Superior Court fee for a Douglas County appeal?

A $25 filing fee goes to the Clerk of Superior Court, and the owner tells the assessors in writing. Owner or assessors can appeal a Board of Equalization decision within 30 days of its mailing.

Where does a Douglas County homestead application go?

To the Tax Commissioner, either online or in person. Bring a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration showing the house address. You need to own and occupy the home on January 1, and April 1 is the usual cutoff.

If I sell in spring, who owes Douglas County's tax for the year?

The person who owned it on January 1 owes for all twelve months, with no partial-year refund from Georgia. Your contract and settlement statement divide the cost with the buyer, so ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance first.

Which Early County office handles what

The Early County Assessor handles valuation, while the tax commissioner handles the bill itself. The county's forms and applications page carries a Tax Commissioner Forms link. The assessor's number is (229) 723-3088. For anything else, the county administration building at 204 Court Square in Blakely answers at (229) 723-4304 on weekdays, closing for lunch at noon and reopening at 1:00 p.m. until 5:00 p.m.

Parcel records are on qPublic under the Early County listing. Payment questions, homestead applications and bill copies go to the commissioner, and appeals and appraised value questions go to the assessor.

  • Appraised value, property record or appeal: the assessor.
  • Bill copy, payment or homestead form: the tax commissioner.
  • Unsure where a form belongs: the administration office in Blakely.

Early County housing and market context

Blakely is the seat. Damascus, Jakin and Arlington are also cities, and Early shares Arlington with Calhoun County. Peanut farming drives much of the local income.

A typical owned home is worth $131,300 among 4,993 housing units, and only 12 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction barely registers. With few new homes competing, a house with clean paperwork and no open tax issues stands out.

The county website also lists a code enforcement page and a code of ordinances on Municode. If your house has sat vacant, look at both, since clearing any open issue first gives a buyer fewer reasons to hesitate.

Appraisal visits and assessment notices

Appraisers may turn up at your parcel in any month. The county's standing notice cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and names the triggers: a return, an appeal, a site improvement permit, a homestead or conservation use application, or a routine review. Keep permit paperwork for any addition you built, since building, electrical and manufactured home permits all reach the county. Staff collect only necessary details and photographs, and they leave a business card at an empty house. A visitor should show photo ID and arrive in a marked vehicle, and a call to the assessor settles any doubt.

Older owners can claim additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead one, with April 1 as the last day to apply. The law behind each exemption controls eligibility.

A redesigned Notice of Assessment under SB 566 lists exemptions and credits, estimates tax savings, names an appeal contact, spells out fair market value and says a homestead application may still be filed inside the 45-day appeal window. It also asks owners who are ineligible for a homestead exemption to say so before the window closes, because the tax and a 50 percent penalty stay with the property.

Appeals and homestead filings

An owner who disputes a value writes to the Early County Assessor within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The statewide appeal form lets you challenge taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and you choose a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator on it.

Nobody at the state level can overrule the local decision makers on one parcel's value, whether that is the assessors, a Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or Superior Court. Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and the homestead exemption comes off that assessed figure before the millage rate applies.

The 2026 HOME Act ends the local opt-out from the HB 581 floating homestead exemption. The statewide version takes effect January 1, 2027 with 2026 values as its baseline, so a 2026 value carries weight beyond one tax year.

A homestead claim requires title and residence on January 1. File with the tax commissioner, or with the assessor in counties that delegate it, by the April 1 return deadline or during the 45-day appeal window. Before filing, do the following:

  • Save the notice and mark its mailing date.
  • Photograph defects and collect repair bids that support a lower value.
  • Request the property record card from the assessor and compare its square footage and condition notes with the house.
  • Ask which local exemptions Early County adds to the state's $2,000 standard exemption.

Early County in numbers

Early is thinly settled, with about 21 residents per square mile across 512.6 square miles of land. The estimated 10,455 residents in mid-2025 are 3.7 percent fewer than the 2020 base, and older adults make up 22.6 percent of the total, which makes the age-based exemptions especially relevant.

An heir or older owner preparing to sell should look for unpaid tax and budget for repairs.

Tax owed at closing

Georgia charges the full year to whoever owned the parcel on January 1 and gives nothing back for a later sale. Most counties allow 60 days to pay with a normal due date of December 20, though local dates vary. The Early County tax commissioner can tell you the billing date and your parcel's balance.

Before signing a sale contract, ask the commissioner for a payoff number and whether any earlier years are still open. Liens issued by the commissioner are dealt with through that office. Filed liens appear on the clerk's general execution docket, so the clerk's index is worth a look as well.

Some Early County owners choose a no-repair cash sale for a house with a worn roof, tenants or back taxes, since the buyer absorbs the repairs and the balance is paid from proceeds.

Documents to have ready

Gather your latest notice of assessment, any permit paperwork for additions, and the homestead approval if you have one. Print the parcel record from qPublic so you can mark errors in square footage or condition.

When you call the assessor at (229) 723-3088, ask for the property record card and whether any exemption on file will end with the sale. When you call the commissioner, ask for the payoff in writing. Give both to the closing attorney so the settlement statement is correct the first time.

If the house is in an estate, ask the assessor which documents are needed before the owner of record can change. Record updates take time, and a payoff letter or homestead change may be held up until the file is complete. Starting that step before you list keeps the closing date from slipping.

Finally, if a mobile or manufactured home sits on the lot, confirm with the commissioner whether it has its own account, and settle it in the same visit as the land.

Frequently asked questions

Which office sets values in Early County?

The Early County Assessor, reachable at (229) 723-3088, sets values and takes appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects.

May Early County appraisers drop by unannounced?

Yes. A standing county notice allows visits all year for returns, appeals, permits, exemption applications or routine review. Staff show photo ID, use a marked vehicle and leave a card at an empty house.

What is the filing window for an Early County assessment appeal?

Forty-five days from the notice's mailing date. Write to the assessor and name your route: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

What is the deadline for an Early County homestead exemption?

April 1 for the current year, or the 45-day appeal window after a notice. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1.

If I sell in spring, is the Early County tax bill still mine?

Yes. The January 1 owner is responsible for the year, and Georgia gives no partial-year refund. Get the balance from the tax commissioner and settle it at closing.

Effingham County at a glance

Effingham sits on the northwest side of metro Savannah. Springfield holds the courthouse, Rincon is the biggest town, and Guyton is the third city. The county counted 64,769 people in 2020 and is estimated at 74,397 as of July 2025, with 212 building permits issued in 2025. Median home value is $276,000, and roughly 78 of every 100 homes are lived in by their owners. Steady growth means buyers are active, and equity tends to build, which makes a clean tax record worth protecting before you list.

Who values your property and who bills it?

Two offices split the work. The Board of Tax Assessors puts a value on each parcel. The Tax Commissioner turns that value into a bill and collects it, and says plainly that it sets neither values nor millage. Rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education.

Effingham County property tax contacts
OfficeHandlesWhere to reach it
Tax AssessorValues, returns, exemptions, appeals802 South Laurel St., Springfield; 912-754-2125; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Tax CommissionerBills, payments, tax sales, tagseffinghamtax.com; phone payments at 470-531-3402
Board of EqualizationHears value appealsMembers appointed by the Grand Jury

The assessors' board meets the first Monday of the month.

The 2026 bill and the county's tax relief

The county advertised a package it calls Project Zero. Bills for tax year 2026 were mailed and posted online after a September 22, 2026 announcement, and homestead property saw about 30 percent in total savings while other property saw about 20 percent. The relief came from four places:

  • The county cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The school district cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The county industrial development authority suspended its 2-mill levy.
  • Qualifying homesteads also receive a state grant.

All of that traces to the Project Camellia land sale. A Local Homeowners Incentive Adjustment Grant could let the county use available funds to erase county tax on qualifying homesteads in 2027, depending on the November 2026 referendum. Check effinghamtax.com for the outcome before you price a 2027 sale, since the bill a buyer inherits may look quite different from yours.

Due dates and penalties

Real estate bills normally come due on November 20. Mobile homes follow a spring schedule, and the commissioner's page gives May 1. Late charges stack up in steps:

  • Interest of one percent per month starts the day after November 20.
  • Every 120 days adds 5 percent, with a cap at 20 percent overall.
  • Once taxes run past 90 days, the commissioner may record a fi. fa. with the court clerk, and credit bureaus can read it.
  • Levy on the property is the last resort, which the office says it would rather avoid.

Bills are addressed to the owner and never to a lender, so anyone with an escrow account should forward theirs to the servicer. Online e-check payment carries a $2 processing fee, noticeably lower than card fees.

How to appeal your assessment

You contest a value by appealing within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. There are two routes, the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and superior court is open after either decision.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, taken as of January 1 each year. The commissioner subtracts exemptions, then multiplies what remains by the millage rate, where one mill equals one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

The assessors accept appeals and waivers only by mail or hand delivery to 802 S. Laurel Street, North Administration Complex. If you hold a no-change notice and would rather skip the hearing, you can submit a waiver until a hearing date is set. A green postcard means an appraiser may visit your area within 60 days under state law. No response is needed.

Homestead exemption

The county publishes its own schedule, and a local amount overrides the state amount whenever it is larger. The main types:

  • Regular (S1): $4,000 for county tax and $2,000 for school tax.
  • Ages 62 to 64, income-tested (S3): $4,000 county and $10,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older (SC): $4,000 county and $12,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older, income-tested (S4): $6,000 county, $20,000 school, and $100 off the sanitation bill.
  • 100 percent disabled veteran (S5) and VA surviving spouse (SS): $101,754.

You qualify by owning and living in the home on January 1, and applications must land by April 1 for that year. The Tax Assessor's office takes them in person and online. Retitling a home to an LLC, renting out part of it, or claiming a second exemption elsewhere can end the exemption, and a double claim can draw a fine of two times the savings for up to three years.

Steps to take before you list

A little preparation keeps the tax side of a sale from stalling. Start with the assessor's office at 912-754-2125 to confirm your exemption is active and your value is what you expect. Then call the commissioner for a written balance. If you pay through an escrow account, ask your servicer what it has paid and when. Bring a copy of your warranty deed to any counter visit. Once those papers are in hand, your listing agent or closing attorney can build the settlement figures without surprises, and a buyer's lender will find no open items to delay approval.

What happens to your tax bill when you sell?

A sale ends the seller's exemption, since the county lists a sold property as grounds for removal, and the buyer applies for a new one. Before you list, ask the commissioner for a written balance covering every open year.

  • Clear old years from the proceeds so no lien rides along with the title.
  • Agree in the contract on who covers the 2026 bill.
  • Stop any lender escrow after payoff.

Years left unpaid can end in a public sale. The commissioner advertised a December 2026 tax sale for Tuesday, December 1, at 804 South Laurel Street between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Property goes for cash or certified funds, as is, with rights of redemption, and the buyer pays for title, transfer, advertising and recording. Parcels drop off the list when an owner pays, so the advertised list changes up to the sale.

A seller facing a sale date can choose a fast cash closing, which skips repairs, showings and lender delays. With a $276,000 median home value there is often real equity to protect, so act before the date, not after it.

Frequently asked questions

When is the regular Effingham County bill due?

November 20 is the usual date. Interest begins the next day at one percent per month. Pay online, by phone at 470-531-3402, or at the commissioner's office.

Who accepts homestead applications in Effingham County?

The Tax Assessor's office does, and it also takes them online. File by April 1 or the exemption starts the following year. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

Is it too late to dispute a 2026 Effingham County value?

Probably. The window runs 45 days from the date printed on each notice, and for most owners that period has ended. File promptly after the next notice, and call 912-754-2125 for the right form.

Does a new Effingham County owner inherit my homestead exemption?

No. The county removes the exemption after a sale, and the new owner applies. Seniors and disabled-veteran filers must also reapply for the higher categories.

What happens at an Effingham County tax sale?

The ex-officio sheriff sells levied parcels at public outcry for cash or certified funds. Sales are as is and subject to redemption rights, and the buyer pays title, transfer, advertising and recording costs.

Elbert County at a glance

Elbert lies in Georgia's northeastern Piedmont along the shore of Lake Richard B. Russell. Elberton is the courthouse town and Bowman is the second city. About 20,072 people lived here in mid-2025, a 2.2 percent gain over 2020. Half of owned homes sit above $142,000, and gross rent is $844 at the median. Owners live in about 71 percent of the homes, and 23.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, the age group that qualifies for the larger exemptions. Builders took out 129 permits in 2025.

Who answers property tax questions?

One office mails and collects the bill. A second office decides what each parcel is worth. Both keep weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • Tax Commissioner: 45 Forest Avenue, Elberton; postal box 603; telephone 706-283-2018.
  • Tax Assessors: 706-283-2008, with parcel lookups through the assessors' web portal.
  • Courthouse records room: 12 Oliver Street, Elberton, where a copy of your warranty deed is available.

Value questions go to the assessors and billing questions go to the commissioner's staff. If a payment check bounces, a third party handles recovery and fee rules apply.

When the Elbert County bill comes due

Elbert's normal deadline for real estate and business personal property is November 15. The state baseline is December 20, and Revenue Department guidance lets a county move that earlier, to December 1 or November 15. Georgia guidance adds a 60-day grace from the postmark before interest runs, and your own bill shows the governing date. After the deadline:

  • Interest keeps accruing month by month.
  • A 5 percent charge lands at each 120-day mark, and the total stops at 20 percent of what is owed.
  • Homestead parcels with a bill under $500 are spared the 5 percent.
  • In the end the office can levy, add fees and sell the parcel.

Mobile and modular homes are billed separately for May 1, and the location permit waits until that year's tax is paid in full. Vehicles are taxed around the owner's birthday.

Yearly property tax calendar

Dates repeat each year. Assessment notices have gone out in late June, with about six weeks to appeal, and the 2026 notices followed that pattern.

Most parcels were not reappraised in 2026. Where a value differs from 2025, the cause is usually a physical change to the property, or the lapse of a value locked in by a 2023 Board of Equalization appeal.

How an Elbert County tax bill is figured

The bill starts with fair market value, takes 40 percent of it as assessed value, subtracts any exemption, and multiplies what is left by the millage rate. One mill means one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of taxable value. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rate each year after estimating what other revenue will cover.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1, with real estate returns going to the assessors. An owner who skips a return is treated by state guidance as having filed the same value as the prior year. A challenge to value moves from the Board of Tax Assessors to either the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then to superior court.

How to appeal an Elbert County value

Read the notice the day it arrives. If the value looks wrong, put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors and keep proof of the mailing date, because the 45 days start on the notice date and not on the day you open the envelope. Say what you think the property is worth and why. Appeals argue value, not the size of the bill. If the assessors hold their number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and superior court sits above both. Owners selling soon sometimes skip an appeal, but a lower value does help the buyer who takes over the bill.

What is different about the newest assessment notice?

Georgia changed the mandated form, and the projected tax bill that used to appear is gone. In its place the notice estimates what you save if the parcel carries a homestead exemption or belongs to one of three agricultural programs.

Last year's millage feeds the savings number, so the true amount may differ. Only a primary residence can carry a homestead exemption. Field appraisers can visit after an appeal, a return, new construction or a Conservation Use filing, and they show photo identification and drive a marked county vehicle. Before listing, read what the notice says about your parcel.

Homestead exemption

You must own and occupy the home on January 1. File before April 1 and the exemption hits that year's bill, while a late filing waits a year. The exemption stays put while you remain in the same house, and a move needs a new application. Turning 62 or 65 opens an extra exemption, so anyone who recently crossed one of those ages should check the account. Freeport and Conservation Use requests go to the assessors.

When you sell, your exemption ends and the buyer files from scratch. Claiming it on two properties is not allowed.

Papers to gather before you list

A short folder saves time later. Pull your latest bill and assessment notice, a copy of the warranty deed from the records room on Oliver Street, and any homestead approval. If a lender pays your tax from escrow, ask the servicer for its payment history. Anyone holding a mobile home on the land should add the May 1 receipt and location permit. Buyers and their lenders tend to ask for these in the first week, and having them ready keeps the sale moving.

Selling acreage in Elbert County

Acreage can be taxed differently from a town lot. Before you describe the land to a buyer, ask the assessors whether any of it sits in Conservation Use, the Forest Land Protection Act or Preferential Assessment, because a sale can change how those parcels are treated and a buyer's lender may ask.

What happens at closing if taxes are open?

Get the commissioner's payoff in writing before closing and hand it to your closing agent. Prior years are cleared first, and the contract divides the current year.

  • Pay each earlier year from the proceeds so nothing stays attached to the house.
  • If November 15 is close to your closing date, put in writing who pays.
  • Mention any mobile home on the land, which is taxed on its own.
  • Tell an escrow lender to close its account after payoff.

A levied parcel can be sold to cover the debt, with fees added along the way, so clear the balance before any sale is advertised. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, though the payoff still comes out of your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Elbert County payment deadline for real estate?

The normal date is November 15, with mobile and modular homes on May 1. Your printed bill shows the date that applies to you.

How long do I have to dispute an Elbert County value?

Count 45 days from the date on your assessment notice, and mail the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors inside that window. Call 706-283-2008 if you cannot find the notice.

How heavy are Elbert County's late charges?

Monthly interest runs, and 5 percent is added every 120 days until the penalties reach 20 percent. Homesteaded property owing less than $500 avoids the 5 percent. Call 706-283-2018 for a balance.

Which office takes an Elbert County homestead application?

Apply with the Tax Assessor's office. Applications need to arrive before April 1, and the home must be yours and occupied on January 1.

Who divides the Elbert County bill between buyer and seller?

The two sides do, through the sales contract. Get the commissioner's payoff figure first, then agree on who covers which months.

Emanuel County at a glance

Emanuel covers 681 square miles of east-central Georgia and holds 23,147 people as of mid-2025. Swainsboro serves as seat and largest city. Housing is inexpensive: owned homes carry a median value of $94,700, rent is $783, and 60.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Builders took out 49 permits in 2025. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,162, and those without one report $424. At those prices, an old tax balance or a roof repair takes a big bite out of a sale, so settle the paperwork early.

Where to go for tax help

Three counters matter. The commissioner handles bills and payoffs, the assessors handle values and exemptions, and the tag office handles vehicles. Use the Moring Street address when you visit the commissioner.

Emanuel County tax offices

Tax Commissioner223 W. Moring St., Suite 136, Swainsboro; mail to P.O. Box 763478-237-3351Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30

The commissioner's information page and the assessors' parcel site hold more detail. Keep your own copies of recorded papers and tax receipts, since replacements take time.

When is Emanuel County property tax due?

Real estate and business equipment generally fall due on December 20. A bill left open can end with the property levied on and sold. Receipts pay for county services, the school board and state government.

Department of Revenue guidance holds off interest for 60 days after the postmark, and penalties can follow on whatever stays unpaid. Dollar figures grow with time, so call the commissioner at 478-237-3351 for your own payoff.

Mobile and modular homes work on a different calendar. A home standing in Emanuel on January 1 needs its return and location permit by May 1, or the owner pays a 10 percent penalty. The office normally mails those bills on January 2.

Returns, values and appeals

Bills print fair market value and, beside it, assessed value, which is 40 percent of that figure. Anyone who bought or altered a parcel should file a real estate return by April 1 with the assessors, while an owner with nothing new may skip it.

  • A required return never filed brings a penalty of 10 percent of the omitted value, with interest on top.
  • Form PT-50P, for business personal property, is an annual April 1 filing.
  • An unhappy owner goes first to the Board of Assessors, and the file passes to the Board of Equalization without a new request if no agreement emerges.
  • Standing timber owes nothing until sold or harvested, when it is taxed at 100 percent of value.

Postmark an appeal within 45 days of the day the notice went out. A refund for tax paid by mistake needs a written claim inside three years. Disagreeing with the value alone does not earn a refund, so use the appeal route for that.

How to challenge a value, step by step

Pull your notice and compare the fair market value to what similar homes nearby have sold for. Write a short letter to the Board of Assessors naming the parcel, the value you believe is right and your reason, and mail it with a postmark inside the 45 days. Keep a copy. If the board and you cannot agree, the file moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. A lower value helps whoever pays the bill next, including your buyer.

Selling a mobile home or business property

Mobile and modular homes run on their own track, so a sale of one means checking that the May 1 return and location permit are current before the buyer takes over. Missing that date costs the owner a 10 percent penalty, and a penalty left open follows the home. Owners of business equipment file Form PT-50P each year by April 1, and a required filing that was never made draws a penalty of 10 percent of the omitted value plus interest. If the parcel carries standing timber, remember it is taxed at full value only when sold or harvested, so tell the buyer what stands on the land.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Emanuel County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead rules before a sale

File with the assessors by April 1. A late application forfeits the current year. The exemption comes off the assessed value first, and only then does the millage rate apply.

The person living in the house on January 1 earns it, which means a buyer cannot inherit yours and files fresh the following year. Not sure yours is active? Call the assessors at 478-237-1222 before listing, and ask what the buyer should bring when applying.

Why the timing of a sale matters

Values are fixed as of January 1, while the bill arrives later in the year and comes due December 20. A house sold in spring can close long before the year's statement exists, so the contract should say who pays and how the share is split. Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark, which gives a buyer who receives the bill after closing a short window. Ask your closing agent to record that arrangement and to hold funds if the amount is still unknown.

What to bring to the office

For a payoff request, bring the parcel number or your latest bill, plus a closing date so the figure stays good through that day. For a homestead or return filing at the assessors, bring a copy of your deed and photo identification. Phone ahead on the commissioner's line, 478-237-3351, since two counters share it. Sellers who live out of town can mail a request to P.O. Box 763, though a visit or call is faster near a closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How to clear taxes before closing

Request a written payoff from the commissioner and pass it to the person handling your closing. Back years are paid first, and the contract decides how the current bill is shared.

  • List every year back to the oldest open bill.
  • Check whether a mobile home or outbuilding is billed separately.
  • Send the commissioner the new owner's mailing address once the deed is recorded.
  • Close any lender escrow after payoff.

A buyer who takes the house as is will price repairs first, and at a $94,700 median value the repair estimate can weigh as much as the tax bill. A cash sale skips the lender appraisal and inspection requests, though the payoff still comes out of your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

By what date must Emanuel County owners pay real estate tax?

December 20 is the general due date. Mobile and modular homes are due by May 1. Confirm the exact date printed on your bill by calling 478-237-3351.

What is the Emanuel County Tax Commissioner's street address?

The main office is at 223 W. Moring St., Suite 136, Swainsboro, and mail goes to P.O. Box 763. The tag office is at 101 South Main Street.

Which office handles Emanuel County homestead filings?

The Tax Assessor at 101 South Main Street, 3rd Floor, takes them, and they must arrive before April 1. Anything later starts with the following year's bill. Call 478-237-1222 with questions.

What is the deadline to appeal an Emanuel County value?

Postmark the appeal within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. The Board of Assessors reviews it first, and an unresolved case goes to the Board of Equalization.

Is an Emanuel County sale possible while taxes remain unpaid?

Yes. The unpaid tax is settled from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff beforehand. An open bill left alone can lead to a levy and a public sale.

Evans County at a glance

Evans is the smallest county in this part of Georgia, with 11,028 residents as of July 2025 and 183 square miles of coastal plain. Claxton holds the courthouse and the most people. Growth since 2020 is 2.3 percent. Owned homes are worth $138,200 at the median, rent is $719, and owners occupy about two of every three homes. The county issued just 25 building permits in 2025, so resales dominate the market. Local businesses are exempt from tax on certain inventory classes, which matches the freeport exemption the assessors describe.

Where the Evans County tax offices are

The commissioner's counter is in Claxton, and the assessor answers on the same county line.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 4 at 201 Freeman Street in Claxton, or by mail at P.O. Box 685; call 912-739-1147 between 8:15 and 4:30 on weekdays.
  • Main county line: 912-739-1141, where option 1 reaches both tax offices. Expect a lunch closing from noon to 1.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

With a small staff, the office would rather receive faxed or emailed paperwork and send answers back, though visitors may still look through records at the counter. Start a payoff request early, because the phones stay busy around the deadline.

What Evans County charges when taxes are late

The late-fee schedule is short. The deadline is December 20. Every month after it adds 1 percent in interest, and a flat 10 percent penalty arrives with day 91.

Evans County due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat happens
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Interest1 percent added every month after the due date
PenaltyOne-time 10 percent after 90 days
Lien (fi. fa.)Filed on the Execution Docket with the court clerk once taxes are past due

A fi. fa. can follow your credit for as long as seven years. The bill is addressed to the owner, since the commissioner cannot tell who holds the mortgage or whether an escrow account pays the tax. Mortgage companies ask for the figures every year, so make sure yours has them.

How assessments and appeals work

Values come from the Board of Tax Assessors. A changed value comes with a notice, and you have 45 days from that notice to object. If the board holds firm, the file moves on its own to the County Board of Equalization, which schedules a hearing. An arbitrator can stand in for that hearing, and superior court sits above both. Only three arguments are accepted:

  • Whether the property is taxable at all.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Whether that value is uniform with similar properties.

Grumbling about the size of the bill does not count, since the bill flows from the millage rate. Mail the appeal early so the postmark lands inside the window. Taxable value is 40 percent of market value.

Exemptions and land programs

Homestead applications are handled at the commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1, and an approved exemption carries forward each year. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. File again if the deed changes hands, if a name is corrected on the deed, or if you move up to another type.

The assessor's page describes a standard $2,000 reduction, a $4,000 reduction for those 65 and up who pass an income test, a school-tax reduction of up to $10,000 starting at age 62, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled service members and certain surviving spouses. Ask the assessors for the current income limits. A deferral program also exists for low-income seniors, and the deferred amount is due when the home changes owners.

Farmland and timber follow separate rules. A Conservation Use filing must reach the assessors by April 1 with a $10 fee, and it commits the land to a qualifying use for ten years. Breaking the covenant can cost double the taxes saved. The deadline for freeport inventory filings is the same April 1.

Before you close on an Evans County sale

Get the commissioner's payoff on paper before the closing table. Older years are cleared first, and the sale contract settles who bears the current bill.

  • Clear any fi. fa. before the title search turns it up.
  • Once the deed is recorded, give the commissioner the buyer's mailing address.
  • With an escrow account, notify your lender after payoff.
  • Hold on to your warranty deed copy; the court clerk can supply recorded ones.

Acreage adds one more step. A buyer who keeps the original use of Conservation Use land can sign the covenant and avoid a penalty, but a change of use inside the ten years triggers all of them.

Why a seller might choose a cash buyer

Someone paying cash and accepting the house as is does not argue over repairs, which helps when a tax bill or lien already sits on the parcel. There is no lender appraisal to wait on, and a fi. fa. can be paid from proceeds at closing. Speed and condition drive the choice, and a cash closing can be scheduled around your move rather than around a bank's calendar. Either way, the commissioner's payoff comes first, so request it as soon as you decide to sell and give your closing agent the figure.

Timeline of an Evans County sale

Early in the year, confirm your homestead is on file, since the January 1 to April 1 window decides the tax year. Through the spring and summer, watch for a notice of changed value and calendar the 45 days. In the fall, the December 20 bill lands, and a contract signed before then should say who pays. At closing, the payoff clears older years first, the deed is recorded, and the buyer's mailing address goes to the commissioner. After closing, your escrow lender needs notice, and the buyer files for a new exemption. Working in that order keeps each step from colliding with the next.

What to ask the offices before listing

Two short calls cover most of what a seller needs. Ask the commissioner for the balance on every year, whether any fi. fa. is recorded, and the current payoff good through your target closing date. Ask the assessors whether your homestead is active, whether any acreage sits in a covenant, and when the next notice is expected. Write down names and dates, and ask for answers by email when the office offers it, since a written record helps if a closing agent questions a figure later. Phones stay busy near December 20, so calling in the spring is easier than calling in the week before a closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When does Evans County expect payment of the annual bill?

The date is December 20. Interest of 1 percent accrues monthly afterward, and the one-time 10 percent penalty comes after 90 days.

Does the Evans County Tax Commissioner mail my bill to the lender?

No. It goes to the owner, since the office has no record of lienholders or escrow arrangements. Lenders ask the office for amounts each year.

What is the window to contest an Evans County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and an unchanged case moves to the Board of Equalization unless you elect arbitration.

What does a fi. fa. mean on an Evans County parcel?

It is a lien the commissioner records with the court clerk when taxes run past due. It can weigh on your credit for up to seven years, so settle it before selling.

Where do Evans County homeowners file for homestead?

At the commissioner's office in Claxton, from January 1 to April 1. Dial 912-739-1141 and press option 1 for questions. An approved exemption renews itself until ownership changes.

Which Fannin County offices handle property tax?

Valuation and billing live in different offices. Assessors decide what each parcel is worth and field exemption forms, and the Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment.

The Tax Commissioner's main office is at 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, Blue Ridge, GA 30513, on the same street as the courthouse. Call (706) 632-2645. The counter opens at 8:30 each weekday, closes at 5:00 Monday through Thursday, and closes at 4:30 on Friday.
