Fannin County tax offices
OfficeWhat it doesContact
Tax CommissionerBills and collects county and school tax400 West Main Street, Suite 103; (706) 632-2645
Tax AssessorsValues property, handles returns and homestead forms(706) 632-5954
Lodging DivisionShort-term rental certificates and lodging tax400 West Main Street, Suite 100; (706) 258-5170
City of Blue RidgeBills its own city taxCity Hall, (706) 632-2091

Fannin County homes and the mountain market

Fannin is a mountain county with a thin settlement pattern. A parcel here is often a few acres on a slope, so access roads, septic systems and well water show up in a buyer's questions early. The county posts ordinances that touch a sale, among them land development, building code enforcement, dilapidated buildings, manufactured homes and trailers, septic installation and short-term rentals. Read the ones that fit your property, and call the building department at (706) 632-8361 about a past permit.

About 26,111 people live in the county as of mid-2025. A typical owned home is valued at $306,600, median gross rent is $900 a month, and 78.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The county counts 19,655 housing units against 11,890 households, so a large share of the stock is not someone's year-round home. That fits the cabin and vacation market and explains why buyers ask about rental history and lodging tax records.

When is Fannin County property tax due?

Check your statement or call the Tax Commissioner for the due date, since Georgia lets each county pick its own. The Department of Revenue calls December 20 the default, with November 15, December 1 and installment billing as local alternatives.

Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark on the statement, and penalties can follow on balances left open. Mobile homes run on their own track: apply for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew it between January 1 and April 1.

Inside Blue Ridge the city sends a second statement. City Hall says notices usually go out in November with a 60-day payment window counted from the postmark, and the mayor and council set the rate from values the county assessors produce. A Blue Ridge address therefore means two bills.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Fannin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Returns and the homestead exemption

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1. Georgia treats silence as agreement: skip a return and last year's value carries forward.

  • Apply for homestead whenever you like during the year; the April 1 cutoff decides which tax year the exemption starts.
  • A missed application is treated as a waiver.
  • Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 before you go in.
  • Commercial and industrial inventory can be exempt under freeport if county voters adopted it; apply with the assessors during the return period.

New buyers should file for homestead after closing and keep a copy of the recorded deed ready. A seller's exemption does not follow the house, so the buyer files a separate application.

How to contest a valuation

Mail the appeal to the Fannin County Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no more than 45 days after the notice date. The notice itself carries the filing instructions.

An appeal challenges the fair market value on the notice. The amount of tax is not a ground. The assessors reread the file, and unresolved cases can reach the Board of Equalization and then Superior Court. Separately, anyone who paid tax that should never have been charged has three years from payment to ask in writing for a refund, and refunds tied to an appealed value are processed automatically once that value is final.

Owners of boats, aircraft or business equipment get a notice when the board rejects their return, and the same 45 days apply.

Short-term rentals when the house is sold

A short-term rental in unincorporated Fannin needs an annual lodging certificate, and a new owner cannot just keep using the seller's. The Lodging Division, at 400 West Main Street, Suite 100, lists the steps on its information page.

  • Complete the short-term rental application packet in full.
  • Email it with a PDF of the warranty deed, and wait until closing is done and the deed is in hand.
  • The county then sets up a portal account and emails instructions.
  • Buy the annual lodging certificate, which covers the current calendar year.
  • Report lodging tax each month, due by the 20th for the prior month's rentals.

An owner who uses Airbnb or VRBO to remit the monthly tax is still the one who enters the reporting amounts. If you sell a rental, give the buyer your recent monthly reports and ask the Lodging Division how the certificate transfers. The rental ordinance has been under revision, so ask the commissioners' office at 400 West Main Street, Suite 110, for the version in force before you advertise a house as a rental.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Fannin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with the tax bill in mind

Get a written payoff from the Fannin County Tax Commissioner before the contract is final, because the closing attorney needs a figure and unpaid balances can pick up interest and penalties.

Spell out in the contract who covers the year's tax: values are set as of January 1, but the statement lands months later. If you hold a mortgage with escrow, tell your servicer about the sale so the escrow refund reaches you. The county also posts five-year tax digest history reports for 2017 through 2026 on its website, which help a buyer see how the levy has moved.

Intangible recording tax on a new mortgage is $1.50 for every $500 of face amount, and the security instrument is recorded within 90 days. If an inherited house has an estate in process, ask the probate court and the tax offices what papers they need before the deed is signed.

What a cash sale skips on a mountain property

A cash buyer does not wait on a lender appraisal, which can be slow on a remote parcel with a steep drive or private well. The tax steps do not go away. You still need the payoff, a clear record of any rental certificate, and the contract language on the year's bill. What drops out is the financing contingency, so the closing date depends on paperwork rather than on a bank's calendar.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the property tax bill in Fannin County?

The Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment, while the Tax Assessors set values. Visit 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, in Blue Ridge, or call (706) 632-2645.

What is the appeal deadline for a Fannin County valuation?

Postmark a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the notice, addressed to the Board of Tax Assessors, and dispute the value shown.

Does the City of Blue Ridge send a separate tax bill?

Yes. City Hall reports November mailings and a 60-day window from the postmark, and it relies on county values.

Can I list my Fannin County cabin as a short-term rental after buying it?

Only after you complete the county's application with the warranty deed and buy the annual lodging certificate. Wait until closing is finished and the deed is secured, then pay lodging tax by the 20th of each month.

How do I stop a homestead exemption from lapsing when I buy a Fannin County house?

Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 for the form. File by April 1 of the first tax year you want covered, since a later application slips to the following year.

Who sends and collects property tax in Fayette County?

Billing sits with the Fayette County Tax Commissioner, and valuation belongs to the Assessors' Office. The assessors issue no tax bills, and billing questions go to 770-461-3652.

The Tax Commissioner works from the county administrative complex at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue in Fayetteville. Suite 110 handles property tax and mobile homes, and Suite 109 handles motor vehicles. The mailing address is P.O. Box 70, Fayetteville, GA 30214. The property tax and mobile home counter keeps weekday hours of eight to five, and a pay-by-phone line, (770) 800-6273, takes payments.

City tax is not billed separately. All city taxes are on the county bill, and the county passes the city share to Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks or Woolsey. For zoning or city service questions, call the city itself, for example Fayetteville at 770.461.6029 or Peachtree City at 770.487.7657.

The Fayette County property tax calendar

Statements go out in the fall, and the commissioner counts the due date as 60 days after the original mailing.

Fayette property tax timeline

Mobile home billsMailed January 1, due on or before April 1, 10 percent penalty after the due date
Real property billsExpected around mid September
DelinquencyAfter November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that is later

Interest accrues once the bill is delinquent. A bill that never arrives does not erase the debt, so call for the balance before the delinquent date. Bills are not sent to a mortgage company unless the lender requests a copy, so give your servicer the lower portion of your bill and include the loan number.

Homestead exemption

An owner who occupies the home on January 1 can claim the regular exemption. It takes $2,000 of assessed value off the school portion and $5,000 off the county portion of the bill. Homestead is limited to one property, which must be your primary residence.

  • File any time of year, but get it complete by April 1 for the current tax year.
  • Filing can run past that date, to the end of the 45-day appeal window on the notice.
  • An approved exemption renews itself at the same address.
  • Someone who qualified for the age 62 exemption must still apply separately when reaching 65.
  • Mobile home residents are not eligible for homestead.

Both the Tax Commissioner and the Assessors' Office may handle forms, so ask which counter takes yours before you go.

Floating homestead exemptions

Fayette voters approved House Bill 1166 in November 2020, an extra homestead exemption that applies to the school board portion of the bill. A similar measure, House Bill 581, was approved by voters in November 2024 and applies to every taxing entity except bonds. The school board opted out of HB 581 in favor of the existing HB 1166 exemption.

Both are floating exemptions, so the amount depends on the gap between the current value and a base year value. Ask the Assessors' Office which base year applies to your parcel. When you sell, buyers who ask what the property tax will be should hear that your bill reflects your own exemption status, and that they need to apply for theirs after closing.

How to dispute a Fayette County value

The appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked inside 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. Notices for commercial and residential property have gone out in late June, and personal property notices in late July, as they did in 2026 (June 23 and July 28).

When the assessors hold their value, the case can move to the equalization board, whose records, notices and decision letters are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court. Superior Court is the next level.

Georgia also permits a written refund claim for tax charged in error, started within three years of the payment date. Filing a return between January 1 and April 1 is how an owner declares an opinion of value, and the commissioner says a return is required in the first full year of ownership and afterward only when the property changes.

Mobile homes and returns

Mobile home owners get their own early bill, mailed January 1 and due on or before April 1, with a 10 percent penalty after that date. Residents of a mobile home cannot claim homestead on it. If you are selling one, confirm the tax is paid and the decal is current, because the buyer will register the home with the commissioner's office and receive a new decal only after payment. For houses, no return is needed in most years once you have filed in the first full year of ownership, unless the property changes. A new addition, a pool or a sold-off lot is the sort of change that calls for a fresh return before April 1.

When property tax goes unpaid

The county sells no tax liens or lien certificates. It runs a single real property sheriff's tax sale a year, with details on the Tax Sales tab of the commissioner's site.

A house carrying back taxes needs a written payoff from the commissioner before closing. Delinquent tax can bring penalties as well as interest, and interest begins after the delinquent date. Title companies check for open tax at closing, and a clean payoff speeds the closing.

Boats, aircraft and business personal property are taxable in whichever county holds them. A seller whose boat sits at a dock in another county gets that bill from the other county.

Fayette County housing at a glance

The July 2025 estimate is 125,156 residents, up 5.0 percent from the 119,193 counted in April 2020. The county holds 47,621 housing units and 44,581 households. Because growth has been steady, buyers often ask what the bill will be, so keep recent tax statements and your exemption approval in one folder.

Steps to take before you sell

Start by confirming with the Assessors' Office that your homestead and any floating exemption are on file. Next, ask the commissioner at 770-461-3652 for a written payoff good through the likely closing date, and check the delinquent date against your closing calendar. Tell your servicer about the sale so escrow is closed and refunded. In the contract, say who pays the current year, since the bill may not exist until fall. After closing, send the buyer's mailing address to the commissioner, and remind the buyer to file for homestead. A cash buyer can close faster, but the payoff and the proration still need to be settled in writing.

Frequently asked questions

When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?

Past November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that falls later. Bills usually arrive around mid September, and interest starts once a balance is delinquent.

Which number reaches the Fayette property tax office?

Dial 770-461-3652 for the Tax Commissioner, at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue, Suite 110, Fayetteville. Value questions go to the Assessors' Office, which issues no bills.

What is the Fayette County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1 is the standard cutoff for the current tax year. Applications can also be taken past that date, until the 45-day appeal window on the notice closes.

Are Fayette County mobile home taxes due on a different date?

Yes. Mobile home statements go out January 1 and come due by April 1, and a 10 percent penalty follows a missed date. New owners register the home with the commissioner's office and receive a decal after payment.

Does Fayette County sell tax liens?

No. Fayette sells neither tax liens nor lien certificates, and it holds one real property sheriff's tax sale a year.

Which Rome offices bill and value Floyd County property?

In Floyd County one office sets values and another collects, and both work out of Rome. The Tax Commissioner is in the Floyd County Historic Courthouse at 5 Government Plaza, Suite 109, Rome, GA 30161, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 26, Rome, GA 30162. For property tax, call (706) 291-5146 or (706) 291-5148 on weekdays between eight and five.

The assessors appraise every real and personal property account in the county and in Rome itself. The Assessor's Office moved to the former Law Enforcement Center at 5 Government Plaza, and its phone is (706) 291-5143.

Tax for the City of Rome is on the county bill. The three rate-setters are the Floyd County Board of Commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Floyd County Board of Education.

Floyd County homes and who owns them

Floyd spreads across 509.81 land square miles, and about 101,378 people lived here in mid-2025. Renters hold a large slice: owners occupy 63.6 percent of homes. A typical owned home is valued at $217,900 and median gross rent is $1,014 a month. The county counts 41,737 housing units and 36,856 households, and issued 330 building permits in 2025. With values near $218,000 and rents just over $1,000, the tax questions below matter to landlords and families selling a parent's house as much as to owner-occupants.

A house in town and a house outside it go through the same assessors but can carry different bills, since the city rate applies only inside Rome. Ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

Due dates and late charges

The usual due date is November 15, with real and personal property statements mailed by September 1.

  • Interest builds monthly once the date passes, and a late penalty reaching 20 percent can be added.
  • Mobile homes get statements by February 1 and owe by April 1; a late payer faces a 10 percent penalty and possibly a citation.
  • For mailed checks the office honors a U.S. Postal Service postmark and rejects metered ones.
  • The office mails to the owner and never to the lender, so pass your copy along if a servicer pays your tax.
  • A bill left open more than 90 days can be answered with a tax fifa, a lien recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court where credit bureaus can read it.

Floyd County holds tax sales in the spring, with listings posted on the Tax Commissioner's website. Ask the office when the next sale schedule is published.

What a Floyd County assessment notice shows

The notice states the current value of the parcel and the estimated millage rates certified by each taxing jurisdiction. The estimated tax on it cannot be the basis for an appeal, since only the value, taxability or uniformity can be argued.

The notice lists four ways to file, and you pick one and must also state a valid opinion of value. Notices returned as undeliverable are posted on a list under Georgia code section 48-5-306(c). Each listed property gets 30 days from the posting date to appeal, and the assessors do not extend that time for an owner who failed to check the list. Anyone who moved, inherited a parcel or changed a mailing address should call the assessors at (706) 291-5143 and confirm the record, so a missed notice does not cost the appeal.

How to challenge your Floyd County value

Send a written appeal to the Floyd County Board of Assessors, 5 Government Plaza, Rome, GA 30161, within a 45-day window that starts on the notice date. One that arrives or is postmarked after the deadline does not count.

Steps after a Floyd County notice of assessment
StepWhat happensTime limit
Written appealFiled with the Board of Assessors along with your own opinion of value45-day window from the notice date
Staff reviewAppraisers raise, lower or keep the value30 days to contest a changed value
Board of EqualizationA three-person panel named by the Grand Jury, serving three-year terms, hears the caseCertified automatically when the value is unchanged
Superior CourtOpen to either side after the board rulesWritten notice to the Board of Assessors

Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization, at the owner's option when the appeal is filed. Grounds are taxability, uniformity, value and denial of homestead. Your letter should carry the map reference from the notice, your chosen method, your estimate of what the value should be, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

Homestead and special programs

Local Floyd exemptions replace the state ones wherever the local amount is bigger. Regular, veteran and elderly homestead exemptions are offered, with an extra exemption at age 62. Go to the Tax Assessor's Office, and carry the warranty deed if this is your first home.

A form can arrive any month, yet an application received after April 1 starts the benefit a year later. After approval it renews on its own until the residence, owner or exemption type changes.

  • A building listed on the Georgia register of historic places may earn preferential assessment, covering the structure, its land and up to two acres around it.
  • Bona fide farm use qualifies for assessment at 30 percent, and conservation use programs ask for a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Timber still standing escapes tax until cut or sold.
  • Manufacturers may qualify for freeport exemption, with applications taken during the return season that ends April 1.

Before signing a contract on land under such a covenant, ask the assessors what the sale does to it.

Selling with the tax bill in mind

Request the balance from the Tax Commissioner and write the year's split into the contract. Values are fixed as of each January 1 and statements generally follow by September 1, so a spring sale can close before the year's bill exists.

The Floyd County Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax office, collects intangible tax on a long-term mortgage, and warranty deed copies come from its deed room at 3 Government Plaza. A mobile home seller should confirm the April 1 tax and decal are current.

Assessment notices are also tied to site visits. The assessors must notify owners before inspecting, as Georgia code section 48-5-264.1 directs, and visits follow a sale or purchase, new construction, an active building permit, a return, an appeal or an exemption application. Appraisers drive marked county vehicles and carry identification.

What a cash sale skips

When a buyer pays cash, there is no lender appraisal and no loan underwriting, so the closing date depends on your paperwork. The tax steps stay the same: get the commissioner's balance, settle older years from proceeds, and agree in the contract on the current bill. For a rental or an inherited house, a fast closing also ends the cycle of monthly interest on a late account.

Frequently asked questions

When are Floyd County property taxes due?

Houses, land and business equipment usually come due November 15, while mobile homes come due April 1.

What is the Floyd County appeal window?

Appeals are written and due within the 45-day window, at 5 Government Plaza in Rome. Late ones are rejected.

What penalty applies to late Floyd County property tax?

Interest accrues monthly after November 15 and a penalty that can reach 20 percent may follow. Continued nonpayment can bring a lien and further collection steps.

Does the City of Rome send its own property tax bill?

No. Taxes for the City of Rome are included on the Floyd County tax bill. The county commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Board of Education each set their own rate.

Where do I get a copy of my Floyd County warranty deed?

The Clerk of Superior Court's deed room, in the new Floyd County Courthouse at 3 Government Plaza in Rome, supplies copies of a warranty deed.

Which Forsyth County offices handle property tax?

Different offices handle valuation and billing. The Board of Assessors sets values and takes exemption and appeal filings, while the Tax Commissioner mails bills and takes payment. Each is independent of the Board of Commissioners and of the other.

  • Board of Assessors: 426 Canton Hwy, Cumming, GA 30040, phone (770) 781-2106.
  • Tax Commissioner: main office at 1092 Tribble Gap Road in Cumming, with a second office at 1950 Sharon Road, Cumming, GA 30041. Phone (770) 781-2110 or email tax@forsythco.com.

Taxable value is 40 percent of market value, and the school board and county commissioners set the millage applied to it. The assessors' site posts the rates, so ask which ones cover your parcel.

The Forsyth County property tax year

January 1 drives everything: value, owner of record and homestead eligibility are all measured on that date.

Forsyth County property tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value, ownership and use are fixed for the tax year
January 1 to April 1Property returns and exemption filings
Late May to JuneAssessment notices go out to real property owners
45 days after mailingLast day to appeal or to apply for homestead from the notice
SeptemberTax Commissioner mails and posts bills

The assessment notice is informational and is not a tax bill. Legislation in 2025 and 2026 removed the estimated taxes and estimated rollback rates from the notice, which now shows the fair market value and the savings from any exemptions you hold.

How to pay, and what if November 15 is a weekend?

Options are forsythcountytax.com (card or e-check), your bank's bill-pay, a check mailed to 1092 Tribble Gap Rd., Cumming, GA 30040, or a visit or drop box at either office. Checks name the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner as payee.

When November 15 falls on a weekend, as it did in 2026, the Tax Commissioner has accepted payments on the next business day without interest. Check the calendar each fall for the same situation.

Bills go to the January 1 owner, and a bill that never arrives still has to be paid. Escrow accounts usually pay through a tax service, yet the county holds the homeowner responsible for making sure the money arrives on time.

Late payment penalties

Taxes unpaid after November 15 are delinquent. Interest runs monthly at the legal rate. On top of that, 5 percent of the unpaid balance is added every 120 days, capping at 20 percent. At 90 days past due the office adds a Fi.Fa. (tax lien) fee of $22.50 on bills under $100 or $32.50 on bills over $100.

  • Partial payments are accepted, though charges keep building on the unpaid part.
  • A 30-day notice of intent goes out before a Fi.Fa. is issued.
  • The clerk's General Execution Docket carries the lien for seven years, and credit reports may pick it up.
  • A bounced check costs $30 or 5 percent of its face, whichever is larger, and the office then wants cash or certified funds.

Continued nonpayment exposes the property to levy and sale. A sale is an auction on a first Tuesday outside the Cumming courthouse, and proceeds above the amount owed are held for the owners as excess funds.

How to appeal a Forsyth County assessment

Counting begins on the day the notice is mailed and runs 45 days. Notices have gone out in late June (June 26 in 2026), and later notices print their own last day.

Appeals can be filed on the county's online property search, by post, or at the assessors' counter at 426 Canton Hwy. Email and fax appeals are no longer accepted, and mailed appeals must be postmarked by the last day shown on the notice. Written appeals should say which process you choose.

  • Board of Equalization, with a later appeal to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, limited to valuation, with an appeal to Superior Court. Fees may apply.
  • Hearing officer, for non-homestead real property and certain high-value personal property, on value and uniformity only.
  • Direct to Superior Court, which needs the Board of Assessors' consent. Fees may apply.

Homestead exemption

Eligibility is set on January 1: you own the house, live there and are a county legal resident, which the county defines through voter or vehicle registration. Nothing happens automatically, so file an application, due April 1 or inside your 45-day appeal window for that year. After approval it carries forward until the deed changes or you stop qualifying.

The standard exemption cuts assessed value by $8,000 for county operations and fire, and by $2,000 for state and school levies. A floating feature freezes your county and fire taxable value at the base year set when you apply, so later increases in value are exempt from those two authorities. School and state taxes still follow current value.

  • Age 65 on or before January 1: full exemption from school general and school bond taxes.
  • Age 62 and up, with income caps: extra school tax relief.
  • Disability and disabled veteran exemptions are listed on the assessors' exemption page.

Standard and 65-plus applications go in online, by notarized mail or in person; the portal is open December through April 1, and notaries at each office are free. Bring a Georgia license or state ID showing the property address, and know the last four digits of your Social Security number.

What happens to the tax bill when you sell?

A sale in the middle of the year leaves the seller's name on the bill, because the county bills the January 1 owner. Either side can email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com and the office will reissue the bill to the buyer, as long as the purchase closed before November 15.

A new name on the deed means the occupant must reapply for homestead with the Board of Assessors. After a death or divorce the new owner applies in person at 426 Canton Hwy.

Past-due tax at closing adds the penalties and fees above to the payoff, so request a figure good through the closing date.

Other filings that could affect a seller

Owners with more than a house on the parcel should look at the extra filings the county runs on its own calendar.

  • Personal property such as boats, aircraft, equipment and business inventory needs a return filed with the Board of Assessors by April 1. Missing it or filing late brings a 10 percent penalty.
  • A mobile home gets its own early bill: sent in January, due April 1, and open to appeal at the Board of Assessors for 45 days after mailing.
  • Specialized assessments cover preferential, historic, residential transitional, conservation use, brownfield and forest land. The Board of Assessors answers questions about each at (770) 781-2106.

A refund of an overpayment is mailed about 14 business days after the payment posts, and it goes to whoever made the latest payment. An overpayment from a tax service goes back to that service rather than to the mortgage company it was paying for.

Forsyth County housing at a glance

Forsyth had 282,805 residents as of July 2025, with 98,879 housing units. Owners occupy 84.4 percent of homes, the median home value for owners is $550,400, and median household income is $143,784. Owning costs a median $2,525 a month with a mortgage and $674 without, and renters pay a median $2,090 in gross rent. At those values, even a small tax error moves real money, so check every figure on your payoff.

November 15. When that date lands on a weekend, the Tax Commissioner has taken payment the next business day without interest, as in 2026.

Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. The last day is printed on your notice, and mailed appeals must be postmarked by then.

By April 1, or during the 45-day window after an assessment notice. You also had to own and occupy the home on January 1.

Interest each month at the legal rate, 5 percent of the balance every 120 days up to a 20 percent cap, and a $22.50 or $32.50 Fi.Fa. fee at 90 days depending on bill size.

Yes, it is the way to get the bill moved. Email the closing statement to tax@forsythco.com, and have the buyer apply for homestead with the Board of Assessors.

Who sends and who values your Franklin County bill

Two Franklin County offices touch your bill. The Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property and approves exemptions. Neither one sets the rate: the county commissioners and the school board do that.

The money pays for county government and the public schools, courts, the jail and law enforcement, county roads and fire protection, public buildings and bridges, and public health and sanitation.

The Tax Commissioner is at 1221 Hull Avenue in Carnesville, the county seat. Mail goes to PO Box 100, Carnesville, GA 30521, and the phone is 706-384-3455. For questions about value, exemptions or returns, call the Tax Assessor at 706-384-4896.

How the amount you owe is calculated

The assessed value is 40 percent of the house's market value. Exemptions come off that figure, and the millage rate is applied to what remains. A mill is $1 for each $1,000. Your bill shows both numbers, so you can check the math line by line.

A buyer, or any owner who changed the property, files form PT-50r with the assessor between January 1 and April 1. Skipping it costs 10 percent of the omitted value plus interest. If nothing changed from last year, no return is needed.

Franklin County tax dates and rates

Franklin County property tax basics
Event or chargeDate or amount
Bills dueNormally November 15
Interest after the due date1 percent per month
Added penalty10 percent, if still unpaid at day 90
Assessment appeal window45 days after the notice

Homesteaded property owing under $500 is spared the 10 percent penalty.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late payment and liens

After November 15 the clock starts. Interest runs at 1 percent a month, and the 10 percent surcharge lands at 90 days. The county then files a fifa, or execution, with the Clerk of Superior Court. Anyone can read it, and credit bureaus may pull it. The tax office has no say over how they use it.

Only full payment of the delinquent taxes releases the lien. If the taxes stay unpaid, the tax commissioner, who also serves as ex-officio sheriff, can levy on the property and auction it. The office calls that a last resort.

If a bill is open when you sell, call 706-384-3455 and ask for the amount owed through your closing date. Give that number to your closing agent so the payoff comes out of your proceeds.

Where does a value dispute go?

The notice carries a date, and your 45 days count from it. The assessors review the value again and send you a decision. If they stand by their number, the Board of Equalization hears the dispute next. After that, Superior Court is open on written notice to the assessors.

Arbitration can replace the equalization hearing. You can raise taxability, value, or uniformity among comparable parcels. You cannot appeal the tax rate itself, since other bodies set it.

Before you file, pull your parcel record and gather recent sales of similar homes nearby. Photos of damage or needed repairs help too.

Exemptions that lower a Franklin County bill

One application with the Tax Assessor starts the exemption, and it renews each year until the owner changes or asks for a different type. Ownership and occupancy count as of January 1. April 1 is the filing deadline. File early and have the assessor confirm the date for your year.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 subtracted from assessed value.
  • Age 65 and older, local exemption: $20,000 against all taxes on the homestead.
  • Age 62 and older, floating exemption: tied to natural increases in value, with an income cap of $30,000.
  • A disabled veteran: $100,896, which a surviving spouse who has not remarried, or minor children, can keep.
  • Deferral program: for homeowners aged 62 or over earning no more than $15,000 gross, payment can wait until the property changes hands or the deferred balance and interest climb to 85 percent of its value.

The assessors make the final call on eligibility. A denied applicant gets notice and an appeal path.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Franklin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Farmland, timber and mobile homes

Qualifying farm property can be assessed at 30 percent rather than 40. Under conservation use, farm and timber land is valued at its current use instead of market value, but the owner signs a covenant to keep it in that use for ten years. File with the assessors by April 1 and pay a $25 recording fee.

Breaking the covenant costs twice the taxes saved. There is no penalty after a death or a condemnation, and one year of savings is owed after a medically shown illness or a foreclosure. A sale does not trigger the penalty when the buyer signs the covenant and keeps the same use.

Standing timber is untaxed until it is cut or sold, then it is valued at 100 percent of market. A mobile or modular home is taxed as personal property each year. Its return and location permit are due by May 1, and the year's tax must be paid first.

Other things the tax office handles

The Tax Commissioner also runs the county tag office in the Court House Annex at 1221 Hull Avenue, open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. Renew a tag in the 30 days leading up to the owner's birthday. A vehicle you just bought must be registered within 30 days. Some private websites charge extra for renewals, so use the Georgia Department of Revenue site.

Tax paid in error can be refunded on a written claim to the board of commissioners made within three years. Refunds rest on errors. A disagreement over value goes through the appeal process instead. Owners of personal property file a PT-50p return every year by April 1, whether or not anything changed.

Older materials may mention a Homeowner's Tax Relief Grant. The state stopped funding that credit after the 2009 tax year, so you will not see it on a current bill.

Tax sales and redemption

Auctions are held on a first Tuesday outside the courthouse. The county advertises each sale in the Franklin County Citizen every week for a month beforehand. Bidding starts at what the parcel owes in taxes, fees and interest.

Redemption stays open for twelve months. The owner, a creditor or another party with an interest can redeem. The price is the buyer's purchase amount, any taxes the buyer paid since, special assessments, and a premium: 20 percent for the first year or portion, then 10 percent for each added year or portion. During that time the buyer cannot take possession, collect rent or improve the property. Take foreclosure questions to an attorney.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling in Franklin County

Franklin County has 25,948 people, up 10.8 percent since April 2020. It holds 11,475 housing units, and owners occupy 77.2 percent of the lived-in ones. The median owner-occupied home is worth $179,000. About 19.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, so the senior exemptions above reach a sizable share of owners.

Before you list, check that your parcel shows no open bill, and confirm which exemptions are on file. A buyer's title search will turn up any execution on record, so clearing one early keeps the closing on schedule. If taxes are owed, a cash sale that closes quickly can pay the balance out of the proceeds and skip the added months of interest.

Frequently asked questions

When must Franklin County taxes be paid?

By November 15 in the usual case. Late bills add 1 percent interest a month, plus a 10 percent penalty at the 90-day mark.

Who explains my Franklin County property value?

The Tax Assessor, 706-384-4896. The Tax Commissioner, 706-384-3455, handles billing and payment only.

How long do Franklin County owners have to contest a value?

Forty-five days from the notice's date. Start with the assessors; the equalization board or arbitration is next, and Superior Court is last.

Does Franklin County give older homeowners a break?

Yes. There is a local $20,000 exemption for homeowners 65 and older, separate state breaks at ages 62 and 65 with income limits, and a deferral option with a $15,000 gross income ceiling.

Can an owner redeem after a Franklin County tax sale?

Yes, for twelve months, by paying the buyer the itemized redemption amount, which carries a 20 percent premium in year one. The tax deed holder gets no possession during that year.

Which Fulton County offices handle my tax bill?

Two offices share the job. The Board of Assessors values the land and buildings. The Tax Commissioner then turns that value into a bill and collects the money.

The Tax Commissioner collects for the county government, the Fulton County and Atlanta school systems, the State of Georgia, and five cities: Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills. If your house sits in another Fulton city, expect that city to run its own bill. Every levy appears on its own line because each body picks its own rate.

A house in dense Sandy Springs and one in rural Chattahoochee Hills can land in very different tax situations, so read the parcel on your own bill before relying on any county average.

Tax office locations and contacts

The Tax Commissioner runs several walk-in centers. Four of them post weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone line is 404-613-6100.

  • Government Center downtown: 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, Atlanta 30303.
  • Maxwell Road center: 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta 30022.
  • North Fulton center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Sandy Springs 30350.
  • South Fulton center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, College Park 30349.
  • Greenbriar Mall center: 2841 Greenbriar Parkway, Suite 124, Atlanta 30331.

For valuation or exemption questions, the Board of Assessors takes calls at 404-612-6440 and email at boa@fultoncountyga.gov, with its main office at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018. You can look up and pay a bill at fultoncountytaxes.org, and assessment notices are posted at fultonassessor.org.

Due dates, bills and late charges

Dates shift from year to year. For 2026, notices of assessment appeared online June 19 and bills went out August 15. The state had not yet certified the digest, so the county asked the Superior Court of Fulton County for a temporary collection order and billed at the 2025 millage rates. A revised bill or a refund follows only when final rates differ from the temporary ones.

How to appeal your assessment

Your appeal window is 45 days from the date stamped on the notice. Only the assessed value can be challenged, because the estimated tax amount is off limits.

You can submit online at fultonassessor.org, mail it in, or hand it over at a Board of Assessors office. The filing form asks you to pick among three routes: a Board of Equalization hearing, arbitration that is non-binding and covers valuation alone, or a Hearing Officer. Arbitration and the officer route may involve fees. Plan on several months, and keep paying any temporary bill that arrives meanwhile, because skipped payments add penalties.

You can raise taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The state revenue agency cannot overrule a local board on a single appraisal.

What to bring to the assessors

Whether you call the Board of Assessors or file online, have your parcel number and the notice in front of you. Add recent sales of similar houses nearby, photos of any damage or deferred repairs, and a repair estimate if the house needs work. A buyer's inspection report can also show a condition problem the county could not see from the street.

Write down the notice date as soon as it arrives. Everything else in the process, including the choice among equalization, arbitration and a Hearing Officer, runs from that date, and the three routes differ in cost and speed. Ask which one fits a dispute over value alone before you commit.

Homestead exemption

A homestead exemption knocks down the taxable value of the house where you live. Georgia's baseline exemption is $2,000 of assessed value, and many counties stack larger ones on top.

Fulton added school-tax exemptions in 2026 with no income test:

  • Fulton County School District: 25% of assessed value is exempt once the owner is 65 by January 1, and 50% once the owner is 70.
  • To qualify there, you must have held a homestead exemption in that district for at least 5 of the last 6 years.
  • Atlanta Public Schools district: up to $50,000 comes off assessed value when the owner turned 65 by January 1, and it can be paired with other APS exemptions.

These apply to school levies only. Owners who already have a basic exemption and fit the new criteria get the discount applied without refiling. If you did not own on January 1, apply the next year. An owner who qualifies but misses April 1 may be able to apply during the appeal period.

Settling the tax bill when you sell

The owner on January 1 carries the whole year's tax. Georgia gives no partial refund when someone sells and moves, so any split with the buyer comes from the contract language.

The state's formula is (assessed value minus $2,000) times the millage rate, with assessed value fixed at 40% of fair market value. Fulton's bill breaks the county, school and city rates apart, so check each line.

  1. Search your parcel on the county tax site and confirm nothing is overdue.
  2. If money is owed, ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff amount.
  3. Hand the payoff to whoever prepares your settlement statement.

County tax liens go on the clerk's general execution docket, and unpaid taxes are best cleared before a sale. A cash sale still runs through a title search, so the payoff is handled the same way.

The Fulton County housing market

Fulton County has 1,098,791 residents and 534,663 housing units across 526.70 square miles of land. Owners live in 54.3% of the county's homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $458,800. Median gross rent is $1,732.

With renters in about 46% of homes, tenant-occupied houses and properties needing work are everyday cases in Fulton, and each changes the timing of a sale. Builders pulled 9,660 permits in 2025.

Frequently asked questions

When does Fulton County collect property tax?

The dates change by year and by jurisdiction. In 2026 the City of Atlanta's share was due September 30 and everything else, including county and school levies, was due October 15. Your own bill prints the date, and the Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100 can confirm it.

What happens if I pay Fulton County tax late?

Interest begins the next day and runs until you pay. A 5% penalty lands on day 120, and another 5% every 120 days after, up to 20%. The office takes partial payments, though interest continues on whatever principal remains.

Can the person who bought my house still appeal the value?

Only the owner named on the notice can appeal, and the notice date starts a 45-day clock. If you sell before the next notice, ask your settlement agent who files for that year.

Does the seller or buyer pay Fulton County tax at closing?

The contract divides it. The January 1 owner carries the full year, and a seller who leaves mid-year gets no state refund. The settlement statement shows how your deal handled the split.

How do I get a homestead exemption in Fulton County?

Apply with the Board of Assessors. April 1 is the normal cutoff, and a second window opens during the 45-day appeal period. Anyone who bought after January 1 files for the following year. Call 404-612-6440 to confirm your case.

If you are processing a vehicle title, arrive by 4:30pm. The office's tax website lets owners search a parcel and pay property tax online.

The tax commissioner collects both county and county school taxes. City taxes are different: a municipal government bills its own tax through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed to send one combined bill. Owners inside Ellijay or East Ellijay should ask both the county office and city hall what they owe.

Selling a house in Gilmer County

Gilmer County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia. Ellijay and East Ellijay are the incorporated cities. The county has 33,894 people, 8.1 percent more than in 2020. Housing units total 19,380, and owners occupy 80.7 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $314,000. The average commute runs 28.9 minutes, so buyers weigh distance and terrain. Expect questions about road access and the lot's slope.

Which due date will my bill show?

Read the due date on the bill itself, because Georgia lets each county pick one. The state default for ad valorem tax is December 20, and a local governing authority may move it to December 1 or November 15 or use installment billing. After the bill is postmarked, the taxpayer gets 60 days before interest accrues.

If your valuation looks too high

Start with the yearly notice of assessment and read the appeal instructions printed on it. The notice has to explain how to appeal. Call the Gilmer County assessors' office with questions about comparable sales, property record errors or what happens after a board decision. Gather these items before you call:

  • Your parcel number, found on the bill or notice.
  • Photos or invoices that show damage, a failed septic system or other condition problems.
  • Recent sale prices of similar homes nearby.
  • The postmark date on the notice envelope, if you kept it.

Exemptions that can lower the bill

Georgia requires every county to offer certain homestead exemptions, and some counties add larger local ones. Some counties take the application at the tax office and others at the assessors, so confirm with Gilmer's staff where yours is filed. Failure to apply counts as a waiver, so a new occupant should file before the cutoff arrives.

Freeport exemptions on commercial and industrial inventory exist only where voters adopted them and are filed with the assessors. An owner of farmland or forest should ask the assessors whether a preferential assessment such as conservation use applies and which form to use.

Yearly filings that matter at sale time

A few chores repeat each year. Confirm details with the Ellijay office.

  • An owner who returned or paid tax last year and skips the return this year is treated as having returned the same property at last year's final value.
  • A refund request for tax that was assessed or collected wrongly has a three year window, though an appealed assessment is refunded right away once the final value is set.
  • Vehicle owners renew the tag with the tax commissioner during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.
  • A mobile home on the January 1 list must be returned by April 1.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid taxes can collect interest after the 60 day window and may also accrue penalties. The tax commissioner is the person to ask about any balance, an execution or older years owed, at (706) 635-4762.

Get a payoff number before accepting an offer. Open tax is paid at closing from the proceeds, so a low offer on a house with several years owed may leave less cash than it appears. A mobile home is returned to the tax commissioner by April 1 each year, so a seller of one should ask whether the home and the land sit under separate accounts.

Steps before you list in Ellijay

Work through these in order and the closing is less likely to stall.

  2. If you live inside Ellijay or East Ellijay, make a second call to city hall, since the city may bill separately.
  3. Find your latest assessment notice and note its mailing date, in case a 45 day appeal is still open.
  4. Check that your homestead exemption is on file, and ask where Gilmer takes the application.
  5. If a mobile home sits on the land, confirm its return and permit are current.

Buyers in the mountains often ask about septic, well and road access, so have those records ready as well. A clear tax record means one less item for a buyer's lender or attorney to chase.

How closing works when tax is owed

Unpaid tax shows up in the title work, so the closing agent asks the Ellijay office for the balance and settles it at the table. Deeds go on record with the superior court clerk. Long-term notes secured by real estate carry an intangible recording tax of $1.50 per $500 (or part of $500) of face value, collected by the clerk in most counties and by the tax commissioner in others. Ask in Ellijay which office takes it here.

Closing costs and who pays them are set by the contract, so read that section before signing. A written cash offer lets you compare a quick sale against a listing that could sit through a mountain winter.

At 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540. The office answers at (706) 635-4762 on weekdays from 8:30am to 5pm.

What is the state's default due date for Georgia property tax?

December 20 is the statewide default. A county can set it earlier, so look at the date on your own Gilmer County bill.

Do I have 45 days or 60 days?

They measure different things. Forty-five days is the appeal clock that starts when the assessment notice is mailed, and sixty days is the grace period after a tax bill is postmarked.

What is Gilmer County's median home value?

The 2020 to 2024 median for an owner-occupied home is $314,000. Your own value is the one printed on your assessment notice.

Can I apply for homestead exemption after April 1?

The state rule runs through April 1 of the first year, and not applying counts as a waiver. Ask the Gilmer office what it will accept after that.

Whom to call about a Glynn County tax bill

The job is divided between two offices. The Tax Commissioner sends bills and takes payments at 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, phone 912-554-7000, and its counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30. The Property Appraisal Office, Suite 101 in the same building at 912-554-7093, sets values and answers exemption and appeal questions from 8:30 to 5:00 each weekday.

The tax commissioner's page lists the office's duties as billing, collecting and distributing ad valorem and title ad valorem taxes, holding delinquent tax sales and preparing the yearly digest. If you are selling, call the tax side for balances, liens and split bills, and the appraisal side for anything about value or a missing exemption.

Selling on the Georgia coast

Glynn County covers the southeast Georgia coast, with Brunswick as the county seat. Its Sea Islands include Jekyll Island, St. Simons Island and Sea Island. The county has 87,599 residents, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 census count, and 45,747 housing units. Owners occupy 66.7 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $301,300. Median household income is $69,799, and builders pulled 448 permits during 2025.

Brunswick is the one incorporated city. A house on St. Simons or on a mainland road outside the city is therefore taxed through the county. Ask the tax commissioner whether your parcel carries any extra district charge.

When Glynn County bills go out and come due

Glynn sends one yearly bill covering land, buildings and business personal property. The 2026 bills were mailed September 17, appeared online September 18, and are due November 17, 2026. The schedule can shift depending on when the state accepts the digest.

Glynn County tax year, from January valuation to the autumn bill
WhenWhat happens

What an overdue bill costs

Waiting costs interest first. It starts the day after the due date, is figured monthly, and follows a rate set at the federal level. On top of that sits a 5 percent charge on the unpaid principal for each 120 day period, topping out at 20 percent of the bill. Levy fees begin only after the collection process starts.

  • The tax commissioner sends a written notice after the payment deadline passes.
  • Thirty days later, with no payment, a Fi.Fa. (execution) is issued against the owner and the parcel. The issuance fee is $13.00.
  • The execution is then recorded on the general execution docket kept by the superior court clerk.
  • Money received is applied to the oldest year owed, and partial payments are possible only through the online portal.

If you are behind and plan to list, request a payoff figure first. An execution on record has to be satisfied before a buyer can take clean title.

Homestead exemption and appeals

File the homestead application by April 1. You can apply at any point after the house becomes your primary residence, through April 1 of the year you first want the benefit, and a missed application is treated as a waiver. The appraisal office can tell you which local exemptions fit your address and which papers it wants to see.

A challenge to value starts with your annual assessment notice. The appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing and sent to the assessors' board. Glynn's calendar puts that stretch in June and July. Separately, a claim for tax that was assessed or collected in error has to be started within three years after the payment.

Getting ready to list

A short list of calls and documents keeps the sale on track. Ask the Tax Commissioner at 912-554-7000 whether your bill for the year has been issued and paid, and whether any older year or execution sits on the parcel. Ask the Property Appraisal Office at 912-554-7093 to confirm which exemptions are on file and whether an appeal is still open.

Gather the assessment notice, your latest bill and any payment receipt. Buyers on the coast often ask about carrying costs, so having the actual bill ready answers that quickly. If you hold a mobile home, remember its bill is mailed in January and always due April 1, separate from the land.

Where and how to pay

The office takes payments online, by mail, at the counter and in drop boxes at the front and back of the Harold Pate building. An online card payment adds a service fee of 2.95 percent, never less than $2.50, and an electronic check adds $1.50. Those fees go to the payment vendor and card companies, since the office keeps none of them. Mail checks to Glynn County Tax Commissioner, 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, GA 31520.

Write these on or enclose them with a mailed payment:

  • The parcel number or bill number.
  • The property address.
  • A current phone number.
  • The payment coupon or a copy of the bill, and a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

The bill follows the January 1 owner. A separate bill goes to a new owner around the same time or late in the year, and the obligation stays with whoever owns the parcel at that point. Who reimburses whom comes from the contract. Lenders do not get copies, so a borrower with an escrow account should ask the servicer to confirm it received the bill.

Who settles the tax bill when a house sells?

Whoever runs the closing requests the open balance from the tax commissioner, and unpaid tax is deducted from what the seller receives. Because the bill is built on the January 1 owner, a sale partway through the year normally needs a proration written into the contract. Ask whether the bill for your sale year has been issued yet, and keep the receipt from any payment so the closing agent can match it to the parcel.

November 17, 2026. The county mailed bills on September 17 and posted them online on September 18, 2026.

Count 45 days from the mailing date shown on your assessment notice. Notices go out in May and June, so the window falls in June and July.

No. The tax commissioner does not send bills directly to mortgage companies. A borrower who pays through escrow should confirm with the servicer that the bill arrived.

Are installment payments allowed on Glynn County property tax?

Only partial payments, and only online. Georgia does not allow increment payments on current year taxes before the digest is accepted and a bill exists.

Monthly interest plus a 5 percent penalty on the past due principal every 120 days, capped at 20 percent. Levy fees are added once that process begins.

Who sends and collects the bill

The elected Tax Commissioner does both jobs. The office mails roughly 28,000 property tax bills a year and collects the county, county Board of Education and state property taxes. It also takes exemption applications, issues executions against delinquent taxpayers and sells vehicle tags.

Walk-in service is on the ground level of Government Plaza at 215 North Wall Street, Calhoun, GA 30701. Call 706-629-9242 on weekdays between 8:30 am and 5 pm. Mailed payments go to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. Enclose a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

Selling a house in Gordon County

Gordon County has 61,701 residents, up 7.2 percent since 2020. Of its 24,859 housing units, owners occupy 73.9 percent, and the median value of an owned home is $222,900. Median household income is $63,650, and 289 building permits were pulled in 2025.

Interstate 75 runs through the middle of the county, so commute distance matters to buyers. Manufacturing is the main source of local jobs. Cities are Calhoun, Fairmount and Plainville, and Resaca is a town.

When Gordon County property tax bills are due

The state default is December 20, but a county can pick a different date, so trust the one on your own bill. For 2026 the county mailed bills before October 31 and set the due date on or before December 31. The county also set a lower rate for 2026.

How payments and balances work

A property may be under appeal even when the website does not show it. Call 706-629-9242 for the most accurate balance before closing, and get the payoff in writing for your closing agent. Staff can tell you whether a parcel has more than one year outstanding.

With about 28,000 bills going out, comparing your value with neighbors' is worth the time.

  • Keep the notice envelope, because the mailing date starts the clock.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses and any contractor repair estimates.
  • Ask the assessors' office which forms and evidence it prefers.
  • Ask the tax commissioner how an appealed parcel appears on the bill before you pay.

Exemptions and filing dates

In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes exemption applications. File once the house becomes your primary residence; April 1 closes the first year you want the benefit, and a skipped application counts as a waiver. The return window runs January 1 through April 1. Skip it after returning or paying last year, and the county treats the property as filed at last year's final value.

Vehicle and mobile home paperwork also runs through this office, which issues county and city mobile home decals and transfers vehicle titles. If you are moving a mobile home off the lot, ask what must be settled first.

  5. If the property includes a mobile home, ask whether the home and the land sit on separate accounts and which decal paperwork must be finished first.

None of this requires a lawyer, though your closing attorney will want the paperwork in hand before the contract date. A buyer's lender will order a title search that picks up any execution, so a clean record means fewer surprises late in the process.

City taxes and school districts

A city can levy a separate tax and bill it through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed on one combined bill. If you live in Calhoun, Fairmount, Plainville or Resaca, find out how many bills to expect.

Calhoun also runs its own city school system, so a home inside city limits may sit in a different district than one served by the county system. Ask the tax commissioner which school levy applies to your parcel before you quote a monthly cost to a buyer.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid balances can pick up interest after the 60 days that follow a bill's postmark, and penalties may be added on top. The tax commissioner issues executions against delinquent taxpayers, and a recorded execution stays on the title until it is paid. If tax was wrongly assessed or collected, you have three years from the payment to ask for a refund.

If you owe, ask for the payoff in writing, hand it to the closing attorney, and expect the title company to settle it from the sale money. A cash buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal or underwriting, so the closing date depends mostly on title work and the tax payoff. Use the county's online payment site, or mail a check to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. The office is at 215 North Wall Street in Calhoun and takes calls at 706-629-9242.

How much did Gordon County lower its tax rate for 2026?

The 2026 rate is 7.7 mills, down from 9.042 mills in 2024 and 2025. The last lower rate was in 2002.

Does Gordon County charge extra for card payments?

Yes. Credit card transactions carry a 2.50 percent convenience fee, charged by the processor. A mailed check avoids it.

The tax commissioner's office, at 706-629-9242. A parcel may be under appeal without the website showing it, so call before closing.

By when must a Gordon County homeowner file for homestead exemption?

April 1 of the first year the owner wants it, and skipping the application is a waiver. In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes the applications.

45 days from the mailing date. Postmark your letter inside that period, address it to the Board of Tax Assessors on state form PT-311A, and name your route.

The state's standard $2,000 exemption applies. Because of the county's 2025 plan to opt out of the base year freeze, ask the assessor which rules cover your home now.

The January 1 owner owes it, and no part of the year is refunded. Your contract and settlement statement set the split, and the commissioner can confirm the amount before closing.

Which Greene County office takes which tax question?

Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro, and three other bodies shape the bill. The county commissioners and the school board each levy a rate to fund their own budgets. A Board of Equalization named by the grand jury hears disputes over the assessors' values.

The commissioner handles bills and collections for land and buildings, business property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues vehicle tags as the state's agent. Values, returns and exemption approvals sit with the tax assessors.

  • Online: the county website has a homestead application page and a separate page on the yearly digest and assessments.

Hours and forms appear on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.

When Greene County expects payment

The county's payment date is December 1. If the 1st falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, the date moves to the next working day. Land with unpaid tax may be levied on and later sold.

Other dates follow a set pattern. A return lists what you held on January 1 and can be filed through April 1. Land and buildings carry forward at their earlier value, but business and other personal property need a new return every year. A mobile home must be returned by April 1, and its location permit is renewed between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, with millage rates set later.

How to appeal a Greene County assessment

Owners get 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. You may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, using the state's PT-311A form sent to the Board of Tax Assessors. That first filing also has to say which route you are taking.

  • Equalization route: the assessors look at it first and may issue a corrected notice, which you can contest within 30 days. An appeal they leave alone is heard by the Board of Equalization, and Superior Court is the final stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser can take value disputes, but only on real property that is not a homestead and is valued at $1,000,000 or above.
  • Arbitration: attach a current certified appraisal. If the assessors turn it down, the case moves to the clerk of Superior Court, a hearing follows inside 30 days, and the arbitrator's ruling is final.

The county page walks through each route and points to the state revenue department for forms.

Homestead exemptions

To qualify for a given year you must own the home and live in it on January 1, then file by April 1. A later filing waits for the next year. Once approved, the exemption carries on yearly until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, made up of $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64, net income capped at $10,000: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over, net income capped at $10,000: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, for a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. The freeze covers the house and land up to five acres, and it excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops.

Deferral and farmland

Owners aged 62 and older can delay, though not cancel, their tax through a deferral program if household income is no more than $15,000. Farmland that qualifies is assessed at 30%. Preparing your file for a sale

Check that the code matches what you expect: a senior or freeze code that dropped off is easier to fix with the assessors before a contract than after.

Call the commissioner at 706-453-3358 about the balance, and the assessors at 706-453-3355 about any pending appeal. A buyer who sees a clean bill and a clear value history has fewer reasons to renegotiate. If you inherited the property or it sits on farmland, ask the assessors whether the land still qualifies for its current assessment, since that can change once ownership changes.

What to do about tax before closing

Whoever holds title on January 1 stays liable for the whole year's tax, even when the house sells the next day, and the state gives no refund for a partial year. Contracts usually split the bill, so the number to find is the exact balance on the parcel.

  3. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, but the title search still checks for unpaid tax, so the same payoff letter applies.

Which day does Greene County collect property tax?

December 1, moving to the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. A parcel with unpaid tax can be levied on and in time sold.

How much time do I have to dispute a Greene County value?

Forty-five days from the mailing date on your assessment notice. The Board of Tax Assessors needs a written appeal naming your route, which can be equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?

April 1 for the present tax year. The home must have been yours and your residence on January 1, and later applications count for the year after.

What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?

The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. It applies to the house and land up to five acres, with pools, barns, detached garages and shops left out.

Several offices share the work. The commissioner sends bills and takes in and passes on the money, with no part in deciding the amount. The Board of Assessors sets values, while millage rates come from the commissioners, the school board and each city.

  • Property tax (tax commissioner): 770-822-8800, tax@gwinnettcounty.com, open weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Board of Assessors, real property: 770-822-7200; personal property: 770-822-7220. Values and appeals go through Gwinnett-Assessor.com.
  • Board of Commissioners, county millage rates and fees: 770-822-7000.
  • Board of Education, school millage: 678-301-6200.
  • Clerk of Court, deeds and liens: 770-822-8100.

The commissioner's brochure page is the best single reference. Mail payments to P.O. Box 372, Lawrenceville, GA 30046.

The yearly tax calendar

These dates are typical and can change, so the bill in your hand outranks any chart.

  • January: mobile home bills go out, with payment due April 1.
  • April 1: returns on business tangibles, aircraft and watercraft reach the Board of Assessors.
  • May and June: the Annual Notice of Assessment goes out, and appeals must be filed within 45 days of its date.
  • July and August: taxing bodies set millage rates through advertised, public processes.
  • August or September: real and personal property bills are mailed and also posted online.
  • October or November: payment comes due.

The Board of Commissioners can change the due date each year, so read your own bill. Personal property worth more than $20,000 combined is taxable, and a late or unreported return may draw a 10% penalty. A late mobile home bill adds a 10% penalty, then 1% interest each month after June 1.

Ways to pay

Paying online by check costs nothing, and online card payments add a convenience fee. Other options are the drop boxes open around the clock at all five tag offices, a mailed check to the Lawrenceville box, or a visit to any tax commissioner office. Cash must be handed over in person, and the county asks that none be mailed.

A few cities run their own property billing. The commissioner covers mobile home, heavy-duty equipment and timber tax in every city, but real property inside a city that bills on its own is a question for that city's tax department.

Homestead and other exemptions

Homestead exemptions cut the tax on a primary residence, and a single application serves every exemption the county offers. File year-round by mail, at an office or online, as long as the home was your legal primary residence on January 1. Approval continues until ownership or eligibility changes. Send mailed forms by certified mail.

Gwinnett also has the Value Offset Exemption, a local measure that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of the bill. School and city taxes are not covered. It attaches automatically with a homestead approval and reaches the home plus as many as five acres of land. The Board of Assessors separately reviews conservation use, agricultural, historic and Brownfield preferential assessments and tax-exempt status for property such as places of worship.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Gwinnett County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appealing an assessment

The Annual Notice of Assessment usually arrives in May or June. You have 45 days from the date on it to appeal to the Board of Assessors, and the county says you can file online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com. Pull recent sales of comparable homes and photos of any condition problems before you file.

Before you list a Gwinnett house

Run through a short list so nothing surfaces at the closing table. First, find out whether you live in a city that bills its own property tax, because then you will hold two bills for one house. Second, confirm that your homestead exemption and the Value Offset Exemption are showing on the parcel, since a buyer's agent will look at the bill to estimate carrying costs.

Third, collect the Annual Notice of Assessment and any appeal you filed, as the value on it drives the bill. Fourth, call the commissioner for the current balance and ask whether any lien or delinquency is recorded with the Clerk of Court at 770-822-8100. A cash buyer can often close on a short timeline, but the title search still checks for liens, so settling the balance first removes the main delay.

Taxes when you sell

Whoever owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for the whole year. After a later sale, the earlier owner and the new owner both get a bill, and the commissioner takes no position on how they split it. The two parties settle that, generally at the closing table.

An unpaid bill leads to a lien in the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows proof within 90 days of the due date that liability moved to the buyer. Acceptable proof pairs closing language in which the seller assigns property tax liability to the purchaser and the purchaser accepts it with a deed recorded in the purchaser's name. A delinquent parcel can ultimately be sold at a tax auction.

Practical steps: ask the commissioner at 770-822-8800 what the parcel owes, tell your closing agent whether a bill has gone out for the year, and keep the receipt. If you sell for cash, the same payoff and proof-of-assignment rules apply.

Frequently asked questions

When are Gwinnett County property taxes due?

Typically in October or November, after bills are mailed in August or September. The Board of Commissioners can change the date each year, so rely on the date printed on your bill.

What is the deadline to contest a Gwinnett County value?

The window is 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in May or June. The Board of Assessors takes the appeal, and it can be filed online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com.

Who pays the tax if my Gwinnett County house sells after January 1?

The January 1 owner carries the full year, and both owners may receive a bill. Buyer and seller decide the split, usually on the closing statement.

What is the Gwinnett Value Offset Exemption?

A local exemption that holds assessed value at its base-year level for the county government share of your bill. School and city taxes are outside it, it reaches the home plus up to five acres, and it attaches automatically when a homestead exemption is granted.

Does Gwinnett County take cash for property tax?

Yes, but only face to face at a tax commissioner office. An online check payment is free and cards add a convenience fee. Never mail cash to the Lawrenceville box.

Habersham County housing and population

Habersham County sits in the Blue Ridge of northeast Georgia. Clarkesville is the seat and Cornelia is the biggest city. The 2020 count was 46,031 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 50,416 means growth of 9.5%. About 20.3% of residents are 65 or older.

Owner-occupants hold close to three of every four homes, and 390 permits in 2025 show new building joining a digest of mostly older property. The appraisal staff sets values using recent sales and market conditions on January 1, so a house's figure can follow neighborhood sales.

Who does what in Habersham County property tax

The tax commissioner holds an elected constitutional office. It sends bills, collects, accounts for and disburses the money, and takes no part in setting values or rates. Values are the job of the Board of Tax Assessors, which has had five members since January 1, 1990, each serving a three-year term. Rates are set by the county commissioners and the school board, while the state's own levy cannot go beyond one-fourth of a mill.

  • Tax commissioner: 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120, open on weekdays from 8:00 until 4:45, with Saturdays closed until further notice.
  • Tax assessors: phone (706) 839-0100, which is also the number for mobile home registration questions.
  • Board of Tax Assessors meetings: second and fourth Mondays monthly, beginning at 9 a.m.

The assessors' board decides which properties are exempt, approves or denies Conservation Use applications and homestead exemptions, reviews tax returns, and levies penalties against property that was never returned. It also meets with taxpayers to talk through concerns, so a seller who doubts a value can ask for that conversation before listing.

Further detail sits on the commissioner's information page and the assessors' board page.

Due dates for real property and mobile homes

Bills are mailed by August 15 and payment is due November 15 of the same year. That is earlier than the state default of December 20. Mobile and modular homes run on a different cycle. Their bills usually go out around February 1, and the tax and location permit are tied to April 1.

Missing the April 1 payment and permit on a mobile home brings a 10% penalty, a citation to appear in the county's Magistrate Court, and possibly a sale of the home. A decal has to be displayed, and registration is done through the assessors' office.
