Paying and checking your bill

The commissioner's office is the place to confirm what you owe, since it bills and collects for every taxing body on the parcel. Ask for the figure by parcel, and ask what the bill covers so you can tell the county, school and state portions apart. If the bill seems off, call the assessors at (706) 839-0100 about the value rather than the commissioner, who cannot change it.

When you plan to sell between mailing and the due date, ask whether the bill has been issued yet. Settlement agents usually want proof of payment or a payoff letter, so keep the receipt where you can find it.

Appealing a Habersham County value

Assessment notices normally arrive in spring. An owner who disagrees has 45 days from the date on the notice. The written appeal may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it goes to the Board of Tax Assessors naming the method you pick.

Mobile homes carry an extra step. If the owner still disagrees after a changed value, an appeal to the Board of Equalization can follow within 21 days of that notice. That board is appointed by the grand jury and hears administrative appeals from the assessors' values. For a regular parcel, ask the assessors' office for forms and the exact sequence.

Bring comparable sales, photos and any repair estimates, since the board works from market conditions on January 1.

Homestead, farm and business exemptions

The Tax Assessor's office handles homestead applications, and new buyers should carry in the warranty deed. Filing by April 1 covers your first claimed year, and a late filing slides to the following year. After approval the exemption renews itself until your residence, ownership or qualifying category changes. Local exemptions replace state ones whenever the local amount is greater.

  • Land in genuine agricultural use can be assessed at 30% rather than 40% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use valuation is granted in return for a covenant with the assessors to keep the land in qualifying use for ten years at least.
  • Freeport exemption for manufacturers can reach three categories: raw goods, goods being processed, and finished goods held in a warehouse for out-of-state shipment. Applications are filed between January 1 and April 1.
  • A business's equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40% of fair market value.

What the assessors can do for a seller

The Board of Tax Assessors meets on the second and fourth Mondays and talks through concerns with taxpayers. A seller who thinks the value runs high can bring recent sales and ask how the figure was reached before the appeal clock matters. Do this early in the year, because the 45 days run from the notice date and are short once the notice arrives.

Selling when tax is still due

Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible for the whole year and refunds nothing for a partial year. The sale contract normally decides who actually pays, so begin by learning the precise balance.

Phone the tax commissioner at (706) 839-0120 and ask what the parcel owes for this year and any before it. When closing lands between the August mailing and the November 15 date, tell the closing agent whether the new bill has gone out and been paid. A mobile home bill follows the April 1 cycle and stands apart from real property. A homestead exemption ends when you move or ownership changes, so tell the assessors after you leave and let the buyer file separately.

Steps before you list

A few calls early on keep a closing on schedule. Ask the commissioner for the balance on every year, not only the current one. Ask the assessors whether your homestead and any Conservation Use covenant are on file, because a buyer of farmland will want to know whether the covenant continues. Gather the assessment notice, the latest bill, and the warranty deed for your own records.

If you own a mobile home, confirm that its tax, permit and decal are current before an offer arrives. A cash buyer who closes quickly still depends on clean tax records, so paying any open balance from your proceeds at the table is the usual route. The payoff letter from the commissioner is the document your closing agent will ask for.

What day is Habersham County property tax due?

Bills are mailed by August 15 and payment is expected by November 15. For mobile and modular homes, bills typically go out near February 1 and the tax is tied to April 1.

Where do I find the Habersham County tax commissioner?

The main office is at 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120. Weekday hours run from 8:00 to 4:45, and Saturdays are closed until further notice.

What is the time limit to appeal a Habersham County value?

You have 45 days from the date on the notice. A written appeal naming your chosen method goes to the Board of Tax Assessors.

By when must a Habersham County homestead application arrive?

April 1 in the first year you claim. Take the application to the Tax Assessor's office, with your warranty deed if the purchase is recent.

Is farmland taxed differently in Habersham County?

Sometimes. Qualifying agricultural property is assessed at 30% of fair market value, not 40%, and Conservation Use valuation applies current-use value in exchange for a covenant of ten years or longer with the assessors.

Who handles property tax in Hall County

Two Gainesville offices split the work. The Board of Assessors sets the value of your property. The Tax Commissioner mails the statements and takes payment. Neither office sets the rate. Mill levies are voted by the county commissioners, the school board and each city that taxes on its own.

Gainesville is the county seat. Check which district your address is in before you compare your bill with a neighbor's.

  • Billing and payment questions: Tax Commissioner, 770.531.6950 option 3, open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • City bills: owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood receive a second statement from that city.

Due dates and payment options

Sixty days after mailing is the rule in Hall. A normal season means a September 15 mailing and a November 15 deadline. The 2026 statements went out October 15, a month late because the state approval of the digest came late, so the deadline became December 15, 2026.

The 60 day gap stays fixed even when the mailing slips, so a later bill gives you a later deadline. Interest starts building monthly once the deadline passes. Plan around the date printed on your own statement.

Paying before the deadline also keeps a clean record for the title company when you list. Save the receipt from the portal and give a copy to your closing attorney.

How to appeal your assessment

You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Hall takes appeals three ways: online in qPublic, by post to P.O. Box 2895, Gainesville, GA 30503, or at the counter at 2875 Browns Bridge Road.

If you do nothing in that window, the value goes to the Tax Commissioner for billing. Notices are mailed to every owner each year, and the 2026 digital copies were posted on qPublic.

An appeal never freezes the bill. Hall County sends an Under Appeal statement for the 2026 cycle, and the amount due by December 15, 2026 is the lower result of 85% of the 2026 value or 100% of the 2025 value. Any unpaid portion still accrues monthly interest from that date. A refund after a final appeal decision is processed automatically. Other refund claims for erroneous or illegal taxes must start within three years of payment.

Exemptions and filing season

Filing season runs January 1 through April 1. Homestead applications, real property returns and personal property returns all use that window, and most of it can be done online through qPublic.

  • Homestead exemptions, including the senior exemptions, the Total School Tax Exemption and the 100% Disabled Veteran exemption, are filed under the Real Property tab in qPublic.
  • Boats, personal watercraft, aircraft, business personal property and manufacturer personal property returns go under the Personal Property tab. Returns filed after April 1 carry a 10% late filing penalty.
  • Conservation Use covenants are taken in person at the Government Center, where an appointment is advised.

You can apply any time once the house is your primary residence, with April 1 as the cutoff for the first year of relief. A missed homestead filing is treated as a waiver for that year. Call 770.531.6720 about real property or 770.531.6749 about personal property.

Who owes the tax when a Hall County house sells?

The January 1 owner of record is answerable for that year's tax, even when the house changes hands in spring or summer. Who actually pays is a closing-table question, and the closing attorney handles it.

Hall County adds a step that sellers should not skip. If you sold real property during 2026, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the due date, which works out to March 15, 2027. When the documents clearly shift liability to the new owner, the seller is no longer billed. Papers that arrive after March 15, 2027 cannot be considered. Boats, planes and business fixtures work the same way: whoever owned them in January stays on the hook after a sale.

If you have an escrow account, the county passes tax data to your mortgage servicer, yet the owner still answers for payment.

Selling with taxes owed

Before you list, ask the Tax Commissioner what your parcel owes and hand that number to the closing attorney. Unpaid balances carry monthly interest after the deadline, and a buyer's title company will want them cleared at closing.

  1. Call 770.531.6950 option 3 and ask for the current balance on the parcel.
  2. Confirm whether a city bill also exists for your address.
  3. Bring the payoff figure to the closing attorney so it can come out of your proceeds.
  4. After the sale, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027 if the sale happened in 2026.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which can shorten the stretch in which a bill might come due mid-contract. The tax rules above still apply to whoever owned the house on January 1.

Housing numbers

Population is 226,568 as of July 1, 2025, up 11.7% since the April 2020 count. A typical owned home is valued at $350,400 for 2020 to 2024, household income is $80,901 and monthly rent is $1,341.

The county has 86,917 housing units and 73,551 households, and 68.6% of homes are owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,742 a month on housing, while owners with none spend $550. The 1,996 building permits issued in 2025 point to steady new construction, which gives resale buyers plenty of competing choices. Price your house with that supply in mind, and have the tax balance settled so it does not slow an offer.

When do 2026 Hall County property taxes have to be paid?

The 2026 bills are due December 15, 2026. They were mailed October 15, and the due date stays at 60 days after mailing. In a typical year the statements go out September 15 and fall due November 15.

What is the deadline to dispute a Hall County valuation?

The cutoff is 45 days after the date on the notice. After that, the value moves on to billing. Use qPublic, the P.O. Box 2895 mailing address, or the counter on Browns Bridge Road.

Can I pay Hall County property tax online?

Yes. HallCountyTax.org accepts E-Check for a flat $1.50, PayPal, and cards at 2.49% for credit and 1.50% for debit. You can also mail a check, use the Government Center drop box, or call 770.531.6950 to pay by card.

Who is billed for 2026 if my Hall County house sells?

The January 1, 2026 owner of record owes that year's tax, and the closing documents decide who actually pays. To move billing to the buyer, send the sales documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027.

Do Hall County cities send their own tax bills?

Yes. Owners inside Gainesville, Flowery Branch, Buford, Braselton or Oakwood get a separate city statement in addition to the county bill. The county bill covers county and school levies only.

Who bills and values property in Hancock County

Two Sparta offices share the work. One sets what each parcel is worth and approves exemptions. The other prints the bills and banks the payments for the county government and the Hancock schools. Rates come from elsewhere: the county commissioners and the school board settle the mill levy every year.

Sparta is the one incorporated city. Hancock is rural, so most listings are acreage, farmhouses and inherited family places, where the legal description of the land counts as much as the building. Population is 8,682 by the latest estimate, down from 8,735 in 2020.

  • Tax Commissioner: 9031 E. Broad Street, Sparta, phone 706-444-5148. The public counter shuts a quarter hour before five.
  • Tax Assessor: the same street address, phone 706-444-5721.

Due dates and what happens if you pay late

Houses, land and business equipment fall due November 15. Manufactured homes fall due April 1. Treat the date printed on your own bill as final, and call 706-444-5148 if anything looks off.

Late real estate bills pick up 1% interest every month. Once three months pass with the balance open, a flat ten percent penalty lands on top. Roughly a month after the deadline, the office can record a tax lien, called a FiFa, in the superior court clerk's docket. These liens are public and credit bureaus can pull them, and the office has no hand in how they are reported. Seizure of the property is the final step, and the office describes it as a last resort.

Manufactured homes

A mobile or modular unit counts as personal property. It needs a return and a location permit, and the permit is withheld until that year's tax is settled. Past April 1 the county adds a ten percent filing penalty and a monthly one percent interest charge. A unit that stays unpaid can go to auction.

If you plan to sell a manufactured home, get the payoff in writing first, because a buyer cannot get a location permit while the year's tax is open.

How to contest a value

You get forty-five days, and the clock starts on the date shown on the notice of assessment, so mail the appeal to the assessors early. When they stand by their number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, then onward to superior court.

The assessors first look at their own figure again and tell you what they decided. If you are still unhappy, a hearing follows before the Board of Equalization, whose members the Grand Jury appoints. Arbitration can replace that hearing. After either result, a written notice to the assessors keeps your case alive for superior court.

Hancock taxes forty percent of a parcel's January market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that slice and the mill rate is applied to the remainder. Ask the assessor's staff to show the math on your own parcel.

Homestead and other exemptions

Most homeowners begin with homestead. Take the form to the assessor's office. Two conditions apply: you lived in and owned the house when the year began, and the form must be in hand before April. A filing after that point earns nothing until the following year.

  • A granted homestead exemption renews itself as long as you stay put. A move requires a new application for the new address.
  • Owners who reach 62 may apply for an extra exemption. The assessor can say which forms are current.
  • Business owners can ask about freeport relief on inventory, and farm and forest owners can ask about the ten-year conservation use and preferential farm programs.

Returns have a spring window that closes April 1. The first real estate return carries forward at last year's value, so you refile only after building or buying more land. A new return with a lower figure is also how a dispute over the current value begins.

What a typical Hancock County house is worth

Home prices here are among the lowest in Georgia. For 2020 through 2024 the middle owned house is valued at $88,600 and the middle monthly rent is $938. Middle household income is $40,082, and about 79% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

There were 5,088 homes counted in mid-2025 against 2,922 occupied households, and only 24 building permits were issued in 2025. That gap matters because a vacant or inherited house still produces a tax bill every year. Vacant housing was 32.6% in the 2020 count. If you hold a house like that, call the commissioner before listing to learn what the parcel owes.

Selling with an unpaid tax bill

The bill for a given year lands on the person who owned the parcel when that year opened, which in a sale is normally the seller. The purchase contract and the closing attorney decide how to divide it. Before closing day, request a written payoff from the Sparta commissioner's office.

A buyer's title search will turn up back taxes, and any recorded FiFa must be satisfied at the closing table. With a lien or an unpaid mobile home tax already on file, phone 706-444-5148 early, since the office may levy on property that stays unpaid.

Heirs should also check whose name is on the deed. A warranty deed copy comes from the courthouse deed room, and new homeowners should carry one to the assessor when filing for homestead. Both tax offices share the East Broad Street address in Sparta, and the courthouse is in town as well, so one trip can settle the payoff figure, the exemption status and the deed copy.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, so a house with old liens or unclear heirs can still close if the title work is clean and the taxes are paid at the table.

  1. Call the commissioner at 706-444-5148 and ask for the balance on the parcel, including any FiFa and any manufactured home tax.
  2. Pull a copy of your deed from the courthouse deed room if heirs or a prior owner are involved.
  3. Stop at the assessor's office to confirm your homestead filing and what the buyer must file.
  4. Give the written payoff to the closing attorney so the taxes come out of the proceeds at the table.

Doing these four things before a buyer is under contract keeps the title search from turning up surprises that could delay the closing.

Frequently asked questions

When do Hancock County property tax bills come due?

November 15 for houses and land, April 1 for mobile homes. Follow the date on your own bill, and call 706-444-5148 if you are unsure.

What does it cost to pay Hancock County property tax late?

Interest of 1% accrues every month on real estate, and a 10% penalty is added when 90 days go by. A FiFa lien becomes possible after a month.

What is the window to dispute a Hancock County value?

Forty-five days, starting at the notice date. The written appeal goes to the assessors first.

What is the last day to file for homestead in Hancock County?

Get the form to the assessor's office before April arrives. The home must also have been yours, and lived in by you, on New Year's Day. A late form counts toward the next year.

Are mobile homes taxed differently in Hancock County?

Yes. They count as personal property with an April 1 deadline, and no location permit is issued until the year's tax has been paid.

Who runs property tax in Haralson County

Haralson County sits in northwest Georgia on the Alabama line, with the courthouse in Buchanan. The newest federal estimate puts population at 33,066, which is 10.5% above the April 2020 base.

Property tax splits across two desks. The assessors appraise each parcel and take exemption filings. The Tax Commissioner builds the digest, issues bills and collects. The commissioner has no say over value or millage. Those come from the assessors and from the county commissioners and the other taxing bodies such as cities and schools.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: 4266 GA Highway 120, Buchanan, 770-646-2022, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-646-2020 for payment and billing questions.
  • Towns inside the county: Bremen, Buchanan, Tallapoosa and Waco. Ask the clerk in the town where the house sits whether it sends its own bill.

Cities and school districts

Four incorporated places and three small unincorporated communities make up the county. Bremen is the largest city, at about 6,500 residents, followed by Tallapoosa at roughly 3,155, Buchanan at 1,159 and Waco at 522. Budapest, Draketown and Felton are unincorporated.

A city may levy its own tax and have its clerk bill it, unless the city and county agreed to one combined bill. A Bremen or Tallapoosa address can therefore mean two statements, while a house in an unincorporated community like Felton or Draketown sees only the county bill. Two public school systems operate here, so confirm which district a house falls in before you set a price.

If your house is in town, ask the city clerk for the latest bill and the payment address, and ask the county for the same, so you know the full amount owed before closing.

Due dates and penalties

December 1 is the payment deadline for land and houses. Mobile homes are billed for April 1. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill's postmark, then builds monthly at a rate pegged to prime.

Haralson County deadlines and late charges
Property typeDue dateLate charges
Land and housesDecember 1Monthly interest plus 5% at each 120 day mark, capped at 20%
Mobile homesApril 1Same interest and penalty schedule

The bill is built from the assessors' value times 40 percent, which gives the assessed value. The millage rate from the commissioners and other levying bodies is then applied to that figure.

The Tax Commissioner's office also handles tag renewals, titles, mobile home decals, timber tax and handicap placards. The title desk stops processing at 4 p.m., so plan a closing-day errand with that in mind.

How to appeal your valuation

Appeals go in writing to the assessors before the cutoff printed on the yearly notice. Read the notice the day it arrives and mark the date, because late appeals are not taken.

The assessors define market value as the price an informed buyer and a willing seller would agree to in an arm's length deal. The notice also shows estimated taxes based on the prior year's millage, so the real bill can differ once the commissioners and the Board of Education set rates, usually between July and August.

Appeals volume has been heavy. When appeals pass the 3 percent threshold in O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, the board gets an extra 180 days to decide and notify owners. Anyone with an open appeal can call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for status. Field appraisers may visit a property under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and carry photo identification in a marked county vehicle.

Homestead, farm and forest programs

The homestead exemption is the common one, and owners file with the Tax Commissioner's office. Ownership on New Year's Day plus an April 1 filing earns the current year's benefit. A late application waits until the next calendar year.

  • Homestead: applies to the house and its land when you live there as your legal residence. A person away for health reasons is not denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office for them.
  • Conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment: both use a 10 year covenant, and apply between January 2 and April 1. Preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage, and conservation use can save more than 50 percent in some cases.
  • Residential transitional assessment: a 10 year covenant for land moving from residential to commercial use.

Covenants matter in a sale. A farm or timber tract under a 10 year covenant carries obligations the buyer has to continue, so ask the Specialized Assessment department at the assessors' office what a transfer does to the covenant before you sign a contract.

What a Haralson County seller should do about the tax bill

Phone the Tax Commissioner at 770-646-2020 to learn the parcel's balance and whether this year's bill exists yet. Bills fall due December 1, so a closing earlier in the year often happens before the statement exists, and the contract has to say who covers that gap.

Interest and penalties stack up after the due date. A buyer's title search will pick up unpaid taxes, so a written payoff figure from the commissioner helps the closing attorney.

  • Confirm whether you filed for homestead by April 1 and whether it applies to the buyer's first year.
  • For a mobile home, remember the April 1 due date, which is separate from the December 1 bill on land.
  • If the land is under a conservation or preferential agricultural covenant, ask the assessors what a transfer does to it.

A cash sale does not wait on a lender's underwriting, but the tax payoff still comes out at closing. Bring the commissioner's written figure and your deed information to the closing attorney.

  1. Call the commissioner for the parcel balance and ask whether the current bill has been issued.
  2. Ask the assessors whether any covenant or specialized assessment is on the land.
  3. Collect the written payoff and give it to the closing attorney before the contract date.
  4. Tell the buyer which statements to expect, including any city bill, so nobody is surprised after closing.

Housing market

Haralson County is mid-priced for rural west Georgia. For 2020 to 2024 the middle value of an owned home is $227,500, the middle household income is $72,127 and the middle rent is $923.

The county has 13,861 housing units and 11,747 households, and 71.6% of homes are owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage typically pay $1,673 a month. Builders pulled 159 permits in 2025, so new supply is modest and resale houses compete mainly with each other.

Frequently asked questions

When is Haralson County property tax due?

December 1 for land and houses, April 1 for mobile homes. Interest builds monthly at a prime-linked rate. A 5% penalty hits at each 120 day mark, and penalties stop at 20%.

Which number do I call about a Haralson County tax bill?

Call the Tax Commissioner's office at 770-646-2020 for billing and payment. Questions about value or appeals belong with the assessors at 770-646-2022.

What is the Haralson County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1. You must own the home on January 1 and file by the return deadline. A later filing is held until the following calendar year.

Does Haralson County offer a break for farmland?

Yes. Both conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment ask for a ten year covenant, with applications taken January 2 through April 1. Preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage over fair market value.

Why is my Haralson County appeal taking so long?

When appeals pass 3 percent of parcels or digest value, O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 gives the assessors an extra 180 days to rule. Call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for the status of your appeal.

Who handles property tax in Hart County

Hart County is lake country in the northeast corner of Georgia, right beside I-85, with Hartwell as the county seat. Population is 28,639 as of 2025. Lake Hartwell drives much of the local market, so a shoreline lot, a farmhouse and a Hartwell bungalow can each raise different tax questions, from acreage covenants to homestead.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: P.O. Box 810, Hartwell, GA 30643, 706-376-3997. Values property, takes homestead applications and handles appeals.
  • Tax Commissioner: in the courthouse in Hartwell. Collects property tax, auto tags, timber payments, mobile home tax and the intangible recording tax.
  • Records: the county website links to a property tax record search and to an online payment site.

Have your parcel number handy before you call either office.

Rural parcels near the lake often combine a house with several acres, so ask whether the land carries any special assessment before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

Key dates at a glance

Hart County property tax calendar
TaskDate
Returns and homestead filingJanuary 1 through April 1
Assessment notices mailedBy April 15
Appeal of a changed valueWithin 45 days of the notice date
Mobile home return and location permitJanuary 1 through May 1
Property tax bill due, normal yearDecember 20

Statewide, December 20 is the default due date. Counties may pick December 1 or November 15 instead. No interest runs until 60 days past the postmark. Your statement's printed date controls, so look there first, then pay by it.

Paying your bill

Penalties can attach to delinquent taxes on top of interest. The Tax Commissioner has added a drop box outside the courthouse for property and auto payments, and an online payment option is linked from the county website.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. A mobile home standing in Hart on January 1 must be returned to the Tax Commissioner by May 1, and the yearly location permit window runs January 1 to May 1 as well. A newly placed home needs a permit within 30 days. Ask the Tax Commissioner when the tax on a mobile home account falls due.

If you cannot make the courthouse during the day, the drop box takes property and auto payments outside business hours. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

How to challenge a Hart County assessment

Your written appeal has to carry a postmark within 45 days of the date on the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. That notice goes out when they disagree with the value you returned.

The county reviews every parcel annually and mails a notice by April 15. Owners in Hartwell and on the lake shore should read that notice as soon as it arrives, because the 45 day clock starts from the notice date. The assessors' office will explain the filing procedure by phone.

Another route runs through the return. You can file a return with the assessors from January 1 through April 1. If you think your value is too high, file a return reducing it by April 1 to have a chance at a lower value for next year's taxes. Tax that was wrongly or illegally collected can be claimed back within three years of payment, with a written claim to the county governing authority.

Homestead exemption

The homestead filer must live in the house as a legal residence, and the paperwork goes to the assessors' office. A person away for health reasons will not be denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office on their behalf.

  • Owning the property on January 1 and filing by the April 1 return date secures the exemption for that tax year.
  • Certain elderly owners qualify for additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead. Eligible owners should apply by April 1 so the benefit carries into later years.
  • Call the assessors at 706-376-3997 to ask whether a local homestead exemption sits on top of the state ones for your parcel.

In the year of a sale, remember that an exemption belongs to a person at an address. Your old filing stays behind when you leave, and a buyer who moves in after New Year's must file fresh. Skip the form and that year's relief is gone.

Elderly owners should ask the assessors which extra exemption forms apply to their age before April 1 arrives, since a missed deadline pushes the benefit to the following year.

Hart County housing numbers

Hart County is affordable by Georgia standards. For 2020 to 2024 the middle owned home is $215,100, the middle rent is $844 and 77.8% of homes are occupied by their owners. Median household income is $59,385.

The county counts 13,800 housing units against 11,034 households, and 197 building permits were issued in 2025. Population rose 10.9% from the April 2020 base to the 2025 estimate. Owners of a house that sits empty part of the year should ask both offices whether an exemption they hold still applies.

Before you list: a Hart County checklist

Missing paperwork causes more trouble than the tax itself. Run through these items a few weeks ahead of listing day.

  1. Pull your latest assessment notice and compare the value to what you think the house would sell for.
  2. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the unpaid balance, if any, and for the status of this year's bill.
  3. Confirm with the assessors that your homestead exemption is on file, and tell your buyer to file their own.
  4. If the property is a mobile home, locate the location permit and the return you filed.
  5. Look for any acreage or covenant paperwork that a buyer will ask about.

With those five items in a folder, your closing attorney can quote a payoff in a single call and your buyer's title company has less to chase. A cash buyer can often close quickly, so having the folder ready early keeps the tax balance from becoming the last open item.

Recording and closing costs

The Tax Commissioner collects the intangible recording tax. A lender holding a long-term note on real estate has 90 days to record the security instrument locally. The charge is $1.50 per $500 of the note, rounded up for any fraction. A cash purchase has no note, so that charge does not arise.

For sellers the main items are a tax payoff figure and clear title. The Clerk of Superior Court handles recording at 185 West Franklin Street in Hartwell.

Before listing a Hart County house, gather your latest assessment notice, the most recent tax bill, any mobile home permit records and any covenant paperwork. Get the unpaid balance from the Tax Commissioner, then settle with the closing attorney which party carries this year's bill. If the house is a mobile home, bring the permit record so the buyer can see the location permit is current.

Frequently asked questions

When are Hart County property taxes due?

December 20 is the normal deadline, and state law holds off interest for 60 days after mailing. Go by the date on your bill.

How soon must a Hart County appeal be filed?

Postmark it within 45 days of the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. Phone 706-376-3997 for the steps.

When is the Hart County homestead exemption deadline?

April 1. You need to have owned and lived in the house on January 1, with the form at the assessors' office by the return deadline.

Where do I pay a Hart County mobile home tax?

Pay the Tax Commissioner. The return and the yearly location permit both fall between January 1 and May 1, and whoever owned the home there on January 1 files.

Does Hart County reassess every year?

Yes. Every parcel is reevaluated each year and notices go out by April 15, with 45 days to appeal a value you dispute.

Which Heard County tax office to call first

Two rooms in the Administration Building in Franklin split the work. Room 300 takes payments. Room 400 sets parcel values and approves exemptions. Walking into the wrong one costs an afternoon.

The Tax Commissioner's counter now stays open through lunch, a change that began September 1, 2026. Schedule an assessor visit outside the noon hour. The commissioner's email is heardtc@heardcountyga.com and the assessors answer at heardtax@heardcountyga.com.

Heard County housing numbers

Heard had 12,149 residents in July 2025, a 6.5% gain on the 2020 base of 11,410. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $186,800, and renters pay a median of $917 a month. There are 4,979 housing units and 4,309 households, and homeowners occupy 72.3% of homes.

Few households move in a given year, and only 54 permits were issued countywide in 2025. A listing here usually competes with older resale houses and country properties. Land area is 295.97 square miles, so many sales are rural parcels, and wooded tracts held for timber bring land-use questions that a Franklin city lot never raises.

Commuters average 34.9 minutes to work, a fairly long drive, which is worth mentioning when a buyer asks about location.

Field visits and your property record

The assessors' office settles taxability, value and equalization, mails owners a notice when a value moves, and approves the exemptions people claim. Field staff visit each parcel to update the digest. They take a front photo and a rear photo of every structure and log changes since the previous countywide update. The state requires this cycle every three years.

Crews carry county identification and vehicle markings. A door hanger is left when nobody answers, so the owner can confirm the interior description. Before you list, phone (706) 675-3786 and ask what the card on your parcel says about bedrooms, baths, outbuildings and finished space. A garage that was converted years ago but still appears as a garage on the record can pull the value in the wrong direction, and a correction before the notice goes out costs you nothing.

  • The valuation date is January 1, and the taxable share is 40% of fair market value.
  • Parcel records are on the qpublic portal.
  • Returns of value are accepted from January 1 until April 1.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Heard County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What to do if your value seems too high

Put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You get 45 days counted from the mailing date on the notice, and the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or an exemption the county denied. State revenue officials cannot override the county on one parcel, so the form should not go to Atlanta.

The uniform PT-311A form asks you to pick a route up front.

  • Board of Equalization: the common choice. The assessors can change the number and mail a fresh notice, which you may contest for another 30 days.
  • Hearing officer: reserved for non-homestead property above $500,000.
  • Arbitration: disputes over value alone, with a certified appraisal due 45 days after the board acknowledges your filing.

A dispute that survives can go on to superior court after written notice within 30 days of the ruling, and the previous year's tax has to be paid first. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside an appeal because elected bodies set the millage rate on their own.

Homestead filing and millage

House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, lets owners file a homestead application while the 45-day appeal window is open after assessment notices go out. The Assessor's Office takes it, and you should bring photo ID showing your current address. Skip the homestead filing on a house you live in and the exemption is treated as waived. April 1 is the usual deadline for a first-time filer.

The Board of Commissioners advertised in 2025 a tentative millage of 6.467 mills against a rollback figure of 5.467, which meant an 18.29 percent rise in collections. The Tax Commissioner's page posts a History of Tax Levy document for the year, which helps when you price a listing.

Who owes the tax when a Heard County house sells?

Whoever holds title on January 1 owes that year, and nothing is refunded to someone who sells early in the year. Read your bill or call (706) 675-3391 for the due date. The statewide default is December 20, though a county may pick December 1, November 15 or installment billing. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill.

Unpaid tax can lead to a recorded lien and then a public auction. After an auction, the owner has twelve months to redeem by paying the winning bid, later taxes and assessments, and a 20% premium. Anyone who inherits a house in that position should phone the commissioner early and get the payoff confirmed in writing.

Keep the commissioner's letter or email confirming what you owe. A written figure gives the closing agent something solid to work from.

Selling with back taxes

A house with back taxes can still sell. The lien just has to be paid at the closing table, and the closing agent can wire the payoff straight to the commissioner.

  1. Call (706) 675-3391 and ask for a payoff figure on the parcel.
  2. Ask the assessors at (706) 675-3786 whether the property record matches the house as it stands.
  3. Give both numbers to the closing agent before signing day.
  4. If an auction has already happened, ask how much time is left to redeem.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so these four steps are most of the work. Bring a photo ID and your deed information to either office.

Heirs have one more task. Check whose name is on the deed and whether the title has been cleared, because a buyer's title company will not close until the record shows who can sign. If the owner has died, tell the commissioner so statements go to the person handling the estate.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I pay a Heard County tax bill?

Pay at Room 300, 201 Park Avenue, Franklin, or send a check to P.O. Box 519, Franklin, GA 30217. The phone is (706) 675-3391. Weekday hours run 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, with no lunch closure since September 1, 2026.

Who decides what my Heard County house is worth?

The Board of Tax Assessors, in Room 400 at the same address, phone (706) 675-3786. The commissioner's office only bills, so value disputes go to the assessors.

How much time do I have to contest a Heard County assessment?

You have 45 days beginning on the date the notice was mailed. A new notice opens a new window. File with the county assessors, not the state revenue department.

Can I add a Heard County homestead exemption after April 1?

Sometimes. House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, opened the 45-day appeal period after notices are mailed to homestead filings. Bring photo ID with your current address to the Assessor's Office.

Can I sell a Heard County house that has back taxes?

Yes, as long as the lien is paid off at the sale. Request a payoff figure from the closing agent before signing day. If an auction has already happened, twelve months are allowed to redeem at the bid plus a 20% premium and other charges.

Drop boxes sit at both commissioner offices. For mailed checks, make them payable to Henry County Tax Commissioner or HCTC, send them to 140 Henry Pkwy, and write the bill numbers on the check. Metered mail does not count as proof of timely mailing.

Henry County housing numbers

McDonough is the county seat, joined by Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove. The county has 264,922 residents as of July 2025 on 318.71 square miles of land, and 1,666 building permits were issued in 2025, so unsold new homes and resales share the market.

  • Typical owner-occupied home: $313,900 (2020 to 2024 median).
  • Homeowners hold 74.9% of occupied housing.
  • Rent at the median: $1,674 per month.
  • Median household income: $83,146.

At those values, a small error in the square footage on file moves the bill, so check your digest record before setting a price.

Due date and late penalties

Statements go to the January 1 owner and are payable on or before November 16, with mailing by mid-September. Counties may move the statewide December 20 default earlier, which is what this date reflects. Whatever the calendar says, follow the date on the bill you receive.

Late payment gets costly. Interest builds monthly and a further 5% penalty attaches every 120 days after the deadline, up to a ceiling of 20%. Mailed checks need a USPS postmark before the deadline. Since December 2025 the county reads that mark as the first automated processing date at a regional center, which can be later than the day you dropped the envelope off. A transfer from your bank's own bill-pay service has no postmark, so the money must be in hand by the deadline.

  • The online portal charges 2.5% on cards or $1.50 for an e-check, a fee set by its outside processor.
  • Daily ceilings are $20,000 on cards and $60,000 on e-checks.
  • Paying at a counter does not waive the card fee.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the lender is the contact for the bill.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Henry County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Will Henry County bill the buyer after closing?

Not automatically. Statements go to the person who owned on January 1, and a lien is filed against that owner unless the office receives a settlement statement inside 90 days of the due date, under Georgia Code 48-3-3. Send page one, where county taxes appear as collected, to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov with the address or a copy of the bill.

The owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year with no partial refund. Look at the Henry County line on your closing statement before signing, and as the seller, send the paper yourself instead of assuming someone else did.

Other charges can share the bill. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation fees appear on it, and a county water charge called the 2 mill tax pays for storage and pipes whether or not a home has a well. The Water Authority at 770-957-6659 explains that line.

  1. Get the settlement statement from the closing agent on closing day.
  2. Email page one to the address above, with the parcel address.
  3. Keep the sent message for your records in case the office asks for it later.

Homestead application

File in person at either commissioner office, through the online option, or by mail postmarked on or before April 1, since only a USPS postmark counts. One filing covers you for as long as you stay put. Bring these items.

  • Driver's licenses for you and your spouse that show the property address.
  • Registrations for every vehicle at that address.
  • The warranty deed.
  • A letter from any other county or state where you own a house, confirming no homestead is claimed there.
  • The divorce decree, if one applies.

Turning 62 by January 1 opens an added reduction on the school portion of assessed value, and approved exemptions step up again at ages 65, 68 and 70. The disability version asks for two doctors' letters, or one doctor's letter with a Social Security award letter, describing 100% disability. A married couple gets only one homestead.

If you think your value is wrong

Count 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Tax Assessor menu on the county site includes Notice of Assessment, Property Appeals, an appeal FAQ and conservation use rules, and the state's uniform PT-311A form asks you to commit to a route.

  • Board of Equalization: the route for value, uniformity, taxability or exemption fights. Henry lists this board under the Clerk of Superior Court, with its own members, forms, calendar, FAQ and appeal process pages.
  • Hearing officer: available only when non-homestead real estate exceeds $500,000.
  • Arbitration: restricted to value, and it needs a certified appraisal 45 days after the county acknowledges the appeal.

A superior court appeal follows written notice given within 30 days of the decision, after last year's tax is paid. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, a final value of 85 percent or less of the board's figure entitles the owner to litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henry County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid bills and tax sales

The commissioner runs judicial in rem tax sales at 140 Henry Parkway on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM. Once a sale happens, a twelve-month redemption period opens for interested parties, who repay the buyer's bid plus later taxes, assessments and a 20% premium. Before a sale, paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest releases the lien.

If you are selling with a lien open, ask the closing agent for a payoff figure well ahead of time. Other levies are separate from the county bill, so ask the commissioner what else appears on yours.

A cash sale can close fast, but the lien still has to be cleared at the table. Call (770) 288-8180 early so the figure is ready.

Frequently asked questions

When are Henry County property taxes due?

November 16, with bills mailed by mid-September to the January 1 owner. The state default is December 20, so trust the date on your own bill.

How do I keep a Henry County lien off my name after selling?

Email page one of the settlement statement to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov inside the 90-day window. Without it the office records a lien against the January 1 owner.

How steep are Henry County late penalties?

Interest builds monthly, and 5% more is added every 120 days until penalties hit 20%. Make sure a mailed check has a USPS postmark before the deadline.

Where can I check a Henry County parcel's value?

Use the records search in the Tax Assessor section of the county website, or call (770) 288-7999, option 1. Billing questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 288-8180.

Can I appeal in Henry County while my house is listed?

Yes. Listing does not pause or cancel the 45-day window. A lower final value also shrinks the bill that is divided at closing.

Which Houston County office to call

Three groups share the job here: the Tax Commissioner, the Tax Assessors and the three city offices. Collections happen at a Warner Robins office and a Perry office. Valuation and homestead filings happen in Perry. The assessors never send out bills.

Who answers what in Houston County
QuestionOfficePhone
County bill and paymentsTax Commissioner, 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, Warner Robins, GA 31088(478) 542-2110
County bill and payments, PerryTax Commissioner, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry, GA 31069(478) 218-4940
Real property value and exemptionsTax Assessors, 201 Perry Parkway, Perry(478) 218-4750
Personal property returnsTax Assessors, Personal Property Department(478) 218-4760
City taxes: Warner Robins, Perry, CentervilleEach city's own office(478) 929-1148; (478) 988-2740; (478) 953-4734

Both commissioner offices open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. The county's pay-and-search portal lets you look up taxes online and adds a convenience fee to each payment.

Housing numbers

Houston County has 178,214 people as of July 2025, an 8.9% rise over the April 2020 base. Robins Air Force Base is the largest employer, and sellers in Perry, Warner Robins and Centerville can expect base-connected buyers. The county holds 74,635 housing units and permitted 1,218 more in 2025. Workers travel 22.8 minutes on average.

  • Typical owner-occupied house: $219,800.
  • Homeowners occupy 66.9% of housing, so roughly a third of households rent.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,208.
  • Typical household income: $80,698.

If you rented a house out before listing it, check whether the homestead exemption still applies. The exemption covers property you own and occupy as a legal residence.

A house that sits near the base can draw buyers who plan around a military move date, and they often want a fast closing. Tax payoffs and homestead questions are easiest to settle before such a buyer is under contract.

How the taxable value is set

Fair market value is pinned to January 1, and the taxable amount is assessed value, set by law at 40% of it. A mill is $1.00 for every $1,000 of assessed value. Whenever the Board of Tax Assessors alters a value from last year, or from the figure an owner returned, it must mail a notice.

Real property returns on form PT-50R, plus applications for conservation use, exempt status and similar programs, must be mailed with a US postmark on or before April 1. Personal property returns share that date and are taken by mail only, with forms sent in January to anyone who owns a boat, an aircraft or a business. Call (478) 218-4750 about real estate. Parcel records are searchable on the county's qpublic site.

A seller wondering whether a city levy was paid must call Warner Robins, Perry or Centerville directly, since the assessors do not bill. Confirmation of county and school tax comes from the commissioner.

Check the value on your most recent notice against the house as it is today. Finished basements, added rooms and outbuildings change the record, and so do demolitions. If the record is wrong, the 45 day appeal window is your chance to correct it, and the assessors' phone line is the quickest way to ask what is on file.

Homestead exemption

Submit your first application to the Tax Assessor's Office before April 1 of the year the benefit should start. Approved exemptions roll over annually. You file again only when ownership changes or you want a different exemption.

The statewide standard exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value, and some counties layer larger local exemptions on top. Ask the assessors at (478) 218-4750 which amounts apply to your parcel. A buyer who closes mid-year should ask how the closing date affects first-year eligibility.

To file, gather your deed information and a photo ID, and note the date you moved in. If you bought mid-year, the exemption you inherit does not transfer, so you apply in your own name. Sellers can help by telling buyers about the April 1 cutoff at the contract stage, long before closing.

How to appeal your valuation

Your clock is 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first, re-examines its number and writes back. Unresolved appeals continue to the County Board of Equalization for a scheduled hearing and a ruling at its close. Superior court comes after that, and arbitration can replace the Board of Equalization step.

  • Permitted grounds: whether the property is taxable, the value assigned, or uniformity against similar properties.
  • Excluded: any gripe about the tax rate or amount levied.
  • Hearing officer option: limited to non-homestead real estate over $500,000.
  • Arbitration option: value only, with a certified appraisal.

If a board rules against you, a written notice of superior court appeal is due in 30 days, and unpaid prior-year tax blocks the hearing. Email property tax questions to taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.

Gather the notice, any photos of the house, and sale prices of nearby homes before you call. Bring them to the assessors in Perry if you want to discuss the value in person.

Due dates and who pays at closing

Read your bill or phone (478) 542-2110 for the due date. The statewide default is December 20, which a county may shift to December 1 or November 15 or replace with installments. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked.

Title on January 1 decides who owes, and a seller leaving partway through the year gets no refund under state rules. For a Perry or Warner Robins sale, have the closing agent list county, school and city taxes on separate lines, because the cities send their own bills.

An unpaid bill can lead to a recorded lien and a later auction. Afterward, a twelve-month window lets interested parties redeem by paying the bid, subsequent taxes, special assessments and a 20% premium.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Houston County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

A seller with an open balance should settle it before or at closing so the title is clean.

  1. Call the commissioner in Warner Robins or Perry for the county balance.
  2. Call the city office for any city levy, since those bills come separately.
  3. Ask the assessors whether your homestead and any conservation use filing are on record.
  4. Hand all three answers to the closing agent in writing.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, so the sale can close quickly. That makes it worth having the payoff numbers ready before you accept an offer, not after.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Houston County Tax Assessor mail my bill?

No, the assessors do not handle billing. Phone the commissioner at (478) 542-2110 (Warner Robins) or (478) 218-4940 (Perry) for county bills, and call your city for a city levy.

By when must I file a Houston County homestead exemption?

The cutoff is April 1 of the first year you want the benefit, and the paperwork goes to the assessors. Once approved it carries forward without a new form, until the home changes hands or you ask for a different exemption.

How many days do I get to appeal in Houston County?

The window is 45 days from the day the notice was mailed, and the assessors receive the filing first. Arguing that the tax is simply too high is off the table, while taxability, value and uniformity are fair game.

Where can I visit the Houston County Tax Commissioner?

The Warner Robins office is on Carl Vinson Parkway (number 202), and the Perry office is on Perry Parkway (number 201). Counters stay open every weekday from half past eight until five.

Who pays Houston County tax when a house sells mid-year?

The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and no partial-year refund exists. Ask the closing agent to break out county, school and city lines.

Jackson County at a glance

Jackson County is about 343 square miles, centered on Jefferson, with Braselton, Hoschton, Commerce, Pendergrass, Nicholson, Talmo and Maysville among its towns. Braselton and Maysville extend into neighboring counties. The countywide school district serves most addresses, while Commerce and Jefferson operate city districts of their own. Which one governs your house shows up on the tax bill.

Growth defines this county. Population is 99,265 as of mid-2025, a 30.7% jump over the 2020 count of 75,907, and 79.3% of homes are lived in by their owners.

If you are selling, find out whether your address sits in a city school district before you advertise, since buyers often ask.

Housing numbers

The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $345,000 for 2020 to 2024, typical gross rent is $1,126 and typical household income is $89,544. The county has 35,563 housing units and 28,402 households.

With 1,827 permits in a single year, new subdivisions keep arriving, and an older house is often compared with builder-new ones down the road. A 31.3-minute average trip to work suggests many residents are employed in other counties.

Who bills, who values and who records

Value and payment sit in separate offices, and neither sets the rate. Property Appraisal decides worth; the Tax Commissioner mails the bill and receives the money.

  • Tax Commissioner: 4965 Jackson Pkwy, Jefferson, weekdays from 8 until 4:30; call 706-367-6320.
  • Property Appraisal (Board of Assessors): 67 Athens Street, Jefferson; phone 706-367-6330. Returns, homestead filings and appeals begin here.
  • Real estate records: deeds, plats and liens back to 1796, mailing address PO Box 7, Jefferson, GA 30549, phone 706-387-6251.

Parcel details are also searchable on qPublic through the county's links, though the data is not refreshed daily. When you need a payoff or bill history, phone the Tax Commissioner.

Due date on a Jackson County bill

December 20 is the normal date for real and personal property. The county mails in October and lets the bill be paid for 60 days after the postmark.

Late mailings do occur. In that case the Tax Commissioner treats the day after the date printed on your own bill as the delinquent date. Part-payments are welcome until that due date and are refused afterward.

Billing waits on the state. Around July 1 the county submits its digest to the Department of Revenue, approval typically returns within a week, and only then can the Tax Commissioner bill and collect.

Other services at the Tax Commissioner's office

The Jefferson office is the county's only counter for several different jobs. Beyond real and personal property, it bills and collects mobile home and timber tax, and it is the single place in the county for motor vehicle transactions.

Real property covers land and the improvements on it. Personal property means furniture, fixtures, tools, inventory and equipment used to run a business. If you are selling a house that also holds a home business, ask which of those items were returned for tax, so the file reflects what you actually owned on January 1.

  • Returns for real estate and business personal property are accepted from January 1 through April 1.
  • Georgia tags are renewed within the 30 days before the owner's birthday.
  • A person who cannot come in during office hours can send someone with a limited power of attorney for motor vehicle business.

Key dates in the tax year

January 1 anchors the calendar, because use, condition and ownership on that day drive value and exemptions.

How to appeal a Jackson County value

Begin by mailing the Board of Assessors a written notice of appeal, no later than 45 days after your assessment notice was dated.

When the assessors revise the value, a notice of the revision arrives, and a written appeal on that revision reaches the Board of Equalization; the notice prints its own deadline. When they revise nothing, they report that to you and to the board, and your appeal proceeds without further action. The board schedules a hearing within 15 days of receipt, held 20 to 30 days after you hear from it.

Three members vote on every question raised, and the ruling is sent by registered or certified mail; Superior Court is the next step. A bill printed before the ruling is a temporary one, based on your return value or 85% of the assessors' figure, whichever is higher, with any difference settled afterward.

Selling with unpaid tax

Request a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner before signing, then have the closing office pay it out of your proceeds. An open bill can turn into a recorded FiFa, which costs $25 to issue and record at the county's records office.

Sales that close in autumn can leave the seller named on a bill the buyer will pay, so spell out who covers it in the contract and the settlement statement. For a former rental, an inherited house or an empty one, ask about each earlier year separately.

  1. Phone the Tax Commissioner at 706-367-6320 and ask for the payoff and any prior-year balances.
  2. Check the records office for any recorded FiFa or lien under your name.
  3. Give the payoff in writing to the closing office.
  4. Confirm in the contract which party covers the current year's bill if closing falls before the October mailing.

A cash buyer will usually order a title search quickly, so clearing these items before you accept an offer keeps the timeline short.

Recording fees

The posted schedule charges $25 for each deed. Plats run $10 a page, liens $25, and UCC filings $25, or $50 when an assignment is attached.

  • Plain copies cost $0.50 a page; a certified copy costs $2.50 for page one and $0.50 for each page after.
  • Cards carry a 4% fee; the office also takes cash, money orders and business checks.
  • Any deed that changes ownership needs a PT-61, even when only a name is added or dropped or the property is given away.

The office recommends the FANS alert site at fans.gsccca.org. Staff will explain where to file; legal advice and title searches are outside what they do.

Frequently asked questions

Which Jackson County number reaches the tax office?

Dial 706-367-6320 or 706-367-6325 for the Tax Commissioner, whose office is at 4965 Jackson Pkwy in Jefferson and keeps weekday hours from 8 to 4:30.

Can I pay part of a Jackson County bill?

Yes, until the due date, normally December 20. After that day the office no longer takes partial amounts.

When can a Jackson County owner file for homestead?

Any time of year. A form filed after April 1 counts for the next tax year, and the home must have been your residence on January 1.

How many days do I have to contest a Jackson County value?

Forty-five days after the notice date, which usually lands in late May. Mail the written appeal to the Board of Assessors.

Does the Jackson County Tax Commissioner set the rate?

No. Local governing bodies set rates, and the Tax Commissioner collects. Questions about value belong with Property Appraisal, while questions about a payment belong with the Tax Commissioner.

Jasper County at a glance

Jasper is small and rural. Monticello, the county seat, is the lone city, and Shady Dale is the lone town. The county covers 373 square miles. Public education is a four-school system that includes Jasper County High School.

Population is 17,632 as of mid-2025, up 20.8% from the 2020 count, where the prior decade added only 4.9%. Anyone buying acreage is likely to raise questions on wells, septic and frontage, so have that information ready if you are listing land.

Housing numbers

Owners live in 85.6% of occupied homes here. Across 2020 to 2024 the middle owned home was worth $243,400, middle rent ran $970 monthly and middle household income was $60,134. Count 7,118 housing units, with 124 permits pulled in 2025.

Owner costs run $1,461 a month with a mortgage and $480 without. Commutes average 39.2 minutes, which shows how far the Atlanta metro area pulls. In 2020, 13.7% of the 6,270 housing units were vacant. Compare those carrying costs with the $243,400 middle value when you set an asking price.

Which office answers which tax question

Several hands touch a bill before it reaches you, and the Tax Commissioner's are the last. The commission and school board set millage. The assessors set value. A Grand Jury appointed board rules on disputes. The commissioner mails and collects.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; (706) 468-4902; counter open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4:30.
  • Tax Assessor: signs off on exemptions and notifies owners when it changes a value.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room provides warranty deed copies.

One mill is a dollar per thousand of assessed value, and 40% of market value is the assessed figure.

When a Jasper County bill comes due

Under the usual schedule, land, buildings and business personal property are billed in two halves, due September 20 and December 20. Statewide, December 20 is the standard deadline, and interest holds off until two months after the bill is postmarked.

The 2026 notice departed from that schedule: mailing on October 16, a first installment dated November 20, and the balance dated December 20. Printed dates can differ from year to year, so the ones on your own statement win.

  • Manufactured housing: payment and a location permit by April 1 each year.
  • Missing it brings a 10% penalty and possibly a citation to Magistrate Court or sale of the unit.
  • Vehicles renew during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.

Unpaid tax and your sale

A lien often surfaces just as a sale nears closing. Once a bill sits unpaid beyond 90 days, the county records a tax FiFa at the Clerk of Superior Court and may levy on the property and sell it.

FiFa entries are open to the public, bureaus among them, and the tax office has no control over their use. Clear a recorded lien before closing.

Call (706) 468-4902 to get the balance. If your closing falls between the two installment dates, settle who pays each half and put that in the settlement papers.

  1. Call the commissioner for the current balance and any earlier years.
  2. Ask the Clerk of Superior Court whether a FiFa has been recorded against the parcel.
  3. Decide who pays each installment and write it into the settlement papers.
  4. Bring a copy of your deed, available from the courthouse deed room, if the title has any gaps.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, which leaves tax payoff and lien release as the main items before the deed changes hands.

Exemptions

Every homestead gets two thousand dollars off assessed value. That cut applies to the county, school and State levies, though the portion of the rate paying off bonds is left out.

Jasper County exemptions

How to dispute a Jasper County value

Forty-five days is the limit, measured from the notice date. Take the case to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After either ruling, a written notice sent to the Board of Tax Assessors moves it to Superior Court.

Prepare ahead. During the January 1 to April 1 return period you can state your own opinion of market value, which gives you firm footing if the assessors change it later. Owners of mobile homes get 45 days to file with the assessors, plus 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Refunds and city tax

If tax was charged or collected by mistake or unlawfully, ask in writing within three years of paying to get it back. A claim that grows out of an appealed value is paid after the final taxable value is settled.

City tax is a separate levy. Municipalities tax on their own, and the city clerk sends and collects that bill unless city and county have agreed on one combined bill. Vehicle tax is always collected by the county Tax Commissioner.

Holders of long-term notes secured by real estate must record them within 90 days, at the intangible recording rate of $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of it.

Returns and special programs

The return season for taxable property runs January 1 through April 1. Skip it and the county simply carries forward last year's value and last year's real property exemptions.

Notices go to the last address on file, so report any move. Three programs change how land or buildings are valued.

  • Historic property: a building listed on the Georgia register, plus up to two acres around it, may qualify for preferential assessment.
  • Brownfield sites: land approved for cleanup can hold its value frozen for a decade.
  • Public safety survivors: a surviving spouse who has not remarried, of a firefighter or officer killed on duty, may be fully exempt once the agency's papers are filed.

If your property is in a program, the Board of Tax Assessors can say what a buyer must do to keep the status.

Frequently asked questions

What is the street address for the Jasper County tax counter?

The counter is at 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064. Call (706) 468-4902. It opens weekdays, 8 to 4:30.

What is the deadline for a first Jasper County homestead claim?

April 1 of the first year you want the benefit. A later filing counts toward the following tax year, and you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1.

Does a Jasper County tax lien reach my credit file?

Possibly. Ninety days past due puts a FiFa lien on record with the Clerk of Superior Court, and those entries are public.

How do I get a Jasper County deed copy?

Visit the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the Jasper County Courthouse.

What is the Jasper County appeal deadline?

Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice. After a ruling, written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors sends the case to Superior Court.

Jeff Davis County at a glance

Jeff Davis County is farm and timber country in southeast Georgia. Hazlehurst, the biggest town, holds the county seat, and Denton is the one other incorporated city. The county has an estimated 15,219 residents as of July 2025, up 3.0% from the 2020 count of 14,779.

Prices run low. For 2020-2024 the middle value of an owned home is $118,300, and owners live in 71.3% of the homes. County builders took out just nine permits in 2025, which leaves resales with little new competition. You will mostly be up against other older houses, and your likely buyer is a local who knows the area. A Hazlehurst house, a rural place by a crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each draw a different crowd, so judge each against its own comparable sales.

Who to call about Jeff Davis County property tax

Start at the Tax Commissioner, 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Letters go to PO Box 558, and the counter closes at 4:30 on weekdays. You can also pay through an online portal. Close to a deadline, ask the staff how to pay so the check does not arrive late.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends and collects bills, hands out mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: sets values and receives appeals
  • Board of Equalization: the Grand Jury names its members to rule on value disputes
  • County commissioners and the school board: choose the millage rates

Have the parcel number or owner's name ready when you call, plus the mailing address you want bills sent to. The commissioner does not set your house's value or the millage rate, so a value complaint belongs with the assessor.

Due dates and penalties

Bills usually go out October 20 and come due December 20, and you may pay in pieces before then. Once that date passes, interest accrues each month at the bank prime rate, and a further 5% penalty lands every 120 days until the total reaches 20%. A balance left for a year grows noticeably, and any payoff quote goes stale fast.

  • Mobile homes are billed in January and due April 1, and a decal goes on the home once you pay
  • After April 1 the home picks up a 10% filing penalty and 1% a month, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • If you own the land under a mobile home, it can be homesteaded and is taxed as real property

Mobile home dates vary from one county page to another, so phone the Tax Commissioner for yours before counting on April 1.

Homestead exemption

The base exemption deducts two thousand dollars from assessed value. It reduces county and school tax, and does not touch municipal school levies or bond debt.

The application window runs January 1 to April 1, and you file at the Tax Commissioner's counter between 8 and 5 on weekdays. Georgia law allows no extension, so if you miss April 1 you go without the exemption that year. After approval it renews on its own until your situation changes, and it can never exceed the tax owed.

Three other programs cover land and buildings:

  • Conservation use, including residential transitional land
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

Every one of them binds the owner, by covenant with the Tax Assessor, to keep the qualifying use going for ten years or longer. Thinking of selling enrolled land? Call (912) 375-6624 and ask what a new owner would have to honor.

How to appeal your assessment

Your appeal is a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors, sent within 45 days of the notice, and it should say which appeal route you want. Spring is when notices for real and personal property normally arrive.

The county hears four complaints: the parcel is not taxable, the value is wrong, it is assessed out of step with similar parcels, or an exemption was refused. Complaining about the millage rate or the size of the bill is not a ground. If you file a return during the January 1 to April 1 window and give your own opinion of the January 1 market value, your appeal rights survive a later change to the figure. Mobile home owners get 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days after a notice of change, to reach the Board of Equalization.

Returns and spring notices

Taxable property gets reported to the Tax Assessors Office between January 1 and April 1. Skip the filing and the prior year's value and real property exemptions simply continue.

Appraisers study recent sales and conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice shows what the county thinks each parcel is worth. Read it the day it arrives. The 45-day appeal clock starts on the notice date, not on the day you open the envelope.

  • Report a new mailing address fast, because notices go to the last address on file
  • Approved exemptions renew yearly until eligibility changes

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff, and let the closing office pay it from your sale proceeds. Interest runs monthly and penalties step up every 120 days, so an old quote may come up short. Request the number near closing, and again if the date slips into another month.

The order is simple: get the payoff, have the closing office pay it, and keep the receipt. A FiFa on the clerk's docket is public record. Any title search finds it, so it has to be cleared before the deed passes.

Timber land may owe timber tax, billed by the same office. If your mobile home sits on rented ground, confirm the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A cash buyer skips lender appraisals and repair haggling, though the payoff, title search and recorded deed all still happen.

Refunds, city tax and recording tax

Tax assessed or collected by mistake, or illegally, can be refunded. Ask in writing, no later than three years after you paid. If an appeal lowers your value, the refund follows once the final taxable value is set.

Both Hazlehurst and Denton may levy a city property tax, and the city clerk usually sends that bill unless city and county agreed on a single combined one. Vehicle tax is collected only by the county Tax Commissioner. Voters can also approve a freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory, applied for in the same window as returns.

If you buy or finance land, a long-term note secured by the property must be recorded within 90 days. The state recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 of face amount or fraction of it.

Frequently asked questions

When is Jeff Davis County property tax due?

December 20. The usual mailing date is October 20, and partial payments are accepted up to the deadline.

How do I reach the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?

Dial (912) 375-6622 or visit 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. For valuation, phone the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

What does paying late cost in Jeff Davis County?

Interest each month at the bank prime rate, and 5% more every 120 days until the penalty hits 20%. A mobile home paid after April 1 owes 10% plus 1% monthly.

When can Jeff Davis County owners claim homestead?

From January 1 through April 1 for that tax year. Georgia law offers no extension.

What is the appeal deadline in Jeff Davis County?

You have 45 days from the date on the notice. Send a letter to the Board of Tax Assessors naming the route you choose.

Jefferson County market snapshot

Jefferson County covers 530 square miles of mostly open country, with fewer than 30 residents per square mile in 2020. Louisville is the seat and largest city, and Avera, Stapleton, Wadley and Wrens are the other towns. Households average 2.58 people.

Prices are low and the headcount is shrinking. The midpoint value of an owner-occupied home is $105,400 for 2020-2024, and the mid-2025 estimate of 15,011 residents sits 4.5% under the 2020 base.
