With 24 permits in 2025 and 7,148 housing units at the 2020 count, 13.7% of them vacant, you are mostly competing with other older houses. Price off recent local sales rather than figures from ten years back. Where buyers are few, clean tax records and tidy paperwork help a listing move.

Who handles what in Jefferson County

Payments and bill questions go to the Tax Commissioner, 736 Peachtree Street, Louisville, GA 30434, telephone (478) 625-7736. The counter is open 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays. For the worth of a parcel, call the Tax Assessor at (478) 625-8209.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills for land, business equipment, vehicles, mobile homes and timber
  • Board of Tax Assessors: receives returns, homestead forms and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: its record center supplies warranty deed copies and runs the FANS alerts, at (478) 625-7922

The county commissioners and the school board set millage. The Tax Commissioner has no vote on it.

Due dates and penalties

Land, buildings and business personal property are generally due November 15. If the bill is still open 90 days later, a 10% penalty is added. A homesteaded bill under $500 escapes that penalty.

Past that point the office can levy on the parcel. Staff treat that as a last resort and would rather collect another way, so if you are behind, calling early gives you the most options.

  • Mobile and modular homes have their own due date, so call the Tax Commissioner and ask which one applies to yours
  • A mobile home's tax for the year must be paid in full before a location permit is issued
  • Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday

Owners with an approved homestead exemption may also see a one-time state homestead relief grant as a line on the bill. Rentals and homes without an exemption were left out of it.

Returns and the homestead exemption

If you hold taxable property on January 1, file at least one return between January 1 and April 1. After that, real property returns roll over at last year's value until you buy more land or build.

Business personal property works differently. Form PT-50P is filed every year, and items you have sold must be reported or the tax keeps coming. If you file a return stating a lower value and the assessors decline it, that is where your appeal begins.

  • First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed to the Tax Assessor's Office
  • The office takes homestead forms any time of year, but one that arrives after April 1 starts a year later
  • An approved exemption stays in place until you move, sell or ask for another kind
  • A denial comes in writing, with the right to appeal

Where a local exemption is larger than the state's, the local one controls. The assessor's office can quote the amounts now in force.

How to appeal a Jefferson County value

When a notice of changed value arrives, mail the Board of Tax Assessors a written appeal. Call the Tax Assessor to confirm the deadline printed on your notice, and file early rather than late.

Three arguments are open to you: the property should not be taxed, the value is wrong, or it is out of line with comparable parcels. A complaint about how much tax was levied is turned away. The assessors review your letter and answer. If you still disagree, the County Board of Equalization holds a hearing, and Superior Court comes after that. Arbitration can stand in for the board, and the assessors' office will explain how to pick it.

Farm, timber and historic property

Active farmland may be assessed at 30% of market value instead of the standard 40%. Conservation use is a second route, and it values farm, timber, sensitive or transitional land by its present use.

  • Covenant: the owner promises the Board of Tax Assessors to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years, and applications are due in April
  • Standing timber: untaxed until sold or cut, then taxed at full market value times the millage rate
  • Historic buildings: a register-listed structure and up to two surrounding acres can get preferential treatment

If you own acreage, talk to the assessor before listing so you know what the covenant asks of a new owner.

Clearing tax before closing

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff figure and have it paid at the closing table. A bill more than 90 days old already carries the 10% penalty, so a stale number will be too low.

The Clerk of Superior Court runs FANS, a free service you opt into that alerts you when records are filed against your property. Sign up before you list so a lien cannot show up in the middle of a contract.

For an inherited or former rental house, ask for each earlier year's balance separately so nothing older is missed. A cash buyer still wants the payoff settled and a clean recorded deed, though the sale skips lender appraisal and repair requests.

What to bring and what to expect

Most Jefferson County tax errands are quick if you arrive prepared. Bring the parcel number or the name on the deed, your mailing address, and a copy of the warranty deed if you just bought the property. For a deed copy, the Clerk's record center is the place to ask.

When you sell, expect this order: payoff request, payoff paid at closing, deed recorded, then a new owner's return to the assessors. Tell the Tax Assessor's office about the sale so bills follow the right owner.

Sellers of timber land should also know that standing timber is untaxed until it is cut or sold. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a pending sale or harvest changes what is owed this year. The same goes for a mobile home sitting on the lot: settle its permit and its year's bill before the buyer's lender asks for proof.

Frequently asked questions

When are Jefferson County property taxes due?

Generally November 15 for land, buildings and business property. After 90 days a 10% penalty applies.

What phone number reaches the Jefferson County Tax Commissioner?

(478) 625-7736. The office is at 736 Peachtree Street in Louisville, with counter hours from 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays.

Is there a penalty on a small homesteaded Jefferson County bill?

No. The 90-day penalty skips homesteaded property whose bill is under $500.

When can a Jefferson County owner apply for homestead?

The deadline for the year is April 1. The office takes applications through the year, though a later one starts a year after.

Which office answers questions about value in Jefferson County?

Call the Tax Assessor at (478) 625-8209. The Tax Commissioner only bills and collects.

Selling in Johnson County

Wrightsville is the seat of Johnson County, and the 1895 courthouse anchors an older downtown that appraises differently from the farmhouses outside town. Expect listings to be acreage, wooded tracts or a farmhouse past the pavement. Land area is 303.02 square miles, with 30.3 residents per square mile in 2020.

Adrian is a quirk worth knowing. Its boundary with Emanuel County zigzags through town, so neighbors on one street can owe tax to different counties. Match an Adrian-area parcel to its county before you phone a tax office.

Home values are low and buyers are mostly local, many of them retired. A house priced near the $94,900 median draws more calls than one priced like a Macon listing, and financing often comes down to small loans or cash.

Johnson County housing and population

The county lost 791 residents between the 2010 and 2020 counts, and the 2025 estimate wins back only part of that. Some 88.5% of people were in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is slow.

Monthly cost of owning

Owners who still have a mortgage report median costs of $1,193 a month. Owners with the house paid off report $440. With median rent at $647, a paid-off home costs less per month than a rental.

A tax surprise stands out against a $440 monthly budget, and a delinquent balance adds interest at a pace that is hard to absorb on a fixed income. Asking for a payoff early gives you a number to plan around before a buyer appears. The tax commissioner's site also accepts online payment, which helps owners who live elsewhere.

Which office to call

Two tax offices share the building at 2484 West Elm Street, Wrightsville, ZIP 31096.

  • Tax Commissioner, (478) 864-2565 ext. 1: sends bills, takes payments, supplies payoff numbers and renews tags. Counter hours are weekdays, 8 until 4:30, and the commissioner's website accepts online payment.
  • Tax Assessors, (478) 864-3325 ext. 2: set value, take returns and exemption forms, and receive appeals. Search parcels through the assessors' qPublic page.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 2557 East Elm Street, (478) 864-3484: holds recorded deeds.
  • Probate Court, (478) 864-3316: opens an estate when the person named on the deed has died.

The commissioner's page on the county site carries one unusual notice. Owners whose timber was damaged and then cut after Hurricane Helene can seek relief with a form from the Georgia Forestry Commission, attaching the documents it lists and delivering the packet to the commissioner. Anyone selling woodland should ask whether a claim exists for the parcel.

Due dates

Georgia's fallback deadline is December 20, but counties may substitute December 1, November 15 or installment billing. Call the commissioner at (478) 864-2565 ext. 1 to get the date that applies to your bill.

Interest waits until 60 days after the postmark, and penalties may follow on late balances. The bill is addressed to the owner, so a lender holding escrow may never see a copy. Heirs should update the mailing address in writing.

If you are unsure whether you have paid, phone the commissioner with the parcel number before you list. A clean receipt in hand makes a buyer's title search shorter and keeps a closing from stalling over a small old balance.

Spring closings raise a common question: does the bill shift to the buyer? It does not. The owner on January 1 carries that year's tax, and nothing is refunded for a mid-year move, so the purchase contract has to divide it.

How an assessment dispute works

A Johnson County notice shows two numbers: the fair market value set for January 1, and the 40% slice of it that is actually taxed. An owner who buys or improves a parcel files a return during the first quarter, through April 1. Value left off a required return draws a 10% surcharge plus interest.

A challenge begins with a letter to the assessing board, postmarked within 45 days after the notice went out. The letter has to pick a path: an equalization board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or superior court. The assessors can supply the state form.

Tax paid by mistake can be reclaimed through a written request filed inside three years. A refund that follows a won appeal is issued automatically.

Homestead exemption

Johnson County has no local homestead exemption, so the state's own exemptions are the only choice.

  • You qualify by owning the house and living in it as your legal residence, with the assessors deciding.
  • A form arriving after April 1 waits for the following year.
  • Once approved, the exemption continues until you move, sell or switch types.
  • Business personal property is returned every April 1, changed or not.
  • Mobile homes need a location permit within 30 days of being set, then a yearly renewal from January 1 through April 1.

To apply, take proof that you own the house and live in it to the Tax Assessors office at 2484 West Elm Street, and bring a copy of the deed if you recently bought. If you plan to sell soon, filing before April 1 still matters, because it lowers the bill that the January 1 owner carries for the whole year.

Business inventory can qualify for a freeport exemption where voters approved one. Request it at the assessors' desk during the return window.

Selling with unpaid tax

Ask the commissioner for a written payoff figure, then have the Clerk of Superior Court's records searched for any lien on the parcel. Parcels that stay delinquent can reach the sales listed on the commissioner's tax sales page.

At the table, the closing agent pays the commissioner from what the seller would otherwise receive, and the lien clears as the deed records. A house passing through an estate has to go through Probate Court first. A buyer paying cash and taking the home as-is can absorb repairs, but the payoff, the recorded deed and any estate paperwork still happen.

If the seller has died, the Probate Court at (478) 864-3316 is the first call, since the person named on the deed cannot sign. Allow time for that step before you set a closing date.

A short checklist helps. Get the payoff in writing, confirm no lien is recorded, settle any estate filing, and tell the assessors about the change of owner so the next bill goes to the right person.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the Johnson County tax bill?

The commissioner's office at 2484 West Elm Street in Wrightsville mails it, and (478) 864-2565 ext. 1 reaches that desk. One bill carries the county, school and state levies. A question about the value itself goes to the assessors at (478) 864-3325 ext. 2.

Does Johnson County add a local homestead exemption?

No. Only the statewide exemptions are available, and the form has to reach the county by April 1 of the first year.

What is the Johnson County appeal window?

Owners get 45 days, counted from the day the notice went in the mail. The challenge is a letter to the assessing board naming the path you want.

What is a typical home worth in Johnson County?

About $94,900 at the median, based on 2020-2024 Census estimates for homes their owners live in. Renters pay a median of $647 monthly.

Does a January closing move the year's tax to the buyer?

Only if the contract says so. Whoever held title on January 1 owes the year, and the closing statement is where the parties divide it.

Buyers include commuters, and the county also draws people interested in historic houses around Clinton.

Median owner-home value$194,500

There are 10,786 households of about 2.63 people each, and 92.4% of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Census medians for owner costs are $1,483 a month with a mortgage and $470 without, against $964 for rent.

Offices to call about Jones County taxes

Walk in at 166 Industrial Blvd. in Gray between 8 and 4:45, or write to P.O. Box 417, Gray, GA 31030.

  • Tax Commissioner, 478-986-6538: bills, payments, mobile home decals, plus timber and heavy-equipment tax. Look up a parcel or pay on jonescountytaxes.com.
  • Board of Tax Assessors, (478) 986-6300: value, returns and exemption forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, courthouse deed room: copies of a recorded warranty deed.
  • Gray City Hall, 478-986-5433: a city bill kept separate from the county's, paid at 109 James Street or mailed to P.O. Box 443.

The Clerk, not the commissioner, collects the intangible tax due when a buyer's lender records a security deed. A house inside Gray gets two property tax bills every year, a county one and a city one, and each has to be paid separately. Neither office can take payment for the other.

Before you call, have the parcel number or the owner's name handy. For a payoff, ask the commissioner to confirm in writing the amount, the good-through date and whether mobile home, timber or equipment tax is included. For anything about value or exemptions, the Board of Tax Assessors is the right desk, and a first-time owner should ask which forms to bring to the courthouse deed room.

Due dates and late payments

Land, house and business personal property bills normally go out by October 1 and come due December 1. After that, the county adds 1% interest per month, counted at close of business on the first day of each month.

Ninety days past the deadline, a penalty is added, and the commissioner can tell you the exact percentage when you ask for a payoff. Homesteaded houses with a bill under $500 are excused from it. After that point the office may file a fifa lien with the Clerk and eventually levy on the property.

  • Mobile homes are billed around January and due April 1. Late ones risk a 10% penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale
  • You may pay part of a bill, but interest keeps running on the unpaid rest
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jones County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exemptions for Jones County homeowners

Local legislation here stacks on the state exemptions. The county's tax pages list these amounts.

  • A $2,000 standard homestead off assessed value, which reaches county and school operating levies and the state levy but not bond debt.
  • A $15,000 local school break for anyone who turned 62 by January 1, and no income limit.
  • Two elderly breaks that depend on income: as much as $10,000 off school tax at 62, and as much as $4,000 off all levies at 65. Each is limited to households with $10,000 of net income.
  • A disabled veteran exemption worth up to $63,780. An unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in armed conflict can claim it as well.
  • A floating exemption for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $30,000 or less. It takes the place of other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that a first-year bill can go up.

New owners should bring a warranty deed, and the form must reach the office by April 1. Homeowners 62 and older earning $15,000 or less in gross income may defer their tax until the property changes hands, or until the deferred amount plus interest hits 85% of fair market value. Farmland can be assessed at 30% in place of 40%, and each preferential program carries a 10-year covenant. Because exemptions change what a buyer will owe, a seller should ask the assessors which of these are attached to the house before listing.

How to challenge a valuation

The clock is 45 days from the notice date. Send the case to the county equalization board or to an arbitrator, and if you lose, take it to superior court by giving notice to the assessors. You may argue that the property is not taxable, that the value is wrong, that it is not uniform with similar parcels, or that an exemption was refused.

A return filed from January 1 to April 1 can carry your own opinion of value, and that protects your appeal rights if the assessors later change the number. If you file nothing, the county assumes you are returning the same property at last year's final value. For a mobile home, the appeal window is 45 days from the bill mailing, followed by 21 days after a revised notice to get before the equalization board.

Selling a Jones County house

Call the commissioner for a payoff dated near closing, and call Gray City Hall too if the house is in town. The January 1 owner is liable for the whole year even when the sale closes in spring, so the contract should say who reimburses whom. Bills go to the homeowner rather than the mortgage company, so check that nothing slipped through before you list.

Here is how it normally goes: get the payoff, order the title search, clear any fifa or other lien that turns up, and pay the tax from proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can close fast, though the title search still has to return clean. With a mobile home, make sure the decal and the April 1 bill are current. With farmland in a preferential program, phone the assessors about the 10-year covenant before you sign a contract. Keep every receipt, because a buyer's attorney may ask for proof that each year's bill was paid.

Frequently asked questions

When must Jones County owners pay their real estate tax?

December 1, with bills mailed around October 1. Interest of 1% a month starts once the date passes.

Which owners qualify for the $15,000 Jones County school exemption?

Anyone 62 or older as of January 1. The amount reduces school operating and school bond tax, and there is no income test.

Where is my Jones County deed on file?

Recorded deeds sit in the courthouse deed room in Gray. The Clerk of Superior Court can provide copies.

How big is the late penalty on Jones County taxes?

A penalty applies after 90 days. Call 478-986-6538 for the exact figure on your bill. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused.

How much is a typical Jones County house worth?

The 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied houses is $194,500. Tenants pay a median of $964, and the median household brings in $75,500.

Lamar County market snapshot

Lamar County lies between Atlanta and Macon, and Barnesville is the seat. It is the fastest growing county in this part of Georgia: the July 2025 estimate of 20,941 residents is 13.2% above the 2020 count, which was 18,500. Land area is 183.50 square miles. Gordon State College and the Barnesville Expo Center give the town some steady local draw, and pecan and peach groves cover much of the farmland.

Prices have moved up with the population. The median owner-home value is $216,500 and the typical commute is the longest around at 31.8 minutes each way. With 136 permits pulled in 2025, an older Lamar County house will be shopped against new construction.

An owner with a mortgage pays a median of $1,469 a month, and one without pays $526. The county has 7,133 households of 2.60 people on average, and 92.5% of residents did not move in the past year.

Property tax offices in Lamar County

Barnesville hosts every office a seller needs.

  • Tax Commissioner: 790 Veteran's Pkwy, Barnesville, GA 30204; mail to P.O. Box 850; phone (770) 358-5162. Walk-in hours are Monday through Thursday, 8 to 4:30, and Friday, 8 to 4:15, with a drive-thru that closes 15 minutes earlier.
  • Tax Assessor, (770) 358-5161: values, appeals and homestead forms, Monday to Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday 8 to 4.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse.

The commissioner's website accepts online payment of property tax and car tag renewals. The commissioner neither sets values nor chooses millage, so a complaint about a high figure goes to the assessors.

Due dates and late charges

Lamar County mails bills by mid-September and wants payment by November 15, a schedule in place since the 2018 tax year. That is five weeks ahead of Georgia's December 20 default, which surprises owners new to the county.

  • Late real estate and business personal property bills collect 1% interest per month.
  • Amounts still open 90 days after the deadline take a 10% penalty.
  • A lien (fifa) goes on file once taxes are over 30 days late, and credit bureaus may see it.
  • Mobile homes are due April 1. Late ones pick up a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly, and can be auctioned.

State guidance puts the start of interest 60 days after the bill's postmark, so keep the envelope. A refund request for tax paid in error must begin inside three years.

Homestead exemptions

The assessors take forms from January 1 to April 1 and cannot extend the window, so a late filer loses that year. Once approved, an exemption renews itself. Carry a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit.

  • State types carry codes: S1 regular homestead, S3 elderly at 62, L4 elderly at 65, S5 disabled veteran and SS surviving spouse of a veteran, the last two requiring VA proof of 100% service-connected disability.
  • Over 65: Lamar takes $20,000 off the county operating levy, nothing else.
  • Over 70: $7,000 comes off school operating tax and school bond tax.
  • Disabled owners: $15,000 off school operating tax when combined household income is under $20,000, documented by two physicians or a Social Security letter that declares 100% disability.

You must meet the state rules before any local break applies. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 may also defer tax. For a mobile home to count as a homestead, the home and the land under it must have the same owner.

How to appeal a value

County appraisers lean on recent sales, measured at January 1, and the spring notice shows the result. An owner who objects has 45 days from the notice date and may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. The letter goes to the assessing board and picks a route. Cases that go to the Board of Equalization are heard by a panel the Grand Jury appoints.

Before you file, pull the sales of similar houses near yours and compare them with the value on the notice. The assessors set value as of January 1, so sales close to that date carry the most weight. Put your reasons in the letter, name the route you want, and keep a copy with proof of the mailing date.

Farm and historic programs

Landowners have preferential programs. Lamar cites section 48-5-7.4 for conservation use and residential transitional land, 48-5-7.4.1 for agricultural land and 48-5-7.2 for rehabilitated historic property, and every one asks for a covenant of 10 years or more. Enrolled acreage needs a call to the assessors before the deed changes hands, so a new owner knows what the covenant requires.

Selling with taxes owed

Request a payoff that folds in interest and penalty, and check with the Clerk for a recorded fifa. The closing agent pays out of the seller's share and secures the release. January 1 ownership decides who owes the year, so most contracts prorate.

When the owner has died, the county Probate Court can explain how to open the estate before a listing goes up. Cash buyers in Barnesville or the rural parts of the county will still expect the payoff settled at closing. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, which can shorten the timeline, but the title work and the recorded deed take the same steps.

In practice the steps run in this order. Phone the Tax Commissioner at (770) 358-5162 for the payoff. Ask the Clerk's deed room whether any lien is on record. Have the closing agent pay the commissioner at the table, and keep the receipt for your files.

What to bring to the office

A trip to the Tax Assessor or Tax Commissioner goes faster with a few things in hand. For a homestead filing, bring a driver license and either your 1040 or a signed income affidavit. For a disabled veteran or surviving spouse exemption, bring the VA proof of 100% service-connected disability. For a disabled owner's school break, bring the two physician statements or the Social Security letter.

Buyers who recently closed on a Lamar County house should file their own homestead form before April 1, since the state rules apply first and the local breaks for older owners come after. Owners 62 and up with gross household income at or below $15,000 can ask the assessors how tax deferral works before they list the house.

Frequently asked questions

When is Lamar County property tax due?

November 15. Bills normally go out by September 15, and mobile homes are due April 1.

What do late Lamar County payments cost?

Interest of 1% per month after the due date, plus a 10% penalty at 90 days. A lien can be recorded after 30 days.

Do older Lamar County owners get extra relief?

Yes. Past 65, $20,000 comes off the county operating levy, and past 70, $7,000 comes off school operating and bond tax, once the state rules are met.

What does a typical Lamar County house cost?

About $216,500, the 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied homes. The county had an estimated 20,941 residents in July 2025.

Who accepts Lamar County homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor's office, from January 1 through April 1. Bring a driver license and a 1040 or signed income affidavit.

When is payment due?

December 20 is the baseline in Georgia. Counties may move it to December 1 or November 15 or divide the bill, so call the Tax Commissioner at (229) 482-3795 for the date on your bill.

Interest is held back for 60 days after the postmark, and penalties can attach to what stays open. A sale in February does not move the burden: whoever held title January 1 owes the year, and Georgia refunds nothing for partial-year ownership. Liens for unpaid county tax are recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which is where a title examiner will look.

Mobile homes keep a separate schedule. A location permit is due within 30 days of placement and renews between January 1 and April 1, and the January 1 owner returns the home to the commissioner by April 1.

  • A form that lands after April 1 misses that tax year.

An exemption renews itself only until ownership or residence changes, so a buyer moving in files a fresh application by April 1. As the seller, ask the commissioner whether your exemption was active so the closing figures reflect it.

How to appeal a value

A real property notice goes out every year, and you have 45 days from its mailing to dispute the fair market value. The first step is a letter to the board of tax assessors. Email counts only if the county has a written policy consenting to electronic service, so mail it unless the assessors confirm otherwise at (229) 482-2090.

The letter must name a route: the county's equalization board, a hearing officer or an arbitrator. A uniform state form exists, and Revenue Department staff cannot overrule the local decision on one parcel.

Selling when back taxes are owed

Request a payoff from the commissioner and ask whether a lien is on file. If the buyer finances, the lender's security instrument is recorded within 90 days, and the state recording tax is $1.50 per $500 (or fraction) of the note.

Heirs should talk to Lanier County Probate about opening the estate before listing. Out-of-town cash buyers can generally accept a payoff deducted at the closing table.

The sequence is short. Get the payoff, check the Clerk for a lien, close, and let the closing attorney pay the commissioner from proceeds. Keep the paid receipt with your closing papers, and tell the assessors about the sale so the next bill reaches the new owner.

Before you list a Lanier County house

A few errands save trouble later. Pull your parcel record on qPublic to confirm acreage and the owner of record, then call the Tax Commissioner for a current payoff and the Tax Assessor to confirm your exemption status. If the house sits on land with a farm or woodland history, the Extension Office can answer questions about how the land has been used.

Tell buyers up front what the yearly tax has been, and keep copies of the last few bills in your listing folder. At the Tax Commissioner, 56 W Main St, Suite 1, Lakeland, GA 31635. The phone is (229) 482-3795, and the office is open weekdays 8 to noon and 1 to 5.

Georgia's baseline of December 20 applies unless the county picked December 1, November 15 or installments, so call (229) 482-3795 to confirm. Interest starts 60 days after the postmark.

No. State exemptions and the disabled veteran exemption are available if the application arrives by April 1.

How much is a house worth in Lanier County at the median?

$162,300, the 2020-2024 Census median for owner-occupied homes. Rent runs $913 a month at the median, and 73.2% of housing units are owner-occupied.

Is an emailed Lanier County appeal accepted?

Selling a Dublin-area house in Laurens County

Dublin hosts the offices that set and collect your bill. Laurens County covers 807.34 square miles of land, and its headcount grew from 48,434 in 2010 to an estimated 51,041 in July 2025.

Owners live in 64.3 percent of the county's 22,277 housing units, and a typical owned home is worth $154,500. Middle household income is $55,010. Builders took out just 102 permits in 2025, which leaves resale houses doing most of the work for newcomers.

What happens to an unpaid bill

Trouble starts about a month after the bill falls due. A tax fifa can then be filed with the Clerk of Superior Court, and because the filing is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

  • Rely on the due date printed on the bill you receive.
  • A recorded fifa can stall a title search, which is why a payoff request belongs before your listing agreement.

Request your account history before listing photos are taken. A complete file helps a buyer's lender. If a mobile home sits on the lot, make sure the location permit was issued, since it waits on full payment of that year's tax, and keep the permit with your papers.

How to dispute a Laurens County value

Put it in writing to the Laurens assessors, inside 45 days of the notice date, and pick a route. Choices: the Board of Equalization with Superior Court behind it; a hearing officer, open only to non-homestead real property over $750,000; or arbitration on your own certified appraisal, which ends the matter.

Call 478-272-6443 for the form. If you file a return between January 2 and April 1, you can state your own number, and that return keeps your appeal rights alive when the assessors change the figure again. The reasons that count are taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. A high tax total does not count.

Exemptions and land programs

The homestead exemption comes first. File by April 1 if you owned the house and lived there on January 1. It continues until you relocate or the deed changes.

Older owners and landowners have more to choose from:

  • An extra exemption at age 62, then relief from the state share at 65 on the house plus up to 10 acres.

  • Farm assessment at 30 percent in place of 40, plus Conservation Use, each tied to a 10 year covenant.

Land applications go to the assessors by April 1. Phone the commissioner first to confirm which office takes your homestead form. One in five Laurens residents is 65 or older, so many sellers hold breaks that the buyer must request again.

Who pays the tax in the year of a sale?

Whoever held title on January 1. Georgia pays no part-year refunds, so the Laurens contract and closing statement must handle the split.

  1. Ask the commissioner if the current bill is out and paid.
  2. Have your closing attorney credit the buyer for the months after the sale.
  3. Expect your exemption to lapse when title transfers.
  4. Tell the buyer to file a fresh application by April 1.

Warranty deeds sit in the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court at the Laurens courthouse. A clean paper trail reassures buyers in a stable market.

Property tax returns

Everyone who owns taxable property on January 1 files at least once. In Laurens the return window runs January 2 through April 1, and forms are available at the Tax Commissioner's office in Dublin.

After the first filing the return renews on its own. You file again only when you add property, improve an existing parcel or want to declare a different value. If you are listing a house, a return on file shows buyers you have kept up with the county, and it is one less thing the buyer's attorney will chase.

Before you list a Laurens County house

Gather the papers a buyer's attorney will ask for, and keep them in one folder. That means your latest bill and proof it was paid, the last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork, proof of your exemption if you hold one, and the deed. Warranty deeds can be copied from the Clerk of Superior Court's deed room, so there is no need to hunt for a lost original. Ask at the courthouse counter for a certified copy if your lender or title company requires one.

Call the commissioner at 478-272-6994 and ask for an account history showing every year, then call the assessors at 478-272-6443 to confirm your exemption is active and the acreage on file is right. If the house was a rental or came through an estate, ask about each earlier year separately so no old balance surprises the title examiner.

Some Laurens properties include land. Farm and conservation assessments are tied to a covenant, and the forest program runs 15 years on tracts past 200 acres, so a buyer needs to know before closing whether the covenant stays in place. Talk to the assessors about what happens to enrolled land when the deed changes.

Frequently asked questions

Who sets values in Laurens County?

The assessors, at 478-272-6443. The tax commissioner, at 478-272-6994, bills and collects. Use the first number for any question about what your Laurens house is worth.

What share of market value gets taxed in Laurens County?

Forty percent. The exemption is subtracted from that amount and the millage rate is applied to the rest.

Is April 1 the cutoff for a Dublin homestead application?

Yes. A form that arrives later starts the exemption the following year.

What if I miss the 45 day appeal window on a Laurens notice?

The ordinary appeal is gone. Note the date on each notice and call the assessors in the first week.

Can a Laurens mobile home get a location permit before the tax is paid?

No. That year's tax must be paid in full first, and April 1 is the due date.

Selling a house in Leesburg and Lee County

Lee County has grown quickly, from 28,298 people in 2010 to an estimated 34,179 in mid-2025, on 355.88 square miles of land. Leesburg holds both tax offices, so most paperwork for a sale starts there.

Owners live in 74.2 percent of the county's 13,411 housing units, and the middle home is valued at $231,800. Median household income is $89,168, and the typical trip to work takes 23.1 minutes. Builders pulled 94 permits in 2025. Buyers with that kind of income read a tax bill closely, so have the latest copy ready.

Costs run above the neighboring counties. Lee owners pay a median $1,605 a month with a mortgage and $532 without, against $1,184 for renters. There are 12,287 households averaging 2.66 people, and 88.1 percent of residents stayed in the same house for a year. Most Lee owners stay put, so a seller who documents taxes and exemptions stands out. Bring the last bill, the deed and any exemption letter to the first meeting with your closing attorney.

Lee County tax offices

Both offices are in Leesburg. The commissioner neither sets values nor sets rates.

Lee County property tax offices
OfficeAddressPhoneOpen
Tax Commissioner100 Starksville Avenue North, Leesburg 31763 (P.O. Box 9)229-759-6015Weekdays, 8 to 4:30
Tax AssessorCourthouse Annex, 104 Leslie Highway, Suite B, Leesburg 31763229-759-6010Weekdays, 8 to 5

Three board members serve three year terms by appointment of the county commissioners, and the board picks the chief appraiser. The board meets on the second Monday of each month at 4:30 p.m. in the Leslie Highway office. The county site links to online property records and a request form for withholding records from public view.

Due dates and how payments count

December 20 is the general due date. A mailed payment counts on a USPS postmark, and a postage meter stamp does not, so mail early. You can also pay online.

Interest and penalties after that date follow O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 and 48-2-44. A parcel left unpaid can be levied upon and sold.

Lee has issued refund checks to the owner of record on January 1 rather than to mortgage or escrow companies. A buyer who closed afterward should check the closing papers for any share, because the commissioner will not divide a check between the two parties. If escrow paid your bill, pass the refund to your servicer so it can be credited back. Escrow customers can ask the assessors for a letter to send their servicer, and a complaint about how refunds are issued belongs with your county commissioner.

Contesting a Lee County value

Lee appraisers look at recent sales and conditions on January 1, and notices usually go out in spring. Appeal in writing to the board within 45 days of the notice date, and say how you want it heard.

The case can go to the Board of Equalization and then Superior Court, or to arbitration. The appeal cannot be about the amount of tax levied. Returns go to the board from January 1 through April 1. Keep your notice, because it states how to file and holds the date your 45 days start from. If the board changes your value after you file a return of your own, that return is what keeps your appeal open. Standing timber is taxed only when sold or cut, at 100 percent of market value. For value questions, ring 229-759-6010.

Exemptions you can claim or pass along

Lee adds local exemptions to the state set, and whichever amount is larger controls. The application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, due April 1.

  • First-time owners bring a copy of the warranty deed.
  • Your driver's license has to show a physical Lee County address, because a post office box is refused.
  • Once granted, it carries forward until you change residence or ownership.

The county's tax page prints the whole menu, from the $2,000 standard exemption through elderly school and general exemptions, disabled veteran relief, a floating exemption and a deferral program, each with income limits. Brownfield sites can have their value frozen for a decade, and manufacturers apply for Freeport before April 1.

Who owes the tax in the year you sell

The January 1 owner, because no part-year refund exists in Georgia. Your closing attorney divides the bill.

  • Phone 229-759-6015 to see whether this year's bill is out and paid.
  • Request a payoff for any open balance.
  • Tell the buyer to file a fresh homestead application, because yours ends with your ownership.

If timber stood on your land, file the county's timber sale or harvest report, which both office pages link to. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, but the payoff, the title search and the recorded deed work the same way.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lee County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Filing a property tax return

File with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1, the same window as the homestead deadline. A real property return renews each year at the value set the year before, so a second filing is needed only after you add property, build or want to declare a new figure. Personal property returns must be refiled every year.

Owners who disagree with the board's number can declare a different one on a new return, which opens the appeal process if the board does not accept it. Call the assessors at 229-759-6010 for forms. A seller who has just built or added property should file in the same window, so the record matches the house a buyer sees.

Before you list a Lee County house

A little preparation shortens the closing. Put these in one folder before you meet your closing attorney: the latest tax bill, the deed, any exemption letter, your last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork. Lee County buyers tend to have strong household income, and they will ask what the yearly bill runs.

Call the commissioner at 229-759-6015 to confirm this year's bill is out and paid and to request a payoff for anything open. Call the assessors at 229-759-6010 to check your exemption and the property record. The county site has online property records you can search yourself, and a request form exists if you want records withheld from public view.

Plan on the mail too. Send any paper payment well before the due date, because only a USPS postmark counts, and keep the receipt. If your mortgage company pays through escrow, ask whether it received the bill, since notices follow the owner and the lender may not see them.

When a Lee County sale closes in spring, the January 1 owner is still responsible for the whole year, so the contract should say how the buyer reimburses you. Your closing attorney will handle the split, but you set the terms when you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay my Lee County tax bill?

At the commissioner's office, 100 Starksville Avenue North in Leesburg, by mail to P.O. Box 9, or online on the Lee tax site.

Does a postage meter stamp count on a Lee payment?

No. Lee accepts a United States Postal Service postmark only. Mail early or pay online.

Who receives a Lee County refund check on a house that sold?

The owner of record on January 1. The commissioner does not split checks, so buyer and seller settle it themselves.

What do first-time Lee homeowners bring to file a homestead exemption?

A copy of the warranty deed and a driver's license showing the Lee County address.

Can I appeal a Lee value only because my tax rose?

No. The appeal must rest on taxability, value or uniformity, or a denied exemption, filed within 45 days of the notice.

Liberty County market snapshot

Hinesville anchors Liberty County, which has grown quickly: 70,313 residents for July 2025 is 7.7 percent above the April 2020 base. The county spreads across 516.47 square miles, with 126.3 people per square mile at the 2020 count. Seven taxing areas share the county, each carrying its own proposed rate, so pin down which one your house falls in.

Owners occupy only 50.9 percent of the housing units, so moves are common and only 80.7 percent of residents stayed at one address for a year. Renters pay a median $1,246, and the typical owned home is valued at $201,500. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,500 a month. Builders took out 355 permits in 2025. There are 23,998 households averaging 2.70 people, with a median household income of $60,456.

A house that has been a rental raises questions about its tax history and homestead status, so settle both with the offices below before you list. Military families are a real part of the buyer pool here, and an organized tax file helps the paperwork move.

Liberty County tax offices

Bills go to the tax commissioner and values to the assessors, and both work out of 100 Main Street in Hinesville. The commissioner's site takes online payments, and the office still accepts them in person or by mail at Suite 1545 (ZIP 31313). Call 912-876-3389.

Assessors work from Suite 1550 at the same address and answer at 912-876-3568. Their phone menu is split this way:

  • Option 1: administration, which covers homesteads and general information.
  • Option 2: mapping, GIS and specialized assessment.
  • Option 3: personal property, including prebill mobile homes, vehicles, boats, business inventory, aircraft and commercial property.
  • Option 4: real property appraisers.

The county's Official Assessment Documents page lets you pull a property record card or a real property assessment notice by typing a parcel number, with a separate search if you do not know yours. The assessors also take email at Tax.Assessors@libertycountyga.gov.

Proposed 2026 millage rates

The county commissioners proposed 19.4000 mills for the unincorporated area and lower rates inside most cities. Your bill is the final word on the rate that applies to your house.

The proposed levy change is 1.32 percent for the unincorporated area and 6.15 percent for Hinesville. Midway and Riceboro show 100 percent only because both set a city rate for the first time in 2026. FLOST, the Floating Local Option Sales Tax, collected from January to June, trims the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills.

Rollback rates are the levels that would raise last year's revenue from the new digest: 19.1460 mills for the unincorporated area, 16.3300 for Hinesville, 17.6830 for Flemington and 18.9030 for Walthourville. Public hearings are required wherever a proposal tops its rollback rate. Ask the commissioner which rate applies to your bill.

Notices and appeal rules

Most notices are mailed in May, and the appeal clock is 45 days from the notice date. The notice is no bill, and the exact deadline is printed on it.

The calendar the assessors publish looks like this:

  • Homestead applications and real property returns: January 1 to April 1.
  • Prebill mobile home bills: mailed around February 1, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Annual notices of assessment: mailed in May, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Personal property returns: mailed around December 22 and returned between January 1 and April 1.

Taxes themselves are not qualifying grounds for an appeal. Owners with 10 acres or more of agricultural, forestry or environmentally sensitive land may qualify for a specialized assessment, and the mapping option on the phone menu handles that and any splitting or combining of parcels.

Expect a visit. Staff inspect a property after a homestead application, a return, an appeal, a purchase or a permit, and when it has not been seen in more than three years. They measure, photograph and note features. State code 48-5-264.1 lets appraisers go onto land outside the buildings, and they are expected to carry visible identification.

Homestead exemption

You qualify if you own the land and the home and live in it, and the application deadline is April 1 of each year. Call 912-876-3568 and press 1 to ask what documents to bring.

The state formula takes 40 percent of market value as the assessed figure and subtracts the $2,000 standard exemption before millage applies. Some counties add bigger local amounts, so ask the administration desk about Liberty. Millage differs by area, so the same exemption is worth a different sum in Hinesville than in the unincorporated area.

Your exemption follows you, and the house loses it when you sell. A buyer who will live in the property should file soon after closing, and by April 1 of the first tax year.

Selling with taxes to settle

Find out if the year's bill is issued and paid, then settle the split at closing. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year under state rules, and a part-year owner gets nothing back.

The commissioner's online system lets you search records and pay, and a printout can serve as proof of payment for a buyer's lender. With about half of Liberty's units owner-occupied, a tenant may live in the home you are selling. If so, hand the buyer the lease and the tax status together. Call 912-876-3389 about any open balance, and have your closing attorney account for it.

Plan the order: confirm the bill is paid, request a payoff for anything open, give the buyer the exemption status in writing, and let the closing attorney handle the split. A cash buyer can close quickly, but the same tax questions still come up.

Before you list a Liberty County house

Pull your record card first. Type the parcel number into the Official Assessment Documents page, check the acreage, the building description and the owner of record, and call 912-876-3568 if anything looks wrong. Then call the commissioner at 912-876-3389 to confirm the year's bill is paid and to request a payoff for any open balance.

Put the folder together before the first showing: the latest bill, proof of payment, your last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork, and proof of your exemption. If a tenant lives in the home, add the lease. A buyer from the military community may close on a tight schedule, so having these ready keeps the closing on its date.

If the house has a mobile home on the land or other personal property, ask the assessors' personal property desk, option 3 on the phone menu, how it is billed. Staff may also visit after a purchase or a permit, so tell the buyer to expect an inspection and to keep the assessment notice that follows.

Frequently asked questions

Who values property in Liberty County?

The Liberty County Assessors Office values it, at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550 in Hinesville. Call 912-876-3568 and press 4 to reach the real property appraisers.

When must I file a Liberty County homestead application?

By April 1 each year. Real property returns use the same January 1 to April 1 window.

Does a Liberty County assessment notice demand payment?

No. It explains the appraised and assessed value, and the 45 day appeal period runs from its date.

Where can I view my Liberty County record card?

Type your parcel number into the county's Official Assessment Documents page.

Does sales tax reduce Liberty County property tax?

Yes. FLOST receipts collected from January to June cut the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills.

Lincoln County market snapshot

Lincoln County is small, with 8,112 residents, and the county seat, Lincolnton, hosts both tax offices on Humphrey Street. Expect short phone queues. Residents past 65 make up 28.1 percent of the county, and 93.9 percent of people kept the same address for a year. Builders took only 55 permits in 2025. Median monthly costs for 2020 to 2024 are $1,597 for a mortgage holder, $500 for a paid-off owner and $786 for a renter, and median household income is $56,907.

The one-way drive to work averages 31.2 minutes, which is long and narrows the buyer pool. A seller who prices with that in mind and hands over a clear tax record will see fewer stalled deals. Retail and lodging activity is small, so most buyers are people who already live nearby or work elsewhere.

Lincolnton tax offices

Humphrey Street holds both. The commissioner works from the courthouse address and the assessors from the county government office.

The Board of Tax Assessors values every Lincoln County parcel, and its page links to the qPublic property search on its assessors' page. Board meetings are the third Tuesday of each month at 5:30 p.m. in the courthouse conference room, with any change posted on the courthouse bulletin board and the assessors' front door.

How to pay your bill

You may pay at the window, by post or online. Cash, personal and cashier's checks, money orders and the four major card brands are accepted. Make paper instruments out to the Lincoln County Tax Commissioner.

  • The county adds 3 percent to each card or online payment, so ask the office whether any fee applies to cash, checks or money orders.
  • The mailing address is P.O. Box 946, Lincolnton, GA 30817.

The state sets December 20 unless the county picks something earlier or splits the bill into installments, so read the date on your own bill. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark. Pay early if you can, because a late balance complicates a sale.

How to appeal a valuation

An appeal is a written letter to the assessors, postmarked within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. Three paths exist under state law: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer and an arbitrator, and the Department of Revenue cannot overrule any of them on one parcel.

If the Lincoln assessors have a written policy on electronic service, an appeal may be emailed. Ask at 706-359-5502. Returns of property go to the county tax office from January 1 to April 1. Skip a year and you are treated as having filed last year's figure again. Keep the notice itself, because it states how to file.

Exemptions, refunds and permits

The deadline to file for homestead is April 1 of the first year you want relief, and skipping it counts as a waiver. Ask the commissioner whether Lincoln has any local amount above the state's.

  • Refunds: a written claim for tax assessed in error must begin within three years of payment, and an appeal win triggers a refund automatically.
  • Mobile homes: the commissioner issues the location permit, requested within 30 days of placement.

City tax is separate. A city clerk bills it unless the city and county have agreed to one combined bill, so ask which applies.

Selling with taxes to settle

Make sure this year's bill is paid and hand the proof to the buyer. Whoever owns the house on January 1 owes the entire year, and a sale in midsummer brings no part-year refund.

  • Call 706-359-5536 for any open balance.
  • Tell the buyer your exemption does not carry over.
  • Ask the closing attorney whether a city bill exists beside the county bill.

With over a quarter of residents past 65, many Lincoln sellers hold an age-based exemption, and the buyer applies separately.

Look up your parcel before listing

A qPublic link on the assessors' page opens online property records, and the office at 182 Humphrey Street takes calls at 706-359-5502 if you would rather ask. Read the record before you list, so nothing in it comes as a surprise to you or the buyer.

Check three things on the card: the acreage, the building description and the owner of record. If any looks wrong, call the same number.

What to gather before listing

A buyer's attorney will ask for a handful of papers. Keep them together and the closing goes faster.

  • The latest tax bill and proof it was paid, from the commissioner on Humphrey Street.
  • Your last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork.
  • Proof of your exemption, if you hold one, so the buyer knows what ends at closing.
  • The deed for the parcel.
  • Any mobile home location permit, if a manufactured home sits on the land.

Builders took out only 55 permits in 2025, so a ready file can set your listing apart from other homes on the market. A cash buyer can skip lender appraisal and repair requests, but the payoff and the recorded deed still happen.

A step by step timeline for a Lincoln County sale

Selling a house in a small county moves best when you work through the offices in order. Start in January through April if you can, because that is the window for returns and homestead filings, and the assessors will have time to answer questions.

  1. Call the Board of Tax Assessors at 706-359-5502 and confirm the acreage, building description, exemption status and owner of record on the parcel card.
  2. Call the Tax Commissioner at 706-359-5536 and ask whether the year's bill is out, whether it is paid, and what any open balance is.
  3. Find out if the city also bills the property. A city clerk bills separately unless city and county agreed to one combined bill.
  4. List the house, and give your buyer's attorney the folder of papers described above.
  5. At closing, have the attorney pay any open balance from your proceeds and divide the year's tax between you and the buyer.
  6. Tell the buyer to file a new homestead application by April 1, because yours ends with your ownership.

Georgia gives no part-year refund, so the contract is the only place the split can be settled. If the house came to you through a family estate, the buyer will want the tax and exemption history in writing, and an organized record will keep the deal from stalling.

Weekdays from 8 to 4:45 at 210 Humphrey Street.

Yes, 3 percent on card and online payments.

Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice, judged by postmark.

Which day do Lincoln bills come due?

December 20 by default, unless the county sets another date. Your bill states it.

Can I get back tax I overpaid in Lincoln County?

Possibly. A written claim has to begin within three years of paying.

  • Long County Board of Commissioners: 468 S. McDonald Street, Ludowici. The board sets the county millage rate at a called meeting. The office works Monday through Thursday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, and has been closed on Fridays since January 26, 2026.

The state's Department of Revenue splits the questions the same way. Bills and payments go to the commissioner. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the assessors. Call the wrong desk and you will get a quick referral to the right one.

Long County at a glance

Long County is rural, mostly farm and forest, with Ludowici as its only city and the county seat. Fort Stewart takes up the northern tip and supplies civilian jobs and a steady stream of renters and buyers. Aimar, Beards Creek, Donald and Tibet are unincorporated, so owners there deal with the county for permits and tax questions.

The county grew fast. Its mid-2025 estimate is 21,557 residents, up from 16,168 in the 2020 count. There are 7,798 housing units, and 65.2% of homes are owner-occupied. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $218,300. Builders pulled 275 permits in 2025, and new construction and added improvements feed the tax digest.

Tax digest and millage rate

The county's five-year history shows a taxable base that keeps growing and a county rate that moves in steps. The net digest rose from about $328.8 million in 2021 to about $546.0 million in the 2026 figures. Net maintenance and operation millage is 17.802 mills in the 2026 presentation.

Long County net digest and net M&O millage, 2021 to 2026 (county levy only)
YearNet digest valueNet M&O millage
2021$328,796,57315.597
2022$375,334,21614.748
2023$391,934,56514.738
2024$402,074,61318.707
2025$515,644,14418.707
2026$546,043,75317.802

The county's levy reflects reductions from Property Tax Relief Local Option Sales Tax proceeds, also called FLOST, which are applied against property tax. County voters approved FLOST in 2025, and the combined sales tax rate in Long County became 9% on January 1, 2026.

The 2025 rate came with a notice of a tentative increase of 20.72 percent: 18.707 mills against 15.496 mills without the increase. School and state levies sit on top of the county figure, so the rate on your own bill is the one that counts.

The 2026 digest has a gross figure of $791,914,814 and exemptions of $245,871,061, which leaves the net value in the table. Exemptions stood at $104,458,820 in 2024 and $234,837,877 in 2025, so the jump in the net base in 2025 came with a much larger exempt share. Real and personal property made up $774,693,757 of the 2026 gross. Motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber are small slices.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Long County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and payment

Long County due dates follow the digest rather than a fixed calendar date. For the 2025 bills, real estate taxes were due May 12, 2026, and mobile home taxes were due June 1, 2026 instead of the usual April 1, because the digest came out late. The state default is December 20, or 60 days from billing, and a county may choose another date.

Read the due date printed on your bill, and ask the commissioner's office when the next mailing goes out.

  • Property returns are accepted from January 1 through April 1.
  • Mobile home tax is normally due April 1.
  • Payment runs through the newer site linked from the commissioner's page.

How to appeal your assessment

You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice is mailed. Put the appeal on paper for the Long County assessors, using the uniform form the state provides.

That first filing is where you pick a route: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue officials have no power to overrule any of those bodies, or Superior Court, on one property's appraisal. Where a county has adopted a written policy accepting electronic service, the appeal may be emailed. Ask the assessors whether Long County has done so, and use longcoappr@longcountyga.gov if it has.

Valid grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, equal treatment with similar parcels, or a turned-down exemption. Before filing, pull your parcel on qPublic and compare it with recent sales nearby. Bring those sales to the conversation with the assessors.

Homestead and other exemptions

The standard state homestead exemption takes $2,000 off the assessed value, which Georgia sets at 40% of market value. The home must be your main residence on January 1.

  • Some counties take homestead filings at the commissioner's desk and others at the assessors. Ask Long County which one applies.
  • Local exemptions can exceed the state one. The assessors can list them with their age and income limits.
  • Farm, timber and conservation assessments rest on a covenant signed with the assessors, so confirm eligibility before assuming acreage qualifies.

If you added a room, a barn or a garage, compare your January 1 value with the parcel record to make sure the improvement is described correctly.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Long County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

The January 1 title holder owes the full year, and a sale on January 2 changes nothing with the state. No refund goes to partial-year owners, so buyer and seller divide the bill in the sales contract.

  1. Ask the commissioner for a payoff amount that includes any interest or penalty.
  2. Give the closing attorney the current bill and that payoff figure.
  3. Check whether a tax lien (a fi fa) has been recorded against the parcel. Payoff or release is needed before a buyer can take clean title.
  4. If a bill reaches you after closing, forward it to the new owner.

An inherited, behind-on-tax or tenant-occupied house in Long County follows the same steps. A cash buyer can close quickly, but the lien still has to be paid at the table. Call early, since a figure quoted weeks ahead can grow as interest adds up.

Frequently asked questions

Which Long County office answers questions about my bill?

Billing and payment questions go to the Tax Commissioner at 912-545-2127, or by mail to P.O. Box 628 in Ludowici. Value, exemption and appeal questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office at (912) 545-9111.

How long is the Long County assessment appeal window?

Forty-five days from the day the notice was mailed. File on paper with the county assessors and name your chosen route in that first filing.

Has the Long County millage rate gone up?

Net M&O millage was 14.738 in 2023, 18.707 in 2024 and 2025, and 17.802 in the 2026 presentation. Sales tax relief proceeds are applied against the levy, so use the rate on your bill.

Is any tax refunded when a Long County home sells mid-year?

No. The January 1 owner owes the whole year, so the buyer and seller settle the split in the sales contract.

Where can I search a Long County parcel online?

Use the qPublic property search linked from the Tax Assessor's page. It shows parcel records, and the assessors' office can explain any value you find.

Where to pay and ask questions

Lowndes County runs its property tax out of Valdosta, with the commissioner and the assessors answering different questions. Bills, payments and liens go through the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs go through the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. Counter service runs 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM on weekdays. Drivers have a separate lane that opens half an hour later and closes at 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County tax assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Deed room run by the Superior Court clerk, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, ground-level 1st Floor: copies of your warranty deed.

A payment box for drivers stands on the right side of the Government Building's front lot. If you mail a check, write the bill number on it and include a return envelope if you want a receipt.

Lowndes County housing at a glance

Lowndes sits in south Georgia, with Valdosta as its center and roughly 497 square miles of land. The mid-2025 population estimate is 122,867, up 3.9% from 118,259 in 2020. There are 54,425 housing units, and owners occupy 56.9% of homes. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $215,600, so a large share of the county rents, which matters if you are selling a rental or a house with a tenant. Builders pulled 804 permits in 2025.

Due dates and penalties

Tax on land, buildings and business equipment is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails each bill two months or more before that date, and bills usually reach mailboxes in early October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges
EventRule
Property returnsFiled from New Year's Day through April 1
Homestead applicationMust reach the office by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessmentForty-five days after the notice date
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15, with weekends and holidays pushing it to the next day the office is open
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of the tax once 120 days pass, added again every 120 days until 20% is reached
Penalty exceptionA homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00
Lien (FiFa)Recorded by the court if the bill stays unpaid

A mailed check avoids interest only if the postmark falls on or before the due date. Owners can pay in two installments, though interest and penalty attach to whatever remains open after the due date. The office warns that the date may change, so use the one on your bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lowndes County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How values are set and challenged

The taxable slice in Georgia is 40% of market value, known as assessed value, and the Lowndes assessors reset it each year. From New Year's Day through April 1, an owner may file a return declaring a proposed value. Should the Board of Assessors see it differently, a notice with the board's own number goes out, usually in May.

Contesting the figure gives you 45 days counted from the notice date. The first hearing belongs to an equalization board or an arbitrator. Still unhappy afterward? Written notice to the assessors moves the case to Superior Court.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • One mill raises a dollar on every thousand dollars of assessed value. The county and the school board each vote a rate every year.

Exemptions come off the assessed figure and the millage rate multiplies the remainder. Your current bill shows the Lowndes rate in force.

From deed to tax bill

The cycle opens when a sale closes and its deed is recorded in Valdosta. The assessors then give the parcel a value and mail a notice the following May. When the appeal period closes, they compile the tax digest, an official listing of every owner, street address, legal address, property location, exemption, assessment and tax due. State revenue officials approve that digest before the commissioner prints bills.

Personal property follows a separate track. Boats and motors, tractors, farm equipment and machinery count, and so do furniture, fixtures, equipment, inventory and supplies for a business. Ownership is settled as of New Year's Day, appraisers mail their values every year, and owners get the same 45 day appeal window.

The commissioner hears about a transfer through the recorded deed. If your closing statement prorated the tax, hand that statement to the commissioner yourself.

Ways to pay

Four ways work: the counter, the mail, the drive-up box and a credit card. The card company, not the county, adds a convenience fee: 2.57% on Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% on American Express, each with a minimum of $1.50.

Past-due notices are mailed at set intervals, not monthly, so check the balance before you send money. Interest accrues monthly until the balance clears, and a lien can stay on a credit record for at least seven years.

If taxes stay unpaid beyond 90 days after the due date, the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before that point about the exact balance and your options.

Who owes the bill when you sell

Whoever held title when the year began gets the bill. A lien is recorded in that person's name unless the commissioner has a contract or closing statement in hand, no more than 90 days after the due date, showing the new owner took on the tax. If tax was prorated at closing, take the signed statement to the Patterson Street office.

State revenue rules put the whole year on the January 1 owner, and a sale the next day earns no refund. Once the deed transfer reaches the office, the buyer may be billed as well.

  1. Get the payoff figure from the commissioner.
  2. Have the closing attorney settle it at the table.
  3. Forward any later bill to the new owner.

A house inherited from a relative or occupied by tenants follows the same path. A cash sale skips the lender's payoff wait, but the tax still has to be settled at closing.

Exemptions and special programs

A home qualifies for homestead and business inventory qualifies for freeport. Who owns and lives in the property on January 1 settles eligibility, and the assessors take the filing.

  • Applications are taken year-round, though one arriving after April 1 applies to the following year.
  • Approval carries forward each year at the same address, and a move requires a fresh filing.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption. Ask the commissioner for the form.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

A mobile or modular home counts as personal property, so its owner files a return each year if it sits in the county.

Frequently asked questions

What is the usual Lowndes County due date?

Generally November 15 each year for land, buildings and business equipment. The commissioner cautions that it can change, so check your bill.

What does a late Lowndes County payment add?

Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty begins at the 120-day mark, recurring on that cycle until it totals 20%. A homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00 escapes the penalty.

Does the Lowndes County commissioner take cards?

Yes. The card company adds its own fee, 2.57% for Discover, Mastercard and Visa and 3% for American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each. A drive-up box is also available.

Who pays the tax if I sell my Lowndes County house mid-year?

The person who owned the home on January 1 is liable for the whole year, and there is no refund for a later sale. Settle any split in the closing statement and bring a copy to the commissioner.

How long does a Lowndes County owner have to contest a value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. An equalization board or arbitrator hears the case first, and written notice to the assessors keeps it alive for Superior Court.
