Lumpkin County tax offices

Two offices sit at 99 Courthouse Hill in Dahlonega, a few suite numbers apart. One handles value and exemptions. The other handles billing and collection.

Lumpkin County property tax offices
OfficeHandlesLocationPhone and hours
Tax CommissionerBilling, collection, payment questions99 Courthouse Hill, Suite E, Dahlonega, GA 30533706-864-2666; weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm, closed 1:00pm to 1:30pm; fax 706-867-6010
Board of Tax AssessorsValues, returns, exemptions, appeals99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, Dahlonega, GA 30533706-864-2433; weekdays 8am to 5pm; fax 706-864-9806

You can search, view and pay property tax on the commissioner's website. Bills go to homeowners only and never to lenders, so if your taxes are escrowed, send a copy to your mortgage company.

Homes and buyers in Lumpkin County

Dahlonega is the county seat. Lumpkin County has an estimated 36,178 residents as of mid-2025, up 8.0% from 33,486 in 2020, spread over about 283 square miles of land. It has 14,302 housing units, and owners occupy 76.3% of homes. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $307,900, and builders pulled 270 permits in 2025.

About 20.6% of residents are past 65. That matters at tax time, because several exemptions in the county's flyer begin at 62 or 65.

What Lumpkin County bills and what lateness costs

December 1 is the due date for houses, land and business equipment. It was December 20 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it up.

  • After the due date, a 5% penalty arrives at the 120 day mark and returns every 120 days until the total reaches 20%.
  • Past 90 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can go on record at the courthouse.
  • Levy on the property is possible, though the commissioner calls it a last resort.
  • Credit bureaus can see the lien, and the tax office has no control over how they use it.

Mobile homes run on their own calendar, so an owner of one should phone 706-864-2666 for that date. A location permit is issued only after the current year's mobile home tax has been paid in full.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lumpkin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal a Lumpkin County value

Three routes exist, and each begins with a written appeal filed within 45 days of the notice date. Grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, uniformity, or a refused exemption.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors look first and may revise the value in a new notice, which the owner has 30 days to contest. Otherwise it goes automatically to a hearing, and Superior Court is the next stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser takes value or uniformity disputes on non-homestead real property above $500,000, or on certain wireless property above that same level.
  • Arbitration: the owner submits a certified appraisal, and the assessors either accept it or certify the appeal to the Clerk of Superior Court for arbitration.

The state provides a uniform appeal form, and you name your chosen route in that first written filing. Unsure which fits your case? Call the assessors at 706-864-2433 before filing.

Before you file, gather a few recent sales of similar homes nearby and note anything wrong in the parcel record, such as square footage or a feature the house does not have. Specific evidence gives the board something to act on.

Exemptions and special assessments

The standard state homestead exemption subtracts $2,000 from assessed value, set by law at 40% of market value. You qualify by owning the home and living in it on January 1. Applications can go in all year, but one received after April 1 starts with the following year. Owners who reach 62 can apply for an additional exemption.

The county's tax information flyer, last dated 2021, also describes local and special programs. Ask the assessors for the current amounts before you rely on any of these.

  • School tax break for owners 62 and over whose federal adjusted gross income is at most $20,000: $30,000 off assessed value.
  • Owners 65 and up, or permanently disabled: as much as $120,000 off for school tax and $60,000 off for county tax, covering the home and at most 5 adjoining acres.
  • Agricultural preferential assessment: qualifying land is assessed at 30% instead of the usual 40%, under a 10-year covenant that carries penalties if broken.
  • Forest land conservation use: 200 acres or more in total, with parcels of 100 acres or more inside the county.
  • Tax deferral: owners 62 or older with household income under $15,000 can postpone the tax, which is different from an exemption.

A conservation use application (PT-283A) needs a notary's signature and must go in by April 1 with a $25.00 recording fee, because the original is recorded at the courthouse. A senior application should enclose a state ID showing birth date and address, and a disabled veteran application needs the VA letter showing a 100% combined rating.

Forms and field inspections

County appraisers make field inspections across Lumpkin County under state law. They carry identification, drive marked vehicles, measure exteriors, take photographs and note improvements. Entering a home is generally unnecessary, and you do not need to be present. Commercial and industrial appraisals are handled for the board by McCormick Solutions, a division of LMC, Inc, whose staff wear county-issued badges you can ask to see.

Forms can be downloaded from the state revenue department's site and mailed in, and the assessors ask for a USPS postmark no later than April 1. They include the state homestead form, the business personal property return (PT-50P), the freeport application (PT-50F), the marine (PT-50M) and airplane (PT-50A) returns, and PT-50R, the taxpayer return of value used to ask for a review.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lumpkin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

State law puts the full year on whoever owned the parcel January 1, and a mid-year sale earns no refund.

  1. Before listing, phone the commissioner at 706-864-2666 and ask what is still owed on the parcel, interest or lien included.
  2. Hand that number to the closing attorney.
  3. Clear any unpaid fifa before closing.
  4. Send any bill that reaches you after closing to the buyer.

An inherited, tax-delinquent or rented house goes through the same sequence. Ask the assessors early whether a senior exemption or deferral is attached to the account, since it can change what is owed at the closing table. A cash buyer will still expect the lien cleared.

Bring your closing statement, your most recent bill and the parcel number when you visit the commissioner's office. If the tax was prorated between you and the buyer, the signed statement shows who took on the bill. Keep the receipt for any payment you make, since the closing attorney will ask for proof that the account is current.

Frequently asked questions

When is Lumpkin County property tax due?

December 1 for houses, land and business equipment. Before a December 2009 resolution by the county commissioners, the usual date had been December 20.

How long is the Lumpkin County dispute window?

Forty-five days after the notice date. Send a written filing to the assessors at 99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, and say which route you pick.

Does Lumpkin County send my bill to my mortgage company?

No. Bills go to the homeowner, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account should send a copy to the mortgage company.

When must a Lumpkin County homestead application arrive?

The assessors need it by April 1 for it to count this tax year. A later one starts with the following year.

Which office should a Lumpkin County seller call first?

Start with the commissioner at 706-864-2666 to learn what is owed. Use the assessors at 706-864-2433 for value or exemption questions.

Where to go in Danielsville

Everything runs out of the Government Complex at 91 Albany Avenue, the former Danielsville Elementary School building. Property Valuation sits upstairs in Suite 404 and speaks for the Board of Assessors. The Tax Commissioner is in Suite 14.

The split is simple. Disputes over worth, acreage on the record or a missing exemption go to Property Valuation. Questions about the amount owed or a cleared check go to the commissioner. The county's home page also links a public parcel lookup run through qPublic.

Madison County tax desks at the Government Complex
OfficeSuitePhoneOpen

Tax Commissioner14706-795-6385Mon to Fri, 8 to 4:30

After hours, a drop box behind the complex takes checks. The commissioner's counter is the one place in Madison County that bills land, mobile homes and timber.

Madison County in brief

Madison County works as a quiet suburb of Athens, Commerce and Elberton. Carlton, Colbert, Comer, Danielsville, Hull and Ila are the six towns. About 23 percent of the acreage is prime farmland, so many sales here involve acreage as well as a house.

The estimated population was 32,919 in July 2025, up 9.3 percent from April 2020. Of 11,242 households, 76.9 percent own their home. A typical owned home is valued at $219,700 and a typical rent is $972. Builders took out 130 permits in 2025.

How appraisers set a house value

The starting point is market value on January 1, and the taxed slice is 40 percent. County appraisers lean on comparable sales, on rebuilding cost with depreciation subtracted and land added, and on rent-based math for income property.

Notices arrive between April and May. Read yours as a preview of the later bill. If you plan to list in spring, open it the day it lands, because the objection clock starts on the notice date.

Returns go to Property Valuation during the first three months of the year. One return keeps working until a garage goes up, acreage is added or the owner wants a different value on record.

  • Field appraisers measure buildings and photograph them, wearing photo ID and driving marked county vehicles.
  • Conservation use and similar specialized assessments need an application on file by April 1.
  • Madison County counts only the Postal Service postmark when judging whether a return, homestead form or appeal was on time.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Madison County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Billing dates and payments

Bills usually go out in September, and December 20 is the usual deadline. The counter takes partial payments, so a seller can chip away at a balance before closing.

Mobile home statements go out in late January with an April 1 deadline. A mobile home that has a homestead exemption skips that early statement, and its tax rides on the year-end property bill.

State rules allow 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts, and a local government may shift the official date. Timber is taxed once, at full market value when cut or sold, with payment going to the commissioner in the county where the trees grew.

Ask the commissioner's staff for a written payoff on your parcel before signing a contract. A closing attorney will want that number.

How to appeal a Madison County value

Mail a written appeal so it is postmarked within 45 days of the date on the notice. Property Valuation refuses faxes, emails and any other electronic delivery, because it cannot confirm who sent them or what value was under appeal.

The process has four steps. First, a letter with the parcel number, the reason and a phone number. Second, a staff review and possibly an appointment. Third, notice of a change, or an automatic move to the Board of Equalization (or arbitration, if you asked for it up front). Fourth, Superior Court for whoever is still unhappy.

  • Grounds that count: value, taxability and equalization. Complaints about the size of the bill do not.
  • The Board of Equalization is drawn from people eligible for grand jury service and charges nothing.
  • Arbitration costs each side its own arbitrator plus half of a third.
  • The court filing fee quoted by the county is $25.
  • A recent state law bars the assessors from altering a board or court result for two years unless they inspect the property or a return is filed.

The county welcomes recent sale information and photos of comparable homes. Miss the window and that year's appeal rights are gone.

Homestead exemption codes

The county sorts homestead relief into letter codes. S1 means an owner-occupied principal residence, with the owner holding title to both home and land. S3 and L3 apply from age 62 with income under $10,000 for the applicant and spouse, leaving out Social Security and retirement pay. L4 starts at 65 and L5 at 70, with no income test at all.

S5 is for a veteran rated 100 percent disabled or the unremarried surviving spouse. SG is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed on duty, and SS is for the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in action.

File between January 1 and April 1 after owning and occupying the home on January 1. The three-member Board of Assessors meets monthly to act on homestead, conservation and preferential status requests, so a late application waits for the next cycle. Colbert has its own city exemption that you request from the town. For the other five towns, ask the city clerk whether a separate city levy exists.

Someone who buys your house has to apply in their own name, so do not count the exemption as part of what you are selling.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Madison County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling: who pays what

The county taxes whoever held title on January 1. A June closing can still leave the seller holding a December bill, which is why the contract language and the closing statement matter.

The state adds a transfer tax at recording. Georgia's revenue department sets it at $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents per further $100, charges it to the seller by default, and refers questions to the Clerk of Superior Court.

Properties once sold at a Madison County tax sale may have money waiting. The Tax Commissioner posts an excess funds list and takes claims on an application form.

  • Get the payoff figure on paper ahead of closing.
  • Make sure your exemption ends once the deed records.
  • Mail your forwarding address so later notices reach you.

If you plan a cash sale, the same steps apply. Ask the commissioner for the payoff, confirm the exemption comes off at transfer, and keep the receipt. Buyers and title companies often ask for proof that the current bill is paid before they fund, and a written payoff from the commissioner answers that question quickly.

Frequently asked questions

What day do Madison County property taxes come due?

Expect a September mailing and a normal deadline of December 20 for land, houses and business property. A mobile home has its own April 1 deadline. If the printed date on your bill differs, believe the bill.

Is an emailed appeal accepted in Madison County?

No. Madison County wants paper, mailed so the postmark lands within 45 days of the notice date. Fax and electronic submissions are turned away.

Which office decides what my Madison County house is worth?

The Board of Assessors does, with Property Valuation staff doing the fieldwork. Value is outside the Tax Commissioner's role.

Does a new owner keep my homestead exemption?

No. A buyer has to apply personally, with January 1 to April 1 as the window. Anything filed after April 1 first helps in the next tax year.

Can I pay part of a Madison County tax bill?

Yes. The commissioner's office takes installments of any size on a property bill. Request the balance in writing so you know the exact remainder at closing.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who does what in McDuffie County

Three separate bodies touch a McDuffie County tax bill. The Board of Assessors, working out of the Tax Assessor's Office, judges taxability, value and equalization. Billing, collecting and passing money to other governments belong to the Tax Commissioner. When the assessors will not budge, the Board of Equalization, a citizen panel appointed by the Grand Jury, hears the dispute.

Reach the assessors at 706-595-2128, in person weekdays 8 am to 5 pm. That office sets values only, so a question about a statement goes to the commissioner. Returns are also filed with the assessors.

  • Value, returns, exemptions and homestead filings: the Tax Assessor's Office.
  • Statements, payments, liens and excess funds: the Tax Commissioner.
  • Millage: voted each year by the county commissioners and the school board, so neither tax office controls it.
  • A rejected appeal: Board of Equalization or arbitration, then Superior Court.

Budget and millage hearings meet at the McDuffie County Government Center, 210 Railroad Street, Thomson.

McDuffie County housing

McDuffie County is a small, steady county in the Augusta metro area, west of Columbia and Richmond counties, with Thomson as the seat and Dearing the only other town. Interstate 20 crosses it along with US 78, US 221 and US 278, which helps commuters. The population was 21,640 in July 2025, almost the same as the 2020 base of 21,628.

The county has 9,725 housing units, 65.0 percent of them owner-occupied. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $170,200 and rents run around $792. Builders pulled 86 permits during 2025.

Bills, due dates and late fees

McDuffie runs one of the earlier schedules in Georgia, with a mailing by September 15 and a November 15 deadline, five weeks ahead of the December 20 default used in other counties.

Dates and charges on a McDuffie bill
EventRule
MailingBy September 15
DeadlineNovember 15
InterestCharged monthly from the 16th, prime rate plus 3 divided by 12
Penalty5 percent each 120 days, topping out at 20 percent
FIFA tax lienFiled with the Clerk of Court 30 days after the bill is delinquent
Mobile homesMailed in January, due April 1

For a seller the lien is the problem. It shows on your credit report and in the public record, so clear the bill before the 30 days are up and the title search stays simple.

Installments are possible. The Tax Commissioner must approve a signed agreement set up before the bill goes delinquent. Ask for the agreement in writing and keep a copy with your closing papers.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McDuffie County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The 2026 fire fee change

The separate fire fee ends, with FLOST sales tax revenue taking its place. The county proposed a rate of 7.998 mills, compared with 7.809 mills in 2025, to absorb the fire cost. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the final rate that applies to your bill.

A Notice of Property Tax Increase may arrive even when the typical homestead bill drops. The comparison is to the rollback rate, shown as 6.085 mills for 2026, and it ignores the fire fee. City and school taxes, 15.124 mills in the estimator, are billed separately.

Buyers sometimes ask whether the lower homestead bill carries over to them. It does not follow the house, because each owner has to file for the exemption. Homesteads also get a one-time state credit. The Tax Commissioner describes it as $18,000 off assessed value, applied automatically when the homestead was filed on time.

How to appeal a new value

Count 45 days from the date on the notice of assessment. An appeal that arrives later is invalid, and it has to be in writing, delivered to the Board of Assessors.

The assessors look again and either adjust the value or send the file to the Board of Equalization, where each side states its position. The loser may go to McDuffie County Superior Court. Arbitration is available in place of the Board of Equalization if you choose it when you file.

  • Accepted grounds: taxability, uniformity and value.
  • Uniformity compares your value with similar properties.
  • Objecting to the size of the tax itself is not a ground.
  • Either the owner or the assessors can take a Board of Equalization ruling to court.

A denied homestead has its own path. The assessors decide eligibility, and a turned-down applicant must be told how to appeal.

Homestead and land programs

File at the Board of Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1, having owned and lived in the house on January 1. The ordinary homestead exemption is $4,000. At 62 and older with net income under $15,000 it is $15,000, and at 65 and older there is $30,000 off assessed value for schools. Owners rated 100 percent disabled may use a local exemption with a doctor's documentation and the same income limit. After approval it continues without reapplying until ownership changes.

Land programs carry a ten-year covenant with the county:

  • Preferential agricultural property is taxed on 30 percent of market value in place of the usual 40.
  • Conservation use values land by what it produces now.
  • Environmentally sensitive property stays in its natural state under state rules.
  • Residential transitional property sits in an area changing to another use.

Timber is taxed one time, at 100 percent of fair market value, when cut or sold. A deferral is also available for homestead owners 62 and older with income of $15,000 or less, usually lasting until ownership changes.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy McDuffie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with an unpaid bill

Phone the Tax Commissioner for the full balance, including interest and any lien charge, and ask how the payoff reaches your closing attorney. A bill a few days late looks nothing like one stacked with penalty layers and a recorded lien.

  1. Get the balance in writing.
  2. Pay it at or before closing so no lien is recorded.
  3. Ask whether any older parcel or account is still open.

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, with fees on cards and no American Express. If land once sold at a delinquent tax sale left money over, claim it in writing with proper ID. The county has a list and an application.

For a mobile home, deal with the April 1 bill first, because it is an account separate from the land.

Before you list, pull your latest notice of assessment and your bill, and check the homestead filing is on record with the Board of Assessors. If you are close to the 45 day appeal window, file first and sort out the sale price later, because a missed window cannot be reopened. At closing, the attorney will want the commissioner's payoff in hand, plus proof that any installment agreement is current. A cash buyer can close quickly, so ask for the balance early enough that interest has not grown by the time the funds move.

Frequently asked questions

What day are McDuffie County property taxes due?

Plan on November 15, with bills out by September 15, which is earlier than the December 20 default in other counties. Mobile homes follow an April 1 deadline.

How long can I appeal a McDuffie County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. The appeal must be written, and a late filing is treated as invalid.

What does it cost to pay a McDuffie County bill late?

Interest builds monthly from the 16th and a 5 percent penalty lands every 120 days up to 20 percent. A tax lien follows once the bill has been delinquent for 30 days.

Is the McDuffie County fire fee gone?

Yes, FLOST revenue replaces it, and the county rate was proposed at 7.998 mills. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the final rate.

Where does a McDuffie County homeowner apply for homestead?

At the Board of Assessors Office, between January 1 and April 1. The assessors handle and approve every exemption application.

McIntosh County tax offices

Darien's North Way holds both tax offices. The assessors at number 601 appraise property and approve exemptions. At number 1200, in the county annex, the Tax Commissioner prints and mails statements and takes in what owners pay. The commissioner sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone
OfficeWhere or whyPhone
Tax Assessor601 North Way, weekdays 8:00 to 4:30912-437-6663
Tax Commissioner1200 North Way, weekdays, same hours912-437-6627
County Commission OfficeBudget and millage912-437-6671
Building and ZoningPermits, flood zone lookups912-437-6603
Superior CourtDeed recording and liens912-437-6641

A house inside Darien may carry a city levy as well. State guidance gives billing of city tax to the city clerk, unless city and county agreed to merge the statements, so City Hall can tell you which applies.

McIntosh County housing

Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county, which covers 574 square miles, 150 of them water. Darien is the seat, and Crescent and Eulonia are the other named communities. The population was 11,989 in July 2025, up 9.3 percent from 10,970 in 2020.

Owners hold 80.0 percent of households, in homes worth $182,700 in the middle, and a typical rental costs $800 a month. Builders were issued 106 permits in 2025.

Flood zones and your sale

Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding. Lenders ask about flood zones, so look yours up before listing.

Both the county and Darien participate in the federal flood insurance program. Regular homeowners coverage typically excludes flood, and a structure in a mapped high-hazard area with a federally backed mortgage must carry its own flood policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • In the AE and VE zones the underside of the lowest horizontal beam has to clear base flood elevation by one foot.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McIntosh County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Payment dates and penalties

November 15, or 60 days after mailing, is the usual deadline, and unpaid property can be levied upon and sold. The 60 days count from the postmark, and each county may choose its own official date.

Returns go in between January 1 and April 1. Without one, last year's return and value stand. An owner who thinks the value is wrong can file a return with their own estimate of market value, which protects appeal rights if the assessors raise it again.

Mobile homes follow a different clock. A home sitting in McIntosh County on January 1 needs tax and location permit settled by April 1, or the owner faces a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale. To contest a mobile home value you have 45 days to reach the Board of Tax Assessors, and then 21 days from the notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Keep proof of every payment. If a statement never arrives, call the commissioner at 912-437-6627 rather than waiting, because the tax is still owed and the clock keeps running.

Send new mailing addresses to the assessor or commissioner quickly, since notices only go to the address on file.

Millage

County millage has stayed flat for years at a stretch. In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate, citing pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs and inflation. A rate above rollback triggers three public hearings under state law.

For the current year, ask the County Commission Office for the county millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

Exemptions and appeal rights

The Tax Assessor's Office takes homestead applications, and new homeowners bring the warranty deed. A filing earns the current year's benefit only if it arrives by April 1, even though Georgia takes applications all year. Approval stays on the account until you move, sell or switch types, and a larger local exemption beats the state figure.

The standard exemption is $2,000, and elderly relief applies to incomes of $10,000 or less: up to $10,000 on school tax from age 62 and up to $4,000 on general tax from age 65. A floating exemption suits owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less and replaces other state and county exemptions. A deferral for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less delays tax until ownership changes or the debt hits 85 percent of value.

  • Qualifying farmland may be taxed on 30 percent of market value rather than 40.
  • Conservation use taxes eligible land on its actual use value.
  • Both programs bind the owner to a 10-year covenant.

A buyer does not inherit your exemption, so expect the new owner to file again after closing. Appeals of a real property value go to the Board of Tax Assessors, with a postmark inside 45 days of the notice's mailing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy McIntosh County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to line up before closing

Start about a month before the closing date. Request each parcel's exact balance from the Tax Commissioner and ask the Assessor's Office whether a change in value or exemption is pending. Gather the flood zone and permit history before the sign goes up, and keep a copy of every receipt for the buyer's attorney.

Deed recording triggers the state transfer tax: $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on every additional $100, which the seller owes unless the contract assigns it to the buyer.

At the closing table, settle who covers the current-year bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption ends. A cash sale moves faster, but it still needs the tax account clear.

A short checklist helps. Bring the warranty deed, the latest statement from the commissioner and any flood zone or permit paperwork to your first meeting with the closing attorney. If the house sits in Darien, add the city bill to the pile, since the city and the county may bill separately. If a mobile home sits on the land, treat it as its own account with its own April 1 deadline, and confirm both are paid before the day of closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the McIntosh County property tax deadline?

November 15, or 60 days after mailing. A mobile home is due April 1. Treat the date on your own statement as final.

Which McIntosh County office handles a disagreement over value?

The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner, 912-437-6627, sends bills and cannot change a value.

Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?

They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require raising the floor after major renovation.

What if a McIntosh County mobile home tax misses April 1?

Expect a 10 percent penalty, with a possible citation to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or sale of the home.

How does a McIntosh County owner apply for homestead exemption?

Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office, with the filing in by April 1 for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.

Meriwether County at a glance

Meriwether County is a rural county in west central Georgia, counted inside the Atlanta metro area, with Greenville as the county seat and Manchester as its largest city. Greenville, Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs and Woodbury are cities. Gay, Lone Oak and Pine Mountain are towns, and Alvaton is unincorporated. A lot inside Manchester and a farm on a county road land on one county bill, while a lot in the Town of Gay adds a separate city bill.

Owners occupy 73.0% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,800. Median gross rent is $920. The county had an estimated 21,516 residents in July 2025, up 4.4% from the 20,613 counted in 2020, and it has 10,478 housing units across 8,391 households. Builders took out 117 permits in 2025. Median household income is $57,340 and the average drive to work takes 34.3 minutes, so buyers here watch carrying costs closely, and a parcel with a clean tax record is easier to sell.

Who sends and collects the bill

Billing and collection happen at the tax commissioner's counter, 17234 Roosevelt Highway, Building A, Greenville. Call (706) 672-4219. The doors are open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30, and letters go to PO Box 729, Greenville, GA 30222.

The Board of Tax Assessors (706 672-4222) appraises. Disputes over its numbers reach a Board of Equalization staffed by grand jury appointees. The county commission and the school board vote on separate millage rates, where a mill means $1 of tax on every $1,000 assessed.

Residents of Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs, Woodbury, Greenville and Lone Oak pay city and county tax together to the county commissioner. The Town of Gay collects its own city tax, so a Gay owner pays the county here and the town separately. The tax site also has tabs for tax sales and excess funds.

Due dates

Land, houses and business personal property owe their tax to Meriwether County by December 20. Bills normally go in the mail by October 1. If yours has not arrived by October 15, call the office.

Meriwether County property tax due dates
Property typeDue date
Land, houses and business equipmentDecember 20
Mobile homesApril 1, with the decal posted by that date
BoatsNovember 15, after May assessment notices and a 45 day appeal window
Boat, equipment and other personal property billsMailed at least 60 days ahead, usually in mid November
Cars and trucksRenewal follows the owner's birth date

State rules let a county shift its official date to December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments, and interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked. The printed bill is what you answer to.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Meriwether County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late penalties and liens

Late real estate bills collect interest starting the day after December 20, then a penalty that builds in steps. The interest rate on real and personal property is reset yearly, so ask the counter for the rate in force.

  • Real and personal property: 5% lands on the 120th day past due, and again every 120 days, with a ceiling of 20%.
  • Mobile homes: one flat 10% penalty, with 1% interest.
  • Lien: a FiFa is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court once a bill is 90 days overdue, and credit bureaus can read it.

The counter takes partial payments while interest keeps running. Paying off a recorded lien before listing keeps it out of the buyer's title search.

How to pay

Payments can arrive at the counter, on the website, by mail or in the drop box out front. Inside, the staff take checks, cash and cards (Visa, MasterCard and Discover), and the website takes cards or PayPal.

  • Website card payments add a fee of 2.57%, with a $1.50 floor.
  • Cards run at the counter or by phone add 3.00%, again with a $1.50 floor.
  • Mail a check to the Meriwether County Tax Commissioner at the PO Box above and write the parcel number on it.

Homeowners with an escrow account can ask the office to share tax data with the lender, or mail the coupons to the lender with a short note.

Contesting a value

Notices usually mail in the spring, and the written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors first, naming the route you pick.

You may argue taxability, worth, fairness against similar parcels, or a refused exemption. A Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears the case, and the state also provides a hearing officer. Any route can end in superior court. Keep a few recent nearby sales and photos of any condition problems with the file, since specifics carry more weight than general complaints.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Meriwether County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions that lower the bill

Homestead is the biggest one. Live in the house on January 1, file before April 1, and it applies that year.

First-time owners should bring a warranty deed, and the driver's license must show the Meriwether County street address, because a post office box is not accepted. An additional exemption begins at age 62. Business owners can ask about the freeport exemption on inventory, and the assessors make the final call on eligibility. Ask the Tax Assessor's office about conservation use or other special programs.

Mobile homes, boats and equipment

Manufactured homes, boats and heavy equipment each follow their own rules at the Greenville counter. Every mobile home must show a current decal by April 1, and decals are issued once tax is paid: on the spot for walk-in payers, by mail for everyone else.

Anyone placing a mobile home in the county should visit the Building and Zoning office next door to the commissioner, which takes appointments at 706-672-1283. A buyer or new owner has 30 days to apply for a title and must bring a paid tax receipt and proof of ownership.

Boats need Department of Natural Resources registration and are taxed on value. Tractors, farm equipment and machinery also count as personal property. Heavy equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in the purchase year, with a return due at the commissioner's office 30 days after that month ends. Timber harvests are reported on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, available from the assessors at (706) 672-4222. Deeds sit in the courthouse deed room run by the Clerk of Superior Court, so ask there for a copy of yours.

Selling mid-year

The January 1 titleholder owes the whole year, with no refund for part of it. Put any buyer and seller split in the contract.

  1. A few days before closing, request a written balance from the tax commissioner that shows penalties and any lien.
  2. Pay back taxes out of your payoff at the table.
  3. If the sale closes before the fall bills mail, ask the closing attorney how that year's bill is being handled.

A cash buyer will still ask for a clear tax record, so a recorded lien is worth paying off before you list.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which number reaches the Meriwether County tax office?

Dial (706) 672-4219 for billing and payments. Value questions go to (706) 672-4222.

When does Meriwether County want its real estate tax?

December 20. Bills normally mail by October 1, and anyone still waiting on October 15 should call.

Can I pay a Meriwether County bill online?

Yes, by card or PayPal on meriwethertax.com, with a 2.57% fee that has a $1.50 floor. The counter, the mail and the front drop box also work.

If I sell in Meriwether County, is that year's tax erased?

No. The January 1 owner stays liable for the year and Georgia gives no refund for part of one, so put the split in the sales contract.

What is the deadline to fight a Meriwether County value?

Counting from the notice date, you get 45 days. The written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

Monroe County homes and buyers

Monroe County belongs to the Macon metro area, and the courthouse stands in Forsyth, the largest city. Forsyth and Culloden are the two incorporated cities, and Bolingbroke, Juliette and Smarr are census-designated places. One school system, the Monroe County School District, covers every address in the county.

The county has grown quickly. The July 2025 estimate is 32,023 residents, up about 14.5% from the 27,957 counted in 2020 and about 5,600 above the 2010 count of 26,424. There are 12,376 housing units, and owners occupy 83.8% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $271,200, median gross rent is $943, and median household income is $83,183. Builders took out 258 permits in 2025. With owner households the large majority, most buyers here are buying a home to live in.

Where to pay and ask questions

The Monroe County Tax Commissioner works from 38 W. Main Street in Forsyth and answers at (478) 994-7020. The doors open at 7:30 and close at 5:00 on weekdays, with a drive-through lane out front and P.O. Box 357, Forsyth, GA 31029 for letters.

The office collects for the county. Its desk handles real property, personal property, mobile homes, timber and vehicles, yet it answers to voters and has no control over a parcel's value or the rate applied to it. Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 about value. Rates are voted on by the county's elected commissioners and the school board.

The statement is addressed to the owner of record on January 1, so anyone who bought or sold after that date should phone the tax office.

Payment options

Monroe County takes checks, cash and cards at the counter, in the drive-through lane, by mail, in a drop box and through the county's online search and pay page. Mailed payments need a postmark dated 12/20, the date the real estate bill is due.

  • Visa, MasterCard and Discover carry a 2.5% fee on the total.
  • American Express carries a 3% fee.
  • The drop box takes car tag, property tax and mobile home payments after hours, on weekends and on holidays.
  • Tag renewals can also be done on the Department of Revenue site or at a kiosk.

For current-year tax, only a postmark from the U.S. Postal Service proves an on-time mailing. Meter-dated postmarks are not honored. For overdue bills, the office urges walking the payment in, especially after a levy or tax sale advertisement has begun. Mobile home owners pay by April 1 instead.

What happens if the bill goes unpaid

An unpaid Monroe County bill leads to interest, penalties and eventually a lien called a FiFa. Ask the counter for the current amounts.

How an unpaid Monroe County bill escalates
StageWhat happens
Past dueInterest and a penalty are added to the balance
Notice of intentA 30 day notice goes to the owner of record before a FiFa is issued, and payment in full within those 30 days stops it
Past 90 daysThe office can record a FiFa on the General Execution Docket, which the Clerk of Superior Court keeps
PayoffPaying the tax, fees, penalties and interest wipes out the FiFa

Liens are not sold over the counter. As many partial payments as needed are accepted, yet penalties and interest keep growing on the remainder, and any open balance can be liened. Lien filings are open to anyone, including credit bureaus, though the tax office sends them nothing. A seller with a lien should plan on a payoff letter before closing.

How to question a value

Before you appeal, pull your parcel record and compare it with a few recent sales of similar homes nearby. Note any error in square footage, acreage or condition, and bring that to the assessors. A phone call often settles a factual mistake without a hearing.

Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 first, and if the answer falls short, put an appeal on paper within 45 days of the notice date. There are four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption. You must name the appeal method.

Owners may declare a proposed value by filing a return with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. If the board disagrees, a notice with its own figure arrives by mail. Fair market value is the full figure the board sets, and the assessed value that gets taxed is 40% of it, less any exemptions. Each mill adds $1 for every $1,000 of that assessed figure.

Homestead exemption

Monroe County does offer one. The Tax Assessors' Office approves homestead requests, and the test is ownership plus residence on January 1. Approved owners skip the annual refiling unless they move or change the deed.

Ask the assessors, at (478) 994-7038, about other exemptions and special assessment programs, and ask which of them fit your situation rather than assuming a neighbor's savings apply to you. Counties may raise homestead amounts above the statewide minimum, so the local figure may differ. A buyer files in their own name after closing.

Departments to check before listing

Check planning and zoning, building inspections and code enforcement, all of which have pages on the county site, monroecoga.org. Clearing an open permit or a code notice first removes a snag from the buyer's inspection period.

The county also runs a water department, recycling centers and a landfill. Ask planning and zoning how the county's long-range plan may affect a particular parcel. For deeds and liens on file, the Clerk of Superior Court is the office to contact, and that office is where you get warranty deed copies.

Closing in spring: who pays

Because bills follow the January 1 owner, the seller usually receives the full-year bill even if the sale closes in spring. There is no partial-year refund, so the contract and the settlement statement decide who ultimately carries which share.

The mailed statement reaches the homeowner, not the lender, although lenders on file receive a data file from the office. If you have an escrow account, confirm with your lender that it plans to pay, and forward the bill if necessary. A call to the tax office before closing will turn up the current balance and any FiFa. A cash sale closes faster, but the tax account still has to be settled at the table.

  1. Call the tax office a few days before closing and ask for the balance on every parcel and vehicle account tied to the property.
  2. Ask whether a FiFa has been recorded, and if so, request a payoff letter that includes it.
  3. Give the closing attorney the letter and the latest statement.
  4. Keep your receipt, and send any later bill to the new owner.

If the house has a mobile home on it, remember that account runs on an April 1 deadline of its own, separate from the land.

Frequently asked questions

What phone number reaches the Monroe County tax commissioner?

(478) 994-7020 reaches the commissioner's office in Forsyth. For value, ring (478) 994-7038 and ask for the assessors.

Can I mail my Monroe County property tax payment?

Yes, provided a Postal Service postmark dated by the due date is on the envelope. Metered mail does not qualify.

Where can I leave a Monroe County payment after hours?

A box outside the office handles tag, property and mobile home payments when the counter is closed.

Who gets the Monroe County tax bill after I sell?

The January 1 owner of record receives it. If the sale came later, call the tax office.

How long can I appeal a Monroe County value?

Within 45 days of the notice date, using a written appeal that goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names your method.

Morgan County at a glance

Madison is the seat of Morgan County, in north central Georgia. Demand for homes here is driven by easy reach of Lake Oconee and four job centers: Atlanta, Athens, Augusta and Macon. Population reached 22,095 by July 2025, a 10.0% gain since April 2020, spread across 9,489 housing units. Roughly 78.2% of those units are lived in by their owners, and the middle home is valued at $342,300.

Residents, July 202522,095

Madison, Bostwick and Rutledge are cities and Buckhead is a town. Madison adds a city levy to the county one, so a seller inside the city limits settles two bills.

Which two offices handle Morgan County property tax?

Two desks share the work. One sends and collects the bill; the other decides what your house is worth and who gets an exemption.

The Tax Commissioner collects property, mobile home and timber taxes, sells and renews car tags (online renewal is available), and processes title transfers. If you go in person, carry a Georgia license or ID with a Morgan County address.

The Tax Assessor's office is at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, Madison, GA 30650. Returns and homestead applications go there, with the return window open January 2 to April 1. A value dispute begins at that counter and can move on to the Board of Equalization, a panel the grand jury appoints.

County commissioners adopt the budget and set the county mill rate. School officials recommend a school rate, and the commissioners almost always have to levy it as recommended. The state's own levy is capped at one fourth of a mill.

Due date and how to pay

Pay by November 15 here. Penalties and interest start after that day. The statewide default is December 20, yet counties may pick December 1 or November 15, and Morgan took the earliest.

Online payment is available through the county's tax payment system. A 60 day grace period runs from the bill's postmark under state rules, so check the bill before counting on a date. The same office collects mobile home and timber tax, so ask the counter for those due dates.

If a sale closes after January 1, settle who pays that year's bill. Whoever owned the house on January 1 is the liable party.

Homestead and senior exemptions

Morgan County layers several exemptions on top of the state basics, and a long-time owner may qualify for more than one. The Tax Assessor decides eligibility.

  • Standard homestead: up to $2,000 is subtracted from assessed value (40% of market value) for county, school and state operating levies.
  • Age 65 and up: a further $10,000 comes off the county and school operating portion, with no income test.
  • Madison residents over 65: another $10,000 off for city maintenance and operations tax.
  • Standard elderly: up to $4,000 off for owners 65 and older when net income, counting a spouse, is $10,000 or less. Social Security and some retirement income do not count toward that limit.
  • Age 65 and older, state portion: the home and up to 10 acres are exempt from the state's levy in full.
  • Disabled veteran rated 100% service connected: a larger deduction that changes every year, with a DD214 and a VA rating letter required.
  • Surviving spouses: an unremarried spouse of a service member killed in war or armed conflict can take up to $50,000, and the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed on duty is fully exempt.

How do I file or keep a homestead exemption?

Apply at the Tax Assessor's office. Turn it in whenever you like, though April 1 closes the window for this year and you must have lived in the house on New Year's Day.

Approval is not a yearly chore. Once granted, the exemption rolls forward by itself. A new filing is needed only after a sale, a move, a change to another exemption type, or when income decides eligibility. A denial must be communicated to you by the county, and you may appeal it. Farmland owners can ask the assessor about conservation use, and business owners about personal property.

How to appeal your assessment

When a change-of-value notice arrives from the Board of Tax Assessors, 45 days is your window to respond. The assessors review and reply. Still disagree? A Board of Equalization hearing follows, unless you picked arbitration on your original filing.

Before filing, collect a recent appraisal, sale prices of similar homes nearby, and photos of defects that hurt value. Documents persuade better than a feeling that the number is too high.

Three grounds are allowed: taxability, value, and how the value compares with similar properties. Grumbling about the bill itself is not a ground, and a late filing is barred. Superior court stays open after the administrative step. A new return filed during the January 2 to April 1 window can set a different value and protect your appeal rights if the board raises it again.

Other county departments that touch a sale

Planning and Development covers zoning, flood plain management, a fee schedule and the comprehensive plan. Look at the zoning and flood plain pages before listing a lot that sits near water, because buyers and lenders will ask. Roads and Bridges publishes a mowing schedule and a road resurfacing list.

Court Services covers Magistrate Court, Probate Court and Superior Court, which matters if you are selling an inherited house. Solid Waste and Sanitation includes recycling.

Before you list, it helps to know which of these offices a buyer will contact. Zoning questions go to Planning and Development, tax questions to the Tax Commissioner, and value questions to the Tax Assessor. Having those three names handy keeps a showing from stalling on a simple question.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff figure first. If you close before the November 15 bill is due, the closing attorney should spell out who pays it. The state offers no refund for part of a year, so splitting the bill is a contract matter.

A Madison address adds a city bill, so ask which office collects it. Sellers over 65 should check that their exemptions are on the account before the buyer's lender reviews the tax figures. Buyers who will occupy the home file their own application, again by April 1.

Work in this order: get the account balance from the Tax Commissioner, have the Tax Assessor confirm which exemptions are active, then give both to the closing attorney. Doing this early avoids surprises on closing day, since the attorney needs the payoff before preparing the settlement statement.

A cash sale has no lender tax review and no appraisal wait, which can help when a bill is already late. Whatever is owed still comes out of your proceeds at closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is Morgan County's property tax deadline?

November 15, after which penalties and interest build.

Who takes Morgan County homestead applications?

The Tax Assessor, at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, in Madison. Aim for April 1 if you want the savings this year.

Can I pay Morgan County property tax online?

Yes, through the county's online tax payment system, which the Tax Commissioner's page links to.

Does Morgan County give seniors an extra exemption?

Yes. Residents 65 and older can take an additional $10,000 off assessed value for county and school maintenance and operations, with no income limit. Madison residents can add the same amount for city tax.

How many days do I have to appeal in Morgan County?

Forty-five, counted from the notice of changed value. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first.

Murray County overview

Murray County is in the mountains and valleys of northwest Georgia and is part of the Dalton metro area. Chatsworth is the county seat and the only city, and Eton is a town. Spring Place, Carters, Tennga, Cisco and Crandall are unincorporated communities. An address inside Chatsworth or Eton may carry city tax on top of the county bill, so ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

About 73.8% of Murray County homes are owner-occupied, so most sales involve a seller who has been paying the county bill directly or through an escrow account. Knowing which of those applies to you is the first step before listing.

An estimated 41,607 people lived here in July 2025, and owners valued their homes at a median of $180,700 across 2020 to 2024.

Who to call about Murray County property tax

The Tax Commissioner is at 101 S 3rd Ave in Chatsworth. The mailing address is P.O. Box 336, Chatsworth, GA 30705. Card and e-check payments run through a third-party company's site, and you can also pay by phone at 470-289-4681. That site offers digital statements and automated reminders.

The main county number is (706) 517-1400. Press extension 1 for the Tax Commissioner and extension 2 for the assessors. The two offices do separate jobs: the assessors set values and never collect the tax.

Deeds and recorded liens live with a different office. The Clerk of Superior Court is in the courthouse at 114 N. Third Ave, across the street from the commissioner. The clerk holds warranty deeds, which you may need for a sale.

Due dates, interest and penalties

Real estate and business personal property tax are normally due December 1, earlier than the statewide default. Manufactured homes come due May 1, and vehicle renewals follow the owner's birthday.

  • Interest runs at 1% a month once December 1 passes.
  • Balances still open 90 days later add a 10% penalty.
  • A homesteaded parcel owing under $500 is spared that 90 day penalty.
  • Past 90 days, the clerk's office can record a FiFa that credit bureaus may pick up.
  • The commissioner may levy on the property, which the office treats as a last resort.

Your printed bill controls the exact amount. If a former owner still gets a bill or notice, they may forward it to the new owner.

Exemptions and special programs

Homestead exemptions are filed with the assessors, not the commissioner, at (706) 517-1400, extension 2. Bring documentation of ownership. Elderly exemptions also require income verification.

  • Regular homestead: you must own and live in the home on January 1. No income test applies, and you can file online.
  • Elderly exemptions: several versions with different ages, filed in the office or by mail because of income checks.
  • Homestead freeze: available after one year of homestead, applied for in the office.
  • Disabled veteran: the taxpayer must be 100% disabled during war, with VA documentation.
  • Low income: household income below $15,000 a year, with documents.
  • Special assessments: Conservation Use, Preferential Assessment and Forest Land Protection, applied for January 1 through April 1.

Manufactured home owners who also own the land can claim homestead, pick up a free decal between January 1 and May 1, and pay the home's tax with the land tax. Other manufactured homes, such as rentals, buy a decal.

How do I appeal a Murray County value?

Send a letter to the assessors within 45 days of the Notice of Property Value Change. Certified mail or hand delivery is the safest route. Explain as fully as you can why the value looks wrong, and attach any appraisal or comparable sales you have.

The Board of Assessors reviews the letter and replies in writing. From there the challenge can go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, again within 45 days of the notice, and superior court is open afterward by written notice to the assessors.

A state-certified five-member board updates county values every year at 40% of market value. Notices and bills go to the owner of record on January 1.

Selling with taxes owed

Ownership on January 1 sets liability, so a seller who closes later in the year still answers for the full bill. The state gives no refund for part of a year, which means the sales contract decides how the bill is split.

Before closing, call extension 1 and ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance on your parcel and any FiFa. If your lender pays from an escrow account, ask whether it has paid, because collection questions go to the commissioner and not the assessors. If you need a copy of a warranty deed, walk across to the Clerk of Superior Court.

A rough order of work for a seller: confirm the balance, confirm which exemptions are on the account, order the deed copy if needed, then give the figures to the closing attorney. A cash sale skips the lender's review and any appraisal delay, though whatever is owed still comes out of the proceeds at closing.

Paying and what to bring

Pick the payment route that fits: the third-party online site for card or e-check, the phone line at 470-289-4681, mail to the P.O. box, or a visit to the office on South 3rd Avenue. Keep a record of the payment date, especially close to December 1, since interest starts the day after.

For an exemption or appeal, bring proof of ownership, a photo ID, and for elderly or low income exemptions the income documents the assessors ask for. Calling ahead on extension 2 saves a second trip. If you plan to sell soon, file anything you are entitled to before the January 1 to April 1 window closes, since a lower bill makes the house easier to price.

If a bill goes unpaid past the dates above, the next step is the 10% penalty, then the FiFa, then possible levy. Paying before the 90 day mark avoids the recorded lien that can show up when a buyer's title company searches the property.

Buying or inheriting a Murray County house

A buyer should look at what the exemptions are doing for the current owner, since a homestead on the account does not move to the new owner. The buyer files a fresh application with the assessors, and the January 1 to April 1 window applies to special assessments.

The same goes for an inherited house: the heirs should ask the assessors what must be filed in their own names and ask the commissioner whether the bill has been paid. Bring proof of ownership either way.

Frequently asked questions

When are Murray County real estate taxes due?

Normally December 1, after which interest builds at 1% a month. Manufactured homes pay by May 1.

Which phone line serves Murray County property tax?

Call (706) 517-1400. Extension 1 reaches the Tax Commissioner and extension 2 reaches the assessors.

Is there a penalty for paying Murray County tax late?

Yes. Interest of 1% accrues monthly after December 1, and 90 days later a 10% penalty arrives, except on homesteaded parcels owing under $500.

Can I file a Murray County homestead exemption online?

Yes for the regular one. Elderly exemptions need income proof, so those go in person or by mail.

What is the cutoff to appeal a Murray County assessment?

Within 45 days of the notice date, by letter to the assessors. Certified mail or hand delivery is the safest route.

Columbus and Muscogee County

Columbus and Muscogee County have shared one government since the start of 1971, so Columbus is both the only city and the county seat. There is no separate city tax bill to track. The county hugs the Alabama border along the Chattahoochee, and Fort Benning takes up roughly a quarter of the land.

The July 2025 estimate is 202,171 people, down 2.3% from the 206,922 counted in 2020. Owners live in 50.8% of homes, which leaves about half of the housing to renters, so many buyers here are investors as well as owner-occupants. Expect those buyers to ask for the tax history on the parcel early in negotiations.

Muscogee County housing figures
MeasureValue
People, July 2025 estimate202,171
People, April 2020 census206,922
Housing units, July 202593,324
Middle home value for owners, 2020-2024$193,900
Middle monthly rent, 2020-2024$1,106

Which office handles what?

Three separate bodies touch a Muscogee County bill: one mails and collects it, one sets the value and rules on exemptions, and one hears disputes.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills, takes payments, tracks delinquent accounts and posts tax sale lists at columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner
  • Board of Tax Assessors: fair market value, exemption approvals and the yearly assessment notice
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury, it rules on disputes over value, a denied homestead, freeport and taxability

The assessors meet Wednesday mornings at 9:00 in the City Services Building, 3111 Citizens Way. Call the Tax Commissioner for counter hours and a written payoff figure before you list the house. The commissioner's site also has a parcel search, homestead forms, a delinquent tax section and a tax sale registration class.

Property tax calendar

Bills for real and personal property reach owners in late summer. Payment comes in two steps: 40% or the full amount in October, then the remaining 60% in December. Follow the dates printed on your own bill, because month details can shift from year to year.

  • April 1: mobile home bills come due, the current-year homestead window closes, and returns on business equipment, aircraft and watercraft are due at the assessor
  • May: assessment notices go out, and the appeal period begins
  • July: millage rates are set after advertised public input
  • August: bills are mailed
  • October: first payment, 40% or everything
  • December: the remaining 60%

Payment can be made online with the parcel number from the bill. Splitting the bill into two payments helps cash flow, but if you are selling, the closing attorney will usually ask for the whole year's balance at once so the lien question never comes up.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Muscogee County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How can an owner challenge an assessment?

Send a written appeal within 45 days after the date printed on the assessment notice. Notices go out in May, so the clock runs through early summer. A homestead application filed in that stretch can stand in for an appeal.

Put your reasons plainly in the letter, such as value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption, and keep a copy. The Board of Equalization decides the matter. Ask the assessors whether another route applies to your parcel type, and call before the 45 days run out rather than after.

Overpayment has its own path. A taxpayer can request a refund in writing for tax assessed in error, with the claim starting inside three years of payment.

Homestead exemptions

The basic exemption takes $2,000 off the state portion and $13,500 off the local assessed value for an owner who lives in the house. It freezes the assessment but skips the slice of millage used to retire bonds.

  • Elderly school-tax exemption: owner 62 or older, net income at or under $10,000 the prior year, school tax only
  • Elderly general exemption: owner 65 or older with the same $10,000 test, up to $4,000 off the state portion and $21,500 off local value
  • Floating exemption: 62 or older, household gross income $30,000 or less, covers state and county tax but not schools
  • Disabled veteran: up to $117,014 off both the state portion and the local assessed value, with proof from the VA

The floating exemption replaces any other state and county exemption and may raise the first year's tax, so ask the assessors before choosing it. A buyer should confirm whether a new application is needed after closing.

Selling with taxes owed

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's whole bill in the eyes of the law. The Tax Commissioner does not divide it between buyer and seller. The closing paperwork does that.

If nobody pays, a lien goes under the January 1 owner's name. A seller can shift it to the buyer by delivering evidence within 90 days of the due date: a recorded deed in the buyer's name and wording in the closing papers that hands the tax to the buyer. The Tax Commissioner's buying and selling page walks through the process.

The office never sells tax liens or lien certificates. A parcel that finds no bidder at a tax sale rejoins the queue for later sales. Staff cannot offer legal advice, so see an attorney if a lien is already recorded.

Steps before you list

Start with the parcel number on your bill. Use it on the commissioner's site to see the balance, and ask for a written payoff figure. Then check with the assessors that your exemption is on the account and that the assessment notice from May was not left unanswered.

If taxes are past due, ask the commissioner where the parcel stands on the delinquent list before an offer comes in, because a buyer's title search will find it. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender's tax review, and the unpaid amount is taken out of your proceeds at the table.

What to bring if you visit an office: the parcel number, a photo ID, the deed or closing statement if ownership just changed, and income records if you are applying for an elderly or floating exemption. For a written appeal, a copy of the assessment notice and any comparable sales or appraisal make the letter stronger. Keep proof of every payment, since a dispute over a missed installment is easier to settle with a receipt.

Fort Benning families should know that children there are zoned to Department of Defense schools for grades K-8, then attend county high schools. The Muscogee County School District serves every other address from kindergarten through grade 12.

Frequently asked questions

If I close in the middle of a year, who is billed for that year?

The owner on January 1 is liable for the full year. The closing documents split it between buyer and seller, and a lien can move to the buyer if proof arrives within 90 days of the due date.

Where do I find a parcel record or balance?

Use the search and pay links on columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner and enter the parcel number printed on your bill. Assessor records are on the city-county public access site.

Does a homestead filing replace an appeal?

Yes, during the 45-day period after the assessment notice a homestead application can be made in place of an appeal. For the current year, the general homestead cutoff is April 1.

Will the Tax Commissioner sell my lien to an investor?

No. The office does not sell tax liens or lien certificates. An unsold property returns to the rotation for future tax sales.

Which public schools cover Muscogee County addresses?

The Muscogee County School District serves everything except Fort Benning for kindergarten through grade 12. Fort Benning children are zoned to Department of Defense schools for grades K-8, then attend county high schools.

Newton County overview

Newton County lies east of Atlanta. Covington is both the seat and the biggest city, with Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle as the other cities and Newborn as a town. A city address may carry a city levy on top of the county bill. Interstate 20 and US 278 run through the county.

Growth has been steady: 62,001 residents in 2000, 99,958 in 2010, 112,483 in 2020, and 125,583 in the July 2025 estimate. Homes here are mostly owner-occupied, and a typical owner-occupied home is valued at $265,000.

Where to pay and who to call

Pay in person at the Tax Commissioner's Admin Building at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101 in Covington, or at the Westside office at 3612 Salem Rd. Both open at 8:00 and close at 4:30 on weekdays, and 770-784-2020 reaches either one.

  • Tax Assessors, 770-784-2030: returns, exemptions, appeals and value questions
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and balances; an elected office, separate from the assessors and the county commission
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the millage rates
  • Deed room at the Newton County Courthouse: copies of recorded deeds

Self-service kiosks stand inside Kroger on Highway 20 South and on Highway 278 NE. The commissioner's website also posts a delinquent tax list, refreshed every quarter, and a page on excess funds. You can mail a written balance request to the Admin Building. Include the parcel number and the property address, and say whether you need the figure for a closing so staff can date it correctly.

Due date, interest and penalties

Newton County bills come due each November 15. That replaced the old December 20 date starting with the 2026 tax year, after the commissioners adopted the change in 2025. When November 15 falls on a weekend, the office has allowed payment through the next business day without interest, so confirm with the office. Real estate and personal property statements are mailed by September 15. Non-homesteaded mobile homes get a statement by February 1 and pay by April 1.

  • Late interest is figured monthly at prime plus 3% a year, with .0875% per month listed on the office's page
  • After 120 days a penalty of 5% of the original tax is added, and it repeats every 120 days up to a combined 20%
  • Mail counts only with a U.S. Postal Service postmark; meter postmarks are rejected
  • The office takes partial payments, but charges keep building on the unpaid remainder

Cards add 2.35% (Visa, MasterCard, Discover) or 3% (American Express), each with a $1.50 floor. An online eCheck costs a flat $1.50. Subdivisions that opted in to pay for street lights see a separate street light fee on the statement. The money the bill raises goes to county government, schools, roads and bridges, courts and the jail, fire protection, public health, parks and libraries.

2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit

The credit prints on its own line marked HTRG Credit and comes off the current taxes due before the total. For 2026, eligible homesteaded properties get an $18,000 cut in assessed value for purposes of the credit, and the dollar result varies by tax district.

Owners file nothing extra with the Tax Commissioner. The credit rides on an existing homestead exemption and sits alongside it rather than replacing it. It applies to the 2026 tax year alone.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, call the lender. The tax office has no say over escrow amounts, and a smaller bill may leave the mortgage payment unchanged.

Homestead exemptions and appeals

Apply by April 1, or inside the 45-day window that follows assessment notices. One filing lasts until ownership or your primary residence changes, and exemptions never transfer to a buyer.

  • Standard: $4,000 off taxable value on county and school levies, one homestead per owner
  • Age 62: $20,000 off county and school levies, with a $15,000 cap on net earned income
  • Age 65: $30,000 off county levies and $50,000 off Newton Schools, with a $25,000 earned income cap
  • Disabled veteran: up to $126,526 off the 40% taxable value, backed by a VA letter

The two senior exemptions also limit household social security and retirement income to $99,648. To contest a value, write to the Board of Assessors inside 45 days of the notice and say which appeal route you pick. The Board of Equalization is one option. Base the appeal on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

Liens and selling with taxes owed

A FiFa is the lien Newton County records for unpaid tax, entered on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. A 30-day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before one is filed.

Once recorded, a FiFa lasts seven years and can be renewed again and again. The filing is public, so credit bureaus can see it. Settling the tax, fees, penalties and interest clears it. The office does not sell liens over the counter and posts a list when a tax sale is set.

Ask for a written balance dated near closing, then have the closing agent settle it out of proceeds. Statements go to the owner, not to the lender, so pass your bill along if a servicer needs it.

Preparing to sell

Gather three things before listing: the current balance in writing from the Tax Commissioner, confirmation from the assessors of which exemptions are active, and a copy of the recorded deed from the courthouse deed room if the closing agent asks for it. The buyer files a fresh homestead application, so tell them the April 1 date.

A cash sale can skip the lender's tax review and the wait that goes with it. Whatever is owed, including any FiFa, still comes out of the proceeds at closing. Newton County also publishes excess funds information, so a seller who is owed money after a tax sale should check that page. Settling an old balance before you list is usually simpler than negotiating it at the table, and paying it clears the public filing that buyers' title companies would otherwise find.

Frequently asked questions

When is Newton County property tax due each year?

On November 15, a date that replaced December 20 beginning with the 2026 tax year. If it lands on a weekend, confirm the grace day with the office.

What is the appeal deadline for a Newton County valuation?

Forty-five days, counted from the assessment notice date. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors, pick your method, and rest it on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

Will my Newton County homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. Exemptions do not move with the house. The buyer files a new application, due April 1 or during the 45-day appeal window.

What are the Newton County tax office hours and addresses?

The Admin Building is at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, and the Westside office is at 3612 Salem Rd, both in Covington. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the phone is 770-784-2020.

Which cities and towns sit inside Newton County?

Covington is the seat, joined by Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn. A city address may also carry a city levy, so read the whole bill.

Oconee County housing market

Its population went from 32,808 in 2010 to 41,799 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 44,893. Owners occupy 81.3% of the homes, and a typical one carries a value of $461,600. Four towns appear on the map: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville. Elder, Farmington and Salem are unincorporated and have no town government. Inside a town limit there may be a separate municipal bill, so find out where your parcel sits.

Who bills and who values property?

A bill and a valuation come from two different desks. The Tax Commissioner is at 7635 Macon Highway in Watkinsville, with mail going to Suite 300. Counter hours are weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30. Call (706) 769-3917 or text (706) 765-7790.

  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: each adopts a mill rate
  • Courthouse record center, 23 North Main Street, (706) 769-3940: copies of warranty deeds

Nearly 70% of a tax bill funds schools and the rest funds county government. The appraisal staff handle value only. The tax amount follows from the millage the two boards set. School zoning is a district decision, so ask the school district which school an address feeds before you describe it to buyers.

How your bill is figured

Assessors fix a fair market value as of January 1. Taxable (assessed) value is 40% of it. One mill equals one dollar of tax for every $1,000 of that taxable figure. The Board of Commissioners adopts a mill rate for county government and the Board of Education adopts one for schools. Your bill is the assessed value, less any exemption, times the combined rate.

The appraisal staff calculate values for real estate, marine, aircraft and business personal property in a computer-assisted mass appraisal system, and the appraisers hold state certification at four levels. That means your value comes from a model applied to every parcel, not a visit to your house, so photos and repair estimates help if you think the model missed a defect.

Four commissioners and a separately elected chairman, all chosen countywide for staggered four-year terms, hold the budget, taxing and ordinance powers. The chairman is the chief executive. If you want to speak to the boards that set the rate, those are the officials who vote on it each year.

Due date, interest and penalties

Business personal property and real estate bills are normally payable by November 15. Mobile home tax is payable by April 1.
