  • Penalty: 5% of principal every 120 days past due, topping out at 20%
  • Enforcement: an unpaid account lets the Tax Commissioner levy on the property
  • Payment plans: set up by phone once bills are mailed, with interest and penalties still running until the balance is paid

Interest moves every month, so an old figure may fall short by closing day. Get the payoff figure on paper before you sell.

How to appeal your assessment

Your assessment notice prints the filing deadline in its upper right corner, under the words last date to file a written appeal. That date sits 45 days past the notice date. A letter or the county's appeal form will do, but an emailed or online filing will not.

Keep your evidence simple: a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby homes, and photos of problems. Write the parcel number and your reason on the letter and keep a copy.

You may go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After that ruling, a written notice sent to the assessors carries the case to superior court. Appraisal staff rule on value only, never on the size of the bill.

Homestead exemption

To qualify you must own the house and live in it on January 1, and the application has to arrive before April 1. Valuation is frozen as of January 1, so a renovation or demolition during the year counts from the next January 1. Call the assessors at (706) 769-3921 for current exemption amounts.

Nothing carries over automatically. The exemption belongs to the current owner. A buyer who will live in the house needs to file their own application, so mention the April 1 date during the sale.

What should a seller sort out before closing?

Both ownership and condition are fixed as of January 1, which means a bill is still waiting to be divided when a house sells midyear. Put the split in the contract.

  • Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and hand a copy to the closing agent
  • Pull a copy of the warranty deed at the courthouse record center when the legal description is needed
  • Check whether the parcel is in unincorporated Oconee County or inside Watkinsville, Bishop, Bogart or North High Shoals, since a town may bill its own tax
  • Wrap up any open appeal before closing so a pending value cannot stall a refund

Refund claims for tax assessed in error have a three-year clock from payment. If a wrong value led you to overpay, ask the assessors about a correction rather than waiting, and keep the closing statement as proof of what was paid and when. If you overpaid at closing because of a wrong value, ask the assessors about a correction rather than waiting, and keep the closing statement as proof of what was paid and when.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid November 15 bill keeps growing while the house is listed, with a 5% penalty at each 120 day mark up to 20%. Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written payoff dated near the closing day.

The closing agent pays it out of your sale proceeds and forwards it to the commissioner. Mention any payment plan to the agent, since a plan does not stop interest. A cash sale avoids the lender's tax review and appraisal wait, which can matter when time is short and an old balance is sitting on the account.

Also confirm your homestead was filed before the April 1 cutoff this year. A missed filing is hard to repair later, and the buyer's lender will review the tax figures when underwriting the loan.

Frequently asked questions

What is the normal property tax due date in Oconee County?

Real estate and business personal property are due November 15 and mobile homes April 1. Charges begin to accrue after the date.

What is the last day to appeal an Oconee County value?

It is printed on the notice itself, 45 days after the notice date. The appraisal office will not accept an appeal filed electronically.

Which boards set the millage rate in Oconee County?

Two bodies: the Board of Commissioners for county government and the Board of Education for schools. A mill means a dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, with assessed value set at 40% of market value.

How much does Oconee County charge for late property tax?

Monthly interest at prime plus 3% a year, and then a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20% of principal.

Which towns are in Oconee County?

Four: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville, the seat. Elder, Farmington and Salem have no town government.

Due date, interest and penalties

Land, buildings and business personal property are normally due December 20. Vehicles follow the owner's birth month, while manufactured homes use April 1.

How the bill is figured

Everything starts with market value on January 1. At the county level 40% of it is taxed. Exemptions are subtracted, and the millage rate is applied to whatever is left. Ask the tax office or the city clerk which base and which levies cover your parcel, especially inside a city.

The state revenue commissioner reviews county digests so assessments stay even between counties, and the state's own levy cannot exceed one quarter of a mill. The county commissioners and the school board each adopt their own rate.

How to appeal or claim homestead

Appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You have 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice, and the letter must name the appeal method you want. Value is the common ground, and taxability, uniformity and a refused exemption also qualify.

For manufactured homes the clock is different: 45 days after the bill is mailed to suggest another value, then 21 days after the assessors' notice to go to the Board of Equalization. Call (706) 743-5166 with questions.

Manufactured homes

A manufactured home is taxed on its own schedule. April 1 is the due date, and payment gets you that year's decal. The home's location permit depends on payment in full, so an unpaid bill can hold up moving or selling the unit. If the tax stays open after April 1, the 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly interest apply, and the county can auction the home.

Disagree with the value of a manufactured home? The 45 and 21 day windows described above are short, so move fast and keep copies of anything you send.

Your warranty deed can be copied in the courthouse deed room. A manufactured home carries a decal issued when that year's tax is paid, and its location permit depends on payment in full.

A buyer who plans to live in the house files a fresh homestead application after closing, so mention that to them early. If you are buying elsewhere, file homestead again at the new house. Balance and decal questions go to (706) 743-8422.

A seller's checklist for Lexington offices

Plan two stops. At the Tax Commissioner's counter on West Main Street, ask for the payoff, the status of any decal, and confirmation that no lien is recorded. At the courthouse deed room, ask for a copy of your warranty deed so the closing attorney has the legal description in hand. Take a driver's license and your parcel number to both.

Then phone the assessors on (706) 743-5166 and ask whether your homestead application is on file and whether the 62-and-over exemption is on the account. Write down the date and the name of whoever you spoke with. If something is missing, a late application only starts the next tax year, so a buyer might want a price adjustment instead.

Last, tell your closing attorney which bills are paid and which are open. Lexington sits in a county where one school district serves every public school, which keeps one question off the table for buyers, but the tax bill is the item they will ask about first.

Selling with taxes owed

You can sell with a balance outstanding; it simply comes out of your proceeds. Get the exact amount from the Tax Commissioner, with monthly interest and any 10% penalty included, and pass it to the closing attorney ahead of time so the payoff wire matches.

When a bill is over 90 days late, look at the lien docket before you list. A recorded FiFa appears in the title search and goes away only when tax, penalty and interest are all paid. A cash buyer skips a lender's review of that history, which can shorten the timeline when you are in a hurry.

Forty-five days from the date of the assessment notice, in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Manufactured homes have separate deadlines.

Paulding County housing market

Paulding is a fast-growing western suburb of metro Atlanta, with Dallas as the county seat and government offices clustered on Constitution Boulevard. The mid-2025 estimate is 190,996 people, up 13.3 percent from 168,630 in the 2020 base, across 312.35 square miles of land.

Half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $326,300, and 80.8 percent of households own where they live. Median gross rent is $1,772 a month, and 1,326 permits were issued in 2025. A seller in a newer subdivision competes with new construction, which sets buyer expectations for finishes and the age of systems. Workers travel a mean of 39.6 minutes to their jobs, so many residents commute toward Atlanta.

On the tax side, value is fixed on January 1, taxed at 40 percent of that figure, and the commissioner multiplies the result by the millage. The sections below cover the points that come up when a Paulding County house is sold.

Which offices handle property tax?

The assessors and the tax commissioner divide the job, and deeds sit with a third office. The Board of Assessors sets values, takes homestead applications and hears the first level of appeals. The tax commissioner bills and collects. The Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse, keeps recorded deeds.

Paulding tax offices in Dallas
OfficeLocationPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3006, Dallas, GA 30132(770) 443-7581Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Board of Assessors240 Constitution Boulevard, Room 3082, Dallas, GA 30132770-443-7606Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The phone line may be cut off early so the commissioner's office can close at 4:00 p.m. The assessors accept homestead applications by email, and the board's public meetings run on Wednesdays at 10 a.m. in the third-floor conference room.

Due date, interest and penalties

Property tax is due November 15 every year. Go by the date printed on your bill when you plan a payoff or a closing.

After the deadline, charges stack up this way:

  • Interest posts to the account on the 16th of every month, calculated as prime plus 3 percent spread over twelve months.
  • A FIFA, which is the county's lien filing, is recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court's office thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and credit bureaus can read it there.
  • Penalties of 5 percent land at the 120-day mark and recur on that cycle until they reach 20 percent in total.
  • Accounts that stay unpaid are turned over to a contractor, and administrative and levy fees of $215 or more can be added to prepare the parcel for tax sale.

A mobile home follows its own calendar. Mobile home bills normally mail near January 2, fall due April 1 and pick up a 10 percent penalty the next day.

How to appeal your assessment

You have 45 days, which is about six and a half weeks, counted from the mailing of the notice. A late filing cannot be accepted, so mark the envelope date when the notice arrives. Grounds are limited to whether the parcel is taxable, what it is worth and whether that value is fair next to similar homes. Anger about the millage or the total on the bill will not carry an appeal.

The path runs in a fixed order:

  • Send the appeal to the Board of Assessors first, which re-checks its number and replies with a decision.
  • No deal at that stage means a hearing before the Board of Equalization.
  • Arbitration is the alternative to that board, and the assessors' staff can walk you through it.
  • If you are still unhappy after that decision, the next step is Superior Court.

The assessors keep an appeals page with a form and a guide to reading the notice, plus a list of recent sales used for comparison. Someone serving abroad can have a relative or friend file for them, with 90 days instead of 45. Mobile home owners have the same 45 days to declare a different value.

Homestead exemptions

Exemptions are never granted automatically, so apply with the Board of Assessors. Expect to show residency and citizenship papers, such as a Georgia license or ID card, and your name has to be on the deed. You can claim a homestead on only one property, including property in other counties or states.

Beyond the standard exemption, the county lists these categories:

  • Lower school tax for owners aged 65 or more.
  • Relief for owners with a total and permanent disability.
  • A break for a veteran rated fully disabled from service.
  • A full homestead break for the unmarried survivor of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • An added exemption for homes inside the city limits of Hiram, approved by that city's voters in 2017.

Eligibility turns on owning and occupying the home on January 1. Applications must arrive by April 1, so file as early as you can. A change in ownership, marriage, divorce or death requires a fresh application with the supporting paperwork. Farmland and timber programs come with a covenant that runs at least 10 years, so a seller of acreage should read the agreement before listing.

What happens to the tax when a house sells?

Your purchase agreement spells out how the year's bill is shared with the buyer, and the settlement statement shows the result.

Request a balance figure from the commissioner before the sign goes up, including any interest, penalty or lien recorded against the parcel. A balance still open comes out of your proceeds, which hands the buyer a parcel with nothing owing. If the sale happens after a November due date but before the bill is paid, confirm in writing who pays it.

After closing, the new owner should make a fresh homestead application, because a change in ownership ends the old one. The seller can notify the assessors that the exemption no longer applies. The courthouse deed room can supply a copy of your recorded deed, which the buyer's title work will want.

Selling with taxes owed

If the account has gone delinquent, work out the order of events. Interest posts on the 16th of each month, the lien filing follows thirty days after the delinquent notice date, and the 5 percent penalties arrive at 120 days. Paying before the lien is recorded keeps your credit record clean and spares the buyer's title company a cleanup.

If a FIFA is already on the record, you can still sell. The closing agent pays the tax, interest, penalties and fees from your proceeds, then records the release. Ask the commissioner for a payoff good through the closing date, since interest changes on the 16th.

A cash sale can shorten this process because there is no lender waiting on a clear tax record. The amount owed is still deducted from what you receive at the table, so the earlier you know the figure, the fewer surprises at closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the property tax due date in Paulding County?

November 15 each year. Go by the bill in your hands when you plan a closing.

Who do I call about a Paulding County property value?

Call the Board of Assessors at 770-443-7606. The tax commissioner at (770) 443-7581 handles billing, payments and payoff figures, not values.

How long do I have to appeal in Paulding County?

Forty-five days from the notice mailing. The county states that appeals cannot be filed after that period ends.

Does a Paulding County homestead exemption renew by itself?

Yes. After approval it carries over from year to year until the owner moves, the title changes or a different exemption is sought. A buyer starts a new application after closing.

What does Paulding County charge on late property tax?

Interest is charged monthly, and a penalty layer stacks on after four months. Its ceiling is one fifth of the tax, so a long-ignored bill grows quickly.

Peach County is a small central Georgia county about 90 minutes south of Atlanta, with Fort Valley as the seat and Byron as the second city. The mid-2025 estimate is 29,877 people, 6.7 percent above the 2020 base, on 150.28 square miles of land.

The median owner-occupied home value is $207,800 (2020 to 2024), and 69.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rental houses are a real part of the local market. Median gross rent is $940, and builders pulled 139 permits in 2025. Many Peach County sellers have inherited a house, rented one out, or fallen behind on a bill, and the tax offices below can give a payoff figure in any of those situations.

Where to go for property tax questions

The Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors values property, takes exemption applications and handles appeals. The commissioner has no role in appraisal or in setting the millage rate, and the county commissioners only appoint and fund the assessors.

Peach County tax offices
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Commissioner902 Campus Drive, Fort Valley, GA 31030 (mail: PO Box 931)478-825-3161

The commissioner's office keeps Monday to Friday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Its site covers county tax only. Separate district codes exist for Byron, Fort Valley, Perry and Warner Robins, so parts of the county fall inside city limits. If your house is inside one of those cities, ask that city's finance office about its separate bill.

Due dates and late charges

December 20 is the customary deadline for real estate and business personal property. Mobile homes run on an April 1 schedule, and vehicle tax follows the primary owner's birthday. Dates can shift, so go by the one on your bill.

Late charges on real estate follow a simple schedule:

  • One percent interest accrues for each month the bill stays open.
  • Taxes still open 90 days after the deadline carry a one-time 10 percent penalty.
  • Owners with a homestead and a bill under $500 are exempt from that penalty.
  • An unpaid bill gives the commissioner both the authority and the responsibility to levy on the property.

Delinquent tax sales are held at the Peach County Courthouse at 205 W Church Street in Fort Valley, and the office posts a tax sale list for download. A seller who is behind should phone the Fort Valley office for a written balance before choosing a listing date.

How an assessment appeal works

You can challenge a new value for 45 days after the notice date. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator takes the case. An owner who loses can go on to Superior Court by giving the assessors a written notice.

Some facts about how value is measured here:

  • Assessed value runs at 40 percent of market value unless a statute sets another ratio.
  • Both the notice and the bill print the market value next to the assessed value.
  • Market value means a price between an informed buyer and a willing seller who deal at arm's length.
  • Assessors review property annually and may enter a parcel during business hours, with identification, to check data after a permit, a sale or an appeal.

Compare a recent contract price with the notice before you contest a value on a house you plan to sell. Put your reasons in writing, keep a copy, and note the day the notice arrived so you can prove you filed inside the 45 days. Photos of damage and a recent appraisal give the board something concrete to weigh. If the appeal is still open when you list, tell your agent and the closing attorney, since the final value decides the tax figure a buyer will see.

Homestead exemption

For the standard exemption, you must be living in the house as owner on January 1. It subtracts $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school levies. Applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. The filing period runs from April 2 of the prior year to April 1 of the year the benefit is wanted.

Other programs include:

  • A $4,000 reduction at age 65, for a household whose income the year before was $10,000 or less. Retirement, pension and disability payments are left out of that figure up to the Social Security cap.
  • Owners at 62 can add a school-tax reduction capped at $10,000 of assessed value, using the same $10,000 income ceiling.
  • A floating, inflation-proof option for households with income up to $30,000 and an owner of 62 or more. It may increase what you pay, so ask before choosing it.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, listed at $109,986 for the 2023 tax year.

Bring proof of age, a warranty deed and income statements as the facts require. Refinancing, or any other deed change, requires a new application. A buyer files separately for the new home. Freeport exemptions for manufacturing and warehouse inventory are filed with the assessors by April 1.

Settling the tax at closing

Call 478-825-3161 and ask what the parcel owes, including this year's tax, interest and anything left from earlier years. How the year's tax is split comes from your sale contract, and the settlement statement shows it.

Fort Valley and Byron levy their own tax, so ask the commissioner whether the parcel is billed through the county alone or has a city component. Mobile homes are billed separately and are due April 1, so a manufactured home on the lot may carry its own balance.

The buyer needs to file a new homestead application after closing. After the sale, tell the assessors your exemption has ended, since owners are asked to report any loss of eligibility.

Selling with taxes owed

If you are behind, the order of work is simple. Get the written balance, decide whether to pay it before listing or from the sale proceeds, and give the figure to the closing attorney. Interest grows by one percent each month and the 10 percent penalty lands at 90 days, so a balance that looks manageable in spring can be larger by the time a buyer is found.

Heirs selling an inherited house should ask the assessors and the commissioner what is on record in the prior owner's name, since an old homestead does not carry over. A landlord selling a rental should check for a mobile home balance as well as the land.

A cash sale skips the lender's review and the wait for an appraisal, which can help when a bill is already past due. The amount owed still comes out of your proceeds at closing.

Frequently asked questions

When are Peach County real estate taxes due?

December 20 is the standard due date for real estate. Mobile homes are due April 1, so confirm the exact date on your bill.

What is the late penalty in Peach County?

Interest of 1 percent monthly begins once the date passes, with a single 10 percent penalty at the 90-day point. A homesteaded home owing less than $500 escapes that penalty.

How do I appeal a Peach County property value?

Counting starts on the notice date and stops at day 45. The hearing body is the Board of Equalization, or an arbitrator if chosen, with Superior Court above.

Who takes homestead applications in Peach County?

Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office in Fort Valley, with a warranty deed and any proof the exemption requires. The deadline to receive the benefit for the same year is April 1.

Does Peach County tax mobile homes?

Yes. A mobile home is treated as personal property, and the permit for its location waits on full payment of the April 1 bill.

With so many older owners, many already hold local exemptions. A buyer who loses those exemptions at closing may see a different bill than the seller paid, and a seller who understands that can explain it before the contract is signed.

Who bills and who values property?

The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and distributes, and also processes motor vehicle registration. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property, approves exemptions and reviews appeals. Grand jurors appoint the Board of Equalization that hears the administrative appeal.

Outside the Administration Building, a drop box takes payments at any hour. Cards cost a 2.60 percent convenience fee at the counter, on the web or by phone, and an e-check adds a flat $3.00. Partial payments are welcome, though interest keeps running on whatever stays unpaid. Owners can ask online for a mailing address change, and the site keeps forms, an excess funds page and a tax sale page for bidder registration.

Due dates and late costs

November 15 is the date for real estate and business personal property. Manufactured homes get a January bill and an April 1 deadline. A US Postal Service postmark counts as timely, but a metered postmark does not.

  • Interest runs at the prime rate plus 3 percent, divided across 12 months.
  • A 5 percent penalty comes at day 120, recurs every 120 days and stops at 20 percent.
  • Taxes more than 90 days late can lead to a recorded FIFA lien at the courthouse.
  • The office can levy on the property but calls that a last resort.

Mail goes to the homeowner only, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account has to pass the bill along. If you sell near the due date, ask whether the lender already paid.

How to appeal your assessment

The last day is day 45 after the notice date. First the assessors reconsider their number and answer. If they hold firm, a Board of Equalization hearing follows, and Superior Court sits at the end of the line.

  • You can appeal on taxability, value, uniformity compared with similar property, or the denial of an exemption.
  • You can request arbitration at the time of filing instead of going to the Board of Equalization.
  • Returns are filed at the assessors' office in the first three months of the year. A return that declares your own value can preserve appeal rights if the board later changes the number.
  • Taxable value begins at 40 percent of market value. County commissioners and the school board each pick a millage rate.

Ask the assessors for the exact mailing date on your notice, since the 45 days count from that date and not from the day it reaches you.

Homestead and senior exemptions

Before county, school and State operating rates are applied, the standard homestead takes $2,000 off assessed value. Applications go to the Board of Tax Assessors, and the books close April 1. Anything received later counts toward the following year. New owners should carry in a copy of their warranty deed.

  • A Pickens-only exemption wipes out the school levy for an owner aged 62 or older when gross household income is $25,000 or under.
  • Standard elderly school exemption: up to $10,000 off for owners 62 or older with net income of $10,000 or less.
  • General elderly exemption: up to $4,000 off at age 65 or older, with the same income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: as much as $50,000 off assessed value.
  • Deferral: the bill is postponed, not erased, for owners 62 or older whose household income is $15,000 or less.

The floating exemption, for owners 62 or older with income of $30,000 or lower, replaces other state and county exemptions, and the first bill may rise. Talk to the assessors before you apply.

Selling a Pickens County house

Dial (706) 253-8882 to learn what the parcel owes, and ask whether earlier years, interest or a lien are involved. The commissioner's site has a tax sale page with procedures and a bidder registration form, which shows how the office handles properties that stay delinquent.

The sale contract, applied by the closing attorney, sets the split of the year's tax. If the seller held an elderly or local school exemption, the buyer starts without it and must apply for a homestead on the new home. Deed copies are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.

What a buyer needs from the tax office

A buyer who relocates from another state will deal with the same Jasper office that bills the house, since the commissioner also registers vehicles. A buyer should expect to bring the following to tag a car:

  • For a car with no loan: the out-of-state title, the registration from the previous state, proof of Georgia insurance, a Georgia driver's license showing a Pickens County address, and the current mileage.
  • For a car with a loan: the loan agreement with the lender's full name and address, the T-17 affidavit of the lienholder, and the same insurance, license and mileage items.

The license requirement means a buyer should update the address on the license after closing. The commissioner's site also has a search for property and mobile home taxes, so a buyer can check the parcel's bill history before signing.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid bill after November 15 grows by interest each month, picks up a 5 percent penalty at 120 days, and may be recorded as a FIFA lien after 90 days. Credit bureaus can read that filing, and a buyer's title search will find it. Pay before the lien is recorded if you can.

If a lien is already filed, the closing attorney pays the tax, interest, penalty and fees from your proceeds and obtains the release. A cash sale skips the lender's wait and review, which can help when time is short, but the balance still comes out of what you receive at closing.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Pickens County property tax due date?

November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

How can I pay a Pickens County tax bill?

Walk-in payments take check, cash or card. Online payment takes cards and e-checks. A drop box outside the Administration Building stays open day and night. Cards add a 2.60 percent fee and e-checks add $3.00.

How many days do I have to appeal in Pickens County?

Forty-five days, starting on the date of the assessment notice. Step one is the Board of Tax Assessors. Step two is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

Does a Pickens County homeowner need to reapply for homestead after buying?

Yes. A new owner or new residence must apply again, and the assessors need it by April 1 for it to count that year.

Does late Pickens County property tax hurt my credit?

It can. Lien filings at the courthouse are public, and credit bureaus may pick them up.

Pierce County housing market

Pierce County is a rural southeast Georgia county with Blackshear as its seat, set along the Alabaha River. The mid-2025 count is 20,764 people, up 5.3 percent from 2020, spread over 340.46 square miles of land. Only 68 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale competes with little new housing.

The median owner-occupied value is $153,300 (2020 to 2024). About three homes in four (76.5 percent) are owner-occupied, and median rent is $799. With prices like these, unpaid tax can swallow a large part of the proceeds, so learn the balance early.

Storm damage can also affect a sale. Hurricane Debby damaged personal and business property in the county. A seller with a damaged roof or outbuilding should keep photographs and repair estimates, since a buyer's inspection will ask about them.

Which offices handle property tax?

Duties divide between the Tax Commissioner and the Board of Assessors, whose offices are both on Nichols Street in Blackshear. The commissioner's office is independent of the assessors and of the county commissioners, who control only its budget. Its main duty is to collect the taxes the assessors set.

Pierce County tax offices in Blackshear

The commissioner takes property tax payments online, and they post on the next business day. Cards other than American Express are accepted with a convenience fee. A Georgia driver's license with a Pierce County address is required to title or tag a vehicle in the county.

Millage rates

Three authorities set millage: the county commissioners, the school board and the State. Which rate applies to you depends on whether the parcel lies in Blackshear, Patterson or unincorporated land, so ask the commissioner which millage is on your bill. The county's millage page links the current digest with its five-year levy history, and it is worth a look before you price the house. Ask too whether any rate change is pending, since a buyer's lender will use the current bill to estimate the monthly payment.

Due date and how to pay

Your bill carries the due date, and the commissioner's office can confirm it by phone. December 20 is the official state date, yet a county can pass a resolution for December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments.

A few rules help sellers:

  • Interest waits 60 days after the bill is postmarked, and penalties can follow if the balance goes delinquent.
  • Pierce County property is taxed to the owner as of January 1.
  • The return window at the county tax office runs January 1 to April 1.
  • A manufactured home parked in Pierce on January 1 gets its return and its location permit on the same visit, before April 1.

Before you visit either office, have your parcel number, a photo ID and your deed handy. If you are filing a return on a manufactured home, bring the home's details as well so the location permit can be issued during the same trip. Calling ahead on 912.449.2025 for the assessors or 912.449.2026 for the commissioner saves a wasted drive in a county where distances are long.

The commissioner's site also lists a tax sale registration form and an excess funds list. If your parcel is behind on payments, call 912.449.2026 before you list so you know how much to pay off at closing.

How to appeal your assessment

After the assessors set a new value, a notice goes to the taxpayer, who has 45 days to appeal in writing. Late appeals are invalid. An appeal may rest on taxability, uniformity or value.

The appeal runs in stages:

  • The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal first and decides whether a change is warranted.
  • If the value stands, the Grand Jury's appointees on the three-person Board of Equalization hear the dispute next.
  • Either side may take the decision to Pierce County Superior Court.

Appraisers work from three methods: cost, comparable sales and income. Field staff may stop at a parcel to look into an appeal, a return, a new addition or a conservation application. Visitors from the office show photo identification and arrive in a marked county vehicle. To meet with the Board of Assessors, book by the Friday before its 9:00 a.m. session; the board sits at least twice monthly.

Homestead and special assessments

The homestead exemption is available at the assessors' office year-round, but it must be filed by April 1 to reduce the current year's bill. A purchase made after New Year's Day misses that year's exemption, since the January 1 test looks at who owned and lived there. Once granted, it stays in place until you move or the ownership changes. The county offers no local homestead exemptions, so state exemptions are what applies. Ask the assessors what your age or veteran status adds.

Special programs can lower the value of land:

  • Preferential farmland is assessed at 30 percent instead of 40, and the owner commits to ten years of farm use.
  • Conservation use assessment values bona fide farm and forest land at current use value.
  • Environmentally sensitive property and residential transitional property can also use current use value.
  • Trees on the stump escape tax until they are sold or cut, then count at full market value.

Land held under a covenant deserves a question to the assessors, before the contract is signed, about how a sale or a new use changes things. Farm and timber parcels are a real part of sales here, and the covenant terms are worth requesting in writing.

Selling with taxes owed

Call the commissioner at 912.449.2026 for a written balance, including any interest or penalty, and hand it to the closing attorney. The year's tax is owed by the January 1 owner, so the sale contract decides how it is split with the buyer. Anything unpaid comes out of your proceeds at closing.

A cash sale skips the lender's review and an appraisal wait, which can help when a bill is behind or the house needs repairs a lender might question. The buyer files a fresh homestead application, and the April 1 date still applies to them. Ask the assessors for the covenant papers if the land is enrolled in a farm or forest program.

If the account is far behind, the commissioner's tax sale page and excess funds list show how delinquent parcels are handled, which is a good reason to settle the balance before a sale rather than after.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Pierce County Tax Commissioner's office?

It is at 312 Nichols Street, Suite 4, in Blackshear, Georgia, with hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is 912.449.2026.

What is the Pierce County property tax due date?

Check your bill or ask the commissioner. December 20 is the state's default, which a county can replace with an earlier date or installments.

What is the appeal window for a Pierce County assessment?

Written appeals must arrive inside 45 days of the notice date. Any later appeal is invalid.

Can I pay Pierce County property tax online?

Yes. The commissioner accepts major cards except American Express, with a convenience fee, and online payments post on the next business day.

When must a Pierce County homestead exemption be filed?

April 1 of the year you want it. Ownership and residence on January 1 of that year are both required.

Pike County at a glance

Pike County had 18,889 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 20,932 in July 2025, up from 17,869 in 2010. Zebulon is the county seat, and the tax commissioner keeps an office there at 79 Jackson Street.

Housing is mostly owner-occupied: 84.6% of homes are lived in by their owners. A typical owned home has a value of $305,600, rent runs about $993 a month, and a typical household takes in $86,719. The county has 7,737 housing units, and 106 building permits were issued in 2025. Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,869 a month in housing costs, and owners without one pay $605. The average commute is 35.7 minutes, so buyers are mostly working households who drive out of the county each day.

Buyers at these prices expect a well kept house. A listing with an open tax lien or half-finished repairs gives them a reason to wait or to ask for a lower price.

Which Pike County office should I call?

Call the tax commissioner about a bill and the assessors about a value. The two phone numbers differ by one digit, so it is easy to dial the wrong one.

  • Tax commissioner: (770) 567-2001, weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00. Online payments run through pikecountypay.com.
  • Tax assessors: (770) 567-2002 for returns, homestead forms, valuation and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room at the county courthouse, and the place where a tax lien is recorded.
  • City of Zebulon: Pike County bills city property tax on the city's behalf, so there is no second counter for city residents.

Bills are addressed to the owner. A lender holding an escrow account will not receive one, so pass your copy along to the servicer.

Due dates and penalties

Real estate and business personal property bills fall due December 1. A mobile home bill is due April 1. A United States Postal Service postmark counts as the payment date, and a metered mark does not.

Pike County bill types and late charges
Bill typeDue dateLate charge
Real estate and business personal propertyDecember 1Monthly interest, then 5% at 120 days, capped at 20%
Mobile homeApril 110% starting April 2

The county applies its penalty schedule in four steps:

  1. Interest posts on the 2nd of every month at prime plus 3%, divided by 12.
  2. A 5% penalty is added at 120 days, then again every 120 days, capped at 20%.
  3. Thirty days past the delinquent notice date, a FIFA is filed in the Clerk of Courts office.
  4. The account then moves to a contractor, and fees of $215 plus can be added for certified mail and a title search before the sale.

In the weeks before an auction the parcel is posted, photographed and advertised in the local paper for four weeks. Paying before the sale stage avoids every one of those costs.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Pike County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Write to the assessors within 45 days of the notice date. An appeal sent after that cutoff cannot be accepted, so mail it early and keep a copy.

Argue one of three things: the property is not taxable, the value is wrong, or the value is out of line with similar parcels. A complaint that the tax amount is too high will not work, because the millage rate is a separate decision made by the county commissioners and the school board.

If the assessors stand by their number, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, or arbitration if you prefer. Superior Court is the last stop. Mobile home owners follow a shorter chain: 45 days with the assessors, then 21 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

Bring sale prices of similar nearby houses and photos of any defects. Those carry more weight than a general feeling that the value is high.

Homestead exemption and other tax breaks

A homestead exemption is the first thing to check. You need to own and occupy the house on January 1, and the assessors must receive your form before April 1.

  • The assessors ask first-time filers to show their deed.
  • Pike adds its own county exemption amounts, and the bigger of the local and state figures applies.
  • Age 62 opens an extra exemption.
  • Working farmland may be taxed on 30% of market value, and conservation land on its use value. Both need a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption in the January 1 to April 1 window.

The exemption continues from year to year until the home, its owner or the kind of exemption changes.

How is a Pike County bill built?

Taxable value is 40% of market value as of January 1, less exemptions. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board separately. Each mill levies $1 on $1,000 of taxable value.

A real estate return is needed only after a purchase or an improvement, and it is filed January 1 through April 1. A required return that never gets filed draws a 10% charge on whatever value was left off. Equipment and other personal property goes on a fresh return every year.

What to have ready before you call

A short prep list saves a second phone call. Have your bill number or parcel number in hand, and know which year you are asking about. The commissioner's office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00, and the assessors answer on their own line.

  • Your deed, if this is the first time you are filing a homestead form.
  • Your latest assessment notice, so you know the 45 day appeal window and its start date.
  • The name of your closing attorney or title company, who will request the written payoff.
  • Your mortgage servicer's contact, if the lender pays your tax from escrow.

Once you have the payoff in writing, compare it with the contract. If the buyer agreed to take on the current year's bill, make sure the settlement statement says so. If a FIFA was filed, ask what documents the office wants before it will release the lien, and ask how long the release takes after you pay.

Selling with taxes owed

Collect a written payoff and have the closing attorney deduct it at the table. Interest keeps growing monthly, so the number changes with the calendar.

  1. Phone (770) 567-2001 for the amount owed and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA exists and what clears it.
  3. If the account is at the contractor stage, request the extra fees as a separate line.
  4. Check which year's bill falls on you under the contract.

Closing before the tax sale stage avoids newspaper and levy costs. A cash sale skips the repair list, the lender's appraisal and the wait for loan approval, so the closing date can fit around an inherited deed or unfinished work. The payoff is still taken from your proceeds at the table, the same way a mortgage payoff is.

Frequently asked questions

When are Pike County property taxes due?

December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home tax is due April 1.

How fast does Pike County add penalties?

Interest posts monthly, the first 5% penalty comes at 120 days, and the cap is 20%. Mobile homes get 10% on April 2.

Which Pike County office takes a homestead form?

The tax assessors, and it must be in hand before April 1. First-time homeowners should carry the deed.

Will a recorded FIFA stop a Pike County sale?

No. It is a lien that gets paid out of the proceeds. Ask the tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 what the payoff is.

Who answers questions about my Pike County value?

The assessors at (770) 567-2002. Billing and payment go to the commissioner at (770) 567-2001.

The buyer pool is mostly local and budget-conscious, and many buyers rely on a mortgage and a clean title. A house that arrives at the table with its tax paid and no recorded FIFA gives a financed buyer fewer reasons to hesitate.

Where are the Polk County tax offices?

  • Rockmart: 316 N Piedmont Ave, GA 30153.

City tax is not billed by the county. Each city sends its own, so a Rockmart or Cedartown seller may need a payoff from the city clerk in addition to the county. The county does not sell tax liens.

Due dates and late charges

The usual due date is December 20, though the county commissioner's page also describes payment as due sixty days after the bill is mailed. Check the date printed on your bill, since that one controls.

Interest of 1% a month starts after the due date, and a 10% penalty hits anything still open at 90 days. A homestead parcel owing under $500 skips that penalty. Once 90 days pass, the tax office may record a FIFA at the Clerk of Superior Court. The record is public, and it can show up in credit reports.

A bill is mailed to the owner and not to a lender. If a mortgage company escrows your tax, forward the bill to the servicer and include your loan number.

Assessment notices and appeals

The Board of Assessors mails notices each summer. Each notice starts a 45-day appeal clock, so respond inside that window or the value stands for the year.

The county directs owners to qpublic.net/ga/polk to see property characteristics, ownership, assessed values, parcel maps and sales history. Its tax estimator asks you to choose the right tax district, choose Not Exempt, key in the market value on the notice, and then subtract the estimated tax savings printed on the notice. The result is an estimate only, because final millage rates may differ.

An appeal goes to the assessors first. A dispute that stays open can move on to the Grand Jury's appointed Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, with a superior court filing available after that.

Homestead and age exemptions

To qualify you must have held title on January 1, treat the house as your legal residence, live there, and claim no homestead elsewhere. You can file any time of year, but the form must arrive before April 1 to change that year's bill.

Polk County homestead exemptions
ExemptionWhat it takes off

Age 65$20,000 off school tax and $4,000 off county tax
Age 62, owner and spouse income under $10,000Extra relief

Only your primary home can be homesteaded, and a move means a fresh application.

Selling a rental in Polk County

With about one home in three occupied by someone other than the owner, plenty of sales here involve a tenant. The tax side of that sale is the same as for any other house: the bill follows the parcel, and the payoff comes out of your proceeds.

The practical issues come from the lease. A buyer who wants to live in the house needs the tenant out first, and a buyer who wants a rental needs the lease terms and the deposit record. Showings need notice and access. If any of that is slowing a standard listing, a cash buyer can take the house with the tenant in place or on a closing date that fits the lease, and the tax still gets settled on the statement.

Landlords sometimes hold more than a house. Owners who also run a business may have equipment on the tax rolls, which means another bill and another payoff to request before closing.

What a cash sale skips

A regular listing leans on the buyer's loan, the appraisal and haggling over repairs. Each step can stall a sale when the house has a tax balance, a recorded FIFA or deferred work. A cash sale removes the loan and the appraisal, so the timeline depends mostly on how fast the title company can get the payoffs from the county and, if needed, the city.

The order is simple. You request the balances, the title company confirms them in writing, the buyer's offer is compared with a standard listing after repairs and holding costs, and the payoffs are listed on the settlement statement. The county gets paid from the sale money, and the rest is yours. Weigh any offer against what a listing would put in your pocket.

How do I close a Polk County sale when tax is owed?

Get the numbers first and pay them from the sale proceeds. The commissioner does not sell tax liens, but a recorded FIFA still clouds the title until it is satisfied.

  1. Phone (770) 749-2125 for the balance, with interest and penalty.
  2. Ask if a FIFA is on file.
  3. Request a city payoff when the house sits inside city limits.
  4. Put each amount on the settlement statement.

If a tenant, a repair list or an inherited deed is slowing a standard listing, an as-is cash buyer can work around them and settle the tax at closing.

What to gather before you list

Call either counter first and say you are selling. Ask what you owe, interest and penalty included. Two offices can matter, so ask the same question of the city clerk if your house sits inside Cedartown or Rockmart.

  • The bill itself, which shows the due date that applies to your parcel.
  • Proof of homestead, if you claim it, so the buyer's lender sees the right tax figure.
  • Lease copies and tenant contact details, if you are selling a rental.
  • Your loan number, if a servicer pays the tax from escrow.

Ask the closing attorney to list each payoff on the settlement statement. Keep a signed copy, since it is your proof of who paid what if a question comes up later.

What is the Polk County due date for tax?

The bill itself controls. The usual date is December 20, and the commissioner's page also describes payment sixty days after the mailing date.

How much interest does Polk County charge?

Interest is 1% a month starting after the due date, with a 10% penalty at the 90-day mark.

Where do Polk County residents pay tax in person?

At 144 West Ave in Cedartown or 316 N Piedmont Ave in Rockmart, on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm.

How long do I have to appeal a Polk County value?

Each assessment notice starts a 45-day clock. File with the assessors first, then the Board of Equalization or arbitration if needed.

Does Polk County bill city tax too?

No. Cities within Polk send their own bills, so request that balance from the city clerk before the closing date.

Putnam County at a glance

Putnam County had 22,047 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 23,722 in July 2025. Eatonton levies its own city tax, and the tax commissioner runs county billing from putnamgatax.com.

The market skews older. Residents 65 and over make up 27.1% of the population, and households average just 2.17 people. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $249,300, rent is about $1,002 a month, and the middle household income is $72,096. Owners live in 80.9% of housing units, and monthly housing costs run $1,522 with a loan and $485 without. Building permits numbered 98 in 2025. The average commute is 31.1 minutes.

The county has 14,017 housing units but 10,435 households, a gap of roughly 3,600. Not every property is someone's legal residence, so ask the assessors whether yours carries a homestead exemption before you promise a buyer a particular tax figure. For an owner on a fixed income, an unpaid tax bill and a deferred repair list are the two problems most likely to push a sale.

Which Putnam County office does what?

The tax commissioner collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors values.

  • Tax Commissioner: collects property, timber and heavy duty equipment tax. Payments can be made on the website, by phone with a card, by mail, or at the office.
  • Tax Assessors: (706) 485-6376, with parcel records at qpublic.net/ga/putnam.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax and deed copies, in the courthouse.
  • Marine equipment specialist: an assessor staffer who handles boats.

The commissioner also hands out a Taxpayer Brochure that walks through returns, exemptions and appeals. County information is at putnamcountyga.us.

Payment dates and penalties

Putnam County billing calendar
Bill typeBills mailedDue date
Real and personal propertyBy October 1December 1
Mobile homeBy February 1April 1

A mobile home decal is no longer required.

Interest starts accruing one day late, then posts again each month on the 1st. The rate is the prime rate in force at the start of the year plus 3%. At 120 days a 5% penalty arrives, with another 5% for each further 120-day period, to a ceiling of 20%. A mobile home pays a flat 10% beginning the day after its due date.

Homesteaded property owing less than $500 skips the 90-day penalty. The commissioner mails each bill to the owner, never to the lender.

If I sell mid-year, who gets the Putnam County bill?

The seller of record on January 1 gets the first bill. Once a new deed is recorded, the commissioner sends the buyer a copy as well.

Read your closing papers or ask the closing attorney who owes the money. Make sure the contract and the settlement statement spell out the year's tax, whether closing lands before or after December 1.

Boats follow the same January 1 logic. Sell one and the fall bill still comes unless the assessors' marine specialist is told. Only accounts totaling $20,000 or more in marine equipment get a bill.

Appeals and ways to lower a bill

Your first appeal goes to the assessors, who may revise the value and mail a second notice. If they hold at the same number, the file is forwarded for a hearing. An arbitrator is another option, with 45 days from the notice date to ask for it.

  • Homestead: own and occupy on January 1, file at the assessors, and get the paper in before April 1.
  • Age 70: owners who reach it can request an extra homestead exemption.
  • Relief grant: the 2023 state grant cut assessed value by $18,000 on homesteaded property, and the commissioner says it returns for tax year 2026. Rentals and non-homesteaded property were not eligible.
  • Refund: a claim for tax wrongly collected has to begin within three years of the payment date.

The final step in a dispute is Superior Court, started by written notice to the assessors.

How bills are calculated

The formula starts at 40% of fair market value, subtracts exemptions, then applies the millage rate. The county commissioners, the school board, the City of Eatonton and the State of Georgia each set a rate, with one mill worth $1 per $1,000 of taxable value.

The money pays for schools and county government, public buildings, bridges and roads, courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation. The assessors take real estate returns during the first three months of the year.

What happens if tax goes unpaid?

A FiFa can be recorded 30 days after the commissioner sends a 30-day notice. Because it is a public lien record, it can reach credit bureaus once a bill is more than 90 days late.

The tax sale is generally annual, held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of July. Registration opens at 9 am, and bidders must show photo ID, pay in certified funds and settle the same day by 4 pm. There is no electronic bidding, and owners with delinquent county accounts cannot register. The list is published in The Eatonton Messenger and on Georgia Public Notice.

Paying the commissioner's payoff at closing keeps your property off that list.

Before you list your house

A little groundwork keeps the closing on schedule. Look up your parcel at qpublic.net/ga/putnam and confirm the owner name, the assessed value and whether a homestead exemption shows. If the exemption is missing and you lived there on January 1, the assessors can tell you what the form needs and whether the April 1 cutoff is still ahead.

  • Pay or schedule the current bill. The commissioner accepts payment on the website, by card over the phone, by mail or in person.
  • Gather the tax bill for the year, since the buyer's lender and the closing attorney will ask for it.
  • Check the settlement statement draft for the line that covers the year's tax.
  • Tell your mortgage servicer about the sale if it pays the bill from escrow, because the commissioner mails bills to the owner and not to the lender.

None of this takes long, and each item removes a reason for a buyer to delay or ask for a lower price.

Selling with a tax balance

Ask the commissioner for a written payoff and give it to the closing attorney, who will subtract it from your proceeds. The figure moves each month because interest posts on the 1st, so request it close to the closing date.

  1. Confirm which year's bill is open and whether the buyer or you agreed to cover it.
  2. Ask whether a FiFa has been recorded and what clears it.
  3. If the city of Eatonton levies tax on your parcel, request that balance too.
  4. For a boat or other equipment on the rolls, tell the assessors about the sale.

A cash buyer can close around an inherited deed, a repair list or a stalled listing. The tax is still paid out of your proceeds at the table, so you leave the closing with the account clear and no list publication ahead of you.

Frequently asked questions

December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home taxes are due April 1.

Does Putnam County auction delinquent properties?

Yes. It generally holds one sale a year, on the first Tuesday in July at the courthouse, with in-person bidding only.

Who owes tax if my Putnam County house sells in mid-year?

The January 1 owner is billed first, and the buyer later receives a copy. Your closing attorney and contract decide who pays.

How is the Putnam County late penalty set?

Interest runs at the January prime rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty follows at day 120 and repeats every 120 days until 20%.

Where do I find a Putnam County parcel record?

At qpublic.net/ga/putnam, or by calling the assessors at (706) 485-6376.

Rabun County at a glance

Rabun County counted 16,883 residents in 2020 and an estimated 17,764 in July 2025. The tax commissioner's office is in Clayton. With 370.13 land square miles and 45.6 residents per square mile, it is thinly settled, and the average commute is a short 23.1 minutes.

Owners live in 77.1% of housing. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $295,200, rent runs about $1,047, and the middle household income is $67,493. Owners with a mortgage pay $1,481 a month in housing costs, and owners without a loan pay $491. People 65 and older are 31.5% of residents.

The county has 12,695 housing units but only 7,615 households, so many properties are not a household's main residence. If yours is one of them, it may not hold a homestead exemption, and the next owner's bill could differ from the one you pay now. Price from nearby closed sales, not county averages. A seller who knows the tax payoff and exemption status before listing negotiates from a stronger position. The spread between a village lot and mountain acreage can be wide. Building permits numbered 128 in 2025.

Tax offices and how to pay

The tax commissioner is at 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, Clayton, GA 30525, phone (706) 782-3613, with weekday counter hours that end at 4:30 pm, major holidays excluded.

Checks by mail should be made payable to the Rabun County Tax Commissioner. A cart lets you pay several bills at once online. The assessors handle values, returns, special programs and appeals, and copies of deeds come from the deed room at the Rabun County Courthouse.

Bills are mailed to whoever owns the property. A lender with an escrow account will not get one, so send yours along.

When is Rabun County property tax due, and what happens late?

December 1 applies to real estate and business personal property.

Past that date, prime plus 3% accrues monthly, and 120 days later a 5% penalty joins it. Once a bill is over 90 days late, a FIFA lien can be recorded, and the commissioner may levy on the parcel. The lien becomes a public record that credit bureaus may read.

The county accepts a United States Postal Service postmark, not a metered one. Mobile homes are billed in January. Call (706) 782-3613 for the due date before paying one.

How to contest a Rabun County value

File the appeal in writing, and file it early. An appeal filed late is invalid. The deadline is 45 days after the notice.

There are three grounds: whether the property is taxable or exempt, whether it is valued in line with comparable property, and whether the dollar value is too high or too low. The assessors review it, and if nothing changes, the Board of Equalization hears the case. Rabun County Superior Court is the next level for either side.

The assessors follow the market and do not create it, using cost, market and income approaches. A recent sale price of a similar nearby house gives the strongest backing.

Land assessment programs

Land owners have more choices here than house owners. Every program below ties the land to its use for 10 years by covenant. Apply between January 2 and April 1.

  • Preferential agricultural: taxed on 30% of fair market value where other property uses 40%.
  • Conservation use: current use value replaces market value.
  • Environmentally sensitive: land left in its natural state, valued by use if it meets Department of Natural Resources standards.
  • Residential transitional: current use value where an area is moving away from residential use.

Standing timber is taxed once it is sold or harvested. Anyone selling land under a covenant should tell buyers, since the 10-year commitment affects what they can do with it.

Homestead exemption and bill math

The test is ownership plus residence on January 1, and the form goes to the assessors. It must arrive before April 1 to count for that year. Call (706) 782-3613 if you are unsure which window applies to you.

Owners aged 62 can ask for an additional exemption. Arithmetic is simple: take 40% of market value, subtract exemptions, and apply the rate set by the county commissioners and the school board. The money pays for police, fire, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

Can I sell a Rabun County house with tax still owed?

Yes, with a payoff from the commissioner and the closing attorney handling it.

  1. Ask for the exact balance with interest and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. If the land is in a covenant program, share that with the buyer.
  4. List each payoff on the settlement statement.

A house stalled by repairs or long vacancy can sell as-is, on a closing day you choose, with the tax paid out of the proceeds.

Step by step: from listing to closing

Taxes touch a sale at four points, and handling them in order keeps the closing calm.

  1. Before listing, pull the parcel's current bill and confirm nothing is past due. Call (706) 782-3613 if you are unsure.
  2. When you accept an offer, tell the closing attorney the amount owed and whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. Ahead of closing, ask the commissioner for an exact payoff that includes interest and any penalty. The balance grows monthly, so ask close to the closing day.
  4. At closing, see that each payoff appears on the settlement statement and that the tax commissioner receives the funds.

If the year's bill has not arrived yet, ask the attorney how the contract splits it. Bills go to the owner of record, and a lender with an escrow account does not receive one, so a buyer's servicer will need a copy from you or from the commissioner.

Preparing a vacation or second home for sale

Because so many Rabun properties are not a household's main residence, check your tax status before you list. Ask the assessors whether a homestead exemption is on file. A buyer's estimate of next year's bill depends on it, and a surprise at closing can sour a deal.

Land with a covenant needs extra care. Tell the buyer which program applies and that the 10-year commitment runs with the land, then confirm with the assessors what the buyer must do to keep the program going. If the parcel mixes house and acreage, the two parts may be valued differently.

Before you call a buyer or an agent, collect the current bill, the payoff from the commissioner, and your deed copy from the courthouse deed room. The assessors also handle special programs and returns, so a short call to them before listing can answer most questions about what carries over to the buyer. A cash buyer can close on a vacant or stalled property without waiting for a lender's appraisal, and the tax is still paid at the table from your proceeds.

When do Rabun County property taxes come due?

December 1, for real estate and business personal property.

Where is the Rabun County tax commissioner?

At 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, in Clayton. Call (706) 782-3613. Counter hours end at 4:30 pm.

What is the appeal deadline in Rabun County?

The deadline is 45 days after the notice. A later appeal is invalid.

Can I pay Rabun County tax by card?

Yes, online. The fee is 2.50% or $1.25 minimum for cards, and $1.50 for each eCheck.

Which Rabun County programs need a 10-year covenant?

Preferential agricultural, conservation use, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional assessments. Apply from January 2 to April 1.

Which Richmond County offices handle my tax bill?

Valuation and collection sit in different hands here. Appraisers working for the Board of Assessors value each parcel, and the elected Tax Commissioner, whose site is arctax.com, prints the bills and accepts payment. Because the commissioner has no hand in the size of any levy, a dispute over rates belongs with the commission and school board, and a dispute over worth belongs with the appraisers.

  • Assessors: 706-821-2310, plus an online property search.
  • Tax Commissioner: 706-821-2391, counter at 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta.
  • Mail to the commissioner: P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903.

Richmond County is consolidated with Augusta, so county notices appear on the Augusta government website and a single government sits behind the county and city side of the bill.

Richmond County housing at a glance

Richmond County had 206,607 residents in 2020 and 206,559 in July 2025, on 324.34 square miles of land. It has 76,694 households and an estimated 94,651 housing units, and 534 building permits were issued in 2025.

Owners hold only 51.2 percent of households, so renters are nearly half. A typical owned home is valued at $178,500 and a typical rent is $1,141. The middle household earns $55,637, and the drive to work averages 21.4 minutes.

With so many rentals, buyers here include landlords as well as first-time owners. A parcel with deferred repairs or an old tax balance sells at a discount, since the buyer subtracts what the county is owed.

2026 millage rates

Four net rates are posted for 2026. The tax district that contains the parcel picks the one that applies.

2026 net millage by tax district
Tax districtNet millage
001 Urban28.284
002 County with fire26.28
003 Hephzibah24.939
004 Blythe with fire26.839

A mill is $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value, and the county commission and the school board each add their own rate to the total. Assessed value is 40 percent of market value. Your assessment notice carries an estimated tax savings box, so check it against the final bill.

Due dates and late charges

For the 2026 bills, the due date is November 30, with mobile home tax due April 1. Bills mail in August or September as a rule.

Whatever remains unpaid is charged .875 percent interest monthly (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40), and a single 10 percent penalty follows. If the account keeps sitting, a lien and levy can follow. Settle an old balance ahead of any sale. The owner remains responsible for payment, whoever was supposed to remit it.

Escrow does not transfer the legal duty. Lenders do not get paper bills from the office, only the data. After a change of servicer, phone the new company and ask whether the county account was paid.

How to challenge a Richmond County valuation

The clock is 45 days and starts on the date the notice was mailed. The notice states its own deadline, so read it the day it arrives.

You can file through the assessor's website, by post, by email or in person. Since 2011 every owner receives a yearly notice, even when nothing changed. A change in 2026 is the layout: Senate Bill 566 replaced the old tax estimate grid with an estimated savings section plus appeal and exemption directions.

  • Pull sale prices of comparable houses close to yours.
  • Photograph defects that lower value.
  • If the assessors keep their number, the Board of Equalization is next, and Superior Court after it.

Homestead relief

You qualify by living in the house on January 1 and filing by April 1. The commissioner takes the form and sends it to the assessors for a ruling, and an owner who is turned down may go to the Board of Equalization.

After approval the benefit rolls forward by itself. Owners refile only after a deed change in name or spelling, an ownership change, or when they want a different exemption. Refinancing leaves it alone. A couple gets one homestead between them, and each vehicle either spouse owns has to be registered here. Solid waste and street light fees stay payable.

Augusta adds a local floating homestead exemption, aimed at holding back growth in the assessed value of a primary home. The form is accepted from January 1 through the end of the 45 day appeal window that follows the mailing of assessment notices, and it can accompany an appeal or replace one. Each applicant states citizenship or immigration status under O.C.G.A. 50-36-1, and qualified aliens attach their federal documents. Senior and other special exemptions need an in-person or mailed application with full documentation. For mailed forms the office recommends certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are refused.

Who owes the tax in a Richmond County sale?

Georgia puts each year's tax on whoever holds title January 1. A contract can pass that burden to the buyer, which the closing table normally handles. The commissioner will not divide the year between the parties.

  • A bill goes to the January 1 owner and to any buyer who took title later that year.
  • If nobody pays, the lien carries the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows the deed plus closing papers inside 90 days of the due date.
  • The office calls its proof an acknowledgment and receipt of settlement statement.

If a fall closing runs on an estimated tax figure, ask the attorney who absorbs any gap when the real bill arrives, and keep your signed settlement statement.

Checking whether a parcel is current

The tax commissioner publishes a mass tax bill file listing outstanding real estate balances, normally refreshed on Mondays. Some accounts are coded bankruptcy, under appeal or awaiting an assessment change, and those are not yet due, so a balance in the file does not by itself mean a delinquency.

For an exact status, call 706-821-2391 and have the bill number or map and parcel number ready. Bad checks go to a recovery partner, Envision Payment Solutions, and a service fee applies under state law.

Can I sell a Richmond County house with taxes behind?

Yes. A payoff request goes from the title company to the commissioner, and the amount is deducted from your proceeds the way a mortgage payoff is.

  1. Call 706-821-2391 and ask for the balance on the parcel.
  2. Ask whether the account is coded bankruptcy, under appeal or awaiting an assessment change.
  3. Hand the written payoff to the title company.
  4. Check the settlement statement before you sign.

Cash buyers suit inherited and empty houses and parcels where a lien has started to grow, because no repair list or loan approval holds up the closing. Compare any offer with a standard listing minus repairs and holding costs, and call the commissioner for the live balance first.

How many days do Richmond County owners get to appeal?

Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice was mailed. The notice states its own deadline.

What is the Richmond County homestead filing date?

April 1, for a home you occupied on January 1. After approval, the benefit continues until the deed or the owner changes.

Will the Richmond County tax commissioner split tax between buyer and seller?

No. Buyer and seller settle that between themselves at closing, and their papers can later show who took on the tax.

What does a late Richmond County bill cost?

Interest of .875 percent per month and one 10 percent penalty.

Where does a mailed Richmond County homestead form go?

To P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903. Use certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are rejected.

Who does what on a Rockdale County tax bill?

Three bodies shape a Rockdale bill. Appraisers under the Board of Assessors value the parcel, the Tax Commissioner collects, and the county commissioners, school board and city council choose the rates. The commissioners control only the assessors' budget, and the Tax Commissioner is elected and answers to voters rather than to the assessors.

  • Assessors: 770-278-7676, P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-278-7600, text line 678-964-4712, and an account portal at rockdaletaxoffice.org.

Real estate returns are filed with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. Anyone who thinks the value is too high may file one. It is mandatory after a lot split or after new construction in the prior year, and a late filing triggers a 10 percent non-return penalty.

Rockdale County housing at a glance

Rockdale County had 93,487 residents in 2020 and an estimated 98,416 in July 2025, on 129.82 square miles of land, about 721 per square mile. It has 34,437 households and 37,611 housing units, and 339 building permits were issued in 2025.

Two of every three households own, 69.6 percent. A typical owned home is valued at $292,900, a typical rent is $1,525, and the typical household earns $77,247. Workers spend 33.7 minutes on the road each way.

At those values a missed tax year is costly. Before listing, ask the Tax Commissioner whether the parcel shows anything unpaid.

How a Rockdale County bill is worked out

Market value is multiplied by 40 percent, exemptions are taken off, and the rate is applied to the remainder. Appraisers lean on three methods: comparable sales, replacement cost and income capitalization. A bill can climb with an unchanged rate if value rises or an exemption is lost.

Appeal routes after an assessment change
RouteHow it works
Board of AssessorsFirst stop once a change notice arrives

ArbitrationSubstitute for the board, with the loser paying the arbitrator
Superior Court$25.00 filing fee
