How to file a value appeal

The quickest path is the assessors' real property page: search your parcel on qPublic, press the Appeal to Board of Assessors button and send the form. Georgia gives 45 days from the notice date, and the notice states the exact deadline.

Four grounds are open: value, taxability, uniformity and denial of an exemption. Complaints about the rate itself have no route here.

  • Gather recent sold prices and photos for comparable houses.
  • Name board or arbitration in the first filing.
  • Once the Board of Equalization or the court decides, the assessors need an on-site inspection before changing that value for two years.

Homestead exemption rules

The final day is April 1, and the county has no authority under the law to extend it. You need to have owned the house and lived in it on January 1.

The regular exemption is 15,000 off county maintenance and operations and 15,000 off school maintenance and operations, with a state component at 100 percent. Further lines serve age 62 and up, total permanent disability, and disabled former service members at 126,526, and variable exemptions apply where household income is $30,000 or less. A floating statewide exemption appears too. The HOST credit covers up to five acres and the main residence, while the state portion covers up to ten acres.

Take a current license, the recorded deed and a utility statement to the assessors. Income-based forms need the latest federal and state returns. One homestead per family unit is the limit.

Due date and ways to pay

The date is November 15. Taxes still open after it become eligible for levy and sale.

Send payment in the pink return envelope, leave it in the drop box beside the front door, pay at the window or log into an online account. Cards cost 2.35 percent with a $1.00 minimum. The office refuses counter checks, third-party checks and employer-issued checks, and a returned check costs the greater of $35 or 6 percent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Rockdale County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a Rockdale County tax sale works

Sales are public auctions at the J.P. Carr Community Center in Conyers, starting at 10 a.m. The next one is listed for March 2027. Properties are advertised in the Rockdale Citizen for four weeks beforehand, and buyers pay by cash or certified check for a tax deed. Liens are not sold.

  • Bidding opens at the tax due plus penalties and costs.
  • The winner cannot move in, improve the land or evict anyone yet.
  • The owner or any party with an interest may redeem, and the buyer waits a year and a day before moving to cut off that right.
  • Money left after costs may be sent to superior court through an interpleader.

The Tax Commissioner's real estate resources page posts downloads of the sale list, excess funds and delinquent tax file. If you sell first, the overdue amount is paid at the closing table, so request a payoff before you accept an offer.

What a tax sale buyer actually gets

Less than a normal purchaser. The tax deed is not a warranty deed, so the bidder carries the risk that the title has defects, and the sale is advertised as buyer beware with no guarantees. The winning bidder must pay within one hour, pays the clerk's recording fee, and takes on later taxes, including any owed to a city if the parcel lies inside one.

A mobile home passes with the land only if a certificate of permanent location was issued. A sale can be set aside for irregularities such as a bankruptcy filing or an assessment error, and the money is then refunded in full. Unbid parcels may be re-auctioned at 3 p.m. that day, or knocked off to the county.

For an owner, the practical point is the redemption window of at least twelve months. Redeeming means paying the deed holder what is owed, so deal with the balance well before any auction date is set, whether by paying it or by selling.

Can I sell a Rockdale County house if tax is owed?

Yes. The closer pays the county from your proceeds and the buyer receives title free of that debt. A cash buyer removes the appraisal, lender repair demands and loan timing that slow an ordinary sale.

  1. Ask the Tax Commissioner at 770-278-7600 for a written payoff.
  2. Ask whether the parcel is on the delinquent list or the sale list.
  3. Give the payoff to the closing attorney or title company before you accept an offer.
  4. Check the settlement statement for the county line.

Heirs, landlords and owners who have fallen behind should get a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and a price opinion from an agent, and compare both with a cash offer. The offer that nets you the most after repairs, back tax and holding costs is the better one.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Rockdale County property tax deadline?

November 15. After that date unpaid taxes are open to levy and a tax sale.

What is the last day for Rockdale homestead applications?

April 1 of the tax year, with no grace period. Call the assessors at 770-278-7676, and mail goes to P.O. Box 562, Conyers, GA 30012.

Who sets a Rockdale parcel's value?

The Board of Assessors, run day to day by its Chief Appraiser. County commissioners appoint the board and hold only the purse strings.

Does the Rockdale Tax Commissioner auction tax liens?

No. Only tax deeds are auctioned, and the original owner keeps a right to redeem.

What share of value does Rockdale County tax?

Forty percent of market value, as set by state law. Exemptions come off that figure before the rate is applied.

Screven County tax offices

Every Screven bill passes through two desks. Valuation belongs to the Board of Tax Assessors. Billing, receipts and tag work belong to the elected commissioner, whose office also handles timber and mobile home accounts.

  • Tax Commissioner, 216 Mims Road #103, Sylvania, GA 30467. Phone 912-564-2206. Walk-in hours: weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Tax Assessors, 912-564-7918, for returns, value questions and homestead forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse holds your recorded deed.

Some cities collect their own levy through a city clerk. The commissioner can tell you whether yours does.

Screven County at a glance

Screven is rural. Its 645.78 square miles hold about 22 people for each square mile, and the July 2025 estimate of 14,408 is 2.5 percent over the April 2020 base of 14,061.

The county has 4,932 households and 6,640 housing units. Homes with a resident owner make up 69.8 percent. Median value of an owned home is $124,300, median monthly rent is $679 and median household income is $52,792. New construction is minimal, with 19 permits in 2025, and 89.1 percent of residents had not moved in the past year.

A house left empty after a death or a move stands out in a county like this. Bills run small beside metro Georgia, yet an unpaid year stays with the parcel and keeps collecting interest.

When Screven County property tax is due

The commissioner posts two dates for real estate and business personal property, November 15 and December 20, so follow the one printed on your own bill. Phone 912-564-2206 to confirm.

Screven County due dates and late charges
Bill typeDueCharges after the date
Real estate and business personal propertyNovember 15 or December 20, as printed on the billMonthly interest, then penalties capped at 20 percent

Mailed checks are judged by the Postal Service postmark; metered stamps are refused. Phone the counter for a current balance.

Liens and levies

Thirty days past due, the office may have a fi. fa. (a tax lien) entered with the superior court clerk. Bureaus pull from those records, and the commissioner cannot control their use of the entry.

The next stage hands the account to a contractor named DTSi. Administration and levy charges of $215.00 or more land on the bill, covering certified mail and a title search. The house is posted and photographed, and an ad runs for the four weeks ahead of a sale in a newspaper, the Sylvester Local, at the owner's expense.

Clear it before listing, because the buyer's title search will find it.

How to dispute a Screven County valuation

Each January 1 the assessors fix a market value, and 40 percent of it is taxed. Until April 1 an owner may return a different figure. If the assessors will not accept it, they send a notice, and the 45 days count from that date.

  • Choose the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator to hear it.
  • To keep going, give written notice that you want Superior Court.
  • The grounds that work are taxability, value and uniformity. Grumbling about the total tax does not qualify.

Skipping a return you were required to file costs 10 percent of whatever value you left off. A mobile home owner has 21 days to carry a corrected value to the equalization board. Where the owner is deployed, a friend or relative may file on their behalf, with 90 days from the value notice.

Homestead and relief programs

Owning and living in the house on January 1 is the test. File with the assessors, and get the form in before April 1 or it waits for the next year. A first-time owner brings the warranty deed. Approval carries forward on its own until you move, retitle or ask for another type.

Screven adds local exemptions of its own, and any local amount larger than the state one replaces it. A further exemption opens at age 62. Separately, the state deferral program lets a homeowner of 62 or more with gross income no higher than $15,000 postpone the tax, with the balance coming due at a transfer or once it hits 85 percent of market value.

Bona fide farm tracts are assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and conservation tracts at current use value. A ten year covenant with the assessors comes with either.

How are mobile homes taxed in Screven County?

A mobile home is personal property in the commissioner's eyes. One sitting in Screven on New Year's Day owes tax by April 1, must be registered with the assessors, needs a location permit and has to show a decal. Neglect can bring a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court summons or a sale of the unit.

Those bills typically mail around January 2. A newly placed home gets 30 days to obtain its permit.

What to gather before listing

A little preparation saves a second trip to Sylvania. Every item below comes from an office listed above.

  • A written balance from the Tax Commissioner for every tax year still open, with the interest to date.
  • A copy of the warranty deed from the Clerk of Superior Court, if the family no longer holds the original.
  • Your latest assessment notice from the Tax Assessors, so the buyer sees the value the county uses.
  • Proof of homestead status, or a note that none was ever filed.
  • For a mobile home, the location permit and decal record.

If the owner has died, the person handling the estate should bring the same papers plus whatever court order gives authority to sign. Ask the commissioner's counter what proof it needs before it will discuss the account.

From payoff to closing

Work through the sale in a fixed order. First, get the written balance and ask whether a fi. fa. has been entered. Second, hand the figure to your closing attorney, who adds it to the settlement statement. Third, if a city clerk also collects a levy on the parcel, request that balance too. Fourth, confirm after closing that the commissioner received the money and that any lien was released on the clerk's records.

Interest keeps running while the account is open, so ask for the payoff close to the closing date. If the account has already reached the contractor stage, ask for the extra charges on a separate line so you can see what each one covers. Settling before an ad is placed avoids the newspaper cost, which falls on the owner.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Can I sell a Screven County house that has unpaid tax?

Yes. Your closing attorney asks the commissioner for a payoff, and the closer pays it from what you receive at the table. A recorded fi. fa. must be released so the buyer can take clean title.

Cash buyers suit inherited, empty or worn houses, since no lender inspection stands in the way. Set any offer beside a listing price less repairs and a slower close.

Frequently asked questions

Does Screven County want its tax in November or December?

The commissioner posts November 15 and December 20. Your bill's printed date rules, and 912-564-2206 can confirm it.

Where does a Screven homeowner file for homestead?

At the Tax Assessors' office, 912-564-7918. Forms that arrive by April 1 count for that year.

How soon must a Screven value dispute be filed?

Within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors hear it first, and then the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

What does a Screven mobile home owner pay each spring?

The tax and the location permit both come due April 1, and a missed date brings a 10 percent penalty.

Can an older Screven owner postpone the tax?

Yes, at age 62 or more with gross household income of $15,000 or less. The postponed amount stays owed and comes due at a transfer or when it reaches 85 percent of market value.

Spalding County tax offices

Spalding County divides the work among five bodies. The Tax Commissioner owns the bill and the payment window. The assessors value property and approve exemptions, and a Grand Jury appointed board of equalization settles disputes. Millage rates come from the commissioners and the school board.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, three blocks from the courthouse. The phone is (770) 467-4360 and the mailbox is PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. Call (770) 467-4240 for the Tax Assessor. County administration works from 119 E. Solomon Street. The Tax Commissioner's office opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

Due dates and penalties

Bills for land, buildings and business equipment normally fall due on November 15. Late fees do not start until 60 days after the bills go out. After the due date the county adds interest monthly at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty accrues every 120 days up to 20%.

Homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty. Mobile homes sit on an April 1 schedule with a location permit, and the office can levy on unpaid property as a last resort.

Spalding County tax rules at a glance

Spalding County property tax rules
TopicRule
Assessed value40% of fair market value
Return seasonOpens January 1 and closes April 1
Land and building billsDue November 15
Appeal cutoffForty-five days after the notice mailing date
Homestead filingApplication in hand before April 1 earns the exemption for that tax year
Mobile home taxDue April 1
Delinquent tax salesHeld on a first Tuesday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

A mill is one thousandth of a dollar per dollar of assessed value. Exemptions come off the 40% assessed value first, and the millage rate applies to what remains.

How to contest a Spalding County value

You have forty-five days after the assessment notice goes out. Argue taxability, value or uniformity, and leave the size of the bill out of it. The assessors review first; the next stops are the equalization board or arbitration, then Superior Court.

The county sometimes stretches the homestead filing window to match the appeal period in a given year, so watch the notice for dates. Exemptions based on income have to be requested in person with proof of the prior year's income.

Homestead exemptions

The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly: age 65 before January 1, net income capped at $15,000, with bigger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption: age 62 or older, or totally disabled at any age, with household gross income capped at $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating school exemption for owners 65 and up, which freezes the value used for school tax.

An approved exemption carries forward until the owner moves, so a buyer applies fresh for the new address. Owners 62 and up with household income below $15,000 may have a deferral on file; the Tax Commissioner can confirm for your parcel.

Spalding County housing numbers

Spalding County has 70,775 people as of mid-2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base, living among 29,850 housing units. Owners occupy 62.7% of units, and 20.6% of residents are 65 or older, which puts the senior exemptions above in play for many sellers.

The middle home value is $228,700, median gross rent is $1,113 a month, and median household income is $62,071.

Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk all sit. Heirs selling an inherited house can reach the county Probate Court at (770) 467-4341.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Spalding County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Before you sell

  1. Call the Tax Commissioner at (770) 467-4360 for your parcel's balance, including interest and any penalty.
  2. Check with the Tax Assessor at (770) 467-4240 that your homestead exemption is on file, and tell a buyer it will not carry over, since they must apply for their own.
  3. Look at the notice of assessment. If the forty-five day appeal period is still open and the value looks high, file before it closes.
  4. If the house is outside Griffin and you plan repairs, call Community Development about permits first.
  5. Ask the closing attorney to show the tax proration on the settlement statement.

The bill goes to whoever owns the property on January 1, so a sale after that date means the contract has to say how the November bill is shared. A cash buyer will usually agree to a straightforward split and pay off any tax balance at closing.

Delinquent taxes and tax sales

Georgia law puts delinquent tax sales on a month's first Tuesday, within a 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. window. The sale takes place at 411 E. Solomon Street. Bidder rules:

  • Register on sale morning between 8:00 and 9:30.
  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Show a driver's license or other official ID.

Bidding usually starts around 10:00 or 10:30.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

When you sell a house with back taxes, ask for a payoff that includes interest and penalties, and have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds. That clears the lien risk and lets the buyer take clean title, and it keeps the closing from stalling at the last minute.

Deeds, zoning and permits

The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds, at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin. Call 770-467-4309 to reach the clerk, whose staff includes a deputy for real estate. The clerk's office is also where to get a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. The Planning Commission gathers on the last Tuesday evening of each month, and the Board of Appeals follows on the second Thursday, both at 6:00 p.m. in the Courthouse Annex. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. It has a permit technician and a business and alcohol license technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the Spalding County payment deadline?

November 15, for bills on land, buildings and business personal property. Late fees wait until 60 days after the bills are mailed.

What is the appeal cutoff after a Spalding County assessment notice?

Forty-five days after the notice is mailed. Assessors review first, then the equalization board or an arbitrator, and finally Superior Court.

What is the Spalding County late penalty?

Once November 15 passes, interest accrues each month, and penalties climb in 5% steps every 120 days to 20%. Homesteaded parcels with less than $500 due skip the penalty.

Where is the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's office?

411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, phone (770) 467-4360. It opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

Can I sell a Spalding County house that owes back taxes?

Yes, though the Tax Commissioner can levy on unpaid property and sell it at a tax sale. Request a payoff figure that includes interest and penalties so the balance can be settled from your closing proceeds.

Stephens County property tax offices

Two offices carry most of the work, and they sit in different buildings. The Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bills from Room 103 at 70 North Alexander Street in Toccoa, in the same government building as the county tag office. Weekday hours end at 4:45 in the afternoon. Call (706) 886-4753 or write to PO Box 187, Toccoa, GA 30577. The Tax Commissioner's website is maintained separately from the county's.

For values and homestead forms, call the Tax Assessor at (706) 886-7435. Returns also go there, because the assessors, not the Tax Commissioner, handle that job in Stephens County. Appraisers who visit a parcel carry photo ID and drive a marked county vehicle, usually after an appeal, a return or new construction.

Millage rates

Three rates apply to every parcel: Georgia's, Stephens County's and the Stephens County School System's. A fourth, the Toccoa city rate, is added for homes inside Toccoa city limits, so an in-town house carries one more layer than a rural parcel that only uses a Toccoa mailing address.

Stephens County taxes 40 percent of a property's market value, and each mill of tax equals $1 per $1,000 of that taxed amount. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education pick the rates. If you are unsure whether the address is in the city or the county, ask the Tax Assessor which digest holds the parcel.

Deadlines for returns, homestead and appeals

Stephens County property tax dates and rules
TopicRule
Who is chargedWhoever owns the property on January 1
Return seasonJanuary 1 through April 1, at the Tax Assessor
Same-year homesteadApply by April 1; a later filing waits for the next year
Bills on real estate and business personal propertyGenerally due November 15
Appeal of a noticeMust reach the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date
Skipping a required return10% on the value left off, plus interest
Refund of erroneous taxWritten claim to the commissioners within 3 years

Refunds cover errors of fault, not valuation disputes. Business personal property needs a yearly return by April 1, and real estate owners with no changes can skip one.

Homestead exemptions

Stephens County offers these exemptions:

  • Standard: $2,000 taken from the assessed value of the owner's primary residence, covering state, county and school tax, though municipal school levies are excepted.
  • Seniors 65 and up: an added local exemption, and another one if the owner's and spouse's net income did not top $10,000 the year before.
  • Age 62 school exemption: same $10,000 income ceiling, and it cannot exceed $10,000 of assessed value.
  • Floating inflation-proof exemption: owners 62 and up, with total household income under $30,000.
  • Disabled former service members: $50,000, passing to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.

Ownership and residence both have to be in place on January 1. An exemption renews itself unless ownership changes, which means a buyer files fresh. A tax deferral is a further option for owners 62 and older at $15,000 of gross income or below. A state Homeowners Tax Relief Grant that once showed up as a bill credit was withdrawn in 2008.

Stephens County housing numbers

Stephens County has 27,854 people as of mid-2025, up 4.0% from 26,780 at the 2020 base, spread over 12,461 housing units. Owners live in 73.6% of those units. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $175,300, a typical rent is $820, and median household income is $54,754. Most of the county's 178.86 square miles are outside any compact city grid, so expect rural and in-town parcels to be taxed differently.

Timber, equipment and vehicles

Property is taxable in the county where it sits, and the categories go beyond the house itself. Business equipment is assessed at 40 percent. Timber on the lot is treated differently, since it is taxed only when sold or harvested, and then at full market value. If you have timber or business equipment in an outbuilding, ask the Tax Assessor how each is carried on the digest.

Vehicle owners renew their registration and pay ad valorem tax every year in the 30 day period that ends on their birthday, and a newly bought vehicle must be registered within 30 days. The tag office is in the Stephens County Government Building at 70 N. Alexander Street, Room 103, with weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00. This registration is separate from the real estate bill.

Other deed related services include recording a plat, trade name registration and power of attorney filings, which can matter if an heir or an agent signs for the owner.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Stephens County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What recording a deed costs

The county's deed charges are:

  • Transfer tax of $1 per $1,000 of money paid.
  • A $25 filing fee.
  • A $5 blank deed form.
  • 50 cents a page for copies.

Per recorded deed, fifty cents of that tax is kept by the county and the rest goes to the state. The grantor's signature must be witnessed and notarized, and the clerk can help calculate what is due.

Warranty deeds must carry a transfer tax form whether or not money changes hands, and the forms can be completed online at the state clerks' authority site. Filing a deed is not required for it to be legal, but filing protects the owner. A closing attorney usually prepares the deed.

Paying or looking up your bill

Start at the county's Online Payments page, then use the Tax Assessor's online record search or tax estimator to look up a parcel.

A seller closing late in the year should agree with the buyer on who covers a bill charged to the January 1 owner. Call the Tax Commissioner for your parcel's balance ahead of any contract signing, and expect the payoff to come out of your sale proceeds. Unpaid tax can lead to a levy and sale, so clear any balance before you list, or have it paid at closing from your proceeds.

If you are selling an inherited house, the same offices apply. The deed work may involve a power of attorney or other filings at the clerk, so ask the clerk what to bring before you travel to Toccoa, and ask the Tax Assessor whether the late owner's homestead exemption must be refiled by the heir.

Bring the parcel number, your deed and your last bill when you call or visit. If you want to dispute a value, remember that the appeal must reach the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date, and one the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

Frequently asked questions

What is the usual payment date for a Stephens County tax bill?

Real estate and business personal property bills are generally due November 15. Check the date on your own bill, or call (706) 886-4753.

When must a Stephens County homestead application be filed?

April 1. A later filing takes effect the year after. Applications go to the Tax Assessor, and you must have lived in the home on January 1.

What is the appeal window for a Stephens County assessment notice?

Forty-five days from the notice date, counted by when the appeal is received. An appeal the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

Do Toccoa residents pay extra property tax?

Yes. Residents inside Toccoa city limits pay the Toccoa city millage in addition to the Georgia, Stephens County and Stephens County School System millage.

What does the county charge in transfer tax on a sale?

$1 per $1,000 of money paid, with fifty cents per deed staying in the county. Ask the Clerk of Court to confirm the figure for your sale.

Sumter County market snapshot

Sumter County has 28,801 people by the mid-2025 estimate, down from 32,819 in 2010 and 29,616 in 2020. Americus is both the county seat and the biggest city. Andersonville, De Soto, Leslie and Plains are the other cities. A shrinking buyer pool punishes a house with a messy tax record, which tends to sit longer than its neighbors.

Owner-held homes have a midpoint value of $120,200, and owners live in 56.6% of occupied homes. That means plenty of sellable properties are rentals or inherited houses, and some come with a tenant on a lease. The county issued just 36 building permits in 2025 against 13,653 housing units, so almost every sale is a resale.

Sumter County housing figures
MeasureValue
Midpoint value, owner-held homes (2020-2024)$120,200
Owner-occupied rate56.6%
Midpoint gross rent$857
Total housing units, 2025 estimate13,653
Building permits in 202536

Who bills and who values

Two county offices split the work, and a house inside Americus draws a third bill from the city. The tax commissioner is at 500 W. Lamar St., Americus. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1044, the phone is (229) 928-4530, and the counter is staffed weekdays from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m.

  • Commissioner: collects money, posts payments, takes homestead filings, handles mobile home and vehicle accounts.
  • Assessors: set fair market value and taxability, and receive returns in the winter filing window.
  • Americus finance office: sends city tax bills for parcels inside Americus.

The state revenue department's sheet for Sumter shows no local homestead breaks beyond the state's, but confirm that with the commissioner. The Tax Assessor page on the county site has contact details for the appraisal side.

Due dates and penalties

The county treats December 1 as the normal due date for land, buildings and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes fall due April 1, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday. Georgia's statewide default is December 20, and a county may move it to December 1 or November 15, so the date printed on your notice settles it.

After the due date, interest runs at 1 percent each month and a 10 percent penalty applies after 90 days. A homesteaded house billed under $500 avoids the penalty. Unpaid property can be levied on, though the office says it prefers other collection methods.

Americus uses its own calendar for the city portion:

  • Two installments, September 1 and December 20.
  • Installment one is based on half the prior year's total, and installment two true-ups to the current value and millage.
  • Interest of .542% per month, built from the federal prime rate plus 3%.
  • Penalty of 5% after 120 days, plus 5% more for each further 120 days, capped at 20%.

Before you pick a closing day, ask both offices for a written payoff with an expiration date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sumter County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who sets the millage rate?

The Sumter County commissioners and the county Board of Education set it each year. A mill means one dollar of tax for each thousand dollars assessed. Each body takes its budget needs, subtracts revenue from other sources, and picks the rate that raises the remainder.

Two neighbors with identical values can pay different totals when only one lives inside Americus, since the city adds its own rate on top of the county and school levies. The rate itself can't be argued in a value appeal. An appeal covers taxability, value and uniformity only.

How to appeal your assessment

Put it in writing no later than 45 days after the notice date. A late appeal is invalid, so mail it promptly and keep proof of the date.

Owners may also declare a value each winter on a return filed between the first of January and the first of April. If the board rejects your number, a notice with its own value follows. Appeals can argue taxability, value, or fairness against similar properties. Disliking the final bill is no ground, since the commissioners and school board set the rate.

Georgia also has a refund rule. A written request for money collected in error or illegally must begin within three years of payment, and an appealed assessment brings an automatic refund when the final value is set.

Homestead and other discounts

Homestead is the main one. You can apply at any point once the house is your main residence, provided the form arrives by April 1 of the first year you want relief. Not applying counts as waiving it.

  • Homestead: one application, then it carries forward.
  • Freeport: business inventory, if voters in the county approved it.
  • Mobile home permit: required 30 days after permanent placement, then renewed each year from January 1 to April 1.

Dollar amounts come from the state constitution and the General Assembly, so ask the commissioner for the current numbers.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sumter County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps before you list

Work through these in order, ideally a few weeks before you accept an offer, so no tax bill ambushes you at the closing table. It is mostly phone calls, and each office can usually answer in one conversation if you have the parcel number ready.

  1. Pull your latest bill and note whether it covers county, school and, inside Americus, city levies.
  2. Phone the commissioner and ask which years carry an open balance on the parcel.
  3. If the house is in Americus, make the same call to the city finance office.
  4. Confirm your homestead filing is on record, since a buyer's title company will look for it.
  5. For a manufactured home, ask about the April 1 permit tax and decal.
  6. Request written payoffs with an expiration date and hand copies to your closing agent.

If a house has sat vacant or passed through an estate, expect more than one open year and plan for a longer payoff list. A cash buyer can take the property as it stands and clear those balances at closing, so you skip the repair requests and lender timelines that slow a traditional sale.

Selling with taxes owed

Start by collecting payoffs: one from the county for each open year and another from Americus if the house lies within the city. A delinquent account can turn into a FIFA, a lien entered in the superior court clerk's records, and a title search will show it.

The year's bill belongs to the January 1 owner, the same date used to measure fair market value. For a June sale, your settlement statement splits the cost with the buyer, and the closing agent covers any balance out of your proceeds. A manufactured home adds an April 1 permit tax and decal to the list.

Inherited houses and former rentals often hold the heaviest balances, especially where nobody opened the mail for a few years. A cash purchase can settle those in a single closing.

Frequently asked questions

What address does the Sumter County tax commissioner use?

The office is at 500 W. Lamar St. in Americus, and mail goes to P.O. Box 1044. Call (229) 928-4530 or stop by weekdays from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m.

Is Sumter County's due date December 1 or December 20?

The county uses December 1 for real estate. Georgia's default is December 20 and a county may pull it earlier, so go by your notice.

How long can I wait to dispute a Sumter County value?

No more than 45 days after the date printed on your assessment notice. It must be written, and a late one is invalid.

Does living in Americus mean a second bill?

Yes. The city sends its own bill, with installments due September 1 and December 20, separate from the county's bill.

Can I sell a Sumter County house that owes back taxes?

You can. Get a payoff from the commissioner, then have the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds so the lien is released when the deed records.

Talbot County is quiet, hilly country in west central Georgia, with Talbotton as the county seat. Besides Talbotton, the municipalities are Woodland, Geneva and Junction City, and a piece of Manchester reaches in. Box Springs is a census-designated place, while Po Biddy Crossroads, Tax Crossroads and Centerville are unincorporated names that turn up on deeds. Population is 5,709, about 15 per square mile.

Most occupied homes here belong to the people living in them, 79.6%, and the midpoint value of such homes is $117,100. Renters pay a midpoint gross rent of $816. No building permits were issued in 2025 and the average commute is almost 43 minutes, so people live here and drive elsewhere for work while nobody adds houses. Nearly three in ten residents are past 65, so estates often put houses up for sale, and an heir meets the tax office before a buyer ever signs.

Where to get tax questions answered

The tax commissioner works from 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton and receives letters at P.O. Box 147. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm with a noon closure, and the phones are 706-665-3240 and 706-665-3280.

  • Tax commissioner: billing, collections, mobile home titles, timber tax, tax sales.
  • Tax assessors at 706-665-3377: value, returns, exemptions, appeal paperwork.
  • Commissioners' office, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: mobile home location permits.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax on recorded loan documents.

You can pay with cash, a check, a money order, or a Visa, MasterCard or Discover card, though card payments carry an added fee. The county's qPublic site lets you look up a parcel by owner or address.

Billing calendar and penalties

Real and personal property statements typically arrive in October and fall due December 20. Part-payments are welcome. After the deadline, interest accrues at prime plus 3%, and every 120 days a further 5% penalty is added until the total hits 20%.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow a January-to-April rhythm. Statements usually go out early in the year with an April 1 deadline, a decal is handed over once the tax is paid, and the return for a home in the county on January 1 is also due April 1. Filing late costs a 10% penalty.

Starting January 1, 2026, the garbage collection fee is $225.00 per year, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that charge rides on your parcel's account so the closing agent includes it.

Timber tax

Standing trees escape tax until sold or cut, and then 100 percent of fair market value is multiplied by the millage rate. There are three kinds of timber event.

  • Lump sum sale: the purchaser fills out form PT-283T and delivers form and tax to the commissioner inside five business days, and is personally liable if the seller fails to pay.
  • Unit price sale: a quarterly report goes to the seller and the assessors 45 days after each quarter closes.
  • Owner harvest: the landowner reports to the assessors 45 days after the quarter and pays the tax.

If you have cut or plan to cut trees, ask the office whether a timber account is open before you list.

Tax sales for unpaid taxes

The commissioner runs levy sales under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. A parcel is advertised in the Talbotton New Era for four straight weeks, then auctioned on the first Tuesday of the month after the notices end.

  • Location and time: the courthouse on South Washington Avenue, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • The county gives no title guarantee, and the bidder gets no access to the property and no rent for at least a year.
  • The high bidder pays in cash or certified funds as soon as the sale ends.
  • Money left after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request to 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

The commissioner's website has a guide to the right of redemption. An owner in arrears has time before the auction, and settling the account in a private sale may leave more equity with the seller.

How to appeal your assessment

A disputed value starts with a written filing to the Board of Assessors that names the route you want: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration, or hearing officer. The postmark must fall no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed.

A real estate return is due between January 1 and April 1 whenever something changed, and omitting a required one costs 10% of the unreported value. Personal property returns, form PT-50P, are filed yearly by April 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Talbot County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions and homestead

Exemptions go through the tax assessors. April 1 is the cutoff for the current year, and later filings roll to the next. Forms are accepted all year. Georgia's statewide exemptions apply here, and no local homestead exemption is added on top. An approved exemption renews itself until the owner moves or ownership changes.

Selling with taxes owed

Request a written payoff for each year still open, adding mobile home and timber accounts where they exist. With an inherited house, learn which years went unpaid before you list, since a recorded lien has to be paid at the table.

Refunds are narrow. A written request for tax paid in error goes to the Board of Commissioners within three years, and refunds are tied to errors of fault, not to a quarrel over value. Dividing the year's bill between buyer and seller happens on the settlement statement.

With so little building and a small buyer pool, a house with a tax cloud is harder to place. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can pay the balance out of your proceeds at closing. That skips the repair list and the wait on a lender, which matters most when an auction date is close.

If the house is inherited, the heirs usually need to settle who signs the deed before payoffs can be arranged, so start the tax inquiries early rather than waiting for a buyer to ask. The commissioner's staff can tell you which accounts, such as real estate, mobile home or timber, sit under the owner's name. Before you call the office, gather the parcel number, any mobile home title, and a note of whether timber has been cut. Ask for payoff figures in writing with the date they stay good through, and send them to your closing agent so every account is cleared when the deed records.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Talbot County tax commissioner's address?

The office is at 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with P.O. Box 147 for mail. Weekday service runs 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with a closure from noon to 1:00.

When are Talbot County property tax bills due?

December 20 for real and personal property, with statements typically mailed in October. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

Does Talbot County accept partial tax payments?

Yes. Interest and penalties still build on the remainder after the due date.

When do Talbot County tax levy sales happen?

They take place on a first Tuesday, once four weeks of Talbotton New Era notices have run, at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

What is the Talbot County homestead exemption cutoff?

April 1 for the current billing year. Forms are accepted all year, and a later one applies to the following year.

Tattnall County at a glance

Tattnall is a farm-and-river county in southeast Georgia. Reidsville holds the courthouse and Glennville is the biggest town. Municipalities are Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas and Reidsville, and Mendes is a census-designated place. Agriculture and the Vidalia onion are a big part of local life.

Population fell 10.5%, from 25,520 residents in 2010 to 22,842 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate of 24,376 shows a rebound. Owner-held homes have a midpoint value of $140,000 for 2020-2024, and owners fill 71.0% of occupied housing. Middle gross rent is $699. The county issued 74 building permits in 2025, and 82.3% of residents stayed in the same house over the past year, so some families are coming and going. The 28.1 minute average commute suggests many people work outside their own town.

Who handles what

Billing and collection happen at 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, with P.O. Box 920 for mail. The phone is 912-557-6736 and the hours are 8 to 5 on weekdays. The county also runs an online payment portal.

  • Tax commissioner: ad valorem tax, mobile homes, public utilities, timber, and vehicle tags.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: five members chosen by the county commissioners, with a chief appraiser directing the staff.
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury to hear disputed values.
  • County commissioners and school board: budgets that drive the millage.

The assessors, rather than the commissioner, receive returns. A state levy cannot exceed one fourth of a mill. The cities benefit from the vehicle and mobile home taxes the commissioner's office collects, so ask which accounts attach to your address.

Returns, homestead and use-based assessments

A taxpayer holding property on January 1 files a return between then and April 1. The first one renews itself at last year's final value, so a new filing is needed only for added property, improvements or a different value you want on record.

Homestead covers the house you own and live in, with paperwork going to the assessors' office. April 1 is the deadline, and Tattnall offers no local homestead exemptions beyond the statewide ones. Some county material asks for applications before March 1, so filing early avoids a miss.

  • Preferential agricultural property: assessed at 30 percent of fair market value instead of 40, with a ten year commitment.
  • Conservation use: valued by current use for bona fide farm or forest land, also ten years.
  • Environmentally sensitive and residential transitional land: current-use value, with applications taken January 2 through April 1.
  • Standing timber: no tax until it is sold or cut, then 100 percent of fair market value.

Before listing enrolled land, ask the assessors what the covenant means for the next owner.

How assessors arrive at a value

Fair market value is the price a knowledgeable buyer and a willing seller would agree on in an arm's length sale, fixed as of January 1. Assessed value is 40 percent of that, and each mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Assessors use three methods. Cost starts from replacement cost less depreciation and adds land, market compares nearby sales, and income capitalizes net rent on commercial or rental property. Business equipment and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent too. If you have a recent arm's length sale, hold on to the contract and settlement statement as your best market evidence.

Due dates and the relief grant

Read your statement first. Georgia treats December 20 as the standard date, lets a county switch to December 1, November 15 or installments, and gives each taxpayer 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts.

Mobile homes follow their own state schedule: a location permit within 30 days of permanent placement, then a return and permit renewal each year from January 1 to April 1.

One credit is not guaranteed. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant shows up only in years the General Assembly funds it, and bills climb when the money is absent. Ask what credit, if any, is on your statement.

How to contest a valuation

Once the assessors change a value, a written answer is due within 45 days of the notice date, and a late one is invalid.

Your reason has to be taxability, uniformity or value, and a gripe about the tax itself does not count. The assessors review first. If the number stands, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, and either side may continue to Tattnall County Superior Court. Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization if you choose it at filing.

Assessors read the market and do not invent prices. If a recent contract differs from the county's number, attach it to the appeal.

Steps before you list

A few calls early in the process keep the tax side from slowing a sale.

  1. Ask the commissioner for a statement of every open year on the parcel, including any mobile home or timber account.
  2. Check with the assessors that your homestead is on file and that any farm or conservation covenant is current.
  3. Find out whether the bill for the year of sale has been issued, and whether any relief grant credit appears on it.
  4. Give the title company the payoff figures so they can plan the closing statement.

Title companies search the courthouse records before closing, and anything recorded against the parcel has to be cleared for the deed to pass cleanly. Raising these items yourself keeps a buyer from finding them first and asking for a price cut.

Selling when tax goes unpaid

Delinquent parcels go to a courthouse sale held in the Commissioners Meeting room on the second floor. An auction caps a long delinquency, so an owner behind has choices well before then.

Get written payoffs by year, and for a mobile home confirm the decal and permit are settled. Tax is charged to whoever owns the property on January 1, and the settlement statement is where you and the buyer divide the year. Any earlier balance is then paid by the title company out of your proceeds.

Bring the parcel number, your last bill and any mobile home paperwork when you visit or call the commissioner. Ask for each open year to be listed separately. If the house is rural farmland enrolled in a use program, ask the assessors too, because leaving the program early can change what is owed. A cash buyer can take a house with a tax problem as it stands and settle the balance at closing, which saves you the repair requests and lender delays of a conventional sale.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I pay Tattnall County property tax?

At the tax commissioner's office, 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, or through the county's online payment portal. The phone is 912-557-6736 and the office keeps hours of 8 to 5 on weekdays.

What is the homestead cutoff in Tattnall County?

April 1 is the deadline, though some county material mentions March 1, so file before March to be safe. The assessors' office takes the form.

How much time do I have to appeal in Tattnall County?

Forty-five days from the date of the notice, in writing. Late appeals are invalid.

Does Tattnall County have its own homestead exemptions?

No. None are offered locally, so owners apply for the statewide exemptions.

Is timber taxed in Tattnall County?

Yes, when it is sold or harvested. The tax uses 100 percent of fair market value, and the rules cover lump sum, unit price and owner harvest sales.

Terrell County at a glance

Terrell County is southwest Georgia farm country around a single city. Dawson holds the courthouse and is the only city, and Bronwood, Parrott and Sasser are the three towns. The headcount keeps sliding: a 2020 count of 9,185 became a July 2025 estimate of 8,656, a 5.7% slide. Who handles property tax paperwork

  • Tax commissioner, (229) 995-5151: statements, payments, penalties and levies.

People who just bought should carry the warranty deed to the assessors when they apply for homestead, so collect it from the deed room first.

Due dates and penalties

Bills for land, buildings and business equipment have come due November 15 since 2018, while Georgia's default is December 20. Your notice carries the date that applies, so rely on it. Mobile homes are due April 1.

Late steps for land and buildings:

  • Interest lands on the 2nd of each month, computed as prime plus 3% over twelve.
  • A FIFA lien is filed with the Clerk of Courts once 30 days run out from the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5% penalty hits at 120 days and again every 120 days, stopping at 20%.
  • A file still open is handed to a collection firm, which tacks on administrative and levy charges that can reach $240.00 plus.

Those charges cover certified mail and a title search that readies the parcel for auction, and the property runs in the Herald Journal for four weeks first. By mail, a United States Postal Service postmark counts as on time, though a postage-meter stamp does not.

Mobile home taxes

Georgia classes a mobile or modular home as personal property. When one is in the county on January 1, the owner owes tax by April 1 and picks up a location permit at the same visit. Statements usually go out on January 2.

Missing April 1 draws a 10% penalty, and the county can send the owner to Magistrate Court or sell the home. On an overdue account, interest accrues on the 16th of each month, the penalty is applied April 2, and a FIFA is filed 30 days after the delinquent notice goes out. A decal must stay visible, and the assessors take questions at (229) 995-5210.

If a manufactured home is sold mid-year, find out which owner paid the permit tax before you set the closing.

Exemptions and how to appeal

Terrell's assessors take homestead filings, and the home must be both owned and lived in on January 1. A form can come in at any time, yet it must land by April 1 to cover that year. After approval it continues until you move.

Terrell County has local exemptions, and a local figure replaces the state one whenever it is larger. Ask the assessors for the current amounts before you list, so the figure on a buyer's tax estimate matches reality. Owners 62 and older may qualify for more relief. A deferral program lets those owners with gross household income of $15,000 or less delay payment until ownership changes or deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Farm land can be assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and Conservation Use values land on its actual use. Both ask for a covenant of ten years or more.

An appeal must start no later than 45 days after the notice, citing taxability, value or uniformity. Unresolved cases go on to the equalization board or an arbitrator, then Superior Court. For an owner on armed forces duty, a friend or relative can file within 90 days.

Business returns

Personal property returns on form PT-50p go to the Board of Assessors every year, no matter whether value or use has changed. An owner who no longer has a listed item must say so or stay on the roll for it, and skipping a required real estate return costs 10% of the value left off.

Business equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent of market value. Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption for raw goods, goods in process, or finished goods held for shipment out of state, filing between the first of January and April 1.

Before you sell

Phone the commissioner's office at (229) 995-5151 and request a written balance for every year, mobile home accounts included. Find out whether a FIFA sits on record at the superior court clerk's office, because a lien has to be paid off for a deed to record cleanly.

Georgia fixes value on the first day of January, so the commissioner can describe how the year of your sale will be billed. Tell the title company about each open item early, and ask the commissioner how long a payoff figure stays good, since interest moves on the 2nd of each month. A lien that surfaces at the closing table pushes the date out, and accounts that reached the collection stage cost more, since the added charges sit on top of the balance.

A cash buyer who accepts the property in its present condition can pay these amounts from your proceeds and close without repairs. If the house came to you through an estate, gather the deed or the paperwork showing who holds title before you visit the offices, since both the commissioner and the assessors will ask who the owner of record is. Having that answer ready saves a second trip.

Frequently asked questions

What number reaches the Terrell County tax commissioner?

Call (229) 995-5151. The office is at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson and is open from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays. Mail goes to P.O. Box 484.

Is Terrell County's due date November 15 or December 20?

Bills for land and buildings have come due November 15 since 2018, and December 20 is the state default. Follow the date shown on your own statement.

What is the Terrell County homestead deadline?

April 1 of the year you want the exemption. Apply with the assessors, and bring your deed if you recently bought.

How soon must I appeal a Terrell County assessment?

No later than 45 days after the notice. Valid grounds are taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint about the amount of tax is not one of them.

What if I skip a Terrell County tax payment?

Interest starts the 2nd of the following month, a FIFA lien follows 30 days after the delinquent notice, and a 5% penalty builds every 120 days up to 20%. A long unpaid account is passed to a collection firm and can end in a sale.

Thomas County market snapshot

Thomas County borders Florida and centers on Thomasville, which is both the seat and the biggest town. Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs and Pavo are cities and Ochlocknee is a town. Barwick and Pavo spill over into Brooks County, and Meigs reaches into Mitchell.

Homeowners hold a solid majority here, 63.8% owner-occupancy for 2020-2024, and prices are firm. The 2020 count was 45,798 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 46,368, growth of 1.3%. The county has 18,684 households, and 21.0% of residents are past their 65th birthday. Builders pulled just 203 permits in 2025, so an older Thomasville bungalow faces little new-construction competition.

Thomasville is the hub of the market, and the Red Hills setting and the Ochlockonee, Suwannee and Aucilla watersheds shape rural parcels in the county's outer areas. For a rural parcel, ask the assessors how acreage is recorded, because that figure feeds the bill.

Public education is split between Thomasville City Schools within the city limits and Thomas County Schools for the rest. A house on one side of that boundary draws a different set of school-minded buyers than one a few blocks over.

Which offices bill and value property

The work is split between two offices. The tax commissioner sends bills and takes payment. The board of tax assessors places a value on each parcel and receives exemption applications.

The tax commissioner is at 225 N. Broad Street, Thomasville 31792, or by mail at P.O. Box 2175, Thomasville 31799. The number is (229) 225-4136. The counter is staffed on weekdays, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at 5, and the office's website posts a holiday closing list.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, delinquent balances, payoff amounts before a tax sale
  • Tax assessor: values, returns, homestead filings, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens
  • Seven city tax departments: Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville bill their own residents

County commissioners pick the county rate, the school board picks the school rate, and the state sets its own by law. Someone living in Thomasville may see a city bill on top of the county one, so ask both offices what is owed.

Due dates and penalties

Payment falls due each November 15, and the county takes anything stamped by the post office on or before that day. A bill lost in the mail does not cancel what you owe.

Delinquent totals reset on the sixteenth of every month, so a payoff quote goes stale quickly. Mobile homes pick up penalties each April 2. Skipping a required return carries its own charge: 10% of whatever value went unreported, with interest on top.

  • Regular property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home penalties: added April 2
  • Past-due totals: change on the 16th
  • Unfiled return: 10% of unreported value plus interest

Tax sales happen at the commissioner's discretion, one or two times annually. Call the office for the precise payoff before any sale date, because a figure printed on last year's bill will not match.

Selling with taxes owed

The January 1 owner is on the hook for that year's bill. Georgia gives no partial-year refund, which means a deed signed the next day still leaves the whole year with the seller.

Most often the closing attorney asks the commissioner for the balance and deducts it from what the seller nets, or the contract spreads the year across both parties. Request the figure in writing, note the date it stays valid through, and ask whether a city bill is also open. Unpaid tax can become a lien filed with the superior court clerk, and a buyer's title company will insist that it be cleared before funds move.

If back tax and deferred repairs pile up on one house, an as-is buyer can absorb both and clear the balance at the closing table. That saves listing prep, showings and the wait on a buyer's lender. It does not erase the debt, because the county is paid either way.

A practical order of work: call the commissioner for the balance, ask the city office if the house sits inside a city, check the clerk's records for any filed lien, and pass every figure to your closing attorney. Bring your parcel number, your last bill and a copy of your deed to any office visit. Doing this before you accept an offer lets you price the house knowing exactly what comes off the top at closing.

How to contest a value

Put the challenge on paper and deliver it to the assessors. You get 45 days, starting from the mailing date printed on the assessment notice. The right to appeal comes from O.C.G.A. 48-5-311.

Georgia allows four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The form must say how you want to proceed, from three choices: an equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. If the assessors and the owner cannot agree, the appeal moves along to the Board of Equalization on its own. Objections to the tax rate are not part of a value appeal.

  • Deadline: 45 days from the notice mailing
  • Where to file: the assessors' office
  • If unresolved: Board of Equalization, then court

Assessed value is set at 40% of market value, measured on the January 1 valuation date. Market value is defined broadly enough to include a short sale, bank sale or auction sale, so a distressed sale of your own home can serve as evidence.

Homestead exemption

Homestead leads the list, and the form goes to the assessor's office. April 1 is the cutoff, and anything arriving afterward takes effect the next year. Forms are accepted all year long.

Thomas County grants local homestead relief that beats the state version, and the assessor can quote the current amounts. Ask for them directly instead of guessing, and write down the date and the name of the person you spoke with so the closing attorney can follow up.

Before you list, confirm the exemption sits on the parcel. A lender and a closing attorney will read the bill, and a missing exemption makes the number look larger than it should. The next owner has to apply for themselves, since a sale partway through the year does not carry your filing forward.

Frequently asked questions

Which phone reaches the Thomas County tax commissioner?

Dial (229) 225-4136. The office sits at 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville and takes calls on weekdays between 8 in the morning and 5 in the evening. Ask for the assessor's office if your question concerns value or an exemption.

What is the Thomas County property tax deadline?

November 15 each year, with mail postmarked by that day accepted. Overdue amounts change on the 16th of every month, and mobile home penalties begin April 2.

Will selling erase this year's tax in Thomas County?

No. Georgia returns nothing for a partial year, so the January 1 owner carries that bill. At closing the attorney typically settles it out of the seller's proceeds, or the contract shares it.

How many days does an assessment appeal allow in Thomas County?

Forty-five days from the date the notice went out in the mail. Write to the assessors, and mark your preferred hearing path on the form.

Does Thomasville bill its own tax separately?

Yes. Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city taxes. Contact that city's tax department for the city portion.

Tift County market snapshot

Tift County is the small, dense county around Tifton in south central Georgia. Tifton is the seat and largest city, Omega and Ty Ty are the other cities, and Phillipsburg and Unionville are census-designated places. Chula and Brookfield are unincorporated. Interstate 75 runs through the county, and a single school system, the Tift County School District, runs the public schools countywide.

Tift packs in 158.5 people per square mile, and owners occupy 61.0% of housing units for 2020-2024. Headcount is up 2.2% since April 2020. With 41.6% of occupied homes rented, a Tifton house with a tenant already in it can attract a landlord-minded buyer. Mention the lease at the start and let the buyer judge.

Tift County housing figures (counts are July 2025 estimates; value and rent span 2020-2024)
MeasureTift County
Residents42,254
Housing units18,311
Middle home value, owners$165,200
Middle monthly rent$777
Building permits in 2025177

Which offices bill and which values

The commissioner collects the money and then sends it on to the state, the county, the city and the school board. Values come from the assessors. Two separate offices, two separate phone lines.

The tax commissioner takes mail at P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793, answers at (229) 386-7820, and stays open on weekdays from half past eight until five. The tax assessors take mail at P.O. Box 134, Tifton, GA 31793, and answer at (229) 386-7840 from eight to five, Monday through Friday.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, online payments, delinquent accounts, tax sales
  • Tax assessors: real and personal property values, mobile home decal reviews, exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and executions

The commissioner's office also collects city taxes, so one office can answer for a Tifton address and an unincorporated one.

Due dates and payment plans

The regular bill is due November 15 and the mobile home bill April 1.

Installments are welcome online for property tax. No minimum opens a payment plan, since the office names an amount once arrangements are made so the balance clears on schedule. Mobile home owners can pay in pieces too, with the decal withheld until nothing is left owing.

  • Property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home tax: April 1
  • Partial payments: accepted online for property tax
  • Decal: issued only after a mobile home balance is paid in full

Clearing a delinquent bill does not hand over the property. That settles any rumor to the contrary.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tift County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How a bill is figured

The bill starts with the assessor's market value as of January 1, then takes 40% of it as the assessed value. Subtract any homestead exemption from that assessed value, including the state's standard $2,000 exemption, and multiply the remainder by the millage rate.

One mill is a dollar of tax per thousand dollars of assessed value. Tift County officials set their own part of the rate, the school board sets its part, and the state adds a small levy of its own. Cities that levy a tax add a further rate on top, which is why two houses with the same value can receive different bills.

  • Step one: market value on January 1
  • Step two: 40% of that value, less exemptions
  • Step three: multiply by the combined millage rate

The county website links to an online parcel search, so you can look up your own value, owner of record and acreage before talking to either office. Check the acreage and the building description for errors, because a wrong square footage carries straight into the bill.

Steps before you list

Tift's offices are separate, so a short round of calls up front saves time later.

  1. Look up your parcel online and check the acreage and building description.
  2. Call the commissioner at the number above for the balance on every open year, and ask whether a city tax applies to the address.
  3. Call the assessors to confirm your exemption is on file and ask whether any recent permit work may raise the value.
  4. Give your closing attorney the written figures so they can build the settlement statement.

If the house is a rental with a tenant, tell the buyer early, and ask the tenant to keep the lease available. Tax is billed to the owner of record, so the tenant does not change what you owe.

What an assessor visit means

It usually means an appraiser is checking on a change. Homes that traded hands during the previous 12 months get a field review, and O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 sets the notice rule.

Further triggers: a permit for a remodel, pool or outbuilding, a reported fire or storm loss, a parcel split or merger, and an application for a covenant or exemption. Field work clusters between December and May. Staff arrive in a marked county vehicle with identification, and an owner who prefers a set time can book one at (229) 386-7840.

If you just finished permitted work, expect the next notice to show a higher value. Hold on to the permit and photos of the house before the work, which help if you contest the new figure.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tift County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax sales and unpaid taxes

The levying office notifies the delinquent taxpayer in writing, and 30 days later an execution, called a fi. fa., can follow on the General Execution Docket kept by the superior court clerk. The lien on property attaches every January 1, even before any execution exists.

That officer acts as ex-officio sheriff and may advertise and auction the parcel. These are buyer-beware sales, opening at the taxes, penalties and costs owed. The winner gets a sheriff's tax deed, which is not a fee simple deed, and state law bars possession for 12 months while redemption rights remain.

A seller gains nothing from reaching that stage. Ring (229) 386-7820 and get a payoff figure in hand before you list or take an offer. A house that is behind on tax and in rough shape can also go to a cash buyer who buys as-is and accounts for the tax. That route skips repairs, showings and the wait on a buyer's loan, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds at closing.

How to appeal your assessment

Submit the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Forty-five days run from the day the notice was mailed. The permitted grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Your first filing has to pick a forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. State staff cannot override local boards on one parcel. Assessment is set at 40% of fair market value, so compare the market value on the notice with recent sales of similar homes near you. Attach what you find to the appeal.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I reach the Tift County tax commissioner?

Call (229) 386-7820 or write to P.O. Box 930, Tifton, GA 31793. Weekday hours begin at 8:30 in the morning and end at 5 in the afternoon.

Are installments allowed for Tift County property tax?

Yes, the county takes partial payments online. No fixed amount starts the plan, and the office sets one after you make arrangements. Mobile home owners can split payments as well but get the decal only once they have paid everything.

Does clearing a delinquent bill give me the property in Tift County?

No. Paying delinquent tax does not transfer ownership. Auction buyers get a sheriff's tax deed and, under state law, wait 12 months after the sale before taking possession.

Who collects city tax inside Tifton?

The Tift County tax commissioner does. The office collects city taxes and distributes funds to the state, the county and the school board as well.

What is the cutoff for contesting a Tift County value?

The cutoff is 45 days after the assessment notice was mailed. Send your appeal to the Tift County assessors, phone (229) 386-7840 with questions, and pick your path on the form.
