Toombs County market snapshot

Toombs County is in southeast Georgia, with Lyons holding the courthouse and Vidalia ranking as the biggest city. The cities are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, and Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson have no municipal government. The Toombs County School District runs the public schools.

Houses here are the least expensive of the Georgia counties near it. The 2020-2024 median is $137,000, and owners occupy 60.5% of units. The county recorded just 35 building permits for 2025, so nearly every sale involves an existing house. Of 12,027 housing units counted in 2020, 12.7% were empty. Population is estimated at 27,545 for mid-2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base.

Toombs County housing figures (units and permits are 2025 data; the rest cover 2020-2024)
MeasureResult
Middle home value, owners$137,000
Owner outlay each month, with mortgage$1,227
Owner outlay each month, no mortgage$378
Middle monthly rent$768
Housing units12,237
Building permits35

Which office mails the bill and which sets the value

The commissioner handles billing and collection from 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, GA 30436. The phone is (912) 526-8575. Weekday service runs from half past eight to half past four.

The assessors, who determine value and take returns and exemption forms, answer at (912) 526-6291. For a copy of your warranty deed, go to the clerk of superior court's deed room in the courthouse.

  • Tax commissioner: statements, payments, decals for mobile homes, delinquent sales
  • Assessors: valuation, returns, homestead filings, first-level appeals
  • Equalization board: named by the Grand Jury to hear disputes
  • County commissioners and school board: adopt the millage rates

The commissioner does not decide value or rates. Anyone upset about how large the bill is should talk to the elected boards that levy it.

Due dates and penalties

Statements leave the office by October 20. Real estate and business personal property bills have been due November 15 since 2018, while Georgia's default is December 20. Rely on the date on your own statement and call (912) 526-8575 if it looks off.

After the deadline, interest runs at 1% monthly and a 10% penalty applies to tax unpaid 90 days out. Past 30 days, a fi. fa., which is a recorded lien, may be filed. Those records are open to the public, so credit bureaus can see them.

  • Interest on real estate: 1% each month
  • Penalty once 90 days pass: 10%
  • Lien: allowed once 30 days pass unpaid
  • Mobile homes: April 1, then 10% plus 1% a month

Delinquent parcels can go to an auction on the courthouse steps. The list for any sale can be seen at the office, where staff can tell you the next one.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Toombs County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Before you sign a contract, have the commissioner state the parcel's balance in writing. Georgia gives no refund for a part year, which leaves the January 1 owner holding the whole amount.

Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia are cities, and a home inside one may owe city tax along with county tax. Ask whether both apply. If you have fallen behind, check the clerk's records for a recorded lien too, since a title company will want it released. When the roof, wiring or plumbing needs money you lack, an as-is cash buyer removes the repair bill, and any tax owed comes out of the price at closing.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed are the two papers that move a closing fastest. Ask the office how long each figure stays valid, since interest adds every month and an old quote will come up short.

Steps before you list

Toombs County sellers can head off most tax delays with a few calls.

  1. Ask the commissioner for a written balance on every open year and any mobile home account.
  2. If the house is inside Lyons, Santa Claus or Vidalia, ask the city about its own bill.
  3. Ask the assessors whether your homestead exemption is on file, since the buyer will start from a clean slate.
  4. Get a copy of your recorded deed from the clerk's deed room.
  5. Hand all of it to the closing agent, who will pay the balances out of your proceeds.

Homes that were rentals or came through an estate tend to carry older balances, so start there. A cash buyer can close on a house with open tax and sort out the payoff at the table.

Property returns

Anything taxable that you own on January 1 is supposed to be returned to the assessors during the first three months of the year, ending April 1. An owner who files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value and real estate exemptions.

An owner who thinks the value is too high may file a return giving their own opinion of market value, and that filing establishes appeal rights if the assessors change the figure again. The commissioner bills real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber taxes.

  • Window: opens January 1, closes April 1
  • Silence: last year's value and exemptions repeat
  • Own-value return: sets up an appeal if the assessors disagree

Household goods are not normally taxable, so a seller does not owe tax on furniture left in the house.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Toombs County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption amounts

The regular exemption goes to owners who live in the house before January 1. The amounts are $20,000 off assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax and $2,000 off the state share. A city house gets a further $10,000 off city and city school tax.

Further categories carry labels: S3 for age 62 and up with an income test, S4 and SC for age 65 and up, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local school-tax exemption at 70 and over. The 62-and-over school exemption uses a $10,000 earned-income limit for the prior year. Because details vary by category, ask the assessors which one fits your situation.

Applications are received between January 1 and April 1, and state law allows no extension. Once approved, the exemption repeats yearly until eligibility changes. Moving to a new address means filing again.

How to challenge an assessment

Mail a letter to the Toombs County assessors. The 45 days are counted from the date on the notice, and notices tend to arrive in spring.

Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. Three tracks are open: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. A dispute can then move on to Superior Court. Mobile homes keep a separate clock. A different value may be declared inside 45 days of the bill mailing, and a change notice opens a 21-day window to go to the equalization board.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best way to reach the Toombs County tax commissioner?

Phone (912) 526-8575 or visit 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons, any weekday between half past eight and half past four.

Does Toombs County tax come due in November or December?

Real estate bills have been due November 15 since 2018, and December 20 is the state default. Use the date on your bill, and double-check with the commissioner.

What does paying Toombs County tax late cost?

One percent interest accrues monthly after the deadline, and tax still open 90 days later takes a 10% penalty. A lien may be filed after 30 days.

When are Toombs County mobile home taxes due?

They fall due each April 1. Later payments draw a 10% filing penalty plus 1% per month, and a location permit and decal come only after full payment.

How much time does an owner get to dispute a Toombs County value?

Forty-five days, starting at the date on the assessment notice. Write to the assessors and say which route you want: equalization board, hearing officer or arbitrator.

Towns County market snapshot

Towns County lies in the north Georgia mountains against the North Carolina border. Hiawassee is the county seat, while Young Harris is the largest city. Lake Chatuge fills the northeast corner, and the Chattahoochee National Forest covers part of the county, which gives many parcels a mountain or lake view.

The population is older, values run high, and owners dominate: 82.3% owner occupancy for 2020-2024 and a typical home value of $316,100. Headcount is up 6.4% over the 2020 base, and 41.2% of residents are past 65. The 2020 count found 8,600 housing units with 36.4% vacant, and some of those may be seasonal or second homes. A person who inherits a mountain cabin from afar should make sure the tax statement is forwarded to a current address.

Towns County housing figures (July 2025 for units and residents, 2020-2024 for the remaining rows)
MeasureResult
Middle home value, owner-held$316,100
Owner cost per month, mortgaged$1,431
Owner cost per month, mortgage-free$470
Middle monthly rent$808
Housing units9,120
Residents13,285

Which office handles which question

Statements and payments go through the tax commissioner in the courthouse annex, 48 River Street, Suite H, Hiawassee, GA 30546, phone (706) 896-2267. Weekday service runs from 8:30 until 4:30, with a lunch closure between noon and 1.

The assessor is down the hall in Suite G, reachable at (706) 896-3984 on the same weekday schedule. Parcel records appear on qPublic, which is free. You can also pay online through the county tax website.

  • Commissioner: statements, payments, levies, mobile home tax
  • Assessor: valuations, returns, homestead and conservation forms, mobile home registration
  • Superior court clerk: deeds, with copies handled in the deed room

The county Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rates. The commissioner's office does not.

Due dates and penalties

January 10 is the real estate due date here, which falls later than the usual Georgia schedule. For a check in the mail, a post office postmark counts, and a postage-meter mark does not.

After the date passes, a monthly interest charge posts on the 10th, calculated as the prime rate plus 3 points spread over 12 months. A 5% penalty follows at 120 days, repeating each 120 days until the total reaches 20%. Mobile home bills generally go out about January 2, payable by April 1, with 10% added on April 2.

  • Real estate: due January 10
  • Interest: posted on the 10th of each month
  • Penalty: 5% every 120 days until it reaches 20%
  • Mobile homes: April 1 deadline, 10% penalty the next day

Twelve months of nonpayment sends an account to a collection agency, with administration and levy fees of up to $215 and more, followed by four weeks of newspaper notices ahead of any sale. Pay or arrange terms well before that point.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Towns County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property returns

An owner files an initial return for taxable real and personal property held on January 1, and real estate returns for changed or newly acquired property are due at the assessor's office from January 1 through April 1. After the first real estate return, the law renews it automatically at the prior year's value unless the owner adds land, builds, or otherwise changes the property.

Personal property differs: returns on form PT-50p are filed every year, whatever happened to value or use. An owner who no longer holds the listed items needs to tell the assessor, or the tax keeps coming. Skipping a required return carries a 10% penalty on the unreported value, plus interest and possibly more penalties.

  • New or changed real estate: file by April 1
  • Personal property: file every year
  • Missed return: 10% of the unreported value, plus interest

An owner unhappy with the current value can file a new return stating a different one. If the assessors reject it, that filing starts the appeal described below.

Deferral and conservation use

Two programs can follow a parcel into a sale. Tax deferral is open to owners age 62 or older whose gross household income is $15,000 or less. It postpones the bill rather than wiping it out, and the deferred amount generally comes due at a change of ownership or once it reaches 85% of fair market value.

Conservation use is the other. Farm or timber land that qualifies is valued by its current use, and in return the owner signs a 10-year covenant with the assessors. A purchaser who continues the same use and signs the covenant owes no penalty, while a change of use triggers one. Acreage in the hills may already be under a covenant, so check before listing.

Call the assessor at (706) 896-3984, ask whether either program applies to your parcel, and request the terms in writing. A cash buyer taking the home in its present condition will ask for the same figures before closing.

Homestead exemption

File a homestead application at the Towns County Tax Assessor's Office, and bring a copy of the warranty deed if you are a first-time homeowner. Anything received after April 1 counts toward the next year.

Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. An approved exemption renews itself, though a move, a transfer of title or a switch to another type means applying again. Local exemptions replace the state amounts when the local figure is bigger, so get the current amounts from the assessor rather than an old chart.

A buyer does not inherit your exemption. The next bill, now in the buyer's name, can run higher until the new owner files.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Towns County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How an appeal works

Take the appeal to the assessors in writing, counting 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. The grounds are taxability, value, and uniformity with similar properties. Disagreement over the amount of tax levied does not qualify.

When the assessors leave the value alone, the case moves to the equalization board, and Superior Court is the next stop. Arbitration can stand in for the equalization hearing. For an owner away on military duty, a relative or friend may file inside 90 days of the notice.

Mobile homes use a separate track, with 45 days to file with the assessors and 21 days after a change notice to reach the equalization board.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the commissioner for a written balance on every open year, mobile home accounts included, before you accept an offer. Check the superior court clerk's records for any recorded lien, since a title company will want it released before funds move.

The closing agent normally pays those balances out of your proceeds. If the cabin has sat empty, mail may have piled up unread, so ask for the full account history rather than just the latest bill. A cash buyer can take a house that carries tax debt as it stands and clear the balance at the table.

Frequently asked questions

When must Towns County real estate tax be paid?

January 10 every year, with mobile home tax due April 1. A mailed check needs a post office postmark, because a postage-meter mark is not accepted.

How do I contact the Towns County tax commissioner?

Call (706) 896-2267 or visit 48 River Street, Suite H, Hiawassee. Staff are in Monday to Friday, 8:30 until 4:30, and step out for lunch at noon for an hour.

What does late payment cost in Towns County?

Monthly interest posts on the 10th using the prime rate plus 3 points. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns every 120 days until it hits 20%. Mobile homes pick up a 10% penalty on April 2.

How long can I take to contest a Towns County value?

The window is 45 days counted from the notice's mailing date. Send it to the assessors at (706) 896-3984, and an unsettled appeal moves on to the equalization board.

Will the buyer inherit my Towns County homestead exemption?

No. It renews each year for the same owner, and a change of ownership calls for a fresh application. The buyer files with the assessor's office by April 1.

Troup County market snapshot

Troup County sits on Georgia's western edge against the Alabama line. LaGrange is the county seat and largest city, and Hogansville and West Point are the other incorporated places. Long Cane, Mountville, Harrisonville and Abbottsford are unincorporated communities. Interstate 85 and Interstate 185 cross the county, so Atlanta commuters and Columbus-area workers both choose to live here.

A bungalow in LaGrange, a lakeside lot near West Point and a farm tract outside Hogansville attract quite different buyers, and each can come with its own tax history. Population is 72,844, which is 4.9% above the April 2020 base. Roughly 61 of every 100 housing units are lived in by their owners, and the middle owner-occupied value is $217,200. Seniors account for 17.8% of residents, so inherited houses and estate sales appear regularly.

Which office does what

Your tax passes through two separate desks. One collects money. The other, a citizens board served by the Property Appraisal Department, decides what the parcel is worth.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 883-1620, open on weekdays from 8 to 5, for bills, mobile home and timber tax, and tag renewals.
  • Property Appraisal: (706) 883-1625, at 100 Ridley Avenue, Suite 2100, LaGrange, for values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Superior Court clerk: where deeds and tax liens are recorded.

The assessors are a part-time citizens board, so a call may land on voicemail and be returned later. That board picks the Chief Appraiser and gets its budget from the county commission. Card and online payments run through the county portal, which has a Property Taxes choice, and the tax office also takes payment by phone.

Due dates and how the bill is figured

November 15 is the official deadline, with penalties and interest piling up after it. Counties may move the statewide default, so read the date printed on the bill you actually receive.

Georgia freezes market value as of January 1 and then taxes 40% of it. Millage comes from the school board, the county governing authority and any other body that covers your parcel. A sample calculation from the appraisal office uses .030260 as the rate and takes off exemptions first. Mobile homes and timber reach the same collector on their own timetables.

  • The state ratio is 40%, applied to market value.
  • One mill means a dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value.
  • A higher value or a dropped exemption can lift a bill while the rate stays flat.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals grow out of the yearly assessment notice, and you get 45 days after the notice date shown on its face. Once that passes, you lose the chance to challenge that year's number.

The appraisers want sales records, photos of similar houses that changed hands lately, and whatever else supports your figure. A Board of Equalization hearing usually follows. Grand jurors name its members, who are neighbors and fellow owners, and filing is free. Arbitration is the other lane: each party hires one arbitrator and splits a third. Going on to Superior Court adds a $25.00 filing fee.

After a board or court rules, the assessors cannot move that value for two years without walking the parcel themselves.

City bills in LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point

Possibly. A city levies its own ad valorem tax, and its clerk bills and collects it, unless the city and county have agreed to one combined statement. Ask the tax commissioner at (706) 883-1620 and the clerk of your city before you assume one payoff covers everything.

Taxpayers get at least 60 days from the postmark of a bill before interest starts. A parcel inside city limits can therefore owe two separate payoffs at closing, one to the county and one to City Hall, and each may carry its own due date. Collect both figures in writing.

Homestead and other exemptions

Homestead filings are taken from the first of January through April 1. Miss the window and you forfeit the benefit for that year. Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 hands out the forms and quotes the amounts.

Other special exemptions are kept in the same office. Skipping a return means you are deemed to have returned the same property at last year's final value, and freeport relief for inventory needs a local vote. A move means filing again for the new address.

  • Own the house and live in it on January 1.
  • A refund claim for a tax wrongly assessed has a three-year limit from payment.
  • Mobile homes sit on a separate location permit and return cycle.

Steps before you list

Troup County has several moving parts, so work through them in order and keep every figure in writing.

  1. Call the tax commissioner at (706) 883-1620 and ask for the balance on each year still open, including any mobile home or timber account.
  2. If the house is inside LaGrange, Hogansville or West Point, ask the city clerk for a separate payoff.
  3. Call Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 to confirm your homestead is on file and to ask whether a recent change to the house has been picked up.
  4. Ask the Superior Court clerk whether any lien is recorded against the parcel.
  5. Give the payoff letters to the attorney or title agent handling the sale.

Written figures matter because interest and penalties keep building, and a verbal quote from last month may fall short. The payoffs come out of your proceeds, so you will know your net before you commit to a price. Sellers of inherited or estate-held or long-vacant houses should allow extra time, since several years of records may need to be pulled.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the collector for a payoff amount ahead of scheduling the closing, and let the attorney or title agent pay it from what you receive. Each year's bill goes to whoever held title on January 1, so an October sale can still leave a statement in your mailbox unless the settlement sheet divides the tax.

The tax commissioner's news page posts a courtesy tax sale list. Excess funds after such a sale go only to the record owner at that time or to other lienholders. A home that spent years as a rental, an estate asset or an empty shell may owe for several years, so request every year's status in writing.

A cash buyer can still close while a balance is open, because the payoff is deducted at the table. Set the closing statement next to the payoff letter and compare each line. Bring your parcel number and a copy of your deed when you call or visit, and ask the clerk of superior court whether any lien is recorded against the property.

Frequently asked questions

How do I phone the Troup County tax office?

The number is (706) 883-1620. Questions about value or exemptions go to Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625.

Is November 15 the Troup County payment deadline?

Yes. November 15 is the official deadline, and penalties and interest follow it. Confirm against your own statement.

How long can I challenge a Troup County assessment?

Forty-five days after the notice date. A late filing forfeits the right for that year, and appeals cannot be filed without a notice.

When does Troup County take homestead applications?

From New Year's Day through April 1. Anything filed later waits for the next year.

Who owes the tax if I sell in October?

The person who owned it on January 1 is billed. Pay it at closing, after getting the payoff letter from the tax commissioner.

Twiggs County market snapshot

Twiggs County calls itself the geographic center of Georgia. Jeffersonville is the county seat. The north end rolls like the Piedmont, while the south has the flat pine woods of south Georgia, and kaolin, forestry and farming have long driven the economy. Interstate 16 runs through the middle, linking Macon and Savannah, and two industrial parks of 150 and 500 acres sit where I-16 meets Highway 96.

Nearly nine in ten Twiggs homes, 88.2%, house their owners, and the middle value is $111,300. People are leaving more than arriving: the 2025 estimate of 7,597 sits 5.4% under the 2020 base of 8,028. Builders pulled just 13 permits in 2025, and 96.1% of residents had not moved in the prior year. The county averages 22.3 people per square mile, so many parcels are acreage, timber or family land handed down. A seller with that kind of property often values a quick as-is closing over weeks of showings.

Households, 2020 to 20242,888

Many owners have little cash set aside for repairs or back taxes. A seller in that position can ask the tax commissioner early what payoff will come out of the proceeds and weigh an as-is sale against fixing the house first.

Which office handles which question

The courthouse at 425 Railroad Street in Jeffersonville holds the offices you need, and each has its own job.

  • Tax commissioner, (478) 945-3359, mail to P.O. Box 187: property and motor vehicle tax, tags and titles.
  • Assessors and Chief Appraiser, Room 102, (478) 945-3663, mail to P.O. Box 111: values, returns, homestead, current-use and forest land programs, and appeals.
  • County commissioners: adopt the budget and help set the county millage.

The assessors' board gathers on the first Thursday of every month in Room 102, starting at nine in the morning, and the office accepts walk-in filings during the nine-to-five business day. A field appraiser with photo identification in a marked county vehicle may stop by a parcel to check data tied to an appeal, return, permit or sale.

Due dates and late payment

Go by the date on your own statement. The Georgia default is December 20, but a county can choose December 1 or November 15 or bill in installments, which makes the Twiggs tax commissioner the final word on yours.

Interest cannot start until 60 days after the bill's postmark, and unpaid balances may add penalties on top. Phone (478) 945-3359 for the exact date, the current interest rate and a payoff on any past-due year. Mobile home owners should ask separately, since the permit and return follow their own early-year cycle.

  • A refund claim for tax wrongly assessed must start within three years after you paid.
  • In some counties the city clerk bills municipal tax, so confirm whether a Jeffersonville or other city bill applies to your parcel.

How to appeal your assessment

Notices of assessment are mailed in late May or early June, and the deadline is 45 days after the printed date. A plain letter works as well as the form if it lists the parcel ID, address, daytime phone, your chosen route and your evidence. Hand-delivered or postmarked papers count. Late filings are not processed, and the office refuses email and fax.

You pick one of three routes when you file:

  • Board of Equalization: free, with three local property owners who each completed at least 40 hours of training. Either party has 30 days to carry the result to Superior Court.
  • Nonbinding arbitration: you provide a certified appraisal dated no more than nine months before January 1, plus a $214 check to the Clerk of Superior Court. If the county accepts your appraisal, the fee comes back.
  • Hearing officer: for value or uniformity disputes over non-homestead property or wireless personal property above $500,000, at no filing cost.

Timing differs by route. On the hearing officer path, the assessors have up to 90 days to review and answer, you then have 30 days to say you are unhappy, and the assessors have another 30 days to send the file to the appeal administrator. If no hearing officer is found, the appeal moves to the Board of Equalization. Either side may ask for the other's witness list and documents at least 10 days before a hearing, and the answer is due at least seven days ahead, or the evidence can be excluded.

Homestead exemption

File in Room 102 with the assessors before April 1 of the first year you want relief. The home must be your primary residence, and a missed deadline counts as a waiver for that year.

The assessors also administer the Conservation Use Valuation Assessment and Forest Land Protection Act programs, which matter in a county where farms and timber dominate. These programs carry covenants, so ask for the commitment length before you enroll land you plan to sell soon. For current exemption amounts, call (478) 945-3663.

Steps before you list

Most Twiggs County parcels are acreage or long-held family property, so a little preparation goes a long way.

  1. Call the tax commissioner for a written balance on each year still open.
  2. Ask the assessors whether the land is enrolled in a conservation or forest program and what the covenant requires of the next owner.
  3. Confirm your homestead is on file if you live in the house.
  4. Pull the parcel ID from your last bill so each office can find the record at once.
  5. Pass every written figure to the closing agent before you accept an offer.

Doing this in advance means no tax surprise slows the closing, and you know what will come out of your proceeds.

Selling with taxes owed

Obtain a payoff in writing from the tax commissioner and compare it to the settlement statement. Because Georgia bills the January 1 title holder, a sale late in the year needs the tax divided clearly on paper.

If you inherited land, ask for the history of every year you or the estate held it, since acreage in a shrinking county sometimes sits unpaid longer than a house in town. A bill unpaid more than 90 days after its due date can become a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court. Settling past years at closing clears the title for a buyer, whether that buyer finances or pays cash.

Bring the parcel ID and a copy of your deed when you visit the courthouse, and ask each office for its figures in writing. A cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal or repair demands, which helps when family land has outbuildings or timber that a loan underwriter might question.

Frequently asked questions

How do I reach the Twiggs County tax commissioner?

Call (478) 945-3359 or visit the Court House Square at 425 Railroad Street in Jeffersonville. Mail goes to P.O. Box 187.

How long can I appeal a Twiggs County value?

Forty-five days after the notice date. Papers must be hand-delivered or postmarked by then, and neither email nor fax appeals are accepted.

Does Twiggs County offer arbitration for appeals?

Yes. Nonbinding arbitration needs a certified appraisal and a $214 filing fee, and either side can later appeal the arbitrator's decision to Superior Court.

What is the homestead cutoff in Twiggs County?

April 1 of the first year you want it. Apply at the assessors' Room 102 in the courthouse.

Why does Twiggs County have so few building permits?

Only 13 permits were issued in 2025 in a county of about 7,600 people. The county is rural, and population has fallen since 2020.

Union County at a glance

Union County sits in the north Georgia mountains, about 90 miles from Atlanta, with Blairsville as the county seat. Brasstown Bald, the state's highest mountain, rises in the southeast corner. Mid-2025 estimates put the population at 27,859, up 13.1% from the 24,632 counted in 2020. Owners live in 84.4% of housing units, and the middle owner-occupied value is $307,400.

Sellers here hold very different properties: a mountain cabin, a lot in Blairsville, or acreage out in the county. Each needs its own pricing and access plan, and each needs a settled tax record before the deed changes hands. About 36.8% of residents are 65 or older, so estates of longtime owners are a common source of listings.

Housing numbers

Acreage, mountain parcels and in-town lots are all assessed under the same 40% rule. The bill therefore depends mostly on land size, exemptions and any current-use covenant that comes with the parcel. Check which of those apply before you set a price.

Which office do I call?

Billing and valuing sit in different offices. The tax commissioner bills, collects and disburses taxes, while the assessors alone determine value. Start with the assessors if you question the value and with the tax commissioner if you question the amount owed.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 439-6017, at the courthouse, 65 Courthouse Street in Blairsville, for bills, payments and tag and title work.
  • Tax assessors: (706) 439-6011, open weekdays until half past four, for values, returns, homestead filings and exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, including a copy of your warranty deed.

Union is unusual in one respect. The assessors, not the tax commissioner, take tax returns and homestead applications. The county has also hired an outside appraisal firm to help revalue residential, commercial, industrial and farm parcels, and field crews drive vehicles marked with a Union County seal. They stay outside homes and buildings.

Rate-setting is shared. The county commissioner sets the county levy, the Board of Education recommends the school rate, and Blairsville's governing body handles the city. The state revenue commissioner oversees the whole process, so a high bill is rarely about one office alone.

Due dates and penalties

Real estate and business personal property tax is due December 20 each year. Mobile and modular home tax comes due on April 1, vehicle tax tracks the owner's birthday, and boats join the December 20 group once May notices have gone out. The county allows at least 60 days to pay the annual bill, and not getting a bill is no defense against owing it.

Once the deadline slips by, interest of 1% builds each month on the balance. Past 90 days, the office can record a tax lien, called a FIFA, at the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Tax sale proceedings may start at the same 90-day mark.

Blairsville issues and collects its own city property tax, so city residents get a second bill from city hall.

Owners with wooded land should know that uncut timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, and is then taxed on its full market value. On a single lump-sum timber sale, the purchaser sends the tax with form PT-283T to the tax commissioner inside five business days.

How does a Union County appeal work?

Notices of value go out in May, and the challenge period runs 45 days after the notice date. The first filing goes to the Board of Assessors. If no agreement follows, the file is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, which the Grand Jury appoints, and a further written notice to the assessors takes the case to Superior Court.

Arbitration or a certified hearing officer can replace the board for some owners, and that choice is made at filing. Mobile and modular home owners can contest twice, once at the return stage and again within 45 days after the bill goes out, usually in mid February.

Skipping a required return can draw a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest. Real estate returns run from January 1 to April 1 for property that changed hands or changed in value.

Homestead exemption

Bring a copy of your warranty deed to the assessors and file before April 1. The house must be yours and be where you live on January 1. Once approved, relief continues until you move, and a late application starts the following year.

Union's local homestead exemptions can be larger than the state's, so ask the assessors for current figures before you rely on any amount. Freeport covers business inventory. Current-use programs for farm and forest land demand a commitment to stay undeveloped, with stiff penalties for breaking it, so a buyer of acreage should ask whether a covenant is in place.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Union County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

The county mails each year's bill to the person who owned the parcel at the start of January, so a buyer closing in March or September will not receive that year's statement. Arrange for the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds, and request a written payoff from the tax office a few days before closing.

A new owner gets no bill for the purchase year, so check any prorated payment on the settlement statement closely. For a mountain rental or a cabin left by a relative, ask about each year it was held and whether any FIFA is on file.

What to bring when you visit the courthouse: your warranty deed copy, the parcel number, and a photo ID. A cash sale can finish the payoff and the deed recording in a single courthouse visit, and it skips the repair requests a financed buyer's lender may raise.

Before you list: a short checklist

Start with the assessors. Confirm the parcel's value, ask whether a homestead exemption or a current-use covenant is on file, and find out whether any return is still owed for work you did on the property. Then call the tax commissioner and ask for the balance on each parcel you plan to sell, including any separate mobile home account.

Next, check the Clerk of Superior Court records for a FIFA against the property. If one is recorded, it must be paid in full before a buyer's title agent will clear it. Finally, tell your closing agent which office will issue the payoff letter, so the figure arrives before the closing date and not on the morning of it.

Estates deserve extra care, and so do mountain cabins used as rentals or second homes that sit empty for part of the year. Heirs often find that the bill was mailed to a relative who has died, and the notice never reached anyone. Ask the commissioner to confirm the mailing address on file and to list every open year before you accept an offer.

Frequently asked questions

When must Union County property tax be paid?

By December 20 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

What does a late Union County payment cost?

Interest runs at 1% a month. A lien can follow once 90 days pass.

How long can I appeal a Union County value?

Forty-five days counted from the notice date. The assessors see it first, then the equalization board.

Can I file a Union County homestead application late?

A late filing does not help the current year, but the assessors activate it for the next one.

Who collects Blairsville city property tax?

Blairsville bills its own portion. The county tax commissioner handles county and school bills.

Upson County at a glance

Upson County sits in Georgia's west central region, about equally far from Atlanta, Macon and Columbus. Thomaston is the county seat. Housing ranges from mill-era homes in town to timber and farm tracts outside it. The county had an estimated 28,500 residents by mid-2025, a 2.9% gain since 2020. The assessors manage more than 15,000 real property parcels and around 1,400 personal property accounts.

Which office answers which question?

Both offices are at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Money owed goes to one door, and questions about value go to the other.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mailing to P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the payoff figure for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mailing to P.O. Box 508, open weekdays through the working day: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an elected office that stands apart from both the assessors and the county commissioners. Statements are addressed to the homeowner and never to the lender, although the office sends mortgage companies a data file. After a change of lender, pass the bill along yourself.

How the bill is calculated

The assessors arrive at fair market value, the whole 100% figure, and assessed value is 40% of that. Exemptions come off the 40%, which leaves the net assessed, or taxable, value. Multiply that by the millage rate to get the bill, with each mill worth one dollar on every $1,000.

Upson's rate is built from separate levies by the Board of Education, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston, so the final rate on your statement depends on where the parcel sits. Property tax pays for county government and the public schools, public buildings, bridges and county roads, the courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation.

Owners may also propose their own value by filing a return during the early-year window that ends April 1. If the assessors disagree, a notice goes out with their figure and the appeal clock starts.

When bills arrive and when they are due

Real and personal property bills are mailed no later than September 15, and the due date is around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements go out by January 30, and that tax comes due on April 1. If your bill rose from one year to the next, compare the rate on the statement with the prior year's, since the school board and the city set separate rates.

The post office's own date stamp proves a timely payment. A postage meter stamp does not.

Late bills and penalties

Unpaid balances accrue monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. After 120 days a 5% penalty is added, and another 5% joins it at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20%.

Hardship can justify partial payments, but only if you phone before the due date to arrange them, and interest and penalties keep running on the rest. The office sends a notice of intent with 30 days to pay before it files a FIFA lien on the General Execution Docket. Tax still unpaid 90 days past the due date is open to a lien, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Full payment, fees included, cancels the lien. Buying liens at the counter is not offered.

How to appeal your assessment

You have forty-five days from the notice date. Four grounds qualify: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption. Address the written appeal to the Board of Assessors and say which route you prefer.

The assessors also post a field review notice letting identified representatives walk onto a property in business hours to check its value, so do not be surprised by a visitor at the edge of your lot. If you disagree with the figure, gather recent sale prices of similar homes nearby and any repair estimates before you write the appeal, because the assessors will want specifics.

Homestead exemption

The county takes homestead applications from the first of the year through March 31, and they must reach the office by April 1. You must hold the house and live in it on January 1, and a stable owner needs no yearly renewal unless the deed or address changes. Ask at (706) 647-8176 which exemption amounts fit your parcel.

Selling with taxes owed

Have the tax commissioner write out a payoff before closing, and see that the closing agent pays it from what the buyer sends. Because the bill carries the name of whoever owned on New Year's Day, an autumn seller should check the settlement sheet to see who covers the current year.

Heirs and landlords should ask about every year they held the house, including any FIFA on file. A lien goes away only when it is paid in full, which is why the buyer's title agent will want the account clear.

A practical order of steps: ask the commissioner for the payoff, ask the assessors whether an exemption is attached to the parcel, order a deed copy from the Clerk of Superior Court if you cannot find yours, and give all three results to the closing agent. A cash purchase can settle old balances at closing and hand you the rest, which helps when a house carries back taxes, repairs or tenants.

What to bring and what to expect

For a first homestead filing, bring your warranty deed and a photo ID to the assessors in Suite D-180. If you do not have the deed, the Clerk of Superior Court at 116 W. Main Street can supply a copy. Filing in January or February leaves plenty of room to fix a missing paper before the April 1 cutoff.

For a payoff, call the tax commissioner and give the parcel number, the owner's name as it appears on the bill and the planned closing date. Ask for the figure to be good through that day, because interest runs monthly and the number changes. Request a separate figure for any mobile or manufactured home on the land, since it follows the April 1 schedule and carries its own decal.

If a notice of intent has already arrived, treat the 30 days as a hard clock. Calling before the due date is the only way to set up partial payments, and a seller who waits until the lien is filed has fewer choices and a longer list of fees. Keep copies of anything you hand over, and note the date of each call.

Frequently asked questions

How do I contact the Upson County tax commissioner?

The number is (706) 647-8931, and the counter is in Suite D-120 at 305 South Hightower Street, Thomaston.

When is Upson County property tax due?

Around November 15 in a typical year. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1.

What does late payment cost in Upson County?

Monthly interest equals prime plus 3%. A 5% penalty arrives at 120 days and returns at each 120-day mark, stopping at 20%.

What is the Upson County appeal deadline?

Forty-five days from the notice. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors and name the appeal method.

Does Upson County mail my bill to my lender?

No. Statements go to the homeowner. Lenders get a data file, and passing the bill along is your job when needed.

Walker County for home sellers

Walker County fills Georgia's northwest corner, right against the Tennessee line, and its northern end belongs to the Chattanooga commuting zone. LaFayette is the county seat. At 447 square miles it holds ridges, caves and coves rather than flat farmland, so one seller may list a lot in town while the next has a mountainside tract or acreage in a valley, and the tax picture differs for each. About 51% of residents lived in rural areas at the last census.

Five incorporated cities sit inside the county: Chickamauga, LaFayette, Lookout Mountain, Rossville and a small piece of Fort Oglethorpe. The Walker County School District covers most of the county, while Chickamauga has its own city system, so check which district applies when you read a bill.

Home values and ownership

Walker County leans heavily toward homeowners, and prices run under the national figure. The population was 67,654 on census day in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 70,250.

Walker County housing and income, 2020 to 2024 estimates except where dated
MeasureWalkerU.S.
Typical owner-occupied home value$197,100$332,700
Share of homes lived in by owners77.2%65.2%
Typical monthly gross rent$940$1,413
Typical household income$59,469$80,734
Housing units on July 1, 202530,599148,260,882
Permits issued in 20252991,431,616

In 2020, 28.2% of occupied homes were rented and 10.1% of all units stood empty.

Which offices handle property tax?

Billing sits with the Tax Commissioner and valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors. The commissioner's office neither determines property value nor sets the tax rate.

  • Rock Spring: 122 Highway 95, mail to P O Box 510, Rock Spring, GA 30739, phone 706-638-2929, weekdays 8:00 A.M. until 4:30 P.M., with a drop box beside the front entrance.
  • Rossville: 2012 McFarland Gap Road in the Fairview community, same phone and hours.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 706-638-4823, also the number for preferential assessment questions.
  • Search and pay online at walkercountytax.com.

Both counters take payments and questions, so use whichever is closer. Ask either one to walk you through the county and school levy lines on the bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Walker County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates

Notices carry a 60-day window, which works out to December 20 in most years. If your printed bill shows another day, follow the bill. A mailed check needs a USPS postmark, not a meter stamp, and interest waits until 60 days past the bill's postmark.

  • Manufactured homes located in the county on January 1 are due April 1 each year and carry a 10% penalty plus 1% monthly interest when late, with a possible State Court citation.
  • The value date is January 1, so anyone who closes on a purchase after that date should confirm that the bill reaches them.

How to appeal a valuation

Your written appeal has to be in the assessors' hands by the 45th day after the notice date. Only three complaints count: taxability, value and uniformity. Disliking the size of the bill is not one of them.

After the assessors' own review, you may take the case to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and Superior Court sits beyond that. An owner who disagrees with the carried-forward value can also file a new return between January 1 and April 1. Taxable assessed value is 40% of market value under O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.

Exemptions and credits

The local homestead amount applies whenever it is larger than the state one. Bring the warranty deed if this is your first application.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 for state, school and county purposes.
  • Local senior exemptions begin at age 70: county tax with a $15,000 adjusted gross income limit, and county school tax with $50,000 off taxable value. A county school exemption at age 75 carries the same $15,000 limit.
  • Disabled veteran and armed forces surviving spouse exemptions: $81,080.
  • Tax deferral: ages 62 and up with gross household income of $15,000 or less, until a change of ownership or until deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of market value.
  • Homeowner Tax Relief Grant: lowers assessed value by $18,000 for credit purposes and shows on the 2026 bill if a homestead exemption was on file by the April 1 cutoff. Rentals and investment property do not receive it.

A form that comes in after April 1 counts from the next tax year. Once approved, the exemption rolls forward on its own until the deed or your residence changes.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Walker County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the commissioner for the balance in writing, then let the closing agent send it out of your sale proceeds. Land with unpaid tax can be levied and sold, so clear every year before the keys change hands.

Treat a manufactured home on the land as its own account, because its tax runs on the April 1 calendar and not the autumn one. Inherited houses and rentals can have more than one tax year open, so request the status of each.

Here is how the sequence usually runs. Ask the commissioner for the balance on each parcel and each manufactured home. Confirm with the assessors that your exemptions are in place. Give the written figures to the closing agent, who pays the county first and sends you the rest. A cash sale to a buyer who takes the house as it stands can follow the same steps without a repair list, which suits hillside cabins and older town houses that would not pass a lender's inspection.

A walk through the courthouse steps

Two counters serve the whole county, so a visit rarely takes long. Rock Spring has the drop box by the front door if you would rather leave a payment than wait in line. Rossville in the Fairview community handles the same business for owners at the north end.

Bring the parcel number or the name on the bill, plus your warranty deed if you are applying for homestead for the first time. If a lender escrows your tax, ask the lender before you pay anything yourself so the bill is not paid twice.

Ask staff to explain the county and school lines on your statement. They will also tell you whether the figure is current through the day you plan to close. A bill printed in October and a payoff needed in December can differ, and the closing agent will want the later number in writing.

Owners of hillside or valley acreage should also ask the assessors about preferential assessment, since that number goes through a separate desk and has its own paperwork. Questions about the grant or the senior exemptions are best settled by phone before you list, so a buyer's agent hears one consistent answer about what the next owner will pay.

Frequently asked questions

When must Walker County real estate tax be paid?

Two months after the notices are mailed, usually December 20. If your bill shows another date, follow the bill.

Who answers questions about a Walker County tax bill?

The Tax Commissioner's staff at 706-638-2929, in either the Rock Spring or the Rossville office. Value questions go to the assessors at 706-638-4823.

What is the deadline to contest a Walker County valuation?

The 45th day after the notice's mailing date. The assessors look first, and a Board of Equalization hearing follows if you stay in dispute.

Where do I file for homestead exemption in Walker County?

At the Tax Commissioner's counter, with April 1 as the cutoff for a new filing. First-time owners take their warranty deed along.

Does a lingering tax balance block a Walker County sale?

No. The balance is paid at closing from your proceeds. Get the amount in writing, and ask about earlier years if a tenant lived in the house or an heir inherited it.

Walton County at a glance

Walton County lies in the Piedmont, roughly 30 miles from downtown Atlanta, and its growth shows the spread of metro Atlanta. Residents numbered 83,768 in 2010 and 96,673 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 112,696, which is 16.6% above the 2020 count. Monroe holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, with Loganville the other major one. Social Circle, Between and Good Hope also sit within the borders.

The Walton County School District serves everything except Social Circle, which runs its own city district. The county and the school system each levy their own share, so the district matters when you read a bill. A six-member commission elected by district, plus a chairman chosen countywide, sets the county's share.

Housing numbers

Homeownership here is high and values sit just above the U.S. median. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied home median is $339,500, compared with $332,700 for the country.

  • 79.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, against 65.2% across the U.S.
  • Monthly gross rent has a median of $1,175.
  • Median household income is $84,945 across 35,755 households.
  • The county had 39,911 housing units on July 1, 2025, and issued 569 building permits during 2025.

With so much new building going up, an older house with deferred repairs or a tax balance is easier to sell to a buyer who accepts it as it stands. A listing may be a lot in Monroe or acreage out in the rural parts, and buyers of either will want to see the current bill before they make an offer.

Where to send questions and payments

The Tax Commissioner issues one statement per parcel. For Monroe owners it also carries the city's share, because Monroe stopped mailing its own bills in 2016 and now relies on the county statement and its date. Delinquent city bills from 2015 and earlier are still paid at Monroe City Hall.

  • Main counter: 303 S. Hammond Drive, Suite 100, Monroe, GA 30655; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Property tax line (770) 266-1736, email WCTC@co.walton.ga.us.
  • Tax Assessors, same building: (770) 267-1352.
  • Search and pay: tax.waltoncountypay.com.

Tag renewals have their own window in the courthouse at 303 South Hammond Drive, (770) 267-1335. Homeowners with a mortgage should know that the mailed copy goes only to the homeowner, so lenders often pull the bill from a third-party service.

The county mails the bill to the owner on record for January 1 only, so a lender or a newly arrived owner should obtain a copy rather than wait. Churches, nonprofit hospitals and public property can be exempt once the assessors approve, with the request due April 1.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Walton County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due date and late charges

Bills are mailed in late August, and November 15 is the due date. Late bills move through the steps below, in this order.

Walton County delinquency steps
WhenCharge or action
After November 15Interest on the unpaid portion, added monthly
At 90 days lateFi.Fa. lien fee: $20.50 under $100, $30.50 over $100
Every 120 days5% penalty on what remains, capped at 20%
Before a lien30-day notice of intent

A Fi.Fa. goes on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court and lasts seven years, and it may show up on credit reports. The office takes partial payments, but charges continue on the leftover amount. A tax sale, when one is scheduled, is an auction outside the Walton County Government Building on a first Tuesday, advertised in the Walton Tribune for four straight Wednesdays.

Returns, appeals and exemptions

Real property returns and homestead applications are due January 1 through April 1 at the Tax Assessors' Office. A required return that is never filed draws a 10% penalty on the value left off, and personal property returns are due every year with the same penalty for late filing.

You can contest the assessment within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The assessors respond first, and the file then goes to the Board of Equalization automatically. Mobile and modular homes get two chances to contest, during the return period and within 45 days of a bill that usually arrives in January.

  • Owners 65 and older are exempt from Walton County School District tax on the house and one acre.
  • Owners 70 and older receive up to $30,000 off on land beyond one acre.
  • A filed PT-61 transfer form can serve as a return if the property was not changed.
  • A refund claim for tax paid in error goes in writing to the board of commissioners within three years, and it must rest on an error, not a value disagreement.

Ask the Tax Assessors' Office to confirm an exemption is on file before you list, since failing to apply by the deadline costs the exemption for that year.

Selling with taxes owed

Email the settlement statement to WCTC@co.walton.ga.us or fax it to (770) 267-1416 right after closing. The office can mail a duplicate bill to the buyer when the purchase happened before November 15 of that tax year.

Before you close, get a payoff figure dated for the closing day, because monthly interest keeps changing it. If a Fi.Fa. is already recorded, paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. The commissioner does not sell liens in bulk to outside investors.

Anyone who sold after January 1 should keep the closing statement handy for the commissioner's records, as the January 1 owner still receives the first bill.

An inherited house, a rental or a place with several years behind can close without repair demands when the buyer purchases as-is and the title company settles the county first. A short order of work helps: request the payoff, confirm exemptions with the assessors, hand both to the title company, and send the settlement statement to the commissioner once the deed is recorded.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Walton County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to have ready

Collect the parcel number, a copy of your deed, and the most recent assessment notice before you call either office. Those three items answer most questions at the counter. If your family has held the house for years, ask the tax line about every open year and whether any Fi.Fa. sits on the docket, since a surprise lien found at the title stage can push back a closing date. Owners who live out of town can handle most of this by phone or email, and the online search shows the current balance. Keep a note of who you spoke with, and ask for any payoff figure by email so you have it in writing when the title company asks.

Frequently asked questions

What day are Walton County real estate bills due?

November 15. The county mails statements in late August, and balances left after the due date begin accruing interest.

Which Walton County office handles exemptions?

The Tax Assessors' Office at 303 S. Hammond Drive, phone (770) 267-1352. April 1 is the usual cutoff for applications.

Does Monroe mail a separate city tax bill?

No. Since 2016 Walton County sends a single consolidated statement that includes Monroe city tax, and it is due on the county's date.

What happens 90 days after the Walton County due date?

A Fi.Fa. lien fee applies, $20.50 on bills under $100 and $30.50 on larger bills, after a 30-day notice. A 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%.

Can a house with a Walton County Fi.Fa. be sold?

Yes. Paying the tax with its fees, penalties and interest cancels the lien, and the closing agent can do that from your proceeds using a current written payoff.

Ware County at a glance

Ware County covers 908 square miles, more than any other county in Georgia, and a large block of that is wetland inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its federal refuge. Waycross, the seat, is the one incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, so outside the city limits an address answers only to county rules. With the swamp so near, a buyer may ask how a given lot drains.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $109,500 for 2020 to 2024, close to a third of the $332,700 national figure. The county had 36,906 residents by the 2025 estimate and holds 12,957 households.

About one in seven housing units stood vacant at the 2020 count (13.9%). A balance left unpaid for several years on a vacant or inherited house can turn into a recorded lien.

Which offices send and collect the bill?

Billing and collecting belong to the tax commissioner. The assessors set values. Rates come separately from the commission and from the school board.

  • Commissioner's counter: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. Phone (912) 490-4305, weekday hours from half past eight to five.
  • Assessors: (912) 287-4383, with written appeals directed to 305 Oak St., Suite 154.
  • Online parcel search and payment: warecountytax.com. Anyone whose lender escrows the tax should call the lender before paying, so the bill is not paid twice.
  • Recorded deeds: the Clerk of Superior Court, 800 Church Street.

Find out from the commissioner if your statement includes a City of Waycross line. City, county and school freezes are all possible, so city tax can matter for houses inside Waycross.

Due dates and penalties

Statements should be in the mail by September 15, with payment due November 15. Manufactured homes follow a calendar of their own: January bills, April 1 payment, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid.

For bills dated July 1, 2016 or later, these rules apply after the due date.

  • Interest builds at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • A 5% penalty lands every 120 days and stops once it reaches 20% of unpaid principal.
  • A homesteaded parcel with tax under $500 owes interest but no penalty.
  • Past 90 days, a FIFA lien can be recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it.

If an account stays open, the county can levy on the property. Sales take place at 305 Oak Street in the Board of Commissioners Room on a first Tuesday, following four weeks of notices in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county does not promise title, and a purchaser waits at least a year before using the land or collecting rent.

Homestead exemption and relief

Own the house and live in it on January 1, then apply at the Tax Assessor's office. Phone the assessor first to learn the live filing deadline. Once approved, it renews every year without a new form.

  • Freeze exemptions hold the operating-tax value for county, school and city at last year's level for as long as you stay.
  • An extra local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income of $24,000 or less takes up to $20,000 off the 40% assessed value.
  • A floating exemption for ages 62 and up with household income of $30,000 or less swaps out other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that it may initially raise the bill.
  • Damaged timber: the commissioner's front page points to the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission.

How can I challenge a valuation?

Count 45 days from the date printed on your assessment notice. Three grounds count: taxability, value and uniformity. A bill that simply feels too high does not qualify.

Once the assessors take a second look, the case can move to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, then to Superior Court by written notice. You can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 that puts down a value of your own.

Before you file, gather what supports your number: recent sales of similar houses nearby, repair quotes, and photos of any damage. Send the written appeal to the Suite 154 address and keep a copy.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the commissioner for a payoff figure. Your closing agent then pays it from what the buyer sends. If a levy has been threatened, check the tax sale list on the county site, since a sale date can set your timeline.

Mobile homes get their own April 1 bill and decal, so treat that account separately from the land. Buyers willing to take the house as is, and to handle the title work, can close quickly. The commissioner also keeps an excess funds list, worth checking if money may be owed to you from an earlier sale.

The usual order: ask the commissioner for a payoff on the land and any mobile home, ask the assessors whether a homestead or freeze exemption is on the parcel, order a deed copy from the Clerk of Superior Court at 800 Church Street if needed, and pass everything to the closing agent. With a cash buyer the county gets paid first at the table, a plus for a house with repair needs or renters.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ware County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to bring and how a visit goes

Take your parcel number or the name on the bill to the commissioner's counter on Oak Street. If you plan to file a homestead application, bring your deed and proof that you live in the house. A deed copy can be ordered from the Clerk of Superior Court if yours is lost.

Owners who live elsewhere can search the parcel and pay from the county tax website, or mail a check to the post office box. Ask for a payoff in writing whenever a sale is on the calendar, because interest keeps adding up each month and the balance on closing day will differ from the figure on your last statement.

If your account has gone several years without payment, expect the office to quote each year separately along with fees. Ask staff to list them one by one so you can see how much of the total is tax and how much is penalty and interest.

Frequently asked questions

Which month do Ware County real estate bills fall due?

November. The county aims to mail statements by mid-September, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April.

Can I pay a Ware County bill without going to Waycross?

Yes. Search the parcel and pay on warecountytax.com, or mail a check to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. If your lender escrows the tax, check with the lender first.

Where is an appeal of a Ware County value sent?

To the Board of Tax Assessors at 305 Oak St., Suite 154, Waycross, within 45 days of the notice date.

Is there a penalty if only part of a Ware County bill is late?

Interest runs on the unpaid principal at prime plus 3%, and the 5% penalty steps (every 120 days, up to 20%) apply to what remains unpaid. Homesteaded parcels under $500 skip the penalty.

How do I avoid a Ware County tax sale on my house?

Pay the commissioner before the first-Tuesday sale date arrives. Once a lien is satisfied it comes off the sale list, and the office will quote the payoff.

Due dates and late bills

Georgia's default is December 20, though a county board can pull the date forward to December 1 or November 15 or use installments. The tax commissioner can tell you which schedule your bill follows. Every owner gets 60 days after the postmark before interest starts.

The city of Warrenton, Warren County itself, the school system and the state each levy tax as of January 1, and every parcel is assessed at 40% of market value. For the current millage rate, ask the commissioner about your parcel or read the county finance page, where the commissioners publish a current digest and a five-year history of levy. Tax hearings are advertised whenever a proposed millage rate exceeds the rollback rate.

  • Returns run January 1 to April 1. If you skip one, last year's value rolls forward.
  • A mobile home owner applies for a location permit within 30 days of placing the unit, then renews each year in the same window.
  • Overpayments can be reclaimed if the request starts within three years.

How to appeal a value

Put the appeal in writing and send it to the assessors' board, carrying a postmark within 45 days of the mailing date printed on your notice. Acceptable reasons are taxability, value, uniformity and denied exemptions. Mail it to the county board rather than the state, which cannot take it.

Form PT-311A makes you choose a path. Most owners choose the equalization board route. A hearing officer only hears non-homestead real estate worth more than $500,000, and arbitration needs a certified appraisal that you supply.

If you are still unhappy, a written notice for superior court has to reach the county board within a month of the hearing officer's, arbitrator's or Board of Equalization's decision, and taxes must be paid at last year's level before a judge hears the case. If the final value ends at 85% or less of the earlier figure, the owner recovers litigation costs and attorney's fees.

Homestead exemption

Warren adds no local exemption of its own, so owners rely on the statewide ones. The form goes in at any point after the home becomes your primary residence, and it needs to arrive by April 1 for the first year you want relief. Missing that date forfeits the exemption for the year.

The tax commissioner's staff handle these applications. Carry proof that you live in the house and ask which age or disability categories you could add. A buyer who will live in the house files a new form of their own, which is worth mentioning when the closing falls late in the year.

Who to call

The tax commissioner is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, phone 706-465-2231, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321. Staff take card payments by phone, and an online option is linked from the commissioner's page, so ask about fees when you call.

How a sale closes out the tax bill

The bill follows whoever owned the property on January 1, so sellers and buyers split it on the settlement statement. Ask the commissioner for a written balance that covers each year up to the closing date, then give that paper to the closing attorney. A house inside Warrenton, Camak or Norwood may owe a city levy on top of the county one.

  • Get separate figures for the county, the school district and any city.
  • Check whether a mobile home or timber account sits under the same name.
  • Keep your receipts for three years in case a refund claim comes up.

In a market with few buyers, an owner who arrives with a clear title and paid-up taxes has an easier path to closing. Heirs with an old family house in town or out on a rural road should ask the commissioner for every open year before listing, since a small balance carried for a long time can grow past what the house will bring. A buyer paying cash and taking the house as it stands can settle those years from the proceeds in one step, with no repair list and no wait for a lender's appraisal.

Steps before you list a Warren County house

Begin with the commissioner on Main Street. Ask for the balance on every account under your name, including any mobile home or timber account, and ask which schedule your bill follows. Then call the assessors and confirm that your homestead exemption is on file and that the acreage and building details on the record match the property.

Next, find your deed. If a copy is missing, ask the clerk's office for one before a buyer's attorney asks. A family house that passed down without paperwork can need extra title work, and that slows a closing more than any tax balance does.

Finally, tell the closing attorney who owned the property on January 1 and which bills are still open. The attorney will pull the written payoff from the commissioner, add the city levy if the house is inside a town, and show the split between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. If a buyer will live in the house, remind them to file their own homestead form, since yours does not carry over.

Owners who inherited a house far from Warrenton can do most of this by phone and mail. Ask the commissioner to send the balance in writing, and keep every receipt, because a refund claim for an overpayment has a three-year window. If you cannot reach the office during the week, write down your parcel number and questions in advance so one call covers everything, and ask staff to confirm any figure by email or letter. A written number protects you if the closing date moves and the balance changes with it.

Frequently asked questions

Who answers questions about a Warren County tax bill?

The tax commissioner does, at 706-465-2231. The office is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321.

By when must a Warren County value dispute be mailed?

Your envelope needs a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing date. Address it to the county's assessors in writing. State offices do not take these appeals.

Is there a Warren County exemption beyond the state homestead one?

No. Owners use the statewide homestead exemptions and apply by April 1 for the first year.

What percentage of value does Warren County tax?

Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value. Exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate applies.

Can I give a card number over the phone to pay Warren County taxes?

Yes. Staff take card payments by phone, and an online option is available too. Call 706-465-2231 to ask about fees.

Who mails the Wayne County tax bill?

The commissioner on East Walnut Street mails it, and the assessors next door decide what the land and buildings are worth. The street address is 341 E Walnut St, Jesup, GA 31546. Letters go to PO Box 287 (ZIP 31598), and the phone is (912) 427-5910, staffed from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon.

A single bill gathers money for five bodies: the State, Odum, Screven, the county government and the school system. Each of those sets its own millage, and the values come from the Chief Appraiser and Board of Assessors. Title on January 1 decides who receives the bill.

Reach the assessor at (912) 427-5920 about value, and the commissioner about payment, penalties or a payoff. Questions can go by email to taxcommissioner@waynecountyga.us. The commissioner's home page links the online payment site and the parcel search, and parcel records are also searchable through the county's qPublic page.

Wayne County housing market

Wayne spreads across the Altamaha River country of southeast Georgia, with Jesup as the seat and Odum and Screven as the other cities. The county had an estimated 32,481 residents in July 2025, a rise of 7.8% over April 2020's 30,141, spread over roughly 642 square miles.

  • Homes: 13,180 units, two-thirds lived in by owners.
  • Value of the typical home its owner lives in (2020 through 2024): $162,800.
  • Midpoint rent: $846, with 102 construction permits in 2025.
  • Households: 11,061, and median household income of $53,427.

Due dates and penalties

Bills for real estate and business personal property leave the office by September 15 and fall due November 15. Mobile homes run on a different clock: April 1, plus a 10% penalty after that. Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday.

Interest begins the morning after the deadline and its rate is reset every January. A four-step penalty follows, starting at 5% once 120 days have gone by and rising on the same rhythm to a 20% cap. State code sections 48-2-40 and 48-2-44 govern the process.

How to contest a value

The appeal address is Board of Tax Assessors, PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598, and the notice gives you 45 days from its mailing date. That notice shows the new value, the prior one, why it changed and an estimate of tax at the rollback millage. A complaint about the bill's size will not succeed, since only the value can be disputed.

The board looks again and reports its decision. Next comes a hearing before the county Board of Equalization, and Superior Court sits above that. Arbitration can replace the hearing, and the assessors will walk you through it.

Assessments equal 40% of market value. An owner may declare a figure of their own on a return during the January through April 1 window, and a refusal by the board opens the appeal. Real property returns roll forward at the previous value until the property changes.

Homestead exemption

You qualify by living in the home you own on January 1. Wayne has local exemptions, and where the local amount beats the state figure it takes over. The assessors take the application, and an approved one renews by itself until you move, sell or switch categories.

Call the assessor for the current filing cutoff before you rely on the exemption. A late filing waits for the next year's bill.

Standing timber has its own rule. It carries no tax until sold or cut, and the tax then uses its full value.

Other offices that matter in a sale

A few county departments, all with phone numbers in the 912 area code, are worth a call when a sale involves an estate, a tenant or a lien.

  • Probate Court, 427-5940, the first call when the house sits in an estate.
  • Magistrate Court, 427-5960, for landlord and tenant matters.
  • County administrator and commissioners, 427-5900, the general county line.
  • Sanitation Department, 427-5985, for pickup and landfill service at the address.
  • Extension Service, 427-5965, for well, septic and land questions.
