Selling with taxes owed

Ask for the balance in writing ahead of closing and carry it as a line item. The bill belongs to the January 1 owner, so a house that changes hands in October still has a full-year charge, which the attorney divides between you and the buyer. The payoff figure tells the title company what to send.

  • Ask for balances on every open year, with penalty and interest.
  • Check whether the lot lies in Odum or Screven and picks up a city bill.
  • Confirm homestead status so the buyer knows whether to apply.
  • If the title company asks, the Clerk of Superior Court can supply your deed.
  • Ask whether a mobile home on the lot gets its own bill.

Heirs and landlords who have not looked at the account for years should do this early. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can have the county paid at closing, so old balances, repairs and tenant issues do not hold up the sale.

What to bring and what to ask

A visit to Jesup usually takes two stops. Start next door with the assessors if you want to check the value, the acreage or the exemption on file. Then go to the commissioner for the balance. Bring the parcel number or the owner name as it appears on the bill, and your deed if you are filing for homestead for the first time.

Ask the commissioner to confirm in writing the balance for each open year, split into tax, penalty and interest. Ask whether the figure is good through your planned closing day, because interest keeps adding and the number moves. If a mobile home sits on the land, request its figure on a separate line.

If you plan to appeal, gather recent sale prices of similar homes nearby and any repair estimates, and mail the written appeal to the board's post office box so it carries a postmark inside the 45 days. Keep a copy of everything you send. An appeal that arrives late is lost for the year, so do not wait for the last week.

Frequently asked questions

What phone number serves Wayne County taxpayers?

The commissioner answers at (912) 427-5910 from 341 E Walnut St in Jesup, and the assessor takes value questions at (912) 427-5920.

When is Wayne County real estate tax due?

Normally November 15, after a September 15 mailing. Mobile homes come due April 1.

How long is the Wayne County window to dispute a value?

Forty-five days counted from when the notice was mailed. Address it to PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. It must dispute the value, since the size of the bill is not appealable.

What are the late charges on Wayne County tax?

Interest runs from the next day, a 5% penalty joins it after 120 days, and further steps follow at 120-day intervals up to 20%. The interest rate is reset each January.

What fraction of market value is taxable in Wayne County?

Forty percent of fair market value forms the assessed amount. Exemptions come off that amount, then the millage rate is applied.

Where to pay in White County

The tax commissioner's lobby is at 506 North Main Street in Cleveland, and the mailing address is P. O. Box 970, Cleveland, GA 30528. Call 706-865-2225. The drive-thru lane opens at 8 am and shuts at 4:30 pm, while the lobby stays open until 4:50 pm, Monday through Friday.

Bills go out each August with a November 15 deadline. You can pay with cash, check or card at the counter, or online, and convenience fees apply to cards and web payments. The same office bills timber, real and personal property, mobile homes, utilities and motor vehicles, and it registers vehicles for the state.

Values are a different counter. The assessors work out of Suite 180 in the Mauney Building, and their board sits on the second Wednesday of each month at 9 a.m. to talk through appeals, homestead requests and changes in taxation status.

Housing numbers

The median owner-occupied home is worth $278,900 for 2020 through 2024. The county covers 240.74 square miles and had 29,802 people in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.4% from April 2020. Cleveland, Helen and Sautee Nacoochee are the main communities, and mountain recreation draws steady demand for second homes and weekend places.

  • Owner-occupied share: 78.8% of 14,547 housing units.
  • Median rent: $1,032. Construction permits in 2025: 190.
  • Median household income: $70,666 across 10,729 households.

How a value becomes a tax bill

The arithmetic is assessed value, minus exemptions, times the millage rate. Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value unless a rule says otherwise, and each mill means one dollar for every $1,000 of assessed value. The assessors set the value, and the taxing bodies set the rate.

The county commissioners and the Board of Education are the main rate setters. The county government announced plans to cut its millage rate to 8.555 mills from the 8.842 mills of 2025, a drop of 0.287 mills. That is the county government's piece only, so school and city levies stack on top. Cleveland and Helen are separate cities, so ask the commissioner whether a city levy touches your address.

Owners file a return of real property from January 1 to April 1, and a missing return means the prior year's value stands. The assessors then mail an Annual Notice of Assessment listing last year's value, this year's value, an estimate at last year's millage and the reason for any change. You can look up your record by name or address on the county's property records site, which is also where the homestead application opens.

How to contest a value

The window lasts 45 days from the date printed on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which usually goes out in early May. Six grounds qualify: value, uniformity, taxability, denial of exemption, breach of covenant and denial of covenant. The bill itself is not appealable in Georgia.

Nobody can extend the deadline. A missed window waives the appeal for that year, and the Board of Assessors has no power to make an exception. If you agree with the notice, you do nothing. If you disagree, gather recent sale prices of similar homes before you file.

Appeals that reach the Board of Equalization go before a special jury for property values and denied exemptions. Questions about it go to the Clerk of Court at 706-865-2613.

Homestead exemption

Use the online application inside the property records site and finish it by April 1 for the current year. The house must be your primary residence, with no homestead claimed elsewhere in Georgia or another state, and a Georgia driver's license or ID showing the street address is required. A late application rolls forward to the following year.

White County offers numerous homestead exemptions, and the assessor can give you the list. Two other programs share the page. Freeport exemption covers business inventory, and a voter-approved local percentage of 20, 40, 60, 80 or 100 applies. Conservation use assessment covers up to 2,000 acres of farm or timber land under Georgia Code 48-5-7.4, for a single owner who signs a ten-year covenant. Freeport applications go to the Board of Assessors in the same period returns are due, and later ones can earn a partial exemption until June 1.

When White County taxes go unpaid

After November 15 a balance picks up penalties and moves through four stages. The commissioner still accepts payment on a delinquent bill, though interest keeps running.

  • Penalties and fees start once November 15 passes.
  • A lien, also called a Fi. Fa., goes on record with the Clerk of Court.
  • A levy can seize part of the property.
  • A tax sale auctions the property at the courthouse.

A lien stays on record with the Clerk of Court for seven years and may hurt credit reports and ratings.

A levy seizes part of the property to cover the debt, and personal property may be taken, counted and stored. A sign may go up, extra fees are added, and the owner can stay in the house. A tax sale gets four consecutive weeks of advertising in the White County News and happens on the first Tuesday of a month at the courthouse steps. The sale adds its own advertising and conduct fees. Buyers pay in certified funds and receive a Sheriff's tax deed, issued with a receipt from the commissioner.

The original owner has a year to redeem, and lien and mortgage holders may redeem as well. After that the buyer may foreclose the right of redemption.

Selling with taxes owed

A lien is removed by paying the delinquent balance with fees and interest. A seller should request that payoff from the commissioner and hand it to the closing attorney, who pays it from the proceeds so the buyer gets a clear title.

Before you list, ask the commissioner for every open year, not just the current one, and check with the assessors that your homestead is on file. Heirs and landlords should also ask whether a lien has been recorded with the Clerk of Court. A cash buyer who takes the house as it is can close with the county paid first, which helps when the house has back taxes or needs work. Keep the payoff letter and the closing statement together, and send the commissioner a copy of the statement so the next bill goes to the right person.

Frequently asked questions

What is the due date for White County property tax?

November 15. Bills are sent every August. After that date penalties begin, and interest keeps accruing on a delinquent bill.

Where is the White County Tax Commissioner?

506 North Main Street, Cleveland, with the phone at 706-865-2225. The lobby closes at 4:50 pm and the drive-thru at 4:30 pm on weekdays.

When must a White County value dispute be filed?

Within 45 days of the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in early May. The Board of Assessors cannot extend that deadline.

By what date does a White County homestead application have to arrive?

April 1, to count for the current year. A late one shifts the benefit forward. The home must be your primary residence.

Will a White County tax lien block a house sale?

A lien comes off when the delinquent balance, fees and interest are paid. Ask the commissioner for that payoff figure and give it to the closing attorney.

Whitfield County at a glance

Dalton anchors Whitfield County, with Cohutta, Tunnel Hill and Varnell as the other cities, all settled along rail lines. The July 2025 estimate is 106,212 residents on 290.45 square miles of land. The midpoint owner-occupied home is worth $218,000, and 67.0% of the 40,987 housing units are owner-occupied.

  • Median rent: $971. Permits issued during 2025: 409.
  • Households: 36,834, averaging 2.78 people. Median household income: $67,070.

Whitfield has designated historic sites, and a parcel inside one faces design review. Before listing land near Rocky Face Ridge or Prater's Mill, ask the county planning office whether the lot lies inside a designated area.

Who sends the bill, and when?

Visit 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, GA 30721, or phone (706) 275-7510 any weekday from 8:00 to 4:55. Online payment has its own county tax site. The Board of Assessors, which sets valuation, keeps a separate tax help site that the county's home page links.

Real property bills typically go out in October and rest on the market value as of each January 1. The usual real estate due date is December 20, but your own bill is what counts. A mobile home is billed in January with April 1 as the deadline.

Owners inside Dalton face one extra wrinkle. The county assesses at 40% of market value and Dalton does so at 100%. A house inside Dalton therefore carries a different base than one in the unincorporated county, and the commissioner can tell you which levies reach your address.

Late bills and penalties

Each month's interest is the prime rate plus 3 points, taken on January 1 and divided by 12.

A penalty of 5% is added each 120 days of delinquency up to a ceiling of 20%. At 120 days the commissioner files a lien against the property and the owner with the Clerk of Court and on the General Execution Docket, adding fees of $12 and $10. These liens are public, so credit bureaus may read them.

How to appeal your assessment

Whitfield gives you 45 days from the notice date to put an appeal on paper. Value, uniformity, taxability and a denied exemption count as grounds, while the size of the bill does not. Send it to the Board of Tax Assessors and name the track you want.

Three tracks are open to you. The county equalization board is the usual one. A hearing officer handles just non-homestead real estate above $500,000, while arbitration depends on a certified appraisal you pay for. Superior court is the last step, reached by written notice within 30 days of the decision. The state revenue department cannot overrule a county board on one parcel.

From January 1 to April 1 you may file a return with a value of your own. If you say nothing, last year's final value carries over, and the assessors mail business and personal property return forms each January. For a mobile home, the tax bill itself serves as the assessment notice and its 45 days run from the mailing date.

Homestead exemptions

Qualifying takes ownership plus residence on January 1. The Tax Assessor takes the form, and one that arrives after April 1 is credited to the following year. An approved exemption renews itself unless you move or request another type. Five codes apply.

  • S1: regular homestead, with no extra conditions.
  • S1-V: regular homestead plus a City of Varnell exemption, for age 65 and income over $40,000.
  • S3: senior homestead at 65 with spousal income under $40,000.
  • S4-7: senior homestead at age 70.
  • S5: disabled veteran exemption, requiring a DD-214 and a 100% disability rating.

An owner who turns 62 can ask about one more exemption. Special assessment programs cover conservation use, residential transitional property, agriculture, rehabilitated historic buildings, qualified timber and the Forest Land Protection Act. Each requires an application and a commitment to keep the property in that use for a set number of years.

Selling with taxes owed

The January 1 owner's name goes on the statement. The office does not decide who owes what once a house sells; buyers and sellers typically work that out at closing. Where the office learns of a sale within 90 days of the due date and verifies the transfer, a bill goes to the new owner.

The owner of record changes once the deed is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. Lenders are not sent the bill, so a seller who escrows should tell the loan servicer. Request a balance covering earlier years and ask whether city levies for Dalton or Varnell apply.

Order of work: get the written balance, confirm your exemption with the assessors, record the deed, and give the figures to the closing attorney. A cash buyer taking the house as is lets the county be paid at the table. That suits an inherited house or a rental with several years open, and it spares you a repair list.

What to bring and what to ask

At the Riverburch Parkway office, bring the parcel number or the name on the bill. Ask for the balance for every open year, and ask whether the figure holds through your closing date, since interest is added monthly. If a mobile home sits on the land, ask for its account separately because it follows the January and April 1 calendar.

At the assessors, confirm that your homestead code is on file and that the acreage and building details are right. Before writing an appeal, gather nearby sales of similar houses and any repair quotes, and keep a copy of what you mail.

Out-of-town owners can do nearly all of this by phone, and payment itself goes through the county's online tax site, so nobody has to drive to Dalton. Whitfield's mix of in-town houses, mill-era neighborhoods and rural lots means two sellers can face quite different bills, so check your own parcel rather than a neighbor's. Have staff confirm every payoff figure in writing so the closing attorney holds it on paper, and note the date and the name of the person who gave it to you.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I find the Whitfield County Tax Commissioner?

The main office is at 1013 Riverburch Parkway, Dalton, Georgia 30721. Call (706) 275-7510 on a weekday between eight and 4:55.

How soon must I contest a Whitfield County value?

Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors, naming the method you choose. The tax amount itself cannot be appealed.

Does the City of Dalton assess differently from the county?

Yes. The county uses 40% of market value and the City of Dalton uses 100%. Ask which one reaches your address.

What is the cutoff for a Whitfield County homestead form?

It must be received before April 1 of the tax year to count for that year. Later forms apply to the following year, and you need to own and occupy the home on January 1.

Who pays if I sell partway through the year?

The January 1 owner receives the statement, and buyer and seller typically settle it at closing. Notice of the sale within 90 days of the due date lets the office bill the new owner. Lenders are not mailed a copy.

Selling in Wilkinson County?

Wilkinson County property tax basics

Wilkinson County splits the work between two desks in Irwinton. The assessors put a value on each parcel. The tax commissioner mails the statement and takes the money. Georgia's rule on timing is simple: whoever holds title on January 1 owes the year's tax, and a spring closing earns no rebate from the county.

Context for pricing: the county had 8,877 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 8,650 for July 2025, down from 10,368 in 1980. Median home value runs $86,300, and owners live in 80.5% of houses. A buyer pool this small makes a clean tax record worth more than it would in a busy market.

Gather these before you talk to any buyer:

  • last year's bill and the newest assessment notice
  • a note of whether the parcel has a homestead exemption on file
  • the location permit and tax receipt for any manufactured home on the land
  • any letter from the commissioner about overdue balances

With those in hand, the title company can order a payoff figure and the closing stays on schedule.

Which office handles what

Match the question to the desk and the visit goes quickly.

  • Tax Commissioner at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136, open 8:00 a.m. until 4:45 p.m. Phone (478) 946-2232, fax (478) 946-1429, postal box P.O. Box 182. Online payments add a convenience fee.
  • Board of Assessors and Chief Appraiser, P.O. Box 189, phone (478) 946-2076. This office keeps the tax maps, the ownership transfers, and the records for mobile homes without a homestead. It meets the first Wednesday of the month at 9:30 in the courthouse.
  • Board of Equalization, whose members the grand jury appoints. Each member completes 40 hours of training in the first year and eight hours yearly after that. The Clerk of Superior Court supplies clerical help only.
  • Commissioners and school board, the two bodies that set the rates.

The county website, wilkinsoncounty.net, links to a property record search and posts the current digest with a five-year levy history. Call the commissioner for anything about a bill and the assessors for anything about value.

2025 millage rates

Your rate depends on where the house sits, since a city levy stacks on top of the county, state and school pieces. These are the 2025 combined totals the assessors post.

Combined 2025 millage by jurisdiction
JurisdictionCombined millage
Unincorporated county32.082
Allentown37.082

A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of fair market value. For 2024 the county government trimmed its own levy from 14.344 to 13.786 mills, still above the 13.227 rollback figure, which is why public hearings were required.

A house in Irwinton carries a higher combined rate than one in Danville or the unincorporated county, so a buyer comparing two listings should ask for the actual millage on each parcel.

Due dates and penalties

December 20 is the usual deadline in Wilkinson County, and the date printed on your bill controls. Georgia lets a county substitute December 1, November 15, or several installments.

No interest accrues for the first 60 days after the postmark on your bill. Penalties may follow later, so get the office's current charges in writing along with your payoff.

  • Returns come in between New Year's Day and April 1.
  • A real property return renews itself at the previous value each year, so a new filing is needed only when you add structures or buy more land.
  • Ignored bills can lead to a levy against the parcel and a forced sale.

If you are selling in the fall, ask the commissioner whether the bill has been mailed yet. A closing that falls just before the due date is the easiest time to leave a balance behind, so settle it at the table.

How to challenge your valuation

An appeal goes to the assessors in writing, and the postmark has to land inside a 45-day span that opens when the notice is sent. You can dispute what the property is worth, how it compares with neighbors, whether it is taxable, or an exemption you were refused.

On the state form you name your forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. Revenue department staff have no power to overturn any of those rulings on one house.

A second entry point is the annual return. Declaring a different value on a return filed by April 1 opens an appeal if the assessors reject your figure.

Bring recent sales of similar houses nearby, photographs of defects, and contractor estimates. With homes valued at a median $86,300 here, a few thousand dollars of correction can matter, so documented condition problems are worth the effort.

Homestead exemption

The exemption trims the assessed value of the house you occupy as your main residence. The state default is $2,000, and a county may offer more through local legislation. In Wilkinson County the Chief Appraiser takes homestead applications.

File whenever you like. A form arriving after April 1 waits for next year, and an owner who never files is treated as having waived it.

A buyer needs a fresh application of their own after closing. If you moved out and rented the house, ask the Chief Appraiser how the parcel is classified before you list it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wilkinson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with back taxes or a lien

Your title company asks the commissioner for a payoff figure and deducts it from your proceeds. If a FiFa lien was filed, it appears on the Clerk of Superior Court's execution docket until the tax, fees and interest clear.

Write the proration into the contract, since the county bills one owner of record and never divides a year between two people.

Manufactured homes have extra steps. State guidance gives the owner 30 days after placement to obtain a location permit, then a yearly renewal each winter, plus a return due April 1. Check that all three are current before you advertise.

A cash buyer who purchases as-is can skip repair negotiations, but the tax payoff and any lien release still happen at closing exactly as they would in a listed sale.

Steps from listing to closing

Start by pulling your latest bill and assessment notice, then call the commissioner's office to ask whether anything is overdue. Next, confirm with the Chief Appraiser that your homestead filing is on record. Once you have a buyer, the title company requests the payoff and the contract sets how the year's tax is split between the two of you. After closing, the buyer files their own homestead application and you forward any stray mail about the parcel. If a manufactured home sits on the land, add the permit and renewal check to that list before the sale date, since the commissioner can refuse to issue paperwork while a balance is open.

Frequently asked questions

Who mails the property tax statement in Wilkinson County?

The tax commissioner does. The office is on Bacon Street in Irwinton and answers at (478) 946-2232. Value disputes belong to the assessors at (478) 946-2076.

Is December 20 the due date for Wilkinson County taxes?

Usually, but follow the date on your own bill, because a county can pick an earlier deadline.

What is the window for contesting a Wilkinson County value?

Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice is sent. Address the written appeal to the assessors at P.O. Box 189.

Does a mid-year sale shift the tax to the buyer?

Not automatically. The owner on New Year's Day is responsible for the full year, so sellers and buyers usually divide the bill inside the contract.

Where is the homestead exemption filed in Wilkinson County?

At the assessors' office, where the Chief Appraiser takes applications.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Worth County?

Who bills and who values property in Worth County

Worth County runs billing and valuation through different offices. The assessors alone set what a parcel is worth. The elected tax commissioner, who answers to neither the assessors nor the county commissioners, mails the statements. A seller needs the payoff from one and the value history from the other.

For pricing context, the county had an estimated 20,059 people in July 2025, with a median home value of $104,900 and owners in 73.7% of houses. Rent runs a median $864, so a landlord buying the house would be pricing against that figure.

On sales, Georgia's rule is short: the January 1 owner owes the year, and a March or June closing returns nothing. Build the closing statement with that in mind.

Which office should I call?

Call the tax commissioner for bills and payoffs, and call the assessors for values, returns and exemptions.

Worth County property tax contacts and what each one answers
OfficeQuestions it handlesContact
Tax CommissionerBilling, payments, payoff figures, liens, tags201 N. Main St., Room 15, Sylvester, GA 31791; (229) 776-8204; Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30
Board of Tax AssessorsProperty values, returns, appeals, homestead(229) 776-8203
Board of CommissionersMillage, solid waste fee waivers(229) 776-8200, extension 1
Clerk of CourtsCopies of your warranty deedFirst floor of the county courthouse

You can pay online, mail a check to the Room 15 address, phone in a payment, or use the drop box in the alley between the courthouse and the jail.

When the Worth County bill is due

Land, buildings and business property are paid in two parts, one due October 15 and the other November 15. Manufactured homes follow an April 1 date instead. A weekend deadline rolls to Monday.

Schedules can move with the digest, so treat the date on your own statement as final and phone the office if a closing lands near a deadline.

Georgia's default is December 20 unless a local government moves it, with interest held off until 60 days past the bill's postmark. Request the exact late charges along with your payoff, and ask whether the bill for your parcel has already gone out.

  • Only a USPS-dated postmark proves a payment was on time. A meter stamp is rejected.
  • The office takes installments of any size, yet charges keep growing on the unpaid remainder.
  • Statements go to the homeowner and never to the lender. Mortgage companies receive a data file, so forward your bill if escrow pays it.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Worth County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Solid waste fee on the tax bill

Any residential or business structure outside the cities carries an annual $264.00 solid waste fee, added to the same bill. The Board of Commissioners adopted it by resolution beginning in 2019.

Two relief paths exist. If a structure is dilapidated or vacant for the entire year, the owner can file a waiver request for the Board of Commissioners to approve. Owners over 65 whose total household income is $15,200 or less can qualify for an elderly exemption by completing an affidavit at the commissioners' office, reachable at (229) 776-8200, extension 1.

An inherited or empty rural house may carry the fee even when nobody has lived there. Ask whether a waiver was ever filed, and include any unpaid fee in the payoff figure.

How to contest a Worth County value

Your written appeal must reach the assessors within 45 days of the date printed on the notice. State the grounds (taxability, value, uniformity, or a refused exemption) and name the route you want.

Before April 1 each year, owners may file a return stating a preferred value. The assessors review it and, if they disagree, mail a notice carrying their figure, which starts the clock. Questions about the form go to (229) 776-8203.

The three routes are the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. State revenue staff oversee the process but cannot reverse a single parcel's outcome. Any refund from a final value is processed automatically.

Gather recent sales of similar houses, photographs of defects and any repair estimates before you file, and keep a copy of the written appeal along with proof of the mailing date.

Homestead and other exemptions

Homestead status requires owning and occupying the house on New Year's Day, and the assessors' office approves each application. Forms can arrive in any month, though April 1 is the last day that helps the current bill.

Approval rolls forward each year while you stay put. A move or a deed change restarts the process, so a buyer files fresh after closing.

Other programs worth asking about:

  • The freeport exemption for business personal property, handled by the assessors.
  • Special assessment programs, which the assessors can describe by phone.
  • The elderly exemption from the solid waste fee described above.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Worth County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Late taxes and liens

A 30-day warning letter goes out before any lien is filed. The lien, a FiFa, lands on the General Execution Docket held by the superior court clerk once a balance passes 90 days late, and because the entry is public, credit bureaus may pick it up.

Full payment of tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. Liens are not sold over the counter here. Once a levy and tax sale advertisement begin, the office urges walking the payment in.

Manufactured and modular homes count as personal property, and the location permit is withheld until the current mobile home tax is paid in full. A seller with one on the lot should settle that account first.

What a seller does before closing

Begin with a call to the tax commissioner for the payoff and the current late charges. Then ask the assessors whether your homestead is on file and what value is on your assessment notice. If the house sits outside a city, ask the commissioners' office about the solid waste fee and any waiver. Order a copy of your warranty deed from the Clerk of Courts if you do not have one handy. At the closing table, the payoff comes out of your proceeds and the year's tax is split in the contract, because the county bills one owner and never divides a year. A cash buyer purchasing as-is skips repair talks, but these tax steps stay the same, so finishing them early keeps the sale from stalling.

Two small habits help. Keep the postmarked envelope or the receipt from every payment, because the postmark is the only proof the office accepts. And if your mortgage company pays from escrow, forward any statement that reaches you, since the lender gets a data file rather than the printed bill. Sellers with a mobile home on the property should also confirm that the current mobile home tax is paid and the location permit is in hand before a buyer walks the lot.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Worth County tax office?

At 201 N. Main St., Room 15 in Sylvester, or by phone at (229) 776-8204. You can also pay online, through the mail, or at the drop box in the alley beside the jail.

What are the Worth County tax due dates?

October 15 and November 15 for land and buildings, and April 1 for mobile homes. Your bill has the final word.

What is the cutoff to dispute a Worth County value?

Forty-five days, counting from the notice. Call the assessors at (229) 776-8203 for the form.

Does the solid waste fee apply to a vacant house?

It can, though a structure dilapidated or empty all year may earn a waiver. The commissioners' office at (229) 776-8200, extension 1 decides.

Will a late payment hurt my credit?

Only if a lien is recorded, which can follow a balance more than 90 days late. The tax office itself reports nothing to credit bureaus.
